He who does not have name and form manifests *(bheje*) names and forms along with his birth and activities. Not to have name and form would be a fault. That is expressed by the word *ananta* (unlimited). If he does not have names and forms, it would mean he does not have śaktis. The Pracetās say *na hy antas tvad-vibhūtīnāṁ so ’nanta iti gīyase*: since there is no end to your splendor (names and forms), you are called Ananta, the unlimited. (SB 4.30.31) The cause of his manifesting name and form is his śaktis. Bhagavān means possessing auspicious śaktis. The word *paramaḥ* (supreme) excludes śaktis made of material māyā. *Paramaḥ* means “he in whom Lakṣmī (*mā*) exists as the para-śakti.” If his śaktis were material, it would be a fault to his supreme position. It is said:

*tasmān na māyayā sarvaṁ sarvam aiśvarya-sambhavam \|*  
*amāyo hīśvaro yasmāt tasmāt taṁ paramaṁ viduḥ \|\|*

**Therefore everything connected with the Lord is not produced by māyā. Everything arises by his spiritual powers. Since the Lord is without māyā he is known as the supreme. (Viṣṇu-dharmottara)**

“The proof of whether the Lord has names and forms or does not have names and forms is the existence of worshippers. Who are these worshippers?” I manifest my forms and names for giving mercy to those who worship my feet. I reveal names and forms, not to the followers of yoga or Sāṅkhya, but to the devotee. *Bhaktir evainaṁ darśayati*: bhakti alone reveals the Lord. (Māṭhara-śruti) Thus it is correct to say that the two parties are only interested in quarrelling. Later it will be said:

*iti stutaḥ saṁstuvataḥ sa tasminn aghamarṣaṇe*  
*prādurāsīt kuru-śreṣṭha bhagavān bhakta-vatsalaḥ*

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit! The Supreme Lord, affectionate to his devotees, on being praised by Dakṣa, appeared at that holy place known as Aghamarṣaṇa. (SB 6.4.35)**

Because he shows his form to persons who worship his feet, the form must have existed previously to that.

*caraṇaṁ pavitraṁ vitataṁ purāṇaṁ yena pūtas tarati duṣkṛtāni:*

**We become purified and can cross saṁsāra by that pure, eternal foot which extends itself everywhere. (Mahā-nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad)**

*Bheje* is in the past tense to indicate that his limbs are eternal. Since the Lord is *ananta* (eternal and infinite), so are his names and forms. Thus the Lord is devoid of material names and forms.

### Text 34

*yaḥ prākṛtair jñāna-pathair janānāṁ*  
*yathāśayaṁ deha-gato vibhāti*  
*yathānilaḥ pārthivam āśrito guṇaṁ*  
*sa īśvaro me kurutāṁ manoratham*

**Перевод:**

**That Lord, who enters the bodies of persons following an immature path of knowledge, appears to be a** ***jīva*** **according to the nature of their hearts, just as air appears variously after taking shelter of various fragrances. That Lord should fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

“Forms like Ganeśa, with upādhis, empowered by me, are suitable for your worship since you desire powers like them. Why do you praise me as the soul of all, devoid of upādhis?” This verse answers. Why worship upādhis? You are situated without upādhis, like the air that produces effects.

### Text 35-39

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti stutaḥ saṁstuvataḥ sa tasminn aghamarṣaṇe*  
*prādurāsīt kuru-śreṣṭha bhagavān bhakta-vatsalaḥ*  
*kṛta-pādaḥ suparṇāṁse pralambāṣṭa-mahā-bhujaḥ*  
*cakra-śaṅkhāsi-carmeṣu- dhanuḥ-pāśa-gadā-dharaḥ*  
*pīta-vāsā ghana-śyāmaḥ prasanna-vadanekṣaṇaḥ*  
*vana-mālā-nivītāṅgo lasac-chrīvatsa-kaustubhaḥ*  
*mahā-kirīṭa-kaṭakaḥ sphuran-makara-kuṇḍalaḥ*  
*kāñcy-aṅgulīya-valaya- nūpurāṅgada-bhūṣitaḥ*  
*trailokya-mohanaṁ rūpaṁ bibhrat tribhuvaneśvaraḥ*  
*vṛto nārada-nandādyaiḥ pārṣadaiḥ sura-yūthapaiḥ*  
*stūyamāno 'nugāyadbhiḥ siddha-gandharva-cāraṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O Mahārāja Parīkṣit! The Supreme Lord, affectionate to his devotees, on being praised by Dakṣa, appeared at that holy place known as Aghamarṣaṇa. The Lord's lotus feet rested on the shoulders of Garuḍa, and he possessed eight long, powerful arms. In his hands he held a disc, conchshell, sword, shield, arrow, bow, rope and club. His garments were yellow and his bodily hue was deep bluish. His eyes and face were very cheerful. His body was covered with a garland of flowers and his chest was decorated with the shining Kaustubha jewel and the mark of Śrīvatsa. On his head was a huge crown, on his feet were anklets, and decorating his ears were shining earrings resembling** ***makaras.*** **The Lord wore a golden belt on his waist, bracelets on his arms, rings on his fingers, and ankle bells on his feet. Having a form attractive the three worlds, the Lord of the three worlds was accompanied by great devotees like Nārada, Nanda and groups of** ***devatās.*** **He was praised by the Siddhas, Gandharvas and Cāraṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Five and a half verses describe the Lord.

### Text 41

*na kiñcanodīrayitum aśakat tīvrayā mudā*  
*āpūrita-manodvārair hradinya iva nirjharaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because his senses were filled with intense bliss, like waterfalls filling up rivers, he could not speak at all.**

**Комментарий:**

He could not speak, with his knowledge senses and mind (*manodvāraiḥ*) filled completely with intense (*tivrayā*) bliss, in the form of prema from his ātmā, like full streams of water pouring from a lake.

### Text 45

*brahmā bhavo bhavantaś ca manavo vibudheśvarāḥ*  
*vibhūtayo mama hy etā bhūtānāṁ bhūti-hetavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva, the Manus, you Prajāpatis, the Manus, and the leaders of the** ***devatās*****, who are all my expansions, strive to increase powers of the living entities.**

**Комментарий:**

“Since you are without desire, why do you desire vibhūtis (powers)? You do so out of affection, being devotees. Brahmā and others who are my vibhūtis are causes of increase of powers (*bhūti*) in others.

### Text 46

*tapo me hṛdayaṁ brahmaṁs tanur vidyā kriyākṛtiḥ*  
*aṅgāni kratavo jātā dharma ātmāsavaḥ surāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O** ***brāhmaṇa*****! Austerity is my heart, Vedic knowledge in the form of hymns and** ***mantras*** **constitutes my body, and daily and occasional rites are my form. Sacrifices are the various limbs of my body. The unseen good fortune proceeding from sacrifice constitutes my mind, and the** ***devatās*** **are my life airs.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhakti is my antaraṅga-śakti.

### Text 47

*aham evāsam evāgre nānyat kiñcāntaraṁ bahiḥ*  
*saṁjñāna-mātram avyaktaṁ prasuptam iva viśvataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I alone existed before the creation, I alone will exist after the creation, and I alone exist now. Nothing exists outside of me or inside of me. I am also pure consciousness, imperceptible to the senses, quiet as if sleeping, and all-pervading.**

**Комментарий:**

He shows that the devotee is the cause of his creation. I was concerned with the material world or lotus, not Vaikuṇṭha.

### Text 48

*mayy ananta-guṇe 'nante guṇato guṇa-vigrahaḥ*  
*yadāsīt tata evādyaḥ svayambhūḥ samabhūd ajaḥ*

**Перевод:**

*balo gaṇāt krodha-vaśād ahīndraḥ*

**Перевод:**

May Yajña protect me from defamation! May Balarāma protect me from injury caused by others! Śeṣa protect me from envious serpents.**

**Комментарий:**

One version has *kṛtāntāt* instead of *janāntāt*. This shows Balarāma has more śakti than Śeṣa. *Janāntāt* means “destruction from other people.”

### Text 20

*māṁ keśavo gadayā prātar avyād*  
*govinda āsaṅgavam ātta-veṇuḥ*  
*nārāyaṇaḥ prāhṇa udātta-śaktir*  
*madhyan-dine viṣṇur arīndra-pāṇiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**May Keśava protect me with his club in the first portion of the day, and may Govinda, who is always engaged in playing his flute, protect me in the second portion of the day. May Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is equipped with all potencies, protect me in the third part of the day, and may Lord Viṣṇu, who carries a disc to kill his enemies, protect me in the fourth part of the day (noon).**

**Комментарий:**

This shows the eternal manifestation of the Lord of Mathurā and Vṛndāvana. The names are linked to various times during the day.

Forenoon is the first division of the day and *prātaḥ* (early morning) and *saṅgava* (morning) are its divisions. Noon is the middle division of the day. The third division is afternoon divided into evening and twilight (*sandhyā*). In the night, pradoṣa is the first division. The middle division is *niśītha*, with midnight include--the two ghaṭikas in the middle of the night. The third division of the night is called *apara-rātra*. Its two last parts are called *pratyūṣa* and *prabhāta.*

According to the sandhyās there is a different classification. In listing that sequence, forenoon is not considered separately, otherwise it would go beyond noon.

*muhūrta-tritayaṁ prātas tāvān eva tu saṅgavaḥ \|*  
*madhyāhnas tri-muhūrto’tha aparāhṇo’pi tādṛśaḥ \|*  
*sāyāhnas tri-muhūrtaḥ syat sarva-karmasu garhitaḥ*

***Prāta*** **is three muhūrtas and** ***saṅgava*** **is the same duration.** ***Madhyāhna*** **(noon) is three muhūrtas and afternoon (*****aparahna*****) is the same. Evening (*****sāyāhna*****) is three muhūrtas. All activities are forbidden at this time.**

### Text 32-33

*Yathaikātmyānubhāvānāṁ vikalpa-rahitaḥ svayam*  
*bhūṣaṇāyudha-liṅgākhyā dhatte śaktīḥ sva-māyayā*  
*tenaiva satya-mānena sarva-jño bhagavān hariḥ*  
*pātu sarvaiḥ svarūpair naḥ sadā sarvatra sarva-gaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**May the all-pervading, omniscient Lord protect us at all times and places by his many forms, if it is true that he is non-different from his** ***śaktis*** **such as his ornaments, weapons, forms and names and that he still maintains them by his** ***svarūpa-śakti.***

**Комментарий:**

**Bhagavat Sandarbha 62:**

The Lord appears without difference from his śakti (*rahita-vikalpaḥ*) to persons absorbed in seeing his supreme form (*aikyātmānubhāvānām*). By his mercy (*sva-māyayā)* he manifests as the supreme form filled with the highest bliss to those who worship him as their master. He manifests śaktis called his ornaments by his svarūpa endowed with various śaktis *(svayam*). If this is true, proved by the experience of the wise (*satya-pramāṇena*), then may he protect us with his ornaments and weapons that arise from his variegated svarūpa *(svarūpaiḥ*).

Bali praises the Lord’s cakra:

*yasya rūpam anirdeśyam api yogibhir uttamair*

**This form is not detected by the best yogīs. (Viṣṇu-dharma)**

*bhramatas tasya cakrasya nābhi-madhye mahī-pate \|*  
*trailokyam akhilaṁ daityo dṛṣṭavān bhūr bhuvādikam \|\|*

**O king! The demon saw within the moving cakra all the three worlds including Bhūr, Bhuvar and other planets. (Viṣṇu-dharma)**

In the Ninth Canto Ambarīṣa also praises the cakra. The word *liṅga* refers to the Lord’s flag marked with Garuḍa and such items. Like the appearance of the Lord, these things sometimes appear to have a beginning. But they are non-different from him:

*kaumodakīṁ bhagavato dayitāṁ smareta*  
*digdhām arāti-bhaṭa-śoṇita-kardamena*  
*mālāṁ madhuvrata-varūtha-giropaghuṣṭāṁ*  
*caityasya tattvam amalaṁ maṇim asya kaṇṭhe*

**One should meditate on the Lord’s dear club Kaumodakī, smeared with the blood of the enemy. One should meditate on his garland buzzing with swarms of bees, and on the pure Kaustubha jewel on his neck, which represents jīva-tattva. (SB 3.28.28)**

*kaustubha-vyapadeśena svātma-jyotir bibharty ajaḥ*  
*tat-prabhā vyāpinī sākṣāt śrīvatsam urasā vibhuḥ*

**Upon his chest the almighty, unborn Lord bears the pure jīva in the form of the vibhūti** **known as the Kaustubha gem along with the Śrīvatsa mark, which is the direct manifestation of this gem's expansive effulgence. (SB 12.11.10)**

The above verses show that his paraphernalia are non-different from himself in worship of the universal form. These items should be seen as directly part of the Lord.

*ātmānam asya jagato nirlepam aguṇāmalam \|*  
*bibharti kaustubha-maṇi-svarūpaṁ bhagavān harir \|\|*

**The Lord wears the Kaustubha gem which is himself, uncontaminated by the material world and without material guṇas. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.22.68)**

**Перевод:**

### Text 10

*dravya-bhūyo-vareṇāpas turīyaṁ jagṛhur malam*  
*tāsu budbuda-phenābhyāṁ dṛṣṭaṁ tad dharati kṣipan*

**Перевод:**

**In return for King Indra's benediction that water would increase the volume of other substances with which it was mixed, water accepted one fourth of the sinful reactions. This is visible in bubbles and foam in water. When one collects water, these should be avoided.**

**Комментарий:**

Another version has *drava* instead of *dravya.* According to Śrīdhara Svāmī it means water would mix with other substances. It is understood that water would not mix previously. Or water, on being raised, would flow in cascades. Previously it did not do so. The reading *drava-bhūyah* means that previously water was thicker, but by the benediction it flowed nicely.

### Text 11

*hata-putras tatas tvaṣṭā juhāvendrāya śatrave*  
*indra-śatro vivardhasva mā ciraṁ jahi vidviṣam*

**Перевод:**

**After Viśvarūpa was killed, his father, Tvaṣṭā, performed a sacrifice to kill Indra, saying, "O enemy of Indra, flourish to kill your enemy without delay."**

**Комментарий:**

The words *indra-śatro* means “killer of Indra!” Vṛtra would be a killer. However the other meaning “Indra, killer!” would mean that Indra would be the killer. The accent should come on the last syllable according to the rule *samāsaysa ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.223) to mean “killer of Indra!” If the word Indra has an accent in this compound it is *bahuvrīhi* compound, and means “Indra, the enemy.” This is according to *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam:* the first member of a compound preserves its original accent in a *bahuvrīhi* compound*.*

By chance he pronounced the words so that they had the opposite meaning, so that Indra, his enemy would increase in power.
