*yat kiñcid om iti brūyāt tena ricyeta vai pumān*  
*bhikṣave sarvam oṁ kurvan nālaṁ kāmena cātmane*

**Перевод:**

***Oṁ*** **indicates separation from wealth, being devoid of wealth. He who utters** ***oṁ*** **and agrees to give becomes lesser in wealth by that. If he decides to give everything to the person who requests, there will not be enough left for his own enjoyment.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains the word oṁ.

### Text 43

*strīṣu narma-vivāhe ca vṛtty-arthe prāṇa-saṅkaṭe*  
*go-brāhmaṇārthe hiṁsāyāṁ nānṛtaṁ syāj jugupsitam*

**Перевод:**

**In flattering a woman, in joking, in order to get married, in earning one's livelihood, in dangerous circumstances, in protecting cows and brahminical culture, or in protecting a person from an enemy's hand, falsity is never condemned.**

**Комментарий:**

Though lying is famous for low people, and explained when describing what is acceptable and unacceptable, sometimes there are opposite results. That is explained. In four situations, one can lie out of dharma for one’s own benefit. One can lie to protect one’s own life or for protecting cows or brāhmaṇas, when there is destruction of their functions. This also includes devotees. Also when there is violence to others lying is permitted. In those cases lying is not condemned. When truth produces violence, it is condemned.

Chapter Nineteen

No commentaries

## Chapter Twenty

### Text 9

*sulabhā yudhi viprarṣe hy anivṛttās tanu-tyajaḥ*  
*na tathā tīrtha āyāte śraddhayā ye dhana-tyajaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O best of the** ***brāhmaṇas*****! Many men have laid down their lives on the battlefield, fearless in fighting, but rarely has one obtained the chance to give his accumulated wealth when there is an opportunity for giving.**

**Комментарий:**

Should one give up one’s life in battle? Giving up life in battle is common. Giving up wealth with faith when there is a suitable candidate is rare. Life is essential in comparison to wealth, but out of illusion people considering wealth essential for everything.

### Text 12

*yadyapy asāv adharmeṇa māṁ badhnīyād anāgasam*  
*tathāpy enaṁ na hiṁsiṣye bhītaṁ brahma-tanuṁ ripum*

**Перевод:**

**Because he has assumed the form of a** ***brāhmaṇa*** **full of fear, even if he irreligiously arrests me, though I am sinless, I shall not retaliate, although he is my enemy.**

**Комментарий:**

He pacifies Śukra in order to get his permission, in two verses. Śrīdhara Svāmī shows the actual meaning of the words. After praying to have the Lord’s feet on his head, he developed real bhakti. This was a conclusion to the bhakti-rasābhāsa.

### Text 13

*eṣa vā uttamaśloko na jihāsati yad yaśaḥ*  
*hatvā maināṁ hared yuddhe śayīta nihato mayā*

**Перевод:**

**Since he is Viṣṇu of imperishable fame, he will not give up that fame. Killing me in battle, he will take the land. I can never kill him.**

**Комментарий:**

He shows Viṣṇu’s fearful nature.

### Text 21

*tad vāmanaṁ rūpam avardhatādbhutaṁ*  
*harer anantasya guṇa-trayātmakam*  
*bhūḥ khaṁ diśo dyaur vivarāḥ payodhayas*  
*tiryaṅ-nṛ-devā ṛṣayo yad-āsata*

**Перевод:**

**The form of the dwarf, the unlimited Lord, containing within himself the whole material realm, within whom existed the earth, ether, the directions, Svarga,** ***antarīkṣa*****, the oceans, animals, humans,** ***devatās*** **and sages, then increased astonishingly.**

**Комментарий:**

That form expanded to include the three guṇas (*tri-guṇātmakam*).

### Text 22

*kāye balis tasya mahā-vibhūteḥ*  
*sahartvig-ācārya-sadasya etat*  
*dadarśa viśvaṁ tri-guṇaṁ guṇātmake*  
*bhūtendriyārthāśaya-jīva-yuktam*

**Перевод:**

**Bali Mahārāja, along with all the priests,** ***ācāryas*** **and members of the assembly, observed within the supreme Lord endowed with six qualities the universe composed of the three** ***guṇas*****--including all gross material elements, the senses, the sense objects, the** ***antaḥkaraṇa*** **and the** ***jīvas.***

**Комментарий:**

Bali observed the universe within the Lord endowed with six qualities (*guṇātmake*).

### Text 23

*rasām acaṣṭāṅghri-tale 'tha pādayor*  
*mahīṁ mahīdhrān puruṣasya jaṅghayoḥ*  
*patattriṇo jānuni viśva-mūrter*  
*ūrvor gaṇaṁ mārutam indrasenaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Bali Mahārāja, who was occupying the seat of Indra, saw the surface of the earth on the soles of the feet of the Lord's universal form. He saw on the Lord's feet objects situated on the earth, on his calves he saw all the mountains, on his knees he saw the various birds, and on his thighs he saw the varieties of winds.**

**Комментарий:**

Indrasena is a name of Bali, as mentioned in Tenth Canto:

*sa indraseno bhagavat-padāmbujaṁ*  
*bibhran muhuḥ prema-vibhinnayā dhiyā*  
*uvāca hānanda-jalākulekṣaṇaḥ*  
*prahṛṣṭa-romā nṛpa gadgadākṣaram*

**Taking hold of the Lords’ lotus feet again and again, Bali, the conqueror of Indra’s army, spoke from his heart, which was melting out of his intense love. O King, as tears of ecstasy filled his eyes and the hair on his limbs stood on end, he began to speak with faltering words. (SB 10.85.38)**

### Text 25-29

*hṛdy aṅga dharmaṁ stanayor murārer*  
*ṛtaṁ ca satyaṁ ca manasy athendum*  
*śriyaṁ ca vakṣasy aravinda-hastāṁ*  
*kaṇṭhe ca sāmāni samasta-rephān*  
*indra-pradhānān amarān bhujeṣu*  
*tat-karṇayoḥ kakubho dyauś ca mūrdhni*  
*keśeṣu meghāñ chvasanaṁ nāsikāyām*  
*akṣṇoś ca sūryaṁ vadane ca vahnim*  
*vāṇyāṁ ca chandāṁsi rase jaleśaṁ*  
*bhruvor niṣedhaṁ ca vidhiṁ ca pakṣmasu*  
*ahaś ca rātriṁ ca parasya puṁso*  
*manyuṁ lalāṭe 'dhara eva lobham*  
*sparśe ca kāmaṁ nṛpa retasāmbhaḥ*  
*pṛṣṭhe tv adharmaṁ kramaṇeṣu yajñam*  
*chāyāsu mṛtyuṁ hasite ca māyāṁ*  
*tanū-ruheṣv oṣadhi-jātayaś ca*  
*nadīś ca nāḍīṣu śilā nakheṣu*  
*buddhāv ajaṁ deva-gaṇān ṛṣīṁś ca*  
*prāṇeṣu gātre sthira-jaṅgamāni*  
*sarvāṇi bhūtāni dadarśa vīraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King! On the heart of Murāri he saw religion; on the chest, both pleasing words and truthfulness; in his mind, the moon; on his chest, the goddess of fortune, with a lotus flower in her hand; on his neck, all the Vedas and all syllables; on his arms, all the** ***devatās*****, headed by Indra; in both ears, all the directions; on his head, Svarga; on his hair, the clouds; in his nostrils, the wind; on his eyes, the sun; and in his mouth, fire. In his words were all the Vedic verses, on his tongue was Varuṇa, on his eyebrows were the rules and prohibitions, and on the opening and closing of his eyelids were day and night. On his forehead was anger, and on his lips was greed. O King! In his touch were lusty desires, in his semen were all the waters, on his back was irreligion, and in his wonderful activities was the fire of sacrifice. On his shadow was death, in his smile was the illusory energy, and on the hairs of his body were all the drugs and herbs. In his veins were all the rivers, on his nails were all the stones, in his intelligence were Lord Brahmā, the** ***devatās*** **and the sages. Throughout his entire body and senses were all living entities, moving and stationary.**

**Комментарий:**

Five verses describe the form. The word *eva* should be added to the other words also. On the lower lip (*adhare eva*) was greed. When the lower lip is very visible it indicates greed. In his shadows or indications of unfavorable moods (*chāyāsu)* was death. In his amusing smile was māyā. Māyā took shelter of his smile.

### Text 32-33

*sunanda-mukhyā upatasthur īśaṁ*  
*pārṣada-mukhyāḥ saha-loka-pālāḥ*  
*sphurat-kirīṭāṅgada-mīna-kuṇḍalaḥ*  
*śrīvatsa-ratnottama-mekhalāmbaraiḥ*  
*madhuvrata-srag-vanamālayāvṛto*  
*rarāja rājan bhagavān urukramaḥ*  
*kṣitiṁ padaikena baler vicakrame*  
*nabhaḥ śarīreṇa diśaś ca bāhubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The chief among the Lord’s associates, among those the chiefs, headed by Sunanda, accompanied by all the** ***devatās*** **protecting the planets, offered prayers to the Lord. The Lord, who wore a brilliant crown, bracelets, and earrings that resembled fish, with Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha on his chest, wearing a yellow garment covered by a belt, with garland surrounded by bees in the shape of the garland, shone brilliantly. O King! The Supreme Lord, whose activities are wonderful, covered the earth belonging to Bali with one footstep, the sky with his body, and all directions with his arms.**

**Комментарий:**

By kicking up his right foot, he covered the earth (*padaikena*).

### Text 34

*padaṁ dvitīyaṁ kramatas triviṣṭapaṁ*  
*na vai tṛtīyāya tadīyam aṇv api*  
*urukramasyāṅghrir upary upary atho*  
*mahar-janābhyāṁ tapasaḥ paraṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the Lord took his second step, he covered the heavenly planets. And not even a spot remained for the third step, for the Lord's foot extended higher and higher, beyond Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka and even Satyaloka.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking his second step, he covered the heavenly planets (*triviṣṭapam*). There was no space at all for his third step (*tadīyam*). His body covered the sky. There was not space for his request for three steps of land. This is not improper, since the word “land” also includes everything above the land.

## Chapter Twenty-one

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*satyaṁ samīkṣyābja-bhavo nakhendubhir*  
*hata-svadhāma-dyutir āvṛto 'bhyagāt*  
*marīci-miśrā ṛṣayo bṛhad-vratāḥ*  
*sanandanādyā nara-deva yoginaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King! After seeing his planet touched by Vāmana’s foot, Lord Brahmā, his abode, his effulgence and his own form became dim by the light from the effulgence of Vāmana’s moon-like toe nails. He offered respects to the Lord and the great sages headed by Marīci and by** ***yogīs*** **like Sanandana also offered respects to the Lord.**

### Text 2-3

*vedopavedā niyamā yamānvitās*  
*tarketihāsāṅga-purāṇa-saṁhitāḥ*  
*ye cāpare yoga-samīra-dīpita-*  
*jñānāgninā randhita-karma-kalmaṣāḥ*  
*vavandire yat-smaraṇānubhāvataḥ*  
*svāyambhuvaṁ dhāma gatā akarmakam*  
*athāṅghraye pronnamitāya viṣṇor*  
*upāharat padma-bhavo 'rhaṇodakam*  
*samarcya bhaktyābhyagṛṇāc chuci-śravā*  
*yan-nābhi-paṅkeruha-sambhavaḥ svayam*

**Перевод:**

**The Vedas, Upavedas, Nyāya scriptures, histories, the** ***aṅgas*** **of the Vedas, Purāṇas, Saṁhitās, along with** ***yamas*** **and** ***niyamas,*** **and persons purified of sinful acts by the fire of knowledge which was ignited by the air of** ***yoga,*** **persons who had attained Brahmaloka (which is devoid of** ***karma-kāṇḍa)*** **by the power of remembering the Lord’s feet, offered respects to the Lord. Brahmā offered foot water to the Lord’s raised feet. Brahmā of spotless fame, who appeared from the Lord’s navel, then worshipped the Lord with devotion and praised him.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together*. Saṁhitāḥ* refers to works like Brahma-saṁhitā. Those who had gone to Brahma-loka, being free of bondage of karma (*akarmakam*), worshipped the Lord’s feet. These persons thus attain liberation along with Brahmā.

### Text 4

*dhātuḥ kamaṇḍalu-jalaṁ tad urukramasya*  
*pādāvanejana-pavitratayā narendra*  
*svardhuny abhūn nabhasi sā patatī nimārṣṭi*  
*loka-trayaṁ bhagavato viśadeva kīrtiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King! The water from Lord Brahmā's pot, purified by washing the lotus feet of Vāmanadeva, became the water of the Gaṅgā. Falling down from the sky, it purifies the three worlds like the pure fame of the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

In the Fifth Canto, in the description of Sumeru, the Gaṅgā arose as the current of water from outside the universe, when Vāmana’s toe pierced the shell. That water, after a thousand yugas, descended onto Sumeru. It is said that as the Gaṅgā appears now, it appears at other times also in the same manner. It is described in other Purāṇas that at the sacrifice of Bāṣkali, as at Bali’s sacrifice, Vāmana deva came and cheated him in the same manner. This happened previously. After Satī gave up her body, the description of Gaṅgā falling on Kailāsa happened. *Viśadā* means pure white.

### Text 5

*brahmādayo loka-nāthāḥ sva-nāthāya samādṛtāḥ*  
*sānugā balim ājahruḥ saṅkṣiptātma-vibhūtaye*

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā and the lords of the planets and their followers in great respect arranged for worship of their master, who reduced his size again.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses describe the worship.

### Text 16-17

*nandaḥ sunando 'tha jayo vijayaḥ prabalo balaḥ*  
*kumudaḥ kumudākṣaś ca viṣvaksenaḥ patattrirāṭ*  
*jayantaḥ śrutadevaś ca puṣpadanto 'tha sātvataḥ*  
*sarve nāgāyuta-prāṇāś camūṁ te jaghnur āsurīm*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda, Sunanda, Jaya, Vijaya, Prabala, Bala, Kumuda, Kumudākṣa, Viṣvaksena, Garuḍa Jayanta, Śrutadeva, Puṣpadanta and Sātvata, as powerful as ten thousand elephants, killed the demonic army.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Because they appeared suddenly, they are understood to be eternal associates of the Lord. They were there but hidden. Jaya and Vijaya are other devotees of Vaikuṇṭha (not the gate keepers). *Nāgas* are elephants who are *vibhūtis* of the Lord in Vaikuṇṭha.

### Text 18

*hanyamānān svakān dṛṣṭvā puruṣānucarair baliḥ*  
*vārayām āsa saṁrabdhān kāvya-śāpam anusmaran*

**Перевод:**

**When Bali Mahārāja saw that his soldiers were being killed by the associates of Viṣṇu and when he remembered the curse of Śukrācārya, he prevented his angry soldiers from fighting.**

**Комментарий:**

This made him remember (*anusmaran*) the curse of Śukrācārya.

### Text 19

*he vipracitte he rāho he neme śrūyatāṁ vacaḥ*  
*mā yudhyata nivartadhvaṁ na naḥ kālo 'yam artha-kṛt*

**Перевод:**

**O Vipracitti, O Rāhu, O Nemi! Please hear my words! Don't fight. Stop immediately, for the present time is not in our favor.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks to appease them. The words are not the highest truth.

### Text 21

*yo no bhavāya prāg āsīd abhavāya divaukasām*  
*sa eva bhagavān adya vartate tad-viparyayam*

**Перевод:**

**The supreme time factor was previously in our favor and not in favor of the** ***devatās*****, but now that same time factor is the opposite.**

**Комментарий:**

The time factor now exists in an opposite way (*tad-viparyayam*). We will defeat them.

### Text 23

*bhavadbhir nirjitā hy ete bahuśo 'nucarā hareḥ*  
*daivenarddhais ta evādya yudhi jitvā nadanti naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The many followers of Viṣṇu who were defeated by you, because you had strength by time, have now defeated us, and are roaring in jubilation.**

**Комментарий:**

*Daivena* here means “by time.”

### Text 31

*padaikena mayākrānto bhūrlokaḥ khaṁ diśas tanoḥ*  
*svarlokas te dvitīyena paśyatas te svam ātmanā*

**Перевод:**

**Of these possessions, with one step I have occupied Bhūrloka, and with my body I have occupied the entire sky and all directions. And in your presence, with my second step, I, with my original form, have occupied Svarga owned by you.**

**Комментарий:**

*Svam svarlokaḥ* included other planets he conquered also.

### Text 32

*pratiśrutam adātus te niraye vāsa iṣyate*  
*viśa tvaṁ nirayaṁ tasmād guruṇā cānumoditaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because you have been unable to give charity according to your promise, you should live in the hellish planets. Therefore, being pleased, enter hell along with your** ***guru.***

**Комментарий:**

*Niraye* (hell) means Pātāla, going somewhere lower.

### Text 33

*vṛthā manorathas tasya dūraḥ svargaḥ pataty adhaḥ*  
*pratiśrutasyādānena yo 'rthinaṁ vipralambhate*

**Перевод:**

**Far from being elevated to the heavenly planets or fulfilling one's desire, one who does not properly give a beggar what he has promised falls down to a hellish condition of life.**

**Комментарий:**

He confirms what he previously said with a general statement in two verses. Some versions do not have the second line but it is accepted by Śrīdhara Svāmī.

## Chapter Twenty-two

### Text 4

*puṁsāṁ ślāghyatamaṁ manye daṇḍam arhattamārpitam*  
*yaṁ na mātā pitā bhrātā suhṛdaś cādiśanti hi*

**Перевод:**

**A father, mother, brother or friend does not punish his subordinate in a thoroughly correct manner. I regard the punishment given by you, the most praiseworthy, as most exalted punishment, since it gives the best results.**

**Комментарий:**

Father, mother, brother or friend do not give proper punishment since they have worldly affection. Or it can also mean “They give proper punishment.” *Na* indicates agreement in this case.

### Text 8

*pitāmaho me bhavadīya-sammataḥ*  
*prahrāda āviṣkṛta-sādhu-vādaḥ*  
*bhavad-vipakṣeṇa vicitra-vaiśasaṁ*  
*samprāpitas tvaṁ paramaḥ sva-pitrā*

**Перевод:**

**My grandfather Prahlāda Mahārāja, honored by your devotees, famous as a devotee, although tortured in many ways by his father Hiraṇyakaśipu, still remained surrendered to you.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses describe the influence of his grandfather.

### Text 10

*itthaṁ sa niścitya pitāmaho mahān*  
*agādha-bodho bhavataḥ pāda-padmam*  
*dhruvaṁ prapede hy akutobhayaṁ janād*  
*bhītaḥ svapakṣa-kṣapaṇasya sattama*

**Перевод:**

**O best of the saintly! Discerning this, my grandfather, a great devotee, deeply knowledgeable and afraid of worldly association, surrendered to your lotus feet which dispel all fear, though you were the destroyer of his own family.**

**Комментарий:**

Prahlāda was afraid of associating with the demons (*janād bhītaḥ*).

### Text 11

*athāham apy ātma-ripos tavāntikaṁ*  
*daivena nītaḥ prasabhaṁ tyājita-śrīḥ*  
*idaṁ kṛtāntāntika-varti jīvitaṁ*  
*yayādhruvaṁ stabdha-matir na budhyate*

**Перевод:**

**Only by good fortune have I been brought under your lotus feet and deprived of all my wealth, by you, perceived as an enemy of our family. With intelligence blinded by this wealth, a person does not realize the temporary nature of life where death is continually present.**

**Комментарий:**

You were perceived to be my enemy by illusion (*ātma-ripoḥ*). By the good fortune (*daivena*) of being the grandson of Prahlāda I have been brought to your feet.

### Text 14

*tasmai balir vāruṇa-pāśa-yantritaḥ*  
*samarhaṇaṁ nopajahāra pūrvavat*  
*nanāma mūrdhnāśru-vilola-locanaḥ*  
*sa-vrīḍa-nīcīna-mukho babhūva ha*

**Перевод:**

**Being bound by the ropes of Varuṇa, Bali Mahārāja could not offer befitting respect to Prahlāda Mahārāja as he had before. Rather, he simply offered respectful obeisances with his head, while eyes filled with tears and his face lowered in shame.**

**Комментарий:**

He was ashamed because of his low actions and his ignorance on first meeting the brāhmaṇa dwarf.

### Text 15

*sa tatra hāsīnam udīkṣya sat-patiṁ*  
*hariṁ sunandādy-anugair upāsitam*  
*upetya bhūmau śirasā mahā-manā*  
*nanāma mūrdhnā pulakāśru-viklavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the great devotee Prahlāda saw the Supreme Lord seated there, being worshiped by his intimate associates like Sunanda, he approached the Lord and offered respects on the ground with his head. He was overwhelmed with tears and his hairs stood on end.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord resumed his form as Vāmana in order to obtain the remainder of the promised land.

### Text 21

*śrī-brahmovāca*  
*bhūta-bhāvana bhūteśa deva-deva jaganmaya*  
*muñcainaṁ hṛta-sarvasvaṁ nāyam arhati nigraham*

**Перевод:**

**Lord Brahmā said: O well-wisher and master of all living entities! O worshipable deity of all the** ***devatās*****! O all-pervading Lord! Please release this person bereft of everything. He does not deserve to be punished further.**

**Комментарий:**

Prahlāda and Vindyavali had implored the Lord for Bali’s offense. Brahmā implored the Lord on Bali’s behalf, seeing him as a devotee.

### Text 26

*janma-karma-vayo-rūpa- vidyaiśvarya-dhanādibhiḥ*  
*yady asya na bhavet stambhas tatrāyaṁ mad-anugrahaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**If a human being is born in an aristocratic family, if he performs wonderful activities, if he is youthful, if he has personal beauty, education or wealth, and if he is nonetheless not proud, it is to be understood that he is especially favored by me.**

**Комментарий:**

One can attain prosperity by karma or by the mercy of the Lord. Verse 24 describes the fault of attaining wealth by karma. Verse 26 describes wealth attained by the Lord’s mercy. This is without fault. Bali would not become proud by ruling Sutaḷa, or again ruling Svarga.

### Text 32

*tāvat sutalam adhyāstāṁ viśvakarma-vinirmitam*  
*yad ādhayo vyādhayaś ca klamas tandrā parābhavaḥ*  
*nopasargā nivasatāṁ sambhavanti mamekṣayā*

**Перевод:**

**Until he achieves the position of king of heaven, he should live on the planet Sutala, which was made by Viśvakarmā. Because it is especially protected by me, in that place the inhabitants are free from mental and bodily miseries, fatigue, exhaustion, defeat and all other disturbances. Bali Mahārāja, you may now go and live there peacefully.**

**Комментарий:**

Instead of *tandrā* sometimes *tandrī* is seen, according to the Unādi-sūtras.

## Chapter Twenty-three

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity uktavantaṁ puruṣaṁ purātanaṁ*  
*mahānubhāvo 'khila-sādhu-sammataḥ*  
*baddhāñjalir bāṣpa-kalākulekṣaṇo*  
*bhakty-utkalo gadgadayā girābravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The great minded, Bali Mahārāja, respected by all devotees, his eyes filled with tears, his hands folded and his voice faltering, filled with devotion, responded to the most ancient Lord, who had just spoken.**

**Комментарий:**

After folding his hands, he blissfully placed his head at the Lord’s feet according to his desire in SB 8.22.2:

*yady uttamaśloka bhavān mameritaṁ*  
*vaco vyalīkaṁ sura-varya manyate*  
*karomy ṛtaṁ tan na bhavet pralambhanaṁ*  
*padaṁ tṛtīyaṁ kuru śīrṣṇi me nijam*

**O most famous Lord, worshipped by all the** ***devatās*****! If you think that my promise has become false, I shall make it true. I should not be made a cheater. Please, therefore, place your third lotus footstep on my head.**

### Text 2

*śrī-balir uvāca*  
*aho praṇāmāya kṛtaḥ samudyamaḥ*  
*prapanna-bhaktārtha-vidhau samāhitaḥ*  
*yal loka-pālais tvad-anugraho 'marair*  
*alabdha-pūrvo 'pasade 'sure 'rpitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Bali Mahārāja said: Ah! Just my eagerness to offer respects is able to yield results sought by the surrendered devotees. This low demon has received your rare mercy, not received previously even by jīvanmuktas.**

**Комментарий:**

He then offers his prayers. Śruti says:

*idaṁ viṣṇur vicakrame tredhā nidadhe padam*

**Viṣṇu stepped three times, crossing the universe. (Black Yajur Veda)**

Sone persons offer respects with great effort (*samudyamaḥ*), paying attention to this surrender which is the ultimate goal (*puruṣārtha)* of the blissful devotees. They eventually attain that goal. This is astonishing (*aho*). There is something more astonishing. This mercy was offered by you to me, a very low demon (*apasade*). I was boldly accepting your wish, out of a desire for my own fame. This mercy was not attained by even jīvanmuktas, who have surpassed death (*amaraiḥ*).

### Text 6

*śrī-prahrāda uvāca*  
*nemaṁ viriñco labhate prasādaṁ*  
*na śrīr na śarvaḥ kim utāpare 'nye*  
*yan no 'surāṇām asi durga-pālo*  
*viśvābhivandyair abhivanditāṅghriḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Prahlāda Mahārāja said: We have attained mercy that Brahmā, Lakṣmī or Śiva, what to speak of others, have not attained. You, whose lotus feet are worshiped by the most respected person in the universe, are the protector of us demons in all respects.**

**Комментарий:**

Since I am unqualified for this mercy, the cause is only your merciful nature and nothing else. In this way he shows the supreme position of the Lord. Others speak of him as their Lord, I see that you have affection for me as a son. To express this he refers to other great devotees. The meaning is clear. Śukadeva will also refer to the great devotees later:

*nemaṁ viriñco na bhavo na śrīr apy aṅga-saṁśrayā*  
*prasādaṁ lebhire gopī yat tat prāpa vimuktidāt*

**Neither Brahmā, nor Śiva, nor even the goddess of fortune, who is always the better half of the Supreme Lord, can obtain from the Supreme Lord, the deliverer from this material world, such mercy as received by mother Yaśodā. (SB 10.9.20)**

None of them have the same type of mercy. Though the Lord binds people, he in this case is bound by the devotee. There is a great difference when the Lord is under control of the devotee.

### Text 7

*yat-pāda-padma-makaranda-niṣevaṇena*  
*brahmādayaḥ śaraṇadāśnuvate vibhūtīḥ*  
*kasmād vayaṁ kusṛtayaḥ khala-yonayas te*  
*dākṣiṇya-dṛṣṭi-padavīṁ bhavataḥ praṇītāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O supreme shelter of all beings! Brahmā and others enjoy their powers simply by tasting the honey of rendering service at your lotus feet. But how did we wicked fellows born of a demonic family, receive such great mercy?**

**Комментарий:**

How can there be any other cause? They predominantly enjoy powers (*vibhūtīḥ*), and not such mercy.

### Text 8

*citraṁ tavehitam aho 'mita-yogamāyā-*  
*līlā-visṛṣṭa-bhuvanasya viśāradasya*  
*sarvātmanaḥ samadṛśo viṣamaḥ svabhāvo*  
*bhakta-priyo yad asi kalpataru-svabhāvaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord with unlimited powers of** ***yoga!*** **Your activities are inconceivable. Though equal to all, you show favoritism. You, who create the universe as your pastime by** ***māyā,*** **who know all beings, and who give life to all beings, show particular affection for your devotees. You have the nature of a desire tree.**

**Комментарий:**

Not only with devotees like me do you act in such a manner beyond logic. You do this for your other devotees.

**Paramātmā Sandarbha 93:**

Though affectionate to devotees *(bhakti-priyaḥ),* you are equal *(samadṛśaḥ*) in nature (*svabhāvaḥ*), without partiality (*aviṣamaḥ*), because your nature is like a desire tree. Though you appear partial you are actually impartial. This is astonishing.

Another meaning is as follows. As the desire tree is equal to all who take shelter of it, because you show partiality to the devotee, and thus have a nature of inequality, you still have a nature of being equal. That conclusion should not be avoided. Thus the word can be taken as *viṣama* instead of *aviṣama.* SB 10.38.22 quoted above shows that the Lord does have partiality to the devotee. Actually, because the Lord has inconceivable powers as his chief quality, this resolves the contradiction in the Lord. It is said:

*namo namas te ’stv ṛṣabhāya sātvatāṁ*  
*vidūra-kāṣṭhāya muhuḥ kuyoginām \|*  
*nirasta-sāmyātiśayena rādhasā*  
*sva-dhāmani brahmaṇi raṁsyate namaḥ \|\|*

**I continually offer respects to you, son of Vasudeva of the Yadus, who remain forever distant from the non-devotees, who are the enjoyer in your spiritual abode in Mathurā and Vraja with your devotees, displaying powers that are unequalled and unsurpassed. (SB 2.4.14)**

Śrīdhara says in his commentary “Though it appears the Lord is partial, he has no fault, since he has inconceivable powers.” Bhīṣma says:

His actions are not a mistake of his judgment for he is faultless, he is the soul of all beings, he sees all equally, he is without a second, and is without pride.

*tathāpy ekānta-bhakteṣu paśya bhūpānukampitam \|*  
*yan me ’sūṁs tyajataḥ sākṣāt kṛṣṇo darśanam āgataḥ \|\|*

**O king! See his mercy to his dedicated devotees! By that mercy he has come before me directly when I am about to leave my body. (SB 1.8.21-22)**

The Lord says:

*samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣyo ’sti na priyaḥ \|*  
*ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham \|\|29\|\|*

**I am equal to all living beings. I do not hate anyone nor do I favor anyone. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them. (BG 9.29)**

Or it is astonishing that you are equal to all and have a partial nature. The partiality is shown in *bhakta-priyo yad as*i: you are affectionate to the devotee. You are perfect in being equal to all in three ways. With your kriyā-śakti you create the unlimited universes by your māyā śakti, an ābhāsa of your unlimited *(amita)* svarūpa śakti (*yoga-māyā*). This is your kriyā-śakti. Next the jñāna-śakti is shown. You know all beings (*viśāradasya*). His svarūpa is then shown. You are the svarūpa of all things (*sarvātmanaḥ*). “Is my nature like the desire tree then?” You are like this because you have the nature of a desire tree. This is astonishing.

### Text 10

*nityaṁ draṣṭāsi māṁ tatra gadā-pāṇim avasthitam*  
*mad-darśana-mahāhlāda- dhvasta-karma-nibandhanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All bondage of** ***karma*** **has already been destroyed by the great bliss of seeing me. Now you will constantly see me there with a club in my hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Previously your karmas were destroyed by seeing me. This has become your nature. Now you will constantly see me.

## Chapter Twenty-four

### Text 1

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*bhagavañ chrotum icchāmi harer adbhuta-karmaṇaḥ*  
*avatāra-kathām ādyāṁ māyā-matsya-viḍambanam*

**Перевод:**

**Mahārāja Parīkṣit said: O great sage! I wish to hear the story in which the Lord who performs astonishing activities imitates a material fish.**

**Комментарий:**

I wish to hear the story which describes the imitation of a fish by the Lord’s māyā.

### Text 2-3

*yad-artham adadhād rūpaṁ mātsyaṁ loka-jugupsitam*  
*tamaḥ-prakṛti-durmarṣaṁ karma-grasta iveśvaraḥ*  
*etan no bhagavan sarvaṁ yathāvad vaktum arhasi*  
*uttamaśloka-caritaṁ sarva-loka-sukhāvaham*

**Перевод:**

**Why did the Lord accept the seemingly abominable form of a fish in** ***tamoguṇa,*** **condemned by the world, as if controlled by** ***karma*****? O sage! Kindly explain to me everything about this pastime of the Lord which gives happiness to the world.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Why did the Lord accept the low form of a fish, as if controlled by karma (*karma-graṣṭa iva*), which is criticized by ordinary people? Accepting such a form is not proper. The Lord’s activities should give happiness to all people.

### Text 6

*uccāvaceṣu bhūteṣu caran vāyur iveśvaraḥ*  
*noccāvacatvaṁ bhajate nirguṇatvād dhiyo guṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Though moving as Paramātmā within species which are higher and lower by their intelligence and qualities, the Lord does not share those qualities of superior or inferior since he is beyond the** ***guṇas*****, just as the air, though moving everywhere, is untouched by all objects.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord appears as devatā, human and animal (*uccāvaceṣu*), and performs pastimes, but does not partake of the higher or lower qualities displayed in those species or their ordinary intelligence, since he is beyond the guṇas, having a form of eternity, knowledge and bliss.

### Text 7

*āsīd atīta-kalpānte brāhmo naimittiko layaḥ*  
*samudropaplutās tatra lokā bhūr-ādayo nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**O King! At the end of the previous day of Brahmā, when Brahmā slept, the daily annihilation took place, and the three worlds were covered by the water of the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

As with Varāha, Matsya appeared twice. When the day of brahma finished, when Brahmā slept, the three worlds were covered by water. This is the periodic destruction.

### Text 8

*kālenāgata-nidrasya dhātuḥ śiśayiṣor balī*  
*mukhato niḥsṛtān vedān hayagrīvo 'ntike 'harat*

**Перевод:**

**At the end of Brahmā's day, when sleepy Brahmā was dozing, the strong demon named Hayagrīva stole the Vedas which emanated from his mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

When Brahmā was sleeping, the demon stole the Vedas which emanated from his mouth by the power of yoga. The Vedas were situated within Brahmā at that time. The reason this happened was that the Lord desired a pastimes of teaching Vedas again at the beginning of the next day.

### Text 9

*jñātvā tad dānavendrasya hayagrīvasya ceṣṭitam*  
*dadhāra śapharī-rūpaṁ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Understanding the acts of the great demon Hayagrīva, the Supreme Lord assumed the form of a fish.**

**Комментарий:**

After the flooding was finished, the Lord appeared as the fish:

*atīta-pralayāpāya utthitāya sa vedhase*  
*hatvāsuraṁ hayagrīvaṁ vedān pratyāharad dhariḥ*

**At the end of the last inundation (during Brahmā’s night), at the beginning of Svāyambhuva Manvantara, the Supreme Lord killed the demon named Hayagrīva and delivered the Vedas to Lord Brahmā when Lord Brahmā awoke from sleep. (SB 8.24.57)**

### Text 10

*tatra rāja-ṛṣiḥ kaścin nāmnā satyavrato mahān*  
*nārāyaṇa-paro 'tapat tapaḥ sa salilāśanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Concerning this topic (during the Cākṣuṣa-manvantara), a great king named Satyavrata, a devotee of Nārāyaṇa, dedicated to Matsya, performed austerities by subsisting only on water.**

**Комментарий:**

Having spoken of the past part of kalpa, he now explains the pastime in the present part of the kalpa. *Tatra* means “in this topic.”

### Text 11

*yo 'sāv asmin mahā-kalpe tanayaḥ sa vivasvataḥ*  
*śrāddhadeva iti khyāto manutve hariṇārpitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this particular day of Brahmā, King Satyavrata later became the son of Vivasvān, the king of the sun planet, and was known as Śrāddhadeva. By the mercy of the Supreme Lord, he was given the post of Manu.**

**Комментарий:**

Special respect is shown for this day of Brahmā, in order to praise the particular Manu.

### Text 23

*ity uktaḥ so 'nayan matsyaṁ tatra tatrāvidāsini*  
*jalāśaye 'sammitaṁ taṁ samudre prākṣipaj jhaṣam*

**Перевод:**

**When thus requested, King Satyavrata took the fish to a perennial reservoir of water. But when that also proved insufficient, the King at last threw the gigantic fish into the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he heard the fish speak like a human, he still thought it was a fish, since he was bewildered by the Lord’s māyā.

### Text 34-35

*tvaṁ tāvad oṣadhīḥ sarvā bījāny uccāvacāni ca*  
*saptarṣibhiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarva-sattvopabṛṁhitaḥ*  
*āruhya bṛhatīṁ nāvaṁ vicariṣyasy aviklavaḥ*  
*ekārṇave nirāloke ṛṣīṇām eva varcasā*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, you should collect all types of herbs and seeds of higher and lower species, and accompanied by the seven sages and surrounded by all kinds of living entities, you should get aboard that huge boat, and without distress you shall easily travel on the dark ocean of inundation by the light from the effulgent sages.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Being surrounded by and placed together (*upabṛṁhitaḥ*) with all creatures required, you should get in the boat.

### Text 38

*madīyaṁ mahimānaṁ ca paraṁ brahmeti śabditam*  
*vetsyasy anugṛhītaṁ me sampraśnair vivṛtaṁ hṛdi*

**Перевод:**

**By my mercy, you will realize my power known as the impersonal Brahman, which will be disclosed in your heart through questions and answers.**

**Комментарий:**

The impersonal manifestation belongs to the Lord, since everything arises from him, the aṁśī of all things, endowed with acintya-śakti. You will know my power (*mahimānam*), the vibhūti without qualities, since it is directly revealed by me. It is revealed by my mercy in the heart and is described by me through questions made by you. Since realization of Brahman is included in realization of me, it is not different from realizing me. However, by realizing me directly through bhakti, this realization alone does not become apparent. If you have some desire for this manifestation of mine, the desire will be fulfilled. Details related to this will be shown in the Eleventh Canto.

### Text 40

*āstīrya darbhān prāk-kūlān rājarṣiḥ prāg-udaṅ-mukhaḥ*  
*niṣasāda hareḥ pādau cintayan matsya-rūpiṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After spreading** ***kuśa*** **with its tips pointing east, the saintly King, facing the northeast, sat down on the grass and began to meditate upon the Lord in the form of a fish.**

**Комментарий:**

He faced in the north-eastern direction.

### Text 41

*tataḥ samudra udvelaḥ sarvataḥ plāvayan mahīm*  
*vardhamāno mahā-meghair varṣadbhiḥ samadṛśyata*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, because of gigantic clouds pouring incessant water, the ocean began to overflow onto the land and inundate the entire world.**

**Комментарий:**

At the end of Cākṣusa-manvantara, there was a sudden deluge.

*rūpaṁ sa jagṛhe mātsyaṁ cākṣuṣodadhi-samplave \|*  
*nāvy āropya mahī-mayyām apād vaivasvataṁ manum \|\|*

**When there was an inundation in the period of the Cākṣuṣa Manu the Lord accepted the form of a fish and protected Vaivasvata Manu, placing him on a boat formed from the earth. (SB 1.3.15)**

It is said in scriptures that there is a deluge after every manvantara. The proofs are given in the scriptures. However, this deluge came suddenly in the middle of the sixth manvantara, not at the end. This was a separate occurrence, a special case during this manvantara. There was not included in four types of destruction. During the destruction after the manvantara, the three worlds are flooded and Brahmā also sleeps daily for some time. Thus mention of Brahmā’s night (verse 37) is not literal. According to Bhāgavatam, supported by other Purāṇas, this event did not happen in another kalpa.

### Text 46

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*anādy-avidyopahatātma-saṁvidas*  
*tan-mūla-saṁsāra-pariśramāturāḥ*  
*yadṛcchayopasṛtā yam āpnuyur*  
*vimuktido naḥ paramo gurur bhavān*

**Перевод:**

**The King said: Those who have lost their self-knowledge because of ignorance without beginning, and who because of this ignorance are suffering from fatigue in the material world, after obtaining the mercy of devotee, attain you, who give special liberation and who are the supreme** ***guru*** **who cuts the knot in the heart*****.***

**Комментарий:**

*Avidyā* refers to the Lord’s māyā.

### Text 48

*yat-sevayāgner iva rudra-rodanaṁ*  
*pumān vijahyān malam ātmanas tamaḥ*  
*bhajeta varṇaṁ nijam eṣa so 'vyayo*  
*bhūyāt sa īśaḥ paramo guror guruḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just as gold ore gives up its impurities by fire, the** ***jīva*** **will give up his ignorance by service to you and attains his** ***svarūpa.*** **May that supreme unchanging Lord, the supreme** ***guru*****, be our** ***guru!***

**Комментарий:**

Having attained you, no one else need be sought. You are the supreme guru of the guru.

### Text 49

*na yat-prasādāyuta-bhāga-leśam*  
*anye ca devā guravo janāḥ svayam*  
*kartuṁ sametāḥ prabhavanti puṁsas*  
*tam īśvaraṁ tvāṁ śaraṇaṁ prapadye*

**Перевод:**

**Neither the** ***devatās,*** **parents nor kings, independently or together, can offer mercy that equals even one ten-thousandth of your mercy. Therefore I wish to take shelter of the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Others who think themselves independent are insignificant.

### Text 50

*acakṣur andhasya yathāgraṇīḥ kṛtas*  
*tathā janasyāviduṣo 'budho guruḥ*  
*tvam arka-dṛk sarva-dṛśāṁ samīkṣaṇo*  
*vṛto gurur naḥ sva-gatiṁ bubhutsatām*

**Перевод:**

**Just as a blind man accepts another blind man to lead him, ignorant people accept another ignorant man as their** ***guru*****. We, desiring** ***bhakti*****, accept you, who are like the sun, who reveal all senses and all knowledge, as our** ***guru.***

**Комментарий:**

Worshipping the Lord because of impressions from previous birth of being a king with bhakti attained from a guru, praising the Lord, he has this disposition. You should come personally and be the guru. Approaching you, I desire you as the guru. You are the best among all those who know the truth (*arka-dṛk*).

### Text 57

*atīta-pralayāpāya utthitāya sa vedhase*  
*hatvāsuraṁ hayagrīvaṁ vedān pratyāharad dhariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**At the end of the last inundation (during Brahmā’s night), at the beginning of Svāyambhuva Manvantara, the Supreme Lord killed the demon named Hayagrīva and delivered the Vedas to Lord Brahmā when Lord Brahmā awoke from sleep.**

**Комментарий:**

Again he shows that the avatāra of Matsya occurs twice, in two verses.

### Text 58

*sa tu satyavrato raja jñāna-vijñāna-saṁyutaḥ*  
*viṣṇoḥ prasādāt kalpe 'sminn āsīd vaivasvato manuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**King Satyavrata, endowed with knowledge and realization by the mercy of the Lord during Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, became Vaivasvata Manu in the present Manvantara.**

**Комментарий:**

Attaining mercy of Viṣṇu during the sixth manvantara, he became Vaivasvata Manu in the seventh manvantara.

### Text 59

*satyavratasya rājarṣer māyā-matsyasya śārṅgiṇaḥ*  
*saṁvādaṁ mahad-ākhyānaṁ śrutvā mucyeta kilbiṣāt*

**Перевод:**

**If one hears this great story in the form of a discussion between the great King Satyavrata and the fish incarnation with a horn, he will be delivered from the reactions of sinful life.**

**Комментарий:**

Māyā means mercy.

### Text 61

*pralaya-payasi dhātuḥ supta-śakter mukhebhyaḥ*  
*śruti-gaṇam apanītaṁ pratyupādatta hatvā*  
*ditijam akathayad yo brahma satyavratānāṁ*  
*tam aham akhila-hetuṁ jihma-mīnaṁ nato 'smi*

**Перевод:**

**I offer my respectful obeisances unto Matsya, the cause of all causes, who, after killing the demon, restored to Lord Brahmā the Vedic literature stolen from his mouths while Brahmā had no powers, during sleep at the time of the devastation, and who explained the essence of Vedic literature to King Satyavrata.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you who appeared as an ordinary fish among beings with crooked hearts *(jihma*).

*nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*mūḍho ’yaṁ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam \|\|*

**Being covered by my bewildering power of** ***māyā*****, I am not visible to all these people. The foolish do not know me, who am without birth and unchanging in qualities. (BG 7.25)**

*mṛtyur bhoja-pater virāḍ aviduṣāṁ tattvaṁ paraṁ yogināṁ*  
*vṛṣṇīnāṁ para-devateti vidito raṅgaṁ gataḥ sāgrajaḥ*

**The King of the Bhojas saw Kṛṣṇa as death, the unintelligent saw him as the Supreme Lord’s universal form, the yogīs saw him as the Absolute Truth and the Vṛṣṇis saw him as their supreme worshipable deity. (SB 10.43.17)**

Saindhava means salt and horse.

*Svabhāva* is the cause of transformation.

This is not the case with installed deities.

## Canto Nine

## Chapter One

*oṁ namaḥ śrī kṛṣṇāya.*  
*navala-krama-sandarbhe sandarbhāṇāṁ samāhṛtiḥ*  
*kriyate yanni deśena sa me ’nanyagatergatiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**He by whose order this collection of Sandarbhas is made into the Ninth Krama Sandarbha is the goal of this person with no other goal.**

### Text 2-3

*yo 'sau satyavrato nāma rājarṣir draviḍeśvaraḥ*  
*jñānaṁ yo 'tīta-kalpānte lebhe puruṣa-sevayā*  
*sa vai vivasvataḥ putro manur āsīd iti śrutam*  
*tvattas tasya sutāḥ proktā ikṣvāku-pramukhā nṛpāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Satyavrata, the saintly king of Draviḍadeśa who received spiritual knowledge at the end of the last Manvantara by the grace of the Lord, later became Vaivasvata Manu, the son of Vivasvān. I have received this knowledge from you. I also understand that such kings as Ikṣvāku were his sons, as you have already explained.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together.

### Text 31

*ṛṣayo 'pi tayor vīkṣya prasaṅgaṁ ramamāṇayoḥ*  
*nivṛttāḥ prayayus tasmān nara-nārāyaṇāśramam*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Lord Śiva and Pārvatī engaged in intimacy, all the sages refrained from approaching and departed for the hermitage of Nara-Nārāyaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Being embarrassed, considering another place, they went to Nara-nārāyaṇa’s āśrama where such intimacy was absent.

## Chapter Two

### Text 7

*vyāghro 'pi vṛkṇa-śravaṇo nistriṁśāgrāhatas tataḥ*  
*niścakrāma bhṛśaṁ bhīto raktaṁ pathi samutsṛjan*

**Перевод:**

**Because the tiger's ear had been cut by the edge of the sword, the tiger fled in great fear from that place, while bleeding on the path.**

**Комментарий:**

Because they were all crowded together, he could not discern the truth.

### Text 8

*manyamāno hataṁ vyāghraṁ pṛṣadhraḥ para-vīra-hā*  
*adrākṣīt sva-hatāṁ babhruṁ vyuṣṭāyāṁ niśi duḥkhitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the morning, when Pṛṣadhra, who was quite able to subdue his enemy, saw that he had killed the cow although at night he thought he had killed the tiger, he was very unhappy.**

**Комментарий:**

He became repentant.

### Text 9

*taṁ śaśāpa kulācāryaḥ kṛtāgasam akāmataḥ*  
*na kṣatra-bandhuḥ śūdras tvaṁ karmaṇā bhavitāmunā*

**Перевод:**

**Although Pṛṣadhra had committed the sin unknowingly, his family priest, Vasiṣṭha, cursed him, saying, "In your next life you shall not be able to become a fallen** ***kṣatriya.*** **Instead, you shall take birth as a** ***śūdra*****."**

**Комментарий:**

Though the atonement should have been slight, the reason for losing his caste was the guru’s compassion for the cow. This is expressed in three verses.

### Text 10

*evaṁ śaptas tu guruṇā pratyagṛhṇāt kṛtāñjaliḥ*  
*adhārayad vrataṁ vīra ūrdhva-retā muni-priyam*

**Перевод:**

**When the hero Pṛṣadhra was thus cursed by his** ***guru,*** **he accepted the curse with folded hands. Controlling his senses, he took the vow of** ***brahmacarya.***

**Комментарий:**

He responded humbly to the curse.

### Text 14

*evaṁ vṛtto vanaṁ gatvā dṛṣṭvā dāvāgnim utthitam*  
*tenopayukta-karaṇo brahma prāpa paraṁ muniḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With this way of life, Pṛṣadhra, having entered the forest, saw a blazing forest fire, which had arisen there. The sage, having burned up his body in the fire, achieved Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Since he was a devotee of Vāsudeva, though he was a śūdra, he attained liberation.

## Chapter Three

### Text 5

*śakṛn-mūtra-nirodho 'bhūt sainikānāṁ ca tat-kṣaṇāt*  
*rājarṣis tam upālakṣya puruṣān vismito 'bravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Immediately all the soldiers of Śaryāti could not pass urine and stool. Upon perceiving this, Śaryāti spoke to his associates in surprise.**

**Комментарий:**

The sage did this because he desired the daughter, and desired that his hermitage be free from contamination at that time. It was a slight disturbance.

### Text 30

*āvartamāne gāndharve sthito 'labdha-kṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇam*  
*tad-anta ādyam ānamya svābhiprāyaṁ nyavedayat*

**Перевод:**

**Since a Gandharva was engaged in performing, Lord Brahmā was busy. After a moment, when the Gandharva finished, Kakudmī offered his respects to Brahmā and expressed his desire.**

**Комментарий:**

After a moment he approached Brahmā.

## Chapter Four

### Text 18-20

*sa vai manaḥ kṛṣṇa-padāravindayor*  
*vacāṁsi vaikuṇṭha-guṇānuvarṇane*  
*karau harer mandira-mārjanādiṣu*  
*śrutiṁ cakārācyuta-sat-kathodaye*  
*mukunda-liṅgālaya-darśane dṛśau*  
*tad-bhṛtya-gātra-sparśe 'ṅga-saṅgamam*  
*ghrāṇaṁ ca tat-pāda-saroja-saurabhe*  
*śrīmat-tulasyā rasanāṁ tad-arpite*  
*pādau hareḥ kṣetra-padānusarpaṇe*  
*śiro hṛṣīkeśa-padābhivandane*  
*kāmaṁ ca dāsye na tu kāma-kāmyayā*  
*yathottamaśloka-janāśrayā ratiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Mahārāja Ambarīṣa always engaged his mind in meditating upon the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, his words in describing the glories of the Lord, his hands in cleansing the Lord's temple, and his ears in hearing the words spoken by Kṛṣṇa or about Kṛṣṇa. He engaged his eyes in seeing the deity of Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa's temples and Kṛṣṇa's places like Mathurā and Vṛndāvana, he engaged his sense of touch in touching the bodies of the Lord's devotees, he engaged his sense of smell in smelling the fragrance of** ***tulasī*** **offered to the Lord, and he engaged his tongue in tasting the Lord's** ***prasāda.*** **He engaged his legs in walking to the holy places and temples of the Lord, his head in bowing down before the Lord, and all his desires in serving the Lord, without desiring material enjoyment, in order to develop** ***rati*** **as possessed by great devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together.

He made the decision (*kāmam*) out of the attitude of dāsyam, so that somehow he would develop rati for the Lord, which is found in the devotees such as Prahlāda, without a desire for material enjoyment.

### Text 21

*evaṁ sadā karma-kalāpam ātmanaḥ*  
*pare 'dhiyajñe bhagavaty adhokṣaje*  
*sarvātma-bhāvaṁ vidadhan mahīm imāṁ*  
*tan-niṣṭha-viprābhihitaḥ śaśāsa ha*

**Перевод:**

**Performing devotional acts daily with** ***rati*** **by his mind and senses to the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa, whose worship is superior to other processes, he ruled the world, taking advice from devotee** ***brāhmaṇas.***

**Комментарий:**

He performed actions for the supreme Lord as previously described, in which there was completely dedicated (*sarvātma*) bhakti (*bhāvam*).

### Text 22

*īje 'śvamedhair adhiyajñam īśvaraṁ*  
*mahā-vibhūtyopacitāṅga-dakṣiṇaiḥ*  
*tatair vasiṣṭhāsita-gautamādibhir*  
*dhanvany abhisrotam asau sarasvatīm*

**Перевод:**

**He worshipped the Supreme Lord by horse sacrifices required by a king for prosperity, with all** ***aṅgas*** **and charities, performed by Vasiṣṭha, Asita, Gautama and other sages in the desert facing the flow of the Sarasvatī River.**

**Комментарий:**

If he performed devotional activities how can he do sacrifices? Are they done together? The sacrifices were done by Vasiṣṭha and other sages, near the Sarasvatī River, respecting the tīrtha (*abhisrotam*). Respect for the river is shown on the path of karma. This took place in holy tīrthas within Dhanvan, which were known for piety.

### Text 25

*saṁvardhayanti yat kāmāḥ svārājya-paribhāvitāḥ*  
*durlabhā nāpi siddhānāṁ mukundaṁ hṛdi paśyataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The material pleasures which surpass those of Svarga and are rare even for Siddhas did not give the citizens bliss because they saw Mukunda in their hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

Material pleasures which surpass those equal to Indra’s position (*svārājya-paribhāvitāḥ*) do not give bliss to the citizens.

### Text 26

*sa itthaṁ bhakti-yogena tapo-yuktena pārthivaḥ*  
*sva-dharmeṇa hariṁ prīṇan sarvān kāmān śanair jahau*

**Перевод:**

**Mahārāja Ambarīṣa, thus satisfying the Lord by devotional service as his main duty along with devotion vows, gradually gave up all material desires.**

**Комментарий:**

*Tapo-yuktena* means “along with Dvādaśī vows in the house, favorable for bhakti.”

### Text 29

*ārirādhayiṣuḥ kṛṣṇaṁ mahiṣyā tulya-śīlayā*  
*yuktaḥ sāṁvatsaraṁ vīro dadhāra dvādaśī-vratam*

**Перевод:**

**Desiring to worship Kṛṣṇa, Mahārāja Ambarīṣa, along with his queen, who was equally qualified, observed the vow of Dvādaśī for one year.**

**Комментарий:**

He performed the Dvādaśī vow for one year in order attain his special goals.

### Text 53-54

*śrī-brahmovāca*  
*sthānaṁ madīyaṁ saha-viśvam etat*  
*krīḍāvasāne dvi-parārdha-saṁjñe*  
*bhrū-bhaṅga-mātreṇa hi sandidhakṣoḥ*  
*kālātmano yasya tirobhaviṣyati*  
*ahaṁ bhavo dakṣa-bhṛgu-pradhānāḥ*  
*prajeśa-bhūteśa-sureśa-mukhyāḥ*  
*sarve vayaṁ yan-niyamaṁ prapannā*  
*mūrdhnyārpitaṁ loka-hitaṁ vahāmaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā said: At the end of my life when the pastimes of the Lord come to an end, Viṣṇu, through time, by a movement of his eyebrows, vanquishes the entire universe, including our places of residence. I, Śiva, as well as Dakṣa, Bhṛgu and Prajāpatis, and also the rulers of the living entities, and the rulers of the** ***devatās*****—all of us surrender to Viṣṇu, whose orders we carry on our heads for the benefit of all living entities.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Brahmā is a guṇāvatāra, he is considered to be an āveśāvatāra (jīva). Thus he says “All of us surrender to Viṣṇu.”

### Text 56

*śrī-śaṅkara uvāca*  
*vayaṁ na tāta prabhavāma bhūmni*  
*yasmin pare 'nye 'py aja-jīva-kośāḥ*  
*bhavanti kāle na bhavanti hīdṛśāḥ*  
*sahasraśo yatra vayaṁ bhramāmaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śiva said: My dear son! We cannot compete with the Supreme Lord within whom the thousands of universes in which we wander in bewilderment arise and are destroyed with time.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva speaks four verses.

### Text 62

*ajānatā te paramānubhāvaṁ*  
*kṛtaṁ mayāghaṁ bhavataḥ priyāṇām*  
*vidhehi tasyāpacitiṁ vidhātar*  
*mucyeta yan-nāmny udite nārako 'pi*

**Перевод:**

**O supreme controller! Without knowledge of your unlimited prowess, I have offended your most dear devotees. O Lord by whose name a person in hell becomes liberated! Please do something to nullify this offense.**

**Комментарий:**

By chanting the Lord’s name a person situated in hell (*nārako ‘pi*) is liberated. What to speak of a person surrendered to you personally.

*yathā yathā harer nāma kīrtayanti sma nārakāḥ*  
*tathā tathā harau bhaktim udvahanto divaṁ yayuḥ*

**Those who chant the name of the Lord in hell, developing bhakti, attain the spiritual world. (Nṛsiṁha Purāṇa 8.31)**

### Text 63

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*ahaṁ bhakta-parādhīno hy asvatantra iva dvija*  
*sādhubhir grasta-hṛdayo bhaktair bhakta-jana-priyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: O** ***brāhmaṇa*****! I am completely under the control of my devotees. I am not at all independent. My heart is controlled by the pure devotees. What to speak of my devotee, even those who are devotees of my devotee are very dear to me.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord establishes that he is controlled completely by the devotees in six verses. He makes a promise in this verse. My heart is completely controlled (*grasta*) by devotees who have given up duplicity (*sādhubhiḥ*), who are devoid of even the desire for liberation. I have great affection for persons are devotees of the devotees. What to speak of the devotees themselves.

### Text 64

*nāham ātmānam āśāse mad-bhaktaiḥ sādhubhir vinā*  
*śriyaṁ cātyantikīṁ brahman yeṣāṁ gatir ahaṁ parā*

**Перевод:**

**O** ***brāhmaṇa*****! Without the devotees, who take shelter of only me, I do not desire to enjoy my own bliss by my six great qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

In five verses he establishes this. He shows that the bliss he experiences in his svarūpa is secondary to realizing the bliss the devotee experiences. This bliss of the devotee is the essence of the hlādinī-śakti.

### Text 65

*ye dārāgāra-putrāpta- prāṇān vittam imaṁ param*  
*hitvā māṁ śaraṇaṁ yātāḥ kathaṁ tāṁs tyaktum utsahe*

**Перевод:**

**Since pure devotees give up their homes, wives, children, relatives, riches and even their lives simply to serve me, without any desire for material improvement in this life or in the next, how can I give up such devotees at any time?**

**Комментарий:**

Showing the devotees pitiable condition, he must show gratitude. They even reject sālokya etc. (*param*).

### Text 66

*mayi nirbaddha-hṛdayāḥ sādhavaḥ sama-darśanāḥ*  
*vaśe kurvanti māṁ bhaktyā sat-striyaḥ sat-patiṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**As chaste women bring their gentle husbands under control by service, the pure devotees, who see others’ suffering as their own and are completely attached to me in the core of the heart, bring me under their full control.**

**Комментарий:**

He establishes the position of both by an example. Because their hearts are attached to me (*nirbaddha-hṛdayāḥ*), these devotees who are devoid of cheating (*sādhavaḥ*), who are devoid of raga and dveṣa (*sama-darṣanāḥ*), control me by bhakti. The example shows bhakti with prominence of friendship.

### Text 67

*mat-sevayā pratītaṁ te sālokyādi-catuṣṭayam*  
*necchanti sevayā pūrṇāḥ kuto 'nyat kāla-viplutam*

**Перевод:**

**My devotees, who are always satisfied to be engaged in my service, are not interested even in the four principles of liberation \[sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya and sārṣṭi\], although these are automatically achieved by their service. What then is to be said of any perishable happiness?**

**Комментарий:**

He shows the extreme sacrifice of the devotees. Sālokya etc. are not perishable. What to speak of perishable happiness?

### Text 68

*sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyaṁ sādhūnāṁ hṛdayaṁ tv aham*  
*mad-anyat te na jānanti nāhaṁ tebhyo manāg api*

**Перевод:**

**The pure devotee is my very heart: what pains him pains me. I am the heart of the pure devotee: what pleases him pleases me. My devotees do not know anything else but me, and I do not know more than they do.**

**Комментарий:**

Mutually the Lord and devotee share their hearts.

## Chapter Five

### Text 2

*tasya sodyamam āvīkṣya pāda-sparśa-vilajjitaḥ*  
*astāvīt tad dharer astraṁ kṛpayā pīḍito bhṛśam*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Durvāsā attempting to praise him, Mahārāja Ambarīṣa was ashamed and, seeing him suffering, was greatly aggrieved. Thus he offered prayers to the weapon of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

*Saḥ udyamam* becomes *sodyamam* according to *so ‘ci lope cet pāda-pūraṇam* (Pāṇini 61.134). Also *lopaḥ śākalaysa* (Pāṇini 8.3.19 and *pūrvatrāsiddham* (Pāṇini 8.2.1 should be considered.

### Text 7

*tvat-tejasā dharma-mayena saṁhṛtaṁ*  
*tamaḥ prakāśaś ca dṛśo mahātmanām*  
*duratyayas te mahimā girāṁ pate*  
*tvad-rūpam etat sad-asat parāvaram*

**Перевод:**

**O master of speech! By your effulgence, composed of** ***dharma,*** **the darkness of the world is dissipated, and the knowledge belonging to great souls is manifested. No one can surpass your effulgence. All things, manifested and unmanifested, superior and inferior, are but your various forms.**

**Комментарий:**

By your effulgence composed of dharma, the darkness is seen (*dṛśaḥ*) to be dissipated and the manifestation of the sun and other great things (*mahātmanām*) occurs. Your greatness cannot be surpassed since this world of sat and asat is your manifestation.

### Text 9

*sa tvaṁ jagat-trāṇa khala-prahāṇaye*  
*nirūpitaḥ sarva-saho gadā-bhṛtā*  
*viprasya cāsmat-kula-daiva-hetave*  
*vidhehi bhadraṁ tad anugraho hi naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O protector of the universe! As the form of all strength, you are engaged by the Supreme Lord in killing the criminals. For the benefit of our entire dynasty, as a favor to us, favor this poor** ***brāhmaṇa.***

**Комментарий:**

You are engaged by the Lord to kill in a decisive manner (*prahānaye*) the criminals.

### Text 22

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ saṅkīrtya rājānaṁ durvāsāḥ paritoṣitaḥ*  
*yayau vihāyasāmantrya brahmalokam ahaitukam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus being satisfied, Durvāsā took permission and left, continuously glorifying the King. Through the sky, he went to Brahmaloka, which is devoid of dry reasoning.**

**Комментарий:**

*Ahaitukam* means “devoid of materialistic persons who interpret the Vedas by dry logic.”

### Text 23

*saṁvatsaro 'tyagāt tāvad yāvatā nāgato gataḥ*  
*munis tad-darśanākāṅkṣo rājāb-bhakṣo babhūva ha*

**Перевод:**

**During the time that Durvāsā Muni had left and had not returned—for one complete year—the King, desiring to see him again, had fasted, having drunken water previously.**

**Комментарий:**

The king, having drunken water previously, remained there anxious to see the sage. It does not mean that he only drank water at that time.

### Text 24

*gate 'tha durvāsasi so 'mbarīṣo*  
*dvijopayogātipavitram āharat*  
*ṛṣer vimokṣaṁ vyasanaṁ ca vīkṣya*  
*mene sva-vīryaṁ ca parānubhāvam*

**Перевод:**

**After one year, when Durvāsā Muni had returned, King Ambarīṣa ate pure food remnants of a** ***brāhmaṇa.*** **When the King saw that the** ***brāhmaṇa*** **Durvāsā had been released from the great danger of being burned, he understood that his power was the Lord’s power alone.**

**Комментарий:**

He ate food pure because it was eaten by brāhmaṇas who were devotees, with whom the Lord is very pleased.

### Text 26

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*athāmbarīṣas tanayeṣu rājyaṁ*  
*samāna-śīleṣu visṛjya dhīraḥ*  
*vanaṁ viveśātmani vāsudeve*  
*mano dadhad dhvasta-guṇa-pravāhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thereafter, the learned Mahārāja Ambarīṣa, having destroyed the agitation of the** ***guṇas*****, divided his kingdom among his sons, who were equally qualified, and entered the forest to concentrate his mind fully upon Lord Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

Worrying that further such incidents would occur, seeing the qualification of his sons, giving the responsibility to them, he concentrated his mind on the Lord’s service in the forest.

## Chapter Six

### Text 10

*sa tu vipreṇa saṁvādaṁ jñāpakena samācaran*  
*tyaktvā kalevaraṁ yogī sa tenāvāpa yat param*

**Перевод:**

**Instituting the instructions given by Vasiṣṭha, Mahārāja Ikṣvāku became renounced and achieved the supreme perfection after giving up his material body.**

**Комментарий:**

*Babhūva* should be supplied after *samācaran*. Another version has *samācarat*. He attained that which is the supreme truth (*param*).

### Text 11

*pitary uparate 'bhyetya vikukṣiḥ pṛthivīm imām*  
*śāsad īje hariṁ yajñaiḥ śaśāda iti viśrutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After his father's disappearance, Vikukṣi returned to the country and thus became the king, ruling the planet earth and worshipped the Lord by performing various sacrifices. Vikukṣi later became celebrated as Saśāda (rabbit eater).**

**Комментарий:**

By the power of performing worship of the Lord, he overcame the fault of rejecting his father.

### Text 25

*bahulāśvo nikumbhasya kṛśāśvo 'thāsya senajit*  
*yuvanāśvo 'bhavat tasya so 'napatyo vanaṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nikumbha was Bahulāśva, the son of Bahulāśva was Kṛśāśva, the son of Kṛśāśva was Senajit, and the son of Senajit was Yuvanāśva. Yuvanāśva had no sons, and thus he retired from family life and went to the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

Nikumbha’s son was Bahulāśva. Bahulāśva’s son was Kṛśāśva.

### Text 51

*saṅgaṁ tyajeta mithuna-vratīnāṁ mumukṣuḥ*  
*sarvātmanā na visṛjed bahir-indriyāṇi*  
*ekaś caran rahasi cittam ananta īśe*  
*yuñjīta tad-vratiṣu sādhuṣu cet prasaṅgaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**A person desiring liberation must give up the association of persons interested in sex life and should not employ his external senses. He should always stay in a secluded place, completely fixing his mind at the lotus feet of the unlimited Lord-- if there is association with devotees also engaged in meditation on the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

When will that person acting in that way fix his mind on the Lord? It will happen if he has association with devotees similarly engaged.

### Text 54

*tatra taptvā tapas tīkṣṇam ātma-darśanam ātmavān*  
*sahaivāgnibhir ātmānaṁ yuyoja paramātmani*

**Перевод:**

**Saubhari, knowing the self, performed severe penances in the forest for realizing the self. He gave up his body along with the fires and attained the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

He united his body along with the fires in the Lord. He thought of everything- self and relations—as following the Lord.

## Chapter Seven

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*māndhātuḥ putra-pravaro yo 'mbarīṣaḥ prakīrtitaḥ*  
*pitāmahena pravṛto yauvanāśvas tu tat-sutaḥ*  
*hārītas tasya putro 'bhūn māndhātṛ-pravarā ime*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The most prominent among the sons of Māndhātā was he who is celebrated as Ambarīṣa. Ambarīṣa was accepted as a son by his grandfather Yuvanāśva. Ambarīṣa's son was Yauvanāśva, and Yauvanāśva's son was Hārīta. In Māndhātā's dynasty, Ambarīṣa, Hārīta and Yauvanāśva were very prominent.**

**Комментарий:**

Three lines go together. This is the version seen in the Gauḍa provinces. Ambarīṣa’s son was Yauvanāśva. Viṣṇu Purāṇa also explains that Yuvanāśva (grandfather of Ambarīṣa) gave birth to Māndhātā. However Viṣṇu Purāṇa also says that Ambarīṣa’s son was Yuvanāśva.

*ambarīṣasya māndhātṛ-tanayasya yuvanāśvaḥ putro’bhūt*  
*tasmād dhāritaḥ, yato’ṅgirasā hārīta*

**Yuvanāśva was the son of Ambarīṣa, who was the son of Māndhātā. From Yuvanāśva came Hārīta. And from Hārīta came Aṅgirasā. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa)**

Śrīdhara Svāmī says that *pravṛta* means “what is accepted by the sages.” The sages accepted Ambarīṣa, Yuvanāśva and Hārīta along with the grandfather as the same line

### Text 4

*trasaddasyuḥ paurukutso yo 'naraṇyasya deha-kṛt*  
*haryaśvas tat-sutas tasmāt prāruṇo 'tha tribandhanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Purukutsa was Trasaddasyu, who was the father of Anaraṇya. Anaraṇya's son was Haryaśva, the father of Prāruṇa. Prāruṇa was the father of Tribandhana.**

**Комментарий:**

Trasaddasyu came n Māndhātā’s line.

### Text 8

*so 'napatyo viṣaṇṇātmā nāradasyopadeśataḥ*  
*varuṇaṁ śaraṇaṁ yātaḥ putro me jāyatāṁ prabho*

**Перевод:**

**Hariścandra had no son and was therefore extremely morose. Once, therefore, following the advice of Nārada, he took shelter of Varuṇa and said to him "My lord! Please give me a son."**

**Комментарий:**

The story of Hariścandra is told to show the excellent nature of the Lord’s will and the devotee. That is understood for other stories also.

### Text 24

*satyaṁ sāraṁ dhṛtiṁ dṛṣṭvā sabhāryasya ca bhūpateḥ*  
*viśvāmitro bhṛśaṁ prīto dadāv avihatāṁ gatim*

**Перевод:**

**The great sage Viśvāmitra, seeing the fortitude and essence of truth in Mahārāja Hariścandra and his wife, gave them imperishable knowledge.**

**Комментарий:**

Absorption in Vedic rites produces merging in Brahman, not a relation with the Lord.

## Chapter Eight

### Text 4

*ājñāyāsyai sapatnībhir garo datto 'ndhasā saha*  
*saha tenaiva sañjātaḥ sagarākhyo mahā-yaśāḥ*  
*sagaraś cakravarty āsīt sāgaro yat-sutaiḥ kṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Knowing that she was pregnant, the co-wives of the wife of Bāhuka gave her poison with her food. The famous son was born along with the poison. Therefore he became famous as Sagara, "one who is born with poison". Sagara later became the emperor. His sons dug up the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

The last line continues into the next verses.

### Text 5-6

*yas tālajaṅghān yavanāñ chakān haihaya-barbarān*  
*nāvadhīd guru-vākyena cakre vikṛta-veṣiṇaḥ*  
*muṇḍāñ chmaśru-dharān kāṁścin mukta-keśārdha-muṇḍitān*  
*anantar-vāsasaḥ kāṁścid abahir-vāsaso 'parān*

**Перевод:**

**Sagara Mahārāja did not kill uncivilized men like the Tālajaṅghas, Yavanas, Śakas, Haihayas and Barbaras. Instead, following the order of his** ***guru*** **Aurva, he made dress some of them awkwardly, he shaved some of them clean but allowed them to wear mustaches, he left some of them wearing loose hair, he half-shaved some, he left some without underwear, and he left some without external garments.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrīdhara Svāmī does not accept *nāvadhīt* but rather *avadhīt* (he killed). Thus he explains that some were not killed but disfigured. Parāśara says *prāyaśas ca haihayaṁ jaghāna*: he killed most of the Haihayas. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) Viṣṇu Purāṇa follows the words of Vasiṣṭha, the words of guru.

### Text 9-10

*prāg-udīcyāṁ diśi hayaṁ dadṛśuḥ kapilāntike*  
*eṣa vāji-haraś caura āste mīlita-locanaḥ*  
*hanyatāṁ hanyatāṁ papa iti ṣaṣṭi-sahasriṇaḥ*  
*udāyudhā abhiyayur unmimeṣa tadā muniḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, in the northeastern direction, they saw the horse near the hermitage of Kapila. "Here is the man who has stolen the horse," they said. "He is staying there with closed eyes. This sinful man should be killed!" The sixty thousand sons of Sagara, raising their weapons, attacked the sage. The sage opened his eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

In the north east, they wandered to Gaṅgā-sāgara, on the edge of the ocean, towards the south. Or Kapila had wandered to the northeast.

## Chapter Nine

### Text 5

*kiṁ cāhaṁ na bhuvaṁ yāsye narā mayy āmṛjanty agham*  
*mṛjāmi tad aghaṁ kvāhaṁ rājaṁs tatra vicintyatām*

**Перевод:**

**O King, I do not wish to go down to the planet earth, for there the people will wash their sins into my water. How will I wash away those sins? You must consider some method of washing away those sins.**

**Комментарий:**

They will destroy (*āmṛjanti*) their sin in me or through me. Sin means the suffering of the mind born from not having a taste for associating with the Lord. The Gaṅgā is famous for destroying millions of serious sins. *Agham* means anxiety due to misfortunes of suffering.

### Text 6

*śrī-bhagīratha uvāca*  
*sādhavo nyāsinaḥ śāntā brahmiṣṭhā loka-pāvanāḥ*  
*haranty aghaṁ te 'ṅga-saṅgāt teṣv āste hy agha-bhid dhariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Bhagīratha said: The peaceful devotees without material attachments, fixed in the Lord, who are purifiers of the world, will remove the sin from your water by bathing in it. The Lord, the destroyer of sin, will destroy the sins that the devotees accumulate.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who are fixed in scriptural conduct according to qualification (*sādhavaḥ*), unattached to results of karma (*nyāsinaḥ*), endowed with pure hearts (*śāntaḥ*), expert at understanding the Vedas (*brahma-niṣṭhāḥ*), purifiers of the world, will remove the sin. The reason for these qualities is that the Lord, who destroys all sins, (*agha-bhit*) exists in them. You will not have suffering because of association at all times with these devotees, by seeing these devotees.

### Text 19

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*kiṁ nimitto guroḥ śāpaḥ saudāsasya mahātmanaḥ*  
*etad veditum icchāmaḥ kathyatāṁ na raho yadi*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: Why did Vasiṣṭha, the** ***guru*** **of Saudāsa, curse that great soul? I wish to know of this. If it is not secret, please describe it to me.**

**Комментарий:**

It should not be revealed (*rahaḥ*) if it makes Vasiṣṭha appear at fault.

### Text 20-21

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*saudāso mṛgayāṁ kiñcic caran rakṣo jaghāna ha*  
*mumoca bhrātaraṁ so 'tha gataḥ praticikīrṣayā*  
*sañcintayann aghaṁ rājñaḥ sūda-rūpa-dharo gṛhe*  
*gurave bhoktu-kāmāya paktvā ninye narāmiṣam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Once Saudāsa, while hunting, killed a Rākṣasa but released its brother. That brother, however, departed with the idea of taking revenge. Thinking to harm the King, he became the cook at the King's house. One day, the King's** ***guru,*** **Vasiṣṭha Muni, was invited for dinner, and the Rākṣasa cook served him human flesh.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon entered the cook (*suda-rūpa-dharaḥ*) since he was not familiar with cooking.

### Text 44

*na bālye 'pi matir mahyam adharme ramate kvacit*  
*nāpaśyam uttamaślokād anyat kiñcana vastv aham*

**Перевод:**

**I was never attracted, even in my childhood, to irreligious principles. I did not find any object acceptable except the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

I did not think of anyone except the Supreme Lord. I did not worship devatās. He was busy protecting the devatās and mankind.

### Text 48

*iti vyavasito buddhyā nārāyaṇa-gṛhītayā*  
*hitvānya-bhāvam ajñānaṁ tataḥ svaṁ bhāvam āsthitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Deciding in this way, while giving up ignorance through intelligence absorbed in Nārāyaṇa, he became situated in the mood of surrender.**

**Комментарий:**

His intelligence was absorbed in Nārāyaṇa (*nārāyaṇa-gṛhitayā*).

*tatra mām anumoderan devās tri-bhuvaneśvarāḥ*  
*muhūrtena brahma-lokaṁ khaṭvāṅgaḥ samasādhayat*

**Thus may the presiding** ***devatās*** **of these three worlds kindly show their mercy upon me. Mahārāja Khaṭvāṅga was able to achieve the spiritual world in a single moment. (SB 11.23.30)**

## Chapter Ten

### Text 4

*gurv-arthe tyakta-rājyo vyacarad anuvanaṁ padma-padbhyāṁ priyāyāḥ*  
*pāṇi-sparśākṣamābhyāṁ mṛjita-patha-rujo yo harīndrānujābhyām*  
*vairūpyāc chūrpaṇakhyāḥ priya-viraha-ruṣāropita-bhrū-vijṛmbha-*  
*trastābdhir baddha-setuḥ khala-dava-dahanaḥ kosalendro 'vatān naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Rāmacandra, King of Kosala, gave up the kingdom to keep his father’s promise and walked from forest to forest on his lotus feet which were so delicate they could not tolerate the touch of Sitā’s hand. His fatigue while walking was relieved by Hanumān and Lakṣmaṇa. He created fear in the ocean by moving his eyebrow in anger caused by separation from Sitā due his severing Sūrpaṇakha’s nose and ear, and built a bridge over the ocean. May Rāmacandra, who burned the forest of demons, protect us!**

**Комментарий:**

Another version has *patha-rujā.*

### Text 11

*rakṣo-'dhamena vṛkavad vipine 'samakṣaṁ*  
*vaideha-rāja-duhitary apayāpitāyām*  
*bhrātrā vane kṛpaṇavat priyayā viyuktaḥ*  
*strī-saṅgināṁ gatim iti prathayaṁś cacāra*

**Перевод:**

**When Sītā was stolen by wolf-like Rāvaṇa in the forest in Rāma’s absence, Rāma, feeling separation from his wife like a suffering man, wandered in the forest with his brother, announcing to the world the result of association with women.**

**Комментарий:**

He showed the activities of sorrow etc. from association with women. This acted as a stimulus to give mercy to the highest devotees. Separated from her, he wandered about in the forest. It will be said in the next verse that he found out where she was from the monkeys.

### Text 12

*dagdhvātma-kṛtya-hata-kṛtyam ahan kabandhaṁ*  
*sakhyaṁ vidhāya kapibhir dayitā-gatiṁ taiḥ*  
*buddhvātha vālini hate plavagendra-sainyair*  
*velām agāt sa manujo 'ja-bhavārcitāṅghriḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After performing the last rites for Jatāyu who acted on Rāma’s behalf, killing the demon Kabandha, making friends with the monkeys, killing Vāli, and understanding where Sītā was from the monkeys, Rāma, whose feet are worshipped by Brahmā and Śiva, went to the shore of the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

*Sam-anujaḥ* (instead of *sa manujaḥ*) can mean Rāma who was accompanied by his younger brother Lakṣmaṇa.

### Text 30

*tato dadarśa bhagavān aśoka-vanikāśrame*  
*kṣāmāṁ sva-viraha-vyādhiṁ śiṁśapā-mūlam-āśritām*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, Rāmacandra saw Sītā sitting in a small cottage beneath a** ***śiṁśapa*** **tree in a forest of Aśoka trees. She was thin, aggrieved because of separation from Rāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Rāma saw Sītā.

### Text 39-40

*pāduke nyasya purataḥ prāñjalir bāṣpa-locanaḥ*  
*tam āśliṣya ciraṁ dorbhyāṁ snāpayan netrajair jalaiḥ*  
*rāmo lakṣmaṇa-sītābhyāṁ viprebhyo ye 'rha-sattamāḥ*  
*tebhyaḥ svayaṁ namaścakre prajābhiś ca namaskṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After placing the wooden shoes before Rāmacandra, Bharata stood with folded hands, his eyes full of tears, and Rāmacandra bathed Bharata with tears while embracing him with both arms for a long time. Accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, Rāmacandra then offered his respectful obeisances to the learned** ***brāhmaṇas*****, who were most respectable. The citizens of Ayodhyā offered their respectful obeisances to the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Bharata had tears in his eyes (*bāspa-locanaḥ*).

## Chapter Eleven

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*bhagavān ātmanātmānaṁ rāma uttama-kalpakaiḥ*  
*sarva-devamayaṁ devam īje 'thācāryavān makhaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The Supreme Lord, Rāmacandra, accepted an** ***ācārya*** **and performed sacrifices with the best paraphernalia. Thus he worshiped himself, by himself.**

**Комментарий:**

He worshipped himself by himself to set an example for other people.

### Text 8

*kadācil loka-jijñāsur gūḍho rātryām alakṣitaḥ*  
*caran vāco 'śṛṇod rāmo bhāryām uddiśya kasyacit*

**Перевод:**

**Once while Rāmacandra was walking at night incognito to learn the opinion of the people, he heard a man speaking about his wife, Sītādevī.**

**Комментарий:**

What he saw is described, to begin his pastime of renouncing the mortal world, becoming detached from everything. The “someone” was a devious person who suddenly came and lived there.

### Text 10

*iti lokād bahu-mukhād durārādhyād asaṁvidaḥ*  
*patyā bhītena sā tyaktā prāptā prācetasāśramam*

**Перевод:**

**Fearing ignorant men who gossip and are difficult to control, Rāmacandra abandoned Sītā, who then went to the hermitage of Vālmīki.**

**Комментарий:**

He was worried about people from other states (*lokāt*) who would gossip.

### Text 16

*tac chrutvā bhagavān rāmo rundhann api dhiyā śucaḥ*  
*smaraṁs tasyā guṇāṁs tāṁs tān nāśaknod roddhum īśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After hearing the news of mother Sītā's entering the earth, the Supreme Lord Rāma, though capable of checking his grief by intelligence, on remembering her good qualities he could not do so, though he was the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

His inner feelings are revealed to confirm what was previously said: he wanted to broadcast the miseries arising from association with women. (SB 9.10.11) Though he was the Lord he acted in this way. Such was the greatness of her qualities of bhakti.

### Text 17

*strī-puṁ-prasaṅga etādṛk sarvatra trāsam-āvahaḥ*  
*apīśvarāṇāṁ kim uta grāmyasya gṛha-cetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Such attraction between man and woman is a cause of** ***saṁsāra*** **even for Brahmā and others in this life and the next*****.*** **What to speak of the common people who are attached to their houses?**

**Комментарий:**

Does one see such results in relationships between men and women elsewhere? Such attraction between Rāma and Sītā produces fear of *saṁsāra (trāsam*) everywhere—now in the next world, even for persons perfected in karma yoga etc. (*īśvarānām*). Naturally for common people (*grāmyasya*), this is the impression. But their bhava was the essence of prema, the highest puruṣārtha.

Or the ordinary relationship of men and women, thought to be similar to theirs, produces fear of saṁsāra*. Pum* with no ending is poetic license. *Trāsam* should be in the genitive but that is absent as poetic license.

### Text 18

*tata ūrdhvaṁ brahmacaryaṁ dhāryann ajuhot prabhuḥ*  
*trayodaśābda-sāhasram agnihotram akhaṇḍitam*

**Перевод:**

**After mother Sītā entered the earth, Rāmacandra observed complete celibacy and performed an uninterrupted sacrifice for thirteen thousand years.**

**Комментарий:**

Rāma’s attachment to Sītā, through external actions, is shown. Observing continuous (*ūrdhvam*) brahmacarya, out of despondency in her absence, he performed sacrifices continuously for thirteen thousand years.

### Text 19

*smaratāṁ hṛdi vinyasya viddhaṁ daṇḍaka-kaṇṭakaiḥ*  
*sva-pāda-pallavaṁ rāma ātma-jyotir agāt tataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Rāmacandra, whose lotus feet were sometimes pierced by thorns when he lived in Daṇḍakāraṇya, placed those lotus feet in the hearts of those who thought of him. Then he entered his own abode.**

**Комментарий:**

After that, giving up the human world filled with rumors causing his separation, he ascended to his own world filled with eternal union. He appeared personally and constantly with great prema to those who remained there with a desire to protect the world. His feet appeared to be pierced, perceived by their prema (*viddham*) in this manner:

*calasi yad vrajāc cārayan paśūn*  
*nalina-sundaraṁ nātha te padam*  
*śila-tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ sīdatīti naḥ*  
*kalilatāṁ manaḥ kānta gacchati*

**Dear master, dear lover, when you leave the cowherd village to herd the cows, our minds are disturbed with the thought that your feet, more beautiful than a lotus, will be pricked by the spiked husks of grain and the rough grass and plants. (SB 10.21.11)**

They remembered how he observed the orders given by his father (which caused many problems). He went to his spiritual planet, a form of light (*ātma-jyotiḥ*).

### Text 20

*nedaṁ yaśo raghupateḥ sura-yācñayātta-*  
*līlā-tanor adhika-sāmya-vimukta-dhāmnaḥ*  
*rakṣo-vadho jaladhi-bandhanam astra-pūgaiḥ*  
*kiṁ tasya śatru-hanane kapayaḥ sahāyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Rāmacandra's reputation for having killed Rāvaṇa with showers of arrows at the request of the** ***devatās*** **and for having built a bridge over the ocean does not constitute the factual glory of Rāma, whose spiritual body is always engaged in various pastimes and who has no equal or superior. He had no need to take help from the monkeys to gain victory over Rāvaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses recollect the special qualities of Rāma.

### Text 21

*yasyāmalaṁ nṛpa-sadaḥsu yaśo 'dhunāpi*  
*gāyanty agha-ghnam ṛṣayo dig-ibhendra-paṭṭam*  
*taṁ nākapāla-vasupāla-kirīṭa-juṣṭa-*  
*pādāmbujaṁ raghupatiṁ śaraṇaṁ prapadye*

**Перевод:**

**In the assembly of kings, even today, the sages glorify Rāma’s spotless fame, which destroys all sin and which spreads in all directions. I surrender to Rāma, whose lotus feet are served by the crowns of the** ***devatās*** **and earthly kings.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering the sweetness of his pastimes on earth, even jīvanmuktas sing his glories in great bliss. In relation to Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes it is said:

*sthity-udbhavāntaṁ bhuvana-trayasya yaḥ*  
*samīhite ’nanta-guṇaḥ sva-līlayā*  
*na tasya citraṁ para-pakṣa-nigrahas*  
*tathāpi martyānuvidhasya varṇyate*
