**For him who orchestrates the creation, maintenance and destruction of the three worlds and who possesses unlimited spiritual qualities, it is hardly amazing that he subdues insignificant opponents because he is playing a human role in his pastimes. (SB 10.50.29)**

### Text 22

*sa yaiḥ spṛṣṭo 'bhidṛṣṭo vā saṁviṣṭo 'nugato 'pi vā*  
*kosalās te yayuḥ sthānam yatra gacchanti yoginaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of Kosala, who touched, saw, sat together with Rāma in friendship and followed Rāma, went to Vaikuṇṭha where the devotees go.**

**Комментарий:**

What to speak of Sītā meeting the Lord again, all the inhabitants of Kosala went to the place where the perfected devotees go (*yoginaḥ*). People of Kosala includes others as well.

Chapter Twelve:

No commentaries

## Chapter Thirteen

### Text 8

*rājño jīvatu deho 'yaṁ prasannāḥ prabhavo yadi*  
*tathety ukte nimiḥ prāha mā bhūn me deha-bandhanam*

**Перевод:**

**"If you are satisfied with this sacrifice and if you are actually able to do so, kindly bring Mahārāja Nimi’s body back to life." The** ***devatās*** **agreed, but Mahārāja Nimi said, "Please do not imprison me again in a material body."**

**Комментарий:**

He spoke by the power of yoga in his subtle body.

### Text 9

*yasya yogaṁ na vāñchanti viyoga-bhaya-kātarāḥ*  
*bhajanti caraṇāmbhojaṁ munayo hari-medhasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The sages who recognize the Lord, suffering fear of separation from the body, therefore do not desire to attain a material body. Rather they worship the Lord’s lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Being disturbed with the fear that again they will be separated from the body, the sages do not desire getting even a body (*yoga*), what to speak of the variety of happiness with birth and relatives. Rather they worship the Lord’s lotus feet.

### Text 10

*dehaṁ nāvarurutse 'haṁ duḥkha-śoka-bhayāvaham*  
*sarvatrāsya yato mṛtyur matsyānām udake yathā*

**Перевод:**

**I do not wish to accept a material body, for such a body is the source of all distress, lamentation and fear everywhere in the universe, just a fish in water will die from other aquatics.**

**Комментарий:**

“In worshipping the Lord’s feet, they show desire for happiness of service. Service is not possible without a body. Do they not desire a body suitable for that service?”

No. I do not desire a body which is subject to sorrow and lamentation and fear. This means he desires a body of an associate, filled with eternal bliss and suitable for the highest service to the Lord.

### Text 11

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*videha uṣyatāṁ kāmaṁ locaneṣu śarīriṇām*  
*unmeṣaṇa-nimeṣābhyāṁ lakṣito 'dhyātma-saṁsthitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The** ***devatās*** **said: Let Mahārāja Nimi live without a gross body, and, being situated in a subtle body, let him be manifest or unmanifest to common materially embodied people as he wishes.**

**Комментарий:**

The devas solved the problem. The sages wanted his body to be brought back to life. The king refused this. They were able to bestow a boon so that his desire could be fulfilled.

### Text 12

*arājaka-bhayaṁ nṝṇāṁ manyamānā maharṣayaḥ*  
*dehaṁ mamanthuḥ sma nimeḥ kumāraḥ samajāyata*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, understanding the dangerous situation for the people without a king, the sages churned Mahārāja Nimi's material body, from which, as a result, a son was born.**

**Комментарий:**

They did something beyond their own statement of giving him a subtle body.

## Chapter Fourteen

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*athātaḥ śrūyatāṁ rājan vaṁśaḥ somasya pāvanaḥ*  
*yasminn ailādayo bhūpāḥ kīrtyante puṇya-kīrtayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī: O King, thus far you have heard the description of the dynasty of the sun-god. Now hear the purifying description of the dynasty of the moon-god, in which famous kings like Aila (Purūravā) are glorified.**

**Комментарий:**

*Athātaḥ* is similar to the use in *athāto brahma jijñāsa*: after hearing the Pūrva-mīmāṁsa, hear about Brahman. (Brahma-sūtra 1.1.1). To begin the story of vaṁśa in which Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān appeared, you should hear about the pure dynasty of the moon, who sustains that dynasty, for auspiciousness and for understanding the intermediate causes and details. Soma can also mean “Śiva along with Umā.”

*yac-chauca-niḥsṛta-sarit-pravarodakena*  
*tīrthena mūrdhny adhikṛtena śivaḥ śivo 'bhūt*  
*dhyātur manaḥ-śamala-śaila-nisṛṣṭa-vajraṁ*  
*dhyāyec ciraṁ bhagavataś caraṇāravindam*

**One should meditate continually upon the Lord’s lotus feet from which the Gaṅgā flows and gives extra blessings to Lord Śiva on his head, and whose thunderbolt is released upon mountains of sin in the meditator’s mind. (SB 3.28.22)**

Or hear about the dynasty purifying for Śiva and Umā, since Svayam Bhagavān appeared in it. Things related to that are also most excellent by nature, such as the appearance of Aila.

### Text 2

*sahasra-śirasaḥ puṁso nābhi-hrada-saroruhāt*  
*jātasyāsīt suto dhātur atriḥ pitṛ-samo guṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**From the lake of navel of Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu sprang a lotus, on which Brahmā was generated. Atri, the son of Lord Brahmā, was as qualified as his father.**

**Комментарий:**

He begins the description with Nārāyaṇa, always glorified for being endowed with the highest bliss.

### Text 7

*sarva-deva-gaṇopeto mahendro gurum anvayāt*  
*surāsura-vināśo 'bhūt samaras tārakāmayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Indra, accompanied by** ***devatās*****, joined the side of Bṛhaspati. Thus there was a great fight, destroying both demons and** ***devatās*****, only for the sake of Tārā, Bṛhaspati's wife.**

**Комментарий:**

There was a fight in which demons and devatās were destroyed. It was caused by Tārā (*tārakāmayaḥ*).

### Text 9

*tyaja tyajāśu duṣprajñe mat-kṣetrād āhitaṁ paraiḥ*  
*nāhaṁ tvāṁ bhasmasāt kuryāṁ striyaṁ sāntānike 'sati*

**Перевод:**

**O foolish woman! Your womb, which was meant for me to impregnate, has been impregnated by someone other than me. Immediately deliver your child! Be assured that after the child is delivered, I shall not burn you to ashes, though you are unchaste, since you are a woman wanting a son.**

**Комментарий:**

Bṛhaspati said this when she returned home.

### Text 11

*mamāyaṁ na tavety uccais tasmin vivadamānayoḥ*  
*papracchur ṛṣayo devā naivoce vrīḍitā tu sā*

**Перевод:**

**A quarrel started between Bṛhaspati and the moon-god, both of whom claimed, "This is my child, not yours!" All the sages and** ***devatās*** **present asked Tārā whose child the newborn baby actually was, but because she was ashamed she said nothing.**

**Комментарий:**

The two argued when they came to the assembly (*tasmin*), which was again formed.

### Text 17-18

*mitrā-varuṇayoḥ śāpād āpannā nara-lokatām*  
*niśamya puruṣa-śreṣṭhaṁ kandarpam iva rūpiṇam*  
*dhṛtiṁ viṣṭabhya lalanā upatasthe tad-antike*  
*sa tāṁ vilokya nṛpatir harṣeṇotphulla-locanaḥ*  
*uvāca ślakṣṇayā vaṁśa devīṁ hṛṣṭa-tanūruhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because of being cursed by Mitra and Varuṇa, Urvaśī came to earth. Upon seeing Purūravā, the best of males, whose beauty resembled that of Cupid, she controlled herself and approached him. When King Purūravā saw Urvaśī, his eyes became jubilant in the ecstasy of joy and the hairs on his body stood on end. With mild, pleasing words, he spoke to her as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

When she first saw him, she was stunned with symptoms like being stunned etc. She then controlled herself and approached him.

### Text 20

*urvaśy uvāca*  
*kasyās tvayi na sajjeta mano dṛṣṭiś ca sundara*  
*yad aṅgāntaram āsādya cyavate ha riraṁsayā*

**Перевод:**

**Urvaśī replied: O most handsome man! Who is the woman whose mind and sight would not be attracted by you? Getting an opportunity in a solitary place, the mind and sight become transformed by a desire for enjoyment.**

**Комментарий:**

Whose mind and sight would not become transformed by desire?

### Text 28

*niśamyākranditaṁ devī putrayor nīyamānayoḥ*  
*hatāsmy ahaṁ kunāthena napuṁsā vīra-māninā*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, hearing the crying the lambs, which were like her sons, as they were being taken by the Gandharvas, Urvaśī rebuked her husband. “I have been killed by an unworthy protector, a eunuch who thinks himself a hero.”**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse Urvaśī (*devī*) speaks (verb omitted). Or hearing the cries of the lambs she spoke. Or *devī* stands for *devyā* and is connected with iti *vāk-sāyakaiḥ* in verse 30.

### Text 29

*yad-viśrambhād ahaṁ naṣṭā hṛtāpatyā ca dasyubhiḥ*  
*yaḥ śete niśi santrasto yathā nārī iva pumān*

**Перевод:**

**Because I depended on him, the plunderers have deprived me of my two sons the lambs, and therefore I am now lost. My husband lies down at night in fear, exactly like a woman, although he appears to be a man during the day.**

**Комментарий:**

During the day he acts like a man and at night he, frightened like a woman, sleeps, locking the doors. He does not wander about awake to give protection.

### Text 32

*ailo 'pi śayane jāyām apaśyan vimanā iva*  
*tac-citto vihvalaḥ śocan babhrāmonmattavan mahīm*

**Перевод:**

**No longer seeing Urvaśī on his bed, Purūravā was most aggrieved. Because of his great attraction for her, he was disturbed. Lamenting, he began traveling about the earth like a madman.**

**Комментарий:**

Sambandhokti has *tac-citto viklavaḥ.* The words mean the same thing.

### Text 33

*sa tāṁ vīkṣya kurukṣetre sarasvatyāṁ ca tat-sakhīḥ*  
*pañca prahṛṣṭa-vadanaḥ prāha sūktaṁ purūravāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Purūravā later saw Urvaśī, accompanied by five companions, on the bank of the Sarasvatī at Kurukṣetra. With jubilation in his face, he then spoke to her in Vedic words as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He spoke words which came for the Vedas (*sūktam*).

### Text 36

*urvaśy uvāca*  
*mā mṛthāḥ puruṣo 'si tvaṁ mā sma tvādyur vṛkā ime*  
*kvāpi sakhyaṁ na vai strīṇāṁ vṛkāṇāṁ hṛdayaṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Urvaśī said: My dear King, you are a man. Do not die. Be sober and don't allow the senses to overcome you like wolves. Don't let the wolves of your senses eat you. Do not make friendship with women who have hearts like wolves’ hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

Do not make friendship with women since their hearts are those of wolves.

### Text 37

*striyo hy akaruṇāḥ krūrā durmarṣāḥ priya-sāhasāḥ*  
*ghnanty alpārthe 'pi viśrabdhaṁ patiṁ bhrātaram apy uta*

**Перевод:**

**Women as a class are merciless, cruel, intolerant, and will do anything for their pleasure. For the slightest reason they will kill a faithful husband or brother.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses describe women. They will rashly act for their pleasure (*priya-sāhasāḥ*).

### Text 43

*sthālīṁ nyasya vane gatvā gṛhān ādhyāyato niśi*  
*tretāyāṁ sampravṛttāyāṁ manasi trayy avartata*

**Перевод:**

**King Purūravā then left the vessel in the forest and returned home, where he meditated all night upon Urvaśī. In the course of his meditation, Tretā-yuga began, and therefore the principles of the three Vedas, including the process of performing sacrifice, appeared.**

**Комментарий:**

He thought that the vessel was Urvaśī. By obtaining it, he thought he had obtained her.

### Text 48

*eka eva purā vedaḥ praṇavaḥ sarva-vāṅmayaḥ*  
*devo nārāyaṇo nānya eko 'gnir varṇa eva ca*

**Перевод:**

**Previously there was one Veda, and** ***oṁ*** **was the principal** ***mantra.*** **Nārāyaṇa was the only deity. There was one fire and one** ***varṇa.***

**Комментарий:**

During the first Satya-yuga in Brahmā’s day there was one Veda, since starting with Svayambhuva, there are descriptions of different Vedas and varṇas arising.

### Text 49

*purūravasa evāsīt trayī tretā-mukhe nṛpa*  
*agninā prajayā raja lokaṁ gāndharvam eyivān*

**Перевод:**

**O king! At the beginning of Tretā-yuga, King Purūravā inaugurated** ***karma-kāṇḍa*** **sacrifice. Thus Purūravā, by sacrifice, was able to go to Gandharvaloka.**

**Комментарий:**

That sacrifice began at the beginning of Tretā-yuga through Purūravā. Previously it was done by others. After some time, the four varṇas appeared.

## Chapter Fifteen

### Text 2-3

*śrutāyor vasumān putraḥ satyāyoś ca śrutañjayaḥ*  
*rayasya suta ekaś ca jayasya tanayo 'mitaḥ*  
*bhīmas tu vijayasyātha kāñcano hotrakas tataḥ*  
*tasya jahnuḥ suto gaṅgāṁ gaṇḍūṣī-kṛtya yo 'pibat*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Śrutāyu was Vasumān; the son of Satyāyu, Śrutañjaya; the son of Raya, Eka; the son of Jaya, Amita; and the son of Vijaya, Bhīma. The son of Bhīma was Kāñcana; the son of Kāñcana was Hotraka; and the son of Hotraka was Jahnu, who drank all the water of the Ganges in one sip.**

**Комментарий:**

From Jahnu came Puru. Balāka was Puru’s son. His son was Ajaka. No other version of the lineage is seen elsewhere. Śrīdhara Svāmī gives the same lineage.

## Chapter Sixteen

### Text 2

*kadācid reṇukā yātā gaṅgāyāṁ padma-mālinam*  
*gandharva-rājaṁ krīḍantam apsarobhir apaśyata*

**Перевод:**

**Once when Reṇukā, the wife of Jamadagni, went to the bank of the Gaṅgā to get water, she saw the King of the Gandharvas, decorated with a garland of lotuses and sporting with Apsarās.**

**Комментарий:**

This was before the killing of Kārtavīrya. After Reṇukā was killed and he gave up anger, Kārtavīrya stole the Kāmadhenu. This is narrated in Skanda Purāṇa.

### Text 3

*vilokayantī krīḍantam udakārthaṁ nadīṁ gatā*  
*homa-velāṁ na sasmāra kiñcic citraratha-spṛhā*

**Перевод:**

**She had gone to bring water from the Gaṅgā, but while looking at the sporting, and desiring to see his colorful chariot, she completely forgot that the time for the fire sacrifice was passing.**

**Комментарий:**

She looked out of curiosity, not out of lust. She desire to see his chariot. See the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa for details.

### Text 5

*vyabhicāraṁ munir jñātvā patnyāḥ prakupito 'bravīt*  
*ghnataināṁ putrakāḥ pāpām ity uktās te na cakrire*

**Перевод:**

**The great sage Jamadagni understood the she had not kept her vow. In anger he told his sons, "O sons! Kill this sinful woman!" But the sons did not carry out his order.**

**Комментарий:**

She had deviated from her vow of serving her husband (*vyabhicāram*).

### Text 15

*te duḥkha-roṣāmarṣārti- śoka-vega-vimohitāḥ*  
*hā tāta sādho dharmiṣṭha tyaktvāsmān svar-gato bhavān*

**Перевод:**

**Bewildered strongly by grief, anger, indignation, affliction and lamentation, the sons of Jamadagni cried, "O father, most religious, saintly person, you have left us and gone to Svarga!"**

**Комментарий:**

Another version has *tad-duḥkha* but this is not accepted by Śrīdhara Svāmī. He thus refers to the sons of Jamadagni according to Sambandhokti.

### Text 18-19

*tad-raktena nadīṁ ghorām abrahmaṇya-bhayāvahām*  
*hetuṁ kṛtvā pitṛ-vadhaṁ kṣatre 'maṅgala-kāriṇi*  
*triḥ-sapta-kṛtvaḥ pṛthivīṁ kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṁ prabhuḥ*  
*samanta-pañcake cakre śoṇitodān hradān nava*

**Перевод:**

**He made a terrifying river of their blood, causing fear in those who disrespect** ***brāhmaṇas.*** **Making the k*****ṣatriyas*** **responsible for killing his father, since they had acted wrongfully, twenty-one times he made the earth devoid of** ***kṣatriyas*** **and made nine lakes of their blood at Samanta-pañcaka.**

**Комментарий:**

The river was fearful because it caused fear in persons who disrespect brāhmaṇas.

### Text 28

*gādher abhūn mahā-tejāḥ samiddha iva pāvakaḥ*  
*tapasā kṣātram utsṛjya yo lebhe brahma-varcasam*

**Перевод:**

**From Mahārāja Gādhi, was born a son, Viśvāmitra, who, as powerful as a blazing fire, gave up the position of a** ***kṣatriya*** **and achieved the position of a powerful** ***brāhmaṇa*** **by undergoing austerities.**

**Комментарий:**

Gradually he begins to narrate the appearance of the Lord, his desired goal. Suddenly he concludes the dynasty at this time in order to describe the Yadu dynasty where the Lord appeared.

### Text 29

*viśvāmitrasya caivāsan putrā eka-śataṁ nṛpa*  
*madhyamas tu madhucchandā madhucchandasa eva te*

**Перевод:**

**O King! Viśvāmitra had 101 sons, of whom the middle one was known as Madhucchandā. In relation to him, all the other sons were celebrated as the Madhucchandās.**

**Комментарий:**

He had a hundred and one sons (*eka-śatam*). In his commentary Śrīdhara Svāmī mentions *prāṇa-bhṛt*, the brick used in sacrifice which is purified by the famous prāṇa-bhṛt mantra.

Chapter Seventeen

No commentaries

## Chapter Eighteen

### Text 20-21

*taṁ vīram āhauśanasī prema-nirbharayā girā*  
*rājaṁs tvayā gṛhīto me pāṇiḥ para-purañjaya*  
*hasta-grāho 'paro mā bhūd gṛhītāyās tvayā hi me*  
*eṣa īśa-kṛto vīra sambandho nau na pauruṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With words saturated with affection, Devayānī said to King Yayāti: O great hero, O King! Conqueror of the cities of your enemies! You have accepted my hand. May no one else accept my hand which has been accepted by you. This relationship has been created by the Lord, not by any human.**

**Комментарий:**

This relationship has been created by the Lord. Through her words Śukadeva’s conclusion is expressed.

### Text 23

*yayātir anabhipretaṁ daivopahṛtam ātmanaḥ*  
*manas tu tad-gataṁ buddhvā pratijagrāha tad-vacaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**King Yayāti did not like it, but because it was arranged by providence and because he considered that his mind was absorbed in** ***dharma,*** **he accepted her request.**

**Комментарий:**

He thought, “She has said it is the will of the Lord. What sin is there in that? Will it not produce adharma, since it encourages the seed of anartha? Since it does not contradict the curse of Kaca, it is not a cause of removing the adharma. How did his behavior arise? ” His mind was absorbed in behavior which took shelter of the Lord.

This arrangement was the desire of the Lord (*daiva*). My mind should not absorbed in actions which yield sinful results. Since I take shelter of the Lord, the Lord would not let adharma happen. My mind also does not enter into such actions. I always consider this my nature. However, since this has happened, it is desire following the independent will of the Lord, and must be considered proper.

*na karma bandhanaṁ janma vaiṣṇavānāṁ ca vidyate*

**The vaiṣṇavas are not bound by karma or birth. (Padma Purāṇa)**

To go against this will is a fault:

*jānāmi dharmaṁ na ca me pravṛttir*  
*jānāmy adharmaṁ na ca me nivṛttiḥ \|*  
*kenāpi devena hṛdi-sthitena*  
*yathā niyukto’smi tathā karomi \|\|*

**I know dharma, but I have no inclination. I know adharma, and do not have an inclination to give it up. I will do as the Lord, situated in my heart, engages me. (Gautamīya-tantra)**

It is not a fault to do this as it is for others, since I am fixed in the Lord.

### Text 26

*vṛṣaparvā tam ājñāya pratyanīka-vivakṣitam*  
*guruṁ prasādayan mūrdhnā pādayoḥ patitaḥ pathi*

**Перевод:**

**King Vṛṣaparvā, understanding that Śukrācārya desired to speak some curse*****,*** **fell down at his feet with his head and satisfied his** ***guru.***

**Комментарий:**

Śukrācārya desires to speak some curse unfavorable for him (*pratyanīka*).

### Text 32

*rāja-putryārthito 'patye dharmaṁ cāvekṣya dharmavit*  
*smarañ chukra-vacaḥ kale diṣṭam evābhyapadyata*

**Перевод:**

**When Princess Śarmiṣṭhā begged King Yayāti for a son, the King, aware of** ***dharma*****, considered the principles of religion, and, though he remembered the words of Śukrācārya, he accepted what was arranged by the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Yayāti considered that this had been arranged by the Lord (*diṣṭam*).

### Text 37

*śrī-yayātir uvāca*  
*atṛpto 'smy adya kāmānāṁ brahman duhitari sma te*  
*vyatyasyatāṁ yathā-kāmaṁ vayasā yo 'bhidhāsyati*

**Перевод:**

**King Yayāti said, "O** ***brāhmaṇa*****! I have not yet satisfied my desires with your daughter." Śukrācārya then replied, "You may exchange your old age for the youth of someone who will accept your old age."**

**Комментарий:**

Genitive case *kāmānām* is used with *tṛpti*, according to Vartikā.

### Text 38

*iti labdha-vyavasthānaḥ putraṁ jyeṣṭham avocata*  
*yado tāta pratīcchemāṁ jarāṁ dehi nijaṁ vayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Yayāti received this benediction from Śukrācārya, he requested his eldest son (born from Devayānī): My dear son Yadu, please give me your youth in exchange for my old age.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses expressed Yayāti’s request.

### Text 43

*śrī-pūrur uvāca*  
*ko nu loke manuṣyendra pitur ātma-kṛtaḥ pumān*  
*pratikartuṁ kṣamo yasya prasādād vindate param*

**Перевод:**

**Pūru said: O King! Who in this world can repay his debt to his father who has produced the son’s body, by whose mercy one attains the Lord?”**

**Комментарий:**

By the mercy of the father--attaining a human body--one attains the supreme Lord (*param*). This is shown in the case of Puṇḍarika.

### Text 48

*ayajad yajña-puruṣaṁ kratubhir bhūri-dakṣiṇaiḥ*  
*sarva-devamayaṁ devaṁ sarva-vedamayaṁ harim*

**Перевод:**

**King Yayāti worshipped Viṣṇu, the composite of all** ***devatās*** **and the Vedas, by performing sacrifices, in which he offered abundant gifts to the** ***brāhmaṇas.***

**Комментарий:**

Viṣṇu is all the Vedas and all the devatās, being their cause, giving them great śakti.

### Text 49

*yasminn idaṁ viracitaṁ vyomnīva jaladāvaliḥ*  
*nāneva bhāti nābhāti svapna-māyā-manorathaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the Lord, this universe is created and is manifested with variety like a cloud in the sky. Then it disappears. The universe is temporary like a dream, an illusion or a desire.**

**Комментарий:**

The universe (*idam*) is produced by the Lord, the shelter of all things. By him the creation manifests variety (*nānā*). The variety does not exist (*na ābhāti*) since it is one with the cause, and since it enters the Lord as the cause. *Nābhāti* means it is not manifested externally. Similar to the universe appearing and disappearing are dreams, illusions and desires (*svapna-māyā-manorathaḥ*) since everything is under the Lord’s shelter. The singular number is used in the compound to express one unit. Because it does not express a collection it is not neuter. The rule is *ū-kāro’c hrasva-dīrgha-plutaḥ.* (Pāṇini 1.2.27)

### Text 50

*tam eva hṛdi vinyasya vāsudevaṁ guhāśayam*  
*nārāyaṇam aṇīyāṁsaṁ nirāśīr ayajat prabhum*

**Перевод:**

**Placing in his heart Vāsudeva, the knower of all** ***jīvas*****, who dwells in the hearts of all, but who is difficult to know, King Yayāti, without desire, worshipped the Lord, his master.**

**Комментарий:**

Vāsudeva means he lives everywhere. Thus there was no effort in worship him, since he dwells in the antaḥkaraṇa (*guhāśayam*). Moreover he inspires all jīvas (*nārāyaṇam*) and is difficult to understand (*anīyaṁsam)*. But still he placed him in his heart with devotion. This means he appeared in his mind. Then he worshipped him. He attained ability gradually by his worship (*prabhuḥ*). This was because he was without material desires (*nirāśīḥ*).

## Chapter Nineteen

### Text 5-6

*sottīrya kūpāt suśroṇī tam eva cakame kila*  
*tayā vṛtaṁ samudvīkṣya bahvyo 'jāḥ kānta-kāminīḥ*  
*pīvānaṁ śmaśrulaṁ preṣṭhaṁ mīḍhvāṁsaṁ yābha-kovidam*  
*sa eko 'javṛṣas tāsāṁ bahvīnāṁ rati-vardhanaḥ*  
*reme kāma-graha-grasta ātmānaṁ nāvabudhyata*

**Перевод:**

**Getting out of the well, the she-goat with attractive hips desired to accept him as her husband. When she did so, many other she-goats also desired him as their husband because he was big, had a mustache and beard, had abundant semen, and was expert at sexual intercourse. Haunted by the ghost of lust, the one hero among the he-goats, increasing his desire among many she-goats, engaged in erotic activities and naturally forgot his spiritual commitment.**

**Комментарий:**

Goats are skillful at sex life.

### Text 12

*tathāhaṁ kṛpaṇaḥ subhru bhavatyāḥ prema-yantritaḥ*  
*ātmānaṁ nābhijānāmi mohitas tava māyayā*

**Перевод:**

**O my dear wife with beautiful eyebrows! In a similar manner, I am a miser, controlled by love for you. Bewildered by your** ***māyā,*** **I do not know the self.**

**Комментарий:**

*Māyayā* means by the power of allurement.

### Text 26

*śrutvā gāthāṁ devayānī mene prastobham ātmanaḥ*  
*strī-puṁsoḥ sneha-vaiklavyāt parihāsam iveritam*

**Перевод:**

**When Devayānī heard Mahārāja Yayāti's story of the he-goat and she-goat, she understood that this story, which was presented as if a joke between husband and wife out of affection, was a censure of herself.**

**Комментарий:**

She took the story as a joke, as a criticism of herself (*prasotbham*), since it showed weakness resulting from affection between man and woman. The other meaning is that it was not a joke but reality.

## Chapter Twenty

### Text 13

*śrī-śakuntalovāca*  
*viśvāmitrātmajaivāhaṁ tyaktā menakayā vane*  
*vedaitad bhagavān kaṇvo vīra kiṁ karavāma te*

**Перевод:**

**Śakuntalā said: I am the daughter of Viśvāmitra. My mother, Menakā, left me in the forest. O hero, the most powerful sage Kaṇva knows this. O hero, how may I serve you?**

**Комментарий:**

She was the daughter of Viśvāmitra, who was of kṣatriya lineage.

### Text 24-26

*cakraṁ dakṣiṇa-haste 'sya padma-kośo 'sya pādayoḥ*  
*īje mahābhiṣekeṇa so 'bhiṣikto 'dhirāḍ vibhuḥ*  
*pañca-pañcāśatā medhyair gaṅgāyām anu vājibhiḥ*  
*māmateyaṁ purodhāya yamunām anu ca prabhuḥ*  
*aṣṭa-saptati-medhyāśvān babandha pradadad vasu*  
*bharatasya hi dauṣmanter agniḥ sācī-guṇe citaḥ*  
*sahasraṁ badvaśo yasmin brāhmaṇā gā vibhejire*

**Перевод:**

**The powerful emperor Bharata, enthroned by a bathing ceremony, had the mark of Lord Kṛṣṇa's disc on the palm of his right hand and he had the mark of a lotus whorl on the soles of his feet. He worshipped the Lord by fifty-five horse sacrifices on the bank of the Gaṅgā, beginning from its mouth and ending at its source. Making the son of Mamaṭā the priest, he bound up seventy-eight horses for sacrifice on the bank of the Yamunā River and gave away wealth. He established the sacrificial fire on excellent sites, during which time he distributed 13,084 cows to each of thousands of** ***brāhmaṇas.***

**Комментарий:**

He bound up the horses for sacrifice.

## Chapter Twenty-one

### Text 3-5

*viyad-vittasya dadato labdhaṁ labdhaṁ bubhukṣataḥ*  
*niṣkiñcanasya dhīrasya sakuṭumbasya sīdataḥ*  
*vyatīyur aṣṭa-catvāriṁśad ahāny apibataḥ kila*  
*ghṛta-pāyasa-saṁyāvaṁ toyaṁ prātar upasthitam*  
*kṛcchra-prāpta-kuṭumbasya kṣut-tṛḍbhyāṁ jāta-vepathoḥ*  
*atithir brāhmaṇaḥ kale bhoktu-kāmasya cāgamat*

**Перевод:**

**Rantideva accepted whatever he got by the arrangement of providence, but when guests came he would give them everything, though he desired to eat. Thus he underwent considerable suffering along with the members of his family. He remained calm though he was without anything. Once, after fasting for forty-eight days without water, in the morning Rantideva, his body trembling because of hunger and thirst, was about to take some water and some food made with milk and ghee, but when he and his family were about to eat, a** ***brāhmaṇa*** **guest arrived.**

**Комментарий:**

After fasting he desired to take (*bhoktu-kāmasya*) water and food which was present (*upasthitam*).

### Text 6

*tasmai saṁvyabhajat so ’nnam ādṛtya śraddhayānvitaḥ*  
*hariṁ sarvatra sampaśyan sa bhuktvā prayayau dvijaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because Rantideva perceived the presence of the Lord everywhere, he received the guest with faith and respect and gave him a share of the food. The** ***brāhmaṇa*** **guest ate his share and then went away.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave the guest the food made of milk and ghee.

### Text 7

*athānyo bhokṣyamāṇasya vibhaktasya mahīpateḥ*  
*vibhaktaṁ vyabhajat tasmai vṛṣalāya hariṁ smaran*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, having divided the remaining food with his relatives, Rantideva was just about to eat his own share when a** ***śūdra*** **guest arrived. Remembering the Lord, King Rantideva gave him also a share of the food.**

**Комментарий:**

Previously it was said that he saw the Lord everywhere. Now the words are repeated to show his compassion. If he saw the Lord everywhere just as antaryāmī, since there would be no vision of jīvas, compassion for them would be absent. Therefore, he saw the Lord everywhere, as being most compassionate. Being touched by the Lord’s mood, he became compassionate. After the Lord appeared along with Brahmā and Śiva, his devotees presiding over the guṇas, the king’s devotion for the Lord is finally shown.

*sa vai tebhyo namaskṛtya niḥsaṅgo vigata-spṛhaḥ*  
*vāsudeve bhagavati bhaktyā cakre manaḥ param*

**King Rantideva, with no ambition to enjoy material benefits, offered them obeisances. Free of all material desires, he fixed his superior mind with devotion on the Supreme Lord Vāsudeva. (SB 9.21.16)**

Compassion for jīva’s alone would be an obstacle as in the case of Bharata. He had no respect for liberation:

*na kāmaye ’haṁ gatim īśvarāt parām*  
*aṣṭarddhi-yuktām apunar-bhavaṁ vā*  
*ārtiṁ prapadye ’khila-deha-bhājām*  
*antaḥ-sthito yena bhavanty aduḥkhāḥ*

**I do not pray to the Supreme Lord for the eight perfections of mystic** ***yoga,*** **nor for salvation from repeated birth and death. I want only to stay among all the living entities and suffer all distresses on their behalf, so that they may be freed from suffering. (SB 9.21.12)**

Thus it is not proper that he would perform bhakti that would show only the quality of compassion for jīvas.

### Text 14

*iti prabhāṣya pānīyaṁ mriyamāṇaḥ pipāsayā*  
*pulkasāyādadād dhīro nisarga-karuṇo nṛpaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Having spoken thus, King Rantideva, although on the verge of death because of thirst, gave his own portion of water to the** ***caṇḍāla*****, for the King was naturally very kind and wise.**

**Комментарий:**

His mercy arose because his nature manifested the Lord’s mercy (*nisarga-karuṇaḥ*).

### Text 15

*tasya tribhuvanādhīśāḥ phaladāḥ phalam icchatām*  
*ātmānaṁ darśayāṁ cakrur māyā viṣṇu-vinirmitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva, who can satisfy all materially ambitious men by giving them the rewards they desire, and who had first disguised themselves as a** ***brāhmaṇa, śūdra*** **and dog keeper, then manifested their real identities before King Rantideva.**

**Комментарий:**

Because they generally give results to people desiring such results, and because they had appeared (*nirmitāḥ*) as false forms (*māyā*) of a brāhmaṇa, śūdra and dog keeper, by agency of the supreme Lord (Viṣṇu), they showed their real forms again.

### Text 16

*sa vai tebhyo namaskṛtya niḥsaṅgo vigata-spṛhaḥ*  
*vāsudeve bhagavati bhaktyā cakre manaḥ param*

**Перевод:**

**King Rantideva, with no ambition to enjoy material benefits, offered them obeisances. Free of all material desires, he fixed his superior mind with devotion on the Supreme Lord Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

Devoid of enjoyment and any desire except to see the Lord (*niḥsaṅgaḥ, vigata-spṛhaḥ*), though offering special respects to the Lord and his devotees Brahmā and Śiva, seeing them all worthy of worship, he fixed his mind on the Lord, knowing him to be the best (*param*), while he felt great prema for the Lord and for Brahmā and Śiva (*bhaktyā)*.

### Text 17

*īśvarālambanaṁ cittaṁ kurvato ’nanya-rādhasaḥ*  
*māyā guṇa-mayī rājan svapnavat pratyalīyata*

**Перевод:**

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit! Because King Rantideva took shelter of the Lord completely, without worshiping anyone else,** ***māyā*** **composed of the** ***guṇas*** **disappeared spontaneously like a dream.**

**Комментарий:**

He took shelter of the Lord completely (*ananya-rādhasaḥ*). This agrees with the previous statement:

*na kāmaye ’haṁ gatim īśvarāt parām*  
*aṣṭarddhi-yuktām apunar-bhavaṁ vā*  
*ārtiṁ prapadye ’khila-deha-bhājām*  
*antaḥ-sthito yena bhavanty aduḥkhāḥ*

**I do not pray to the Supreme Lord for the eight perfections of mystic** ***yoga,*** **nor for salvation from repeated birth and death. I want only to stay among all the living entities and suffer all distresses on their behalf, so that they may be freed from suffering. (SB 9.21.12)**

Māyā disappeared as in the following:

*rte ’rthaṁ yat pratīyeta na pratīyeta cātmani \|*  
*tad vidyād ātmano māyāṁ yathābhāso yathā tamaḥ \|\|*

**One should understand my māyā** **to be anything other than me which is perceived, and which cannot be perceived without me. It is like reflected light or darkness. (SB 2.9.34)**

### Text 18

*tat-prasaṅgānubhāvena rantidevānuvartinaḥ*  
*abhavan yoginaḥ sarve nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All those who followed Rantideva became** ***yogīs*** **and devotees of Nārāyaṇa by the power of his association.**

**Комментарий:**

His devotion to the Lord is praised. Even those who associated with him became devotees.

### Text 25

*sa kṛtvyāṁ śuka-kanyāyāṁ brahmadattam ajījanat*  
*yogī sa gavi bhāryāyāṁ viṣvaksenam adhāt sutam*

**Перевод:**

**King Nīpa begot a son named Brahmadatta through the womb of his wife, Kṛtvī, who was the daughter of Śuka. And Brahmadatta, who was a great** ***yogi,*** **begot a son named Viṣvaksena through the womb of his wife, Sarasvatī.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks of another lineage from the daughter of Śuka, whom Nīpa married after a long time. Śuka does not say that this was his daughter. It was another person named Śuka. That is suitable. Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa describes that Śuka was absorbed in Viṣṇu, since he received the great mercy of Kṛṣṇa. He could speak the Bhāgavatam because he was capable of giving the highest truth, which was given by parabrahman in human form Kṛṣṇa. The Śuka mentioned here is described in Mahābhārata, and is from another kalpa, and is a shadow form of the real Śuka. The story told in Brahmā-vaivarta Purāṇa is mentioned here:

*garbha uvāca—*

*vyāsa uvāca—*

*sūta uvāca—*

*nārāyaṇaṁ vyavasito hṛdi tasya hetor*

*kartavyam etad iha nāma kiyan madīyaṁ*  
*gehaṁ pavitrayitum adya tavāgatasya \|*  
*tīrthasya jaṅgama-gatiṁ dadhato’ntaraṅga-*

*nārāyaṇāpaciti-bhājanam evam eṣa*

*prāha praviśya punar eva sa kāndiśīkaḥ*  
*kiñcit parānubhava-dhiṣṭhita-garbha-śaṅkī \|\|*  
*vyāsa uvāca—*  
*ayam asty āgato garbha! dvāravatyā gadādharaḥ \|*

*garbha uvāca—*  
*tvaṁ brūhi mādhava! jagan-nigaḍopameyā*

*badhnāti ṁāṁ na yadi garbham imaṁ vihāya*

*ā brahma viśvam akhilaṁ tava māyayaiva*

*vyāsa tvadīya-tanayaḥ śukavan manojñaṁ*  
*brūte vaco bhavatu tac chuka eva nāmnā \|*  
*harmye ca vatsyati tathāpi na māyayāyaṁ*

*yat tvām ayaṁ parama-bhāgavato’bhyuvāca \|*  
*gantāsi mokṣam adhunaiva mama prasādāt*  
*jīvann avāpsyati mahodaya-saukhyam aṅga \|*  
*yaṁ taṁ vadanti munayo bahu-duḥkha-yoga-*  
*buddhir viyogam aviyoga-karaṁ mayā yat \|\|*  
*itthaṁ jagat-traya-guruḥ puruṣottamas taṁ*  
*sambodhya bodha-nidhim āśu rathādhirūḍhaḥ \|*  
*āmantrya bhārata-kaviṁ dvija-varyam uccais*  
*tāṁ dvārakāṁ yadu-purīṁ drutam ājagāma \|\|*

**When Kali-yuga came Vyāsa wrote Mahābhārata, the essence of the meaning of all the Vedas. On the order of his mother, unable to tolerate the obligation to his ancestors, just an elephant cannot tolerate a post to which he is tied, Vyāsa gave up his celibacy and took the daughter of Javalī named Vīṭikā as his wife. He performed austerities with her and, desiring a son, she became pregnant. the embryo grew gradually.**

**Effulgent like the full moon, she did not give birth for twelve years. In the womb he heard Mahābhārata, the essence of the Vedas, the scripture explaining dharma, spoken by Vyāsa. Understanding it all, he recited it in his heart. Though situated in the womb, he decided not to come out.**

**In the twelfth year Vyāsa, after bathing, sat down and advised the child in the womb with pacifying words, filled with logic. “You give pain to my wife by staying a long time in the womb. Speak the truth. You should come out. Do not be foolish. Doing this contrary act, you will kill your mother.”**

**The fetus said, “I am in illusion by all this. Who am I? I ask you. Becoming a human now, situated in the womb, I will not come out of the womb. O Vyāsa! Being weak-hearted, I will not have myself attacked by māyā.”**

**Vyāsa said, “If that is your wish, it should be condemned. Coming out of the womb, equivalent to hell, take shelter completely of the master of life, the only cause of liberation. Consider these two alternatives.”**

**The fetus said, “There will be knowledge with discrimination and detachment without thinking of material enjoyment as long as the living entity does not come out. There will not be bondage by māyā of the Lord who stays in the heart.**

**Vyāsa said, “You will not be overcome by the Lord’s māyā. Please immediately show your face, dear child!”**

**The fetus said, “If the Lord of the Yadu dynasty, Murāri, were to appear before me, I would come out of the womb now. Nothing else. This is what I have decided.”**

**Sūta said“Hearing those words, Vyāsa, depressed, slightly unimpeded by the ocean of material suffering, immediately departed, fixing in his mind on bringing Kṛṣṇa. Offering respects, he was worshipped by Kṛṣṇa, the master of the three worlds, the friend of the universe, the deity of the brāhmaṇas. Vyāsa informed Kṛṣṇa of everything that was in his heart. Kṛṣṇa accepted it.”**

**Kṛṣṇa said, “This is something I must do. You, a moving tīrtha, skillful at cleansing the mind of weeds, have come to purify my house.”**

**Being respected by Kṛṣṇa, Vyāsa went with him. Entering the house he spoke, worried that the fetus had changed his mind. Vyāsa said, “O fetus! Kṛṣṇa has come from Dvārakā. O son! Having received this surety, please come out. You will not be overcome by the Lord’s māyā. Please immediately show your face, dear child!”**

**The fetus said, “Please speak, O Mādhava! Māyā is like chains on the universe. If your māyā, which cannot be surpassed by anyone, will not bind me, I willimmediately leave the womb and come out. You are the guarantee, now standing outside the womb. The whole universe up to Brahmā is bound by your māyā. You alone destroy the suffering of material existence.”**

**Sūta said “Hearing his words the Lord spoke while gently smiling.”**

**The Lord said, “You will not have connection with māyā. O fetus whose limbs are covered by yoga! Come out without worry. You will now be liberated by my mercy. While living you will attain the happiness of liberation which the sages describe. I arrange that suffering will end and not return.”**

**When he finished speaking, the yogī, twelve years old, came out of the womb immediately. He offered respects to Vyāsa, the Lord and his mother and departed.**

**After a discussion between father and son, the Lord said, “O Vyasa! Your son speaks attractively like a parrot. He should be called Śuka. Though he may live in a palace, he will not be touched by māyā since my words are in his heart. Do not lament. Let us go home. You should speak what this great devotee spoke to you.”**

**Informing him in this way, the guru of the three worlds, the supreme person mounted his chariot and saying farewell to Vyāsa, the best of the brāhmaṇas, in a loud voice, departed quickly for Dvārakā, the city of the Yadus.**

### Text 28-29

*supārśvāt sumatis tasya putraḥ sannatimāṁs tataḥ*  
*kṛtī hiraṇyanābhād yo yogaṁ prāpya jagau sma ṣaṭ*  
*saṁhitāḥ prācyasāmnāṁ vai nīpo hy udgrāyudhas tataḥ*  
*tasya kṣemyaḥ suvīro ’tha suvīrasya ripuñjayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**From Supārśva came a son named Sumati, from Sumati came Sannatimān, and from Sannatimān came Kṛtī, who achieved mystic power from Brahmā and taught six** ***saṁhitās*** **of the Prācyasāma verses of the Sāma Veda. The son of Kṛtī was Nīpa; the son of Nīpa, Udgrāyudha; the son of Udgrāyudha, Kṣemya; the son of Kṣemya, Suvīra; and the son of Suvīra, Ripuñjaya.**

**Комментарий:**

By the power of yoga he taught the six saṁhitās.

## Chapter Twenty-two

### Text 14-15

*śāntim āpnoti caivāgryāṁ karmaṇā tena śāntanuḥ*  
*samā dvādaśa tad-rājye na vavarṣa yadā vibhuḥ*  
*śāntanur brāhmaṇair uktaḥ parivettāyam agrabhuk*  
*rājyaṁ dehy agrajāyāśu pura-rāṣṭra-vivṛddhaye*

**Перевод:**

**Because the King was able to make everyone peaceful by the touch of his hand, his name was Śāntanu. Once, when there was no rainfall in the kingdom for twelve years, the** ***brāhmaṇas*** **said, "You are faulty for enjoying the property of your elder brother. For the prosperity of your kingdom and home, you should return the kingdom to him."**

**Комментарий:**

Smṛti says *dārāgnihotra-saṁyogaṁ kurute yo ’graje sthite parivettā sa vijñeyaḥ parivittis tu pūrvajaḥ*: the person who gets married and performs sacrifice while the older brother is present is called *parivettā* and the elder brother is called *parivitti*. He enjoyed before his brother (*agrabhuk*).

### Text 16-17

*evam ukto dvijair jyeṣṭhaṁ chandayām āsa so 'bravīt*  
*tan-mantri-prahitair viprair vedād vibhraṁśito girā*  
*veda-vādātivādān vai tadā devo vavarṣa ha*  
*devāpir yogam āsthāya kalāpa-grāmam āśritaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the** ***brāhmaṇas*** **said this, Mahārāja Śāntanu requested his elder brother Devāpi to take charge of the kingdom. Previously, however, Śāntanu's minister Aśvavāra instigated some** ***brāhmaṇas*** **to induce Devāpi to transgress the injunctions of the Vedas. He thus blasphemed the Vedic principles. Under the circumstances, Śāntanu again became the king, and Indra, being pleased, showered rains. Devāpi later took to the path of mystic** ***yoga*** **in a village named Kalāpagrāma.**

**Комментарий:**

The instigation was done secretly.

### Text 21-24

*vicitravīryaś cāvarajo nāmnā citrāṅgado hataḥ*  
*yasyāṁ parāśarāt sākṣād avatīrṇo hareḥ kalā*  
*veda-gupto muniḥ kṛṣṇo yato 'ham idam adhyagām*  
*hitvā sva-śiṣyān pailādīn bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ*  
*mahyaṁ putrāya śāntāya paraṁ guhyam idaṁ jagau*  
*vicitravīryo 'thovāha kāśīrāja-sute balāt*  
*svayaṁvarād upānīte ambikāmbālike ubhe*  
*tayor āsakta-hṛdayo gṛhīto yakṣmaṇā mṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Citrāṅgada, of whom Vicitravīrya was the younger brother, was killed by a Gandharva who was also named Citrāṅgada. Satyavatī, before her marriage to Śāntanu, gave birth to the master authority of the Vedas, Vyāsadeva, known as Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, who was begotten by Parāśara Muni. From Vyāsadeva, I, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, was born, and from him I studied,** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*****. The incarnation of Godhead Vedavyāsa, ignoring his disciples headed by Paila, instructed** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **to me because I was free from all material desires. After Ambikā and Ambālikā, the two daughters of Kāśīrāja, were taken away by force, Vicitravīrya married them, but because he was too attached to these two wives, he died of tuberculosis.**

**Комментарий:**

*Śāntāya* means fixed in Brahman.

### Text 41

*tasmāc ca vṛṣṭimāṁs tasya suṣeṇo 'tha mahīpatiḥ*  
*sunīthas tasya bhavitā nṛcakṣur yat sukhīnalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**From Śuciratha will come the son named Vṛṣṭimān, and his son, Suṣeṇa, will be the emperor of the entire world. The son of Suṣeṇa will be Sunītha, his son will be Nṛcakṣu, and from Nṛcakṣu will come a son named Sukhīnala.**

**Комментарий:**

Viṣṇu Purāṇa says:

*nṛ-cakṣus tasyāpi sukhī-balaḥ, tataḥ pariplavaḥ, tasmāc ca sunayaḥ, tasyāpi medhāvī*

**From Nṛcakṣu came Sukhībala. From Sukhībala came Pariplava. From Pariplava came Sunaya. From Sunaya came Medhavī.**

### Text 44-45

*daṇḍapāṇir nimis tasya kṣemako bhavitā yataḥ*  
*brahma-kṣatrasya vai yonir vaṁśo devarṣi-satkṛtaḥ*  
*kṣemakaṁ prāpya rājānaṁ saṁsthāṁ prāpsyati vai kalau*  
*atha māgadha-rājāno bhāvino ye vadāmi te*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Mahīnara will be Daṇḍapāṇi, and his son will be Nimi, from whom King Kṣemaka will be born. I have now described to you the moon-god's dynasty, which is the source of** ***brāhmaṇas*** **and** ***kṣatriyas*** **and is worshiped by** ***devatās*** **and sages. In this Kali-yuga, Kṣemaka will be the last monarch. Now I shall describe to you the future Māgadha dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

This dynasty is worshipped by devaṭās and sages (*devarṣi-satkṛtaḥ*).

## Chapter Twenty-three

### Text 15

*ārabdhas tasya gāndhāras tasya dharmas tato dhṛtaḥ*  
*dhṛtasya durmadas tasmāt pracetāḥ prācetasaḥ śatam*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Setu was Ārabdha, Ārabdha's son was Gāndhāra, and Gāndhāra's son was Dharma. Dharma's son was Dhṛta, Dhṛta's son was Durmada, and Durmada's son was Pracetā, who had one hundred sons.**

**Комментарий:**

Some versions have *prācetasam* instead of *prācetasaḥ. Prācetasaḥ* is correct.

### Text 29

*teṣāṁ jyeṣṭho vītihotro vṛṣṇiḥ putro madhoḥ smṛtaḥ*  
*tasya putra-śataṁ tv āsīd vṛṣṇi-jyeṣṭhaṁ yataḥ kulam*

**Перевод:**

**Of the sons of Tālajaṅgha, Vītihotra was the eldest. The son of Madhu was named Vṛṣṇi. Madhu had one hundred sons, of whom this Vṛṣṇi was the eldest, from which a dynasty started.**

**Комментарий:**

The hundred sons were called Mādhavas.

### Text 33

*teṣāṁ tu ṣaṭ pradhānānāṁ pṛthuśravasa ātmajaḥ*  
*dharmo nāmośanā tasya hayamedha-śatasya yāṭ*

**Перевод:**

**Among these many sons, six were the foremost (such as Pṛthuśravā). The son of Pṛthuśravā was known as Dharma, and his son was known as Uśanā. Uśanā was the performer of one hundred horse sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Among the sons six were most prominent. *Pradhānam* is neuter.

## Chapter Twenty-four

### Text 9

*babhrur devāvṛdha-sutas tayoḥ ślokau paṭhanty amū*  
*yathaiva śṛṇumo dūrāt sampaśyāmas tathāntikāt*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Devāvṛdha was Babhru. Concerning Devāvṛdha and Babhru our predecessors sang two verses. Though we hear these verses from a distant past, we see them as if they were present.**

**Комментарий:**

Some versions have *amum* instead of *amū*. In that case, the following verses are considered to be Śukadeva’s words.

### Text 10-11

*babhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṁ devair devāvṛdhaḥ samaḥ*  
*puruṣāḥ pañca-ṣaṣṭiś ca ṣaṭ-sahasrāṇi cāṣṭa ca*  
*ye 'mṛtatvam anuprāptā babhror devāvṛdhād api*  
*mahābhojo 'tidharmātmā bhojā āsaṁs tad-anvaye*

**Перевод:**

**"Among human beings Babhru is the best and that Devāvṛdha is equal to the** ***devatās.*** **Because of the association of Babhru and Devāvṛdha, all of their descendants, numbering 14,065, achieved liberation." In the dynasty of King Mahābhoja, who was exceedingly religious, there appeared the Bhoja kings.**

### Text 28-31

*tasyāṁ sa janayām āsa daśa putrān akalmaṣān*  
*vasudevaṁ devabhāgaṁ devaśravasam ānakam*  
*sṛñjayaṁ śyāmakaṁ kaṅkaṁ śamīkaṁ vatsakaṁ vṛkam*  
*deva-dundubhayo nedur ānakā yasya janmani*  
*vasudevaṁ hareḥ sthāna vadanty ānakadundubhim*  
*pṛthā ca śrutadevā ca śrutakīrtiḥ śrutaśravāḥ*  
*rājādhidevī caiteṣāṁ bhaginyaḥ pañca kanyakāḥ*  
*kunteḥ sakhyuḥ pitā śūro hy aputrasya pṛthām adāt*

**Перевод:**

**Through Māriṣā, King Śūra begot Vasudeva, Devabhāga, Devaśravā, Ānaka, Sṛñjaya, Śyāmaka, Kaṅka, Śamīka, Vatsaka and Vṛka. These ten sons were sinless. When Vasudeva was born, the** ***devatās*** **sounded kettledrums. Therefore Vasudeva, who provided the proper place for the appearance Kṛṣṇa, was also known as Ānakadundubhi (sound of drums). The five daughters of King Śūra, named Pṛthā, Śrutadevā, Śrutakīrti, Śrutaśravā and Rājādhidevī, were Vasudeva's sisters. Śūra gave Pṛthā to his friend Kunti, who had no issue, and therefore another name of Pṛthā was Kuntī.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva is the place of Hari. Śiva says that *viśuddha-sattva* is called *vasudeva*:

*sattvaṁ viśuddhaṁ vasudeva-śabditaṁ*  
*yad īyate tatra pumān apāvṛtaḥ*  
*sattve ca tasmin bhagavān vāsudevo*  
*hy adhokṣajo me namasā vidhīyate*

**The pure** ***antaḥ-karaṇa*** **is called Vasudeva, because there the Supreme Lord appears without coverings. In that** ***antaḥ-karaṇa*****, I worshipped the Supreme Lord Vāsudeva, beyond the material senses, by offering respects. (SB 4.3.23)**

The appearance of *viśuddha-sattava in* this word is called Ānakadundubhi. One should see Bhagavat Sandarbha for more details.

### Text 37

*śrutadevāṁ tu kārūṣo vṛddhaśarmā samagrahīt*  
*yasyām abhūd dantavakra ṛṣi-śapto diteḥ sutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Vṛddhaśarmā, the King of Karūṣa, married Kuntī's sister Śrutadevā, and from her womb Dantavakra was born. Having been cursed by the sages headed by Sanaka, Dantavakra had formerly been born as the son of Diti named Hiraṇyākṣa.**

**Комментарий:**

Sambandhokti has *ṛṣi-śapta iti*. He had been cursed in his previous life and became the son of Diti. *Iti* means it is so said.

### Text 57

*na hy asya janmano hetuḥ karmaṇo vā mahīpate*  
*ātma-māyāṁ vineśasya parasya draṣṭur ātmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King! But for the mercy of the excellent Lord, who is the witness, there is no cause for the Lord’s appearance or activities.**

**Комментарий:**

“For others, the cause for birth and activities should be old karmas. The cause of the karmas is māyā. Does this apply to the Lord?” No. he has no cause for his appearance and activities except his mercy (*māyām)* to the devotees who are like himself (*ātma*).

*sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyaṁ sādhūnāṁ hṛdayaṁ tv aham*  
*mad-anyat te na jānanti nāhaṁ tebhyo manāg api*

**The pure devotee is my very heart: what pains him pains me. I am the heart of the pure devotee: what pleases him pleases me. My devotees do not know anything else but me, and I do not know more than they do. (SB 9.4.68)**

This mercy is manifested because he is the Supreme Lord and witness.

### Text 58

*yan māyā-ceṣṭitaṁ puṁsaḥ sthity-utpatty-apyayāya hi*  
*anugrahas tan-nivṛtter ātma-lābhāya ceṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**Even the actions of the Lord in the form of the** ***puruṣa*** **in relation to** ***māyā*** **for creation, maintenance and destruction of the universe, are his mercy alone. That mercy acts to produce detachment from the world and attainment of the Lord in the spiritual world.**

**Комментарий:**

This mercy is shown by kaimutya. The actions towards prakṛti (*māyā-ceṣṭitam*) consisting of the Lord’s glance at it for creating, maintaining and destroying the universe is mercy to the jīvas and nothing else, since in the process the produces senses and intelligence for the jīvas. That mercy acts so that the jīvas become detached from the material creation (*tan-nivṛtteḥ*) and attain (*lābhāya*) the Lord (*ātma),* what to speak of attaining other things like dharma.

*buddhīndriya-manaḥ-prāṇān janānām asṛjat prabhuḥ*  
*mātrārthaṁ ca bhavārthaṁ ca ātmane ’kalpanāya ca*

**The Supreme Lord manifested the material intelligence, senses, mind and vital air of the living entities so that they could indulge their desires for sense gratification, take repeated births to engage in fruitive activities, become elevated in future lives and ultimately attain liberation. (SB 10.87.2)**

### Text 59

*akṣauhiṇīnāṁ patibhir asurair nṛpa-lāñchanaiḥ*  
*bhuva ākramyamāṇāyā abhārāya kṛtodyamaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord acted to relieve the burden of the earth which was being overtaken by demonic leaders of great armies, who posed as kings.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord appeared in this world, showing his mercy specifically to the earth, his highest devotee, who gives shelter to unlimited devotees. Two verses describe this.

### Text 66

*jāto gataḥ pitṛ-gṛhād vrajam edhitārtho*  
*hatvā ripūn suta-śatāni kṛtorudāraḥ*  
*utpādya teṣu puruṣaḥ kratubhiḥ samīje*  
*ātmānam ātma-nigamaṁ prathayañ janeṣu*

**Перевод:**

**When he was born, Kṛṣṇa left Vasudeva’s house and went to Vraja in order to display to the world the highest** ***prema.*** **After killing the demons and liberating them, he married many women and produced hundreds of sons by them. As** ***para brahman*** **in human form, he worshipped himself through sacrifice and established path of the Vedas belonging to him alone, for the benefit of the people.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes all Kṛṣṇa’s activities which manifested suddenly all together, with a desire to appease his own longing and increase the longing of Parīkṣit. Manifesting (*jātaḥ*) in Vasudeva’s house, he went to Nanda’s village. Having described him according to his lineage, and dissatisfied, he describes how Kṛṣṇa increased the sense of fatherhood etc. more than previously (*edhitārthaḥ*). This is shown in Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha and also in the commentaries on SB 10.8.51, 10.5.1 and 10.9.46.

Devatās are worshipped through sacrifice. Why did he worship himself through sacrifice (*ātmanam samīje kratubhiḥ*)? He resides (*ṣaḥ* for *śete*) permanently as his expansion antaryāmī in all bodies *(puru*) of devatās etc. (*puruṣaḥ*). All worship is ultimately for him.

Since he is completely perfect, what does he gain by such worship? He shows people that he is the root of everything (*ātma-nigamam*). By this statement, his main goal is indicated. Since one derives meaning from contiguous words, how is it possible to separate words and supply words? It is tolerated, there should be no contradiction in meaning. Thus the word *puruṣa* not be completely separated from the context.

It is said that his human form is the highest:

*na cāntar na bahir yasya na pūrvaṁ nāpi cāparam*  
*pūrvāparaṁ bahiś cāntar jagato yo jagac ca yaḥ*  
*taṁ matvātmajam avyaktaṁ martya-liṅgam adhokṣajam*  
*gopikolūkhale dāmnā babandha prākṛtaṁ yathā*

**Thinking of the invisible Lord--who has no inside or outside, has nothing previous or after him, who existed in the past and will exist in the future, inside and outside of the universe, who is the universe-- as her son, appearing with a human form though he was beyond material senses-- she tied him to the mortar like a normal child with rope. (SB 10.9.13-14)**

### Text 67

*pṛthvyāḥ sa vai guru-bharaṁ kṣapayan kurūṇām*  
*antaḥ-samuttha-kalinā yudhi bhūpa-camvaḥ*  
*dṛṣṭyā vidhūya vijaye jayam udvighoṣya*  
*procyoddhavāya ca paraṁ samagāt sva-dhāma*

**Перевод:**

**He destroyed the heavy burden of the earth by annihilating with his glance the armies of kings in battle, by creating enmity within the family, and loudly proclaimed the victory of Arjuna. After speaking spiritual knowledge to Uddhava, he resided in Dvārakā in** ***aprakaṭa-līlā.***

**Комментарий:**

The Lord said:

*ativrajya gatīs tisro mām eṣyasi tataḥ param*

**Help the sages cross beyond the conditions of the three** ***guṇas*** **and finally you will come to me. (SB 11.29.44)**

Saying this to Uddhava, he went (*agāt*) to his eternal abode or his svarūpa (*sva-dhāma*) along with his associates (*sam*).

Other versions have prabhum.

## Canto Ten

## Chapter One

### Text 1

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*kathito vaṁśa-vistāro bhavatā soma-sūryayoḥ*  
*rājñāṁ cobhaya-vaṁśyānāṁ caritaṁ paramādbhutam*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: My dear lord, you have elaborately described the dynasties starting with Svayambhuva Manu and exalted and wonderful activities of the kings of dynasties of the moon-god and the sun-god.**

**Комментарий:**

In the list of ten characteristics of a Purāṇa given in the Twelfth Canto, description of the vaṁśa of Kṛṣṇa is given as one topic. This was described in the Ninth Canto. In the Second Canto, another list of the ten items was given. This included a description of the Manvantara periods. Both these descriptions lead to the tenth topic. Realizing the special happiness by describing the form of Kṛṣṇa, his dear deity, at the end, the king eagerly asks in order to understand about Kṛṣṇa with his special qualities directly through stories. Referring to the list of kings, he then expresses his desire in verse 2.

### Text 2

*yadoś ca dharma-śīlasya nitarāṁ muni-sattama*  
*tatrāṁśenāvatīrṇasya viṣṇor vīryāṇi śaṁsa naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O best of sages, you have also described the descendants of devotional Yadu. Now, kindly describe the wonderful, glorious activities of Kṛṣṇa, the perfection of all-pervasiveness, who appeared in that Yadu dynasty with Baladeva, his expansion.**

**Комментарий:**

*Aṁśena* means “with Balarāma.”

### Text 3

*avatīrya yador vaṁśa bhagavān bhūta-bhāvanaḥ*  
*kṛtavān yāni viśvātmā tāni no vada vistarāt*

**Перевод:**

**Please tell me elaborately about the glorious activities, from the beginning to the end, that the Lord, protector of all beings, benefactor of all beings, performed after appearing in the Yadu dynasty.**

### Text 4

*nivṛtta-tarṣair upagīyamānād*  
*bhavauṣadhāc chrotra-mano-’bhirāmāt*  
*ka uttamaśloka-guṇānuvādāt*  
*pumān virajyeta vinā paśughnāt*

**Перевод:**

**Except for a killer, what person would ever cease hearing glorification of the qualities of the famous Lord, sung profusely by liberated souls, by persons desiring relief from material suffering, and by persons desiring pleasure for the ear and mind?**

**Комментарий:**

He gives a general glorification of the topics. In the next verse he becomes more particular.

### Text 5

*pitāmahā me samare ’marañjayair*  
*devavratādyātirathais timiṅgilaiḥ*  
*duratyayaṁ kaurava-sainya-sāgaraṁ*  
*kṛtvātaran vatsa-padaṁ sma yat-plavāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Taking the boat of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, my grandfather Arjuna and others easily crossed the difficult ocean of the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra, in which such commanders as Bhīṣma resembled great fish that could very easily have swallowed him since that ocean became the size of the hoof print of a calf.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa’s feet are an extraordinary boat, making the ocean of the battlefield insignificant, like a hoof print of the calf. The boat was not even necessary to cross that ocean. Or with the boat of Kṛṣṇa’s feet, one could easily cross the ocean.

### Text 6

*drauṇy-astra-vipluṣṭam idaṁ mad-aṅgaṁ*  
*santāna-bījaṁ kuru-pāṇḍavānām*  
*jugopa kukṣiṁ gata ātta-cakro*  
*mātuś ca me yaḥ śaraṇaṁ gatāyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because my mother surrendered unto Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, the Lord, Sudarśana-cakra in hand, entered her womb and saved my body, the body of the last remaining descendant of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, a body which was almost destroyed by the fiery weapon of Aśvatthāmā.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord protected Parīkṣit using his club according to the First Canto:

*astra-tejaḥ sva-gadayā nīhāram iva gopatiḥ*

**The Lord was thus engaged in vanquishing the radiation of the** ***brahmāstra*** **using his club, just as the sun evaporates a drop of dew. (SB 1.12.10)**

### Text 7

*vīryāṇi tasyākhila-deha-bhājām*  
*antar bahiḥ pūruṣa-kāla-rūpaiḥ*  
*prayacchato mṛtyum utāmṛtaṁ ca*  
*māyā-manuṣyasya vadasva vidvan*

**Перевод:**

**O learned Śukadeva! Please reveal the confidential activities of Kṛṣṇa, appearing in a human form by his mercy, appearing within and outside of all materially embodied living beings as time and Paramātmā and giving prema or death to various persons.**

**Комментарий:**

It was previously mentioned that Kṛṣṇa gave benefit to even the materialists. Parīkṣit asks about this.

The Lord gives death or eternal life to jīvas of all sorts without rule. He arranged for Bhīṣma to give up his body, though it was otherwise difficult for him to do, since Bhīṣma could die at his own will. He gave liberation (*amṛtam*) to Kaṁsa and others, difficult to do since they were hostile to him. The word *ca* indicates that he gave bhakti to Pūtanā and others. Speak of such powerful activities performed at his will. The reason is given: he is situated internally and externally as the puruṣas and as various measures of time*. Viṣṇos tu trīṇi rūpāṇi puruṣākhyāni*: Viṣṇu has three forms called puruṣas. You are para-brahman in human form. You appear to be a material human by your māyā (*māyā-manuṣyasya*). One should hear about your activities for one’s own benefit. They produce surrender since they have such power.

### Text 9

*kasmān mukundo bhagavān pitur gehād vrajaṁ gataḥ*  
*kva vāsaṁ jñātibhiḥ sārdhaṁ kṛtavān sātvatāṁ patiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Why did Kṛṣṇa leave the house of his father, Vasudeva, and transfer himself to Vṛndāvana? Where did the Lord, the protector of the devotees, live with his relatives?**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

Parīkṣit uses the word “father” to indicate Vasudeva, because of the apparent birth from Vasudeva, and not from the point of view of bhāva. Śukadeva however later identifies Kṛṣṇa’s actual father with the words *nandaḥ sva-putram ādāya pretyāgatam udāra-dhīḥ:* generous Nanda immediately took his son Kṛṣṇa on his lap as if Kṛṣṇa had returned from death. (SB 10.6.43) Since bhāva is most important, Nanda also is the main father. This is described in Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha.

Where does he live with the cowherds in Vṛndāvana and with the Yādus in Dvārakā?

Both are considered relatives:

*yāta yūyaṁ vrajaṁn tāta vayaṁ ca sneha-duḥkhitān*  
*jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṁ sukham*

**Now you should all return to Vraja, dear father. We shall come to see you, our dear relatives who suffer in separation from us, as soon as we have given some happiness to your well-wishing friends. (SB 10.45.23)**

### Text 11

*dehaṁ mānuṣam āśritya kati varṣāṇi vṛṣṇibhiḥ*  
*yadu-puryāṁ sahāvātsīt patnyaḥ katy abhavan prabhoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, has no material body, yet he appears as a human being. For how many years did he live with the descendants of Vṛṣṇi? How many wives did he marry, and for how many years did he live in Dvārakā?**

**Комментарий:**

*Dehaṁ mānuṣam āśritya:* he took shelter of this material world (*deham*) filled with humans (*mānuṣam*).

### Text 13

*naiṣātiduḥsahā kṣun māṁ tyaktodam api bādhate*  
*pibantaṁ tvan-mukhāmbhoja- cyutaṁ hari-kathāmṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**Because I am drinking the nectar of topics about Kṛṣṇa, which is flowing from your lotus mouth, though I have given up even drinking water, my hunger and thirst, which are extremely difficult to bear, cannot hinder me.**

**Комментарий:**

This shows Parīkṣit’s intense attraction to the topics. Though he had given up even water, he could not stop listening.

### Text 19

*brahmā tad-upadhāryātha saha devais tayā saha*  
*jagāma sa-tri-nayanas tīraṁ kṣīra-payo-nidheḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, having heard of the distress of mother earth, Brahmā, with mother earth, Śiva and all the other** ***devatās,*** **approached the shore of the ocean of milk.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

They went to the shore of the milk ocean which was protected by a form of Viṣṇu. This is understood from the *Padma Purāṇa* and *Viṣṇu-sahasra-nāma-stotra.* *Viṣṇuḥ kṣīrabdhi-mandiraḥ:* Viṣṇu has an abode in the Milk Ocean.

### Text 21

*giraṁ samādhau gagane samīritāṁ*  
*niśamya vedhās tridaśān uvāca ha*  
*gāṁ pauruṣīṁ me śṛṇutāmarāḥ punar*  
*vidhīyatām āśu tathaiva mā ciram*

**Перевод:**

**While in trance, Brahmā heard words vibrating in the sky. Thus he told the** ***devatās:*** **O** ***devatās,*** **hear immediately from me the order of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and execute it without delay.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses describe the message.

### Text 22

*puraiva puṁsāvadhṛto dharā-jvaro*  
*bhavadbhir aṁśair yaduṣūpajanyatām*  
*sa yāvad urvyā bharam īśvareśvaraḥ*  
*sva-kāla-śaktyā kṣapayaṁś cared bhuvi*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is already aware of the distress on earth. For as long as the source of all forms of the Lord remains visible on earth to diminish its burden, all of you** ***devatās*** **should appear as sons and grandsons along with his eternal associates in the family of the Yadus at the proper time.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

Brahmā repeated Viṣṇu’s words in four verses. Kṛṣṇa (*puṁsā*), of whom I (Viṣṇu) am a portion of a portion, has already understood the distressful condition of the earth. You do not have to inform him.

### Text 24

*vāsudeva-kalānantaḥ sahasra-vadanaḥ svarāṭ*  
*agrato bhavitā devo hareḥ priya-cikīrṣayā*

**Перевод:**

**The expansion of Kṛṣṇa is Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is unlimited and has a thousand heads and exists along with Kṛṣṇa. He is worshipped by all.Previous to the appearance of Kṛṣṇa, this Saṅkarṣaṇa will appear as Baladeva, just to please the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa in his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

He would not appear after Kṛṣṇa, as Lakṣmaṇa did for Rāmacandra. He appeared first, with special friendship as a devotee, in order to destroy obstructions by his own desire. It is said *pūrva-bhakti-khedācyutāgrajaḥ*: he is the elder brother of Kṛṣṇa but had lesser bhakti previously. (Padma Purāṇa) In his portion as Lakṣmaṇa he had laxity, but as Balarāma, this never happened. Or, though he was elder, he could not independently accept suffering, just as Rāma was not independent of Lakṣmaṇa. He desired to do this independently at this time. He lamented concerning his bhakti (*bhakti-kheda*) since he could not destroy suffering on his own, being similar to Lakṣmaṇa.

### Text 47

*nirbandhaṁ tasya taṁ jñātvā vicintyānakadundubhiḥ*  
*prāptaṁ kālaṁ prativyoḍhum idaṁ tatrānvapadyata*

**Перевод:**

**When Vasudeva saw that Kaṁsa was determined to kill his sister Devakī, considering the matter, he immediately thought of a way to cheat imminent death.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa was considering in his mind the method of killing her (*nirbandham*).

### Text 49–50

*pradāya mṛtyave putrān mocaye kṛpaṇām imām*  
*sutā me yadi jāyeran mṛtyur vā na mriyeta cet*  
*viparyayo vā kiṁ na syād gatir dhātur duratyayā*  
*upasthito nivarteta nivṛttaḥ punar āpatet*

**Перевод:**

**By delivering all my sons to Kaṁsa, who is death personified, I shall save the life of Devakī. Perhaps Kaṁsa will die before my sons take birth, or, since he is already destined to die at the hands of my son, one of my sons may kill him. Maybe the prediction is not true. The ways of the Lord are hard to understand. For the time being, let me promise to hand over my sons so that Kaṁsa will give up this immediate threat, and if in due course of time Kaṁsa dies, I shall have nothing to fear.**

**Комментарий:**

He considers that the message from the sky was some sort of deceit. He considers that it may be true.

### Text 54

*śrī-vasudeva uvāca*  
*na hy asyās te bhayaṁ saumya yad vai sāhāśarīra-vāk*  
*putrān samarpayiṣye ’syā yatas te bhayam utthitam*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva said: O best of the sober, you have nothing to fear from your sister Devakī because of what you have heard from the unseen omen. The cause of death will be her sons. Therefore I promise that when she gives birth to the sons from whom your fear has arisen, I shall deliver them all unto your hands.**

**Комментарий:**

The deep meaning is “I will offer you her sons from whom there is no cause for fear.”

### Text 55

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*svasur vadhān nivavṛte kaṁsas tad-vākya-sāra-vit*  
*vasudevo ’pi taṁ prītaḥ praśasya prāviśad gṛham*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Kaṁsa agreed to the logical arguments of Vasudeva, and, having full faith in Vasudeva’s words, he refrained from killing his sister. Vasudeva, being pleased with Kaṁsa, praising him further and entered his own house.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva’s words were firm (*vākya-sāra*).

### Text 62–63

*nandādyā ye vraje gopā yāś cāmīṣāṁ ca yoṣitaḥ*  
*vṛṣṇayo vasudevādyā devaky-ādyā yadu-striyaḥ*  
*sarve vai devatā-prāyā ubhayor api bhārata*  
*jñātayo bandhu-suhṛdo ye ca kaṁsam anuvratāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, headed by Nanda Mahārāja and including his associate cowherd men and their wives, are none but associates of the Lord, O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, and so too are the descendants of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty, headed by Vasudeva, and Devakī and the other women of the dynasty of Yadu. The friends, relatives and well-wishers of both Nanda Mahārāja and Vasudeva and even those who externally appeared to be followers of Kaṁsa are all associates of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Almost all of the Yadus were associates of the Lord, but not all--because there were five or six demons among them.

## Chapter Two

### Text 8

*devakyā jaṭhare garbhaṁ śeṣākhyaṁ dhāma māmakam*  
*tat sannikṛṣya rohiṇyā udare sanniveśaya*

**Перевод:**

**Within the womb of Devakī is my expansion known as Saṅkarṣaṇa or Śeṣa. Secretly, with joy, transfer him into the womb of Rohiṇī.**

**Комментарий:**

He is known as Śeṣa: he is famous as my aṁśa. Transfer Saṅkarṣaṇa, my svarūpa or shelter (*dāma*) to the womb of Rohinī.

### Text 9

*athāham aṁśa-bhāgena devakyāḥ putratāṁ śubhe*  
*prāpsyāmi tvaṁ yaśodāyāṁ nanda-patnyāṁ bhaviṣyasi*

**Перевод:**

**O all-auspicious Yogamāyā, I shall then appear in different forms as the sons of Devakī and Yaśodā and you will reside in Yaśodā, the wife of Mahārāja Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

I shall become the son of Devakī, in my full form which contains all aṁśas (*aṁśa-bhāgena*).

### Text 13

*garbha-saṅkarṣaṇāt taṁ vai prāhuḥ saṅkarṣaṇaṁ bhuvi*  
*rāmeti loka-ramaṇād balabhadraṁ balocchrayāt*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Rohiṇī will also be celebrated as Saṅkarṣaṇa because of being sent from the womb of Devakī to the womb of Rohiṇī. He will be called Rāma because of his ability to please all the inhabitants of Gokula, and he will be known as Balabhadra because of his extensive strength of prema.**

**Комментарий:**

*Rāmeti* is a compound explained in the following *sūtra: saha supā (*Pāṇini 1.1.4)

### Text 15

*garbhe praṇīte devakyā rohiṇīṁ yoga-nidrayā*  
*aho visraṁsito garbha iti paurā vicukruśuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the child of Devakī was attracted and transferred into the womb of Rohiṇī by Yogamāyā, Devakī seemed to have a miscarriage. Thus all the citizens lamented, “Alas, Devakī has lost her child!”**

**Комментарий:**

Devakī seemed to have a miscarriage, out of fear of Kaṁsa (*vicraṁsitaḥ*).

### Text 17

*sa bibhrat pauruṣaṁ dhāma bhrājamāno yathā raviḥ*  
*durāsado ’tidurdharṣo bhūtānāṁ sambabhūva ha*

**Перевод:**

**He held the form of the Lord and became as bright as the sun. He became clearly difficult to see or approach through sensory perception and impossible to defeat by any being.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva held the form of the Lord (*pauruṣaṁ dhāma*).

### Text 19

*sā devakī sarva-jagan-nivāsa-*  
*nivāsa-bhūtā nitarāṁ na reje*  
*bhojendra-gehe ’gni-śikheva ruddhā*  
*sarasvatī jñāna-khale yathā satī*

**Перевод:**

**Devakī then kept within herself the Supreme Lord, the cause of all causes, the foundation of the entire cosmos, but because she was under arrest in the house of Kaṁsa, she was like the flames of a fire covered by the walls of a pot, or like a person who has knowledge but cannot distribute it to the world for the benefit of human society.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

She who was famous as the function of śuddha-sattva (*sā*), who was aptly named Devakī, because of her effulgence, did not shine at all. She was like light and knowledge. Just as light covered up does not give bliss to all eyes, so knowledge covered up does not give bliss to all minds. In Kaṁsa’s prison house, she could not been seen and could not enter people’s minds.

### Text 22

*sa eṣa jīvan khalu sampareto*  
*varteta yo ’tyanta-nṛśaṁsitena*  
*dehe mṛte taṁ manujāḥ śapanti*  
*gantā tamo ’ndhaṁ tanu-mānino dhruvam*

**Перевод:**

**A person who is very cruel is regarded as dead even while living, for while the sinful person is living and after his death, everyone condemns him and he is undoubtedly transferred to the hell known as Andhatama.**

**Комментарий:**

Though a cruel person appears to be living from the external point of view, he is actually dead.

### Text 23

*iti ghoratamād bhāvāt sannivṛttaḥ svayaṁ prabhuḥ*  
*āste pratīkṣaṁs taj-janma harer vairānubandha-kṛt*

**Перевод:**

**Deliberating in this way, Kaṁsa, although determined to continue in enmity toward the Lord, refrained from the vicious killing of his sister and decided to wait until the Lord was born.**

**Комментарий:**

He decided to wait till the child was born, since the Supreme Lord (*svayam prabhuḥ*) was present as antaryāmī. His faults have been described. Hari-vaṁśa describes his innate qualities.

### Text 24

*āsīnaḥ saṁviśaṁs tiṣṭhan bhuñjānaḥ paryaṭan mahīm*  
*cintayāno hṛṣīkeśam apaśyat tanmayaṁ jagat*

**Перевод:**

**While sitting on his throne or in his sitting room, while lying on his bed, or while situated anywhere, and while eating or walking, Kaṁsa saw only the Supreme Lord. His world became filled with the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

In the end his fault took this form.

### Text 25

*brahmā bhavaś ca tatraitya munibhir nāradādibhiḥ*  
*devaiḥ sānucaraiḥ sākaṁ gīrbhir vṛṣaṇam aiḍayan*

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā and Śiva, accompanied by great sages like Nārada, Devala and Vyāsa and by other** ***devatās*** **like Indra, Candra and Varuṇa, invisibly approached the room of Devakī, where they all joined in offering their respectful obeisances and prayers to please the Supreme Lord, who can bestow blessings upon everyone.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

Because the sages came as assistants, after Brahmā and Śiva, they are mentioned in the instrumental case. Though they praised simultaneously, the main persons are mentioned as the subject. Brahmā and Śiva came first and others followed, but all of them praised together. Because the others are secondary and came late, the first verb participle may be used to indicate Brahmā and Śiva and the second verb to indicate all who came, though the normal rule is that the participle and main verb should have the same subject.

### Text 26

*satya-vrataṁ satya-paraṁ tri-satyaṁ*  
*satyasya yoniṁ nihitaṁ ca satye*  
*satyasya satyam ṛta-satya-netraṁ*  
*satyātmakaṁ tvāṁ śaraṇaṁ prapannāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The** ***devatās*** **prayed: O Lord, you are true to your promise, truth incarnate, pervading all aspects of time with truth, before the creation, during its existence and after its destruction. You are the revealer of sweet words and truth. We surrender to you, the embodiment of truth.**

**Комментарий:**

They deliberate on *satya-vratam.*

### Text 29

*bibharṣi rūpāṇy avabodha ātmā*  
*kṣemāya lokasya carācarasya*  
*sattvopapannāni sukhāvahāni*  
*satām abhadrāṇi muhuḥ khalānām*

**Перевод:**

**O son of Devakī, source of all other forms! You constantly manifest other forms through** ***sūddha-sattva*** **for the benefit of all beings, for giving joy to the followers of** ***dharma*** **and punishing the deviants.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

You manifest forms which are authorized by scripture, endowed with sattva, pure eternity, knowledge and bliss (s*attvopapannāni*). Appearing as a son through Devakī, your śakti does not contradict that nature. Not only do you appear in order to protect, but in order to absorb your devotees in your experience of bliss. By this, they do not know material existence. Others are not like this.

### Text 30

*tvayy ambujākṣākhila-sattva-dhāmni*  
*samādhināveśita-cetasaike*  
*tvat-pāda-potena mahat-kṛtena*  
*kurvanti govatsa-padaṁ bhavābdhim*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Lord! By concentrating on your pure form of** ***śuddha-sattva*** **in meditation some people cross the ocean of nescience as easily as one steps over the hoof print of a calf, by those lotus feet which act as a boat, obtained by the grace of devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

O lotus eyed Lord! This indicates his beauty. You are the abode of sattva beyond matter. Another version has *amala-sattva* instead of *akhila-sattva.* This directly indicates that the phrase means *śuddha-sattva.* Those who absorb their minds in you, giving the highest joy to cross the material ocean, make the material ocean into a calf’s hoof print, by the boat of your lotus feet, which are greatly respected (*mahatkṛteṇa*). By the bliss, their minds are not aware of the material world.

### Text 31

*svayaṁ samuttīrya sudustaraṁ dyuman*  
*bhavārṇavaṁ bhīmam adabhra-sauhṛdāḥ*  
*bhavat-padāmbhoruha-nāvam atra te*  
*nidhāya yātāḥ sad-anugraho bhavān*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, shining brilliantly! The merciful devotees, easily crossing the insurmountable and terrifying ocean of material life, attain their goal using the boat of your lotus feet. You are merciful to your devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Using the word “feet” previously indicates that the devotee performs sādhana-bhakti. They use the boat of your lotus feet. This means they follow the path of bhakti, according to Śrīdhara Svāmī.

They easily cross the ocean, giving up material enjoyment and liberation.

### Text 32

*ye ’nye ’ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas*  
*tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ*  
*āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ*  
*patanty adho ’nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Lord, although nondevotees, having impure intelligence because of not having devotion to you, think that they are liberated and become** ***jīvanmuktas*** **after severe austerities and penances, they fall down from their position of imagined superiority because they have no regard for the lotus feet of you and your devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse describes other people.

### Text 33

*tathā na te mādhava tāvakāḥ kvacid*  
*bhraśyanti mārgāt tvayi baddha-sauhṛdāḥ*  
*tvayābhiguptā vicaranti nirbhayā*  
*vināyakānīkapa-mūrdhasu prabho*

**Перевод:**

**O Mādhava, Supreme Lord, Lord of the goddess of fortune, if devotees completely in love with you sometimes fall from the path of devotion, they do not fall like non-devotees, for you still protect them. Thus they fearlessly traverse the heads of their opponents and continue to progress in devotional service.**

**Комментарий:**

Again the devotees are described.

### Text 35

*sattvaṁ na ced dhātar idaṁ nijaṁ bhaved*  
*vijñānam ajñāna-bhid āpamārjanam*  
*guṇa-prakāśair anumīyate bhavān*  
*prakāśate yasya ca yena vā guṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, possessor of** ***śaktis*****! If your body were not beyond the modes of material nature, knowledge of your true nature, which destroys ignorance, would be destroyed. You can be inferred by sattva-guṇa, for one can realize that sattva-guṇa is related to you and that by you alone does it function.**

**Комментарий:**

By this explanation it is understood that Vasudeva and Devakī had bodies of śuddha-sattva. Even his name is self-manifesting.

### Text 36

*na nāma-rūpe guṇa-janma-karmabhir*  
*nirūpitavye tava tasya sākṣiṇaḥ*  
*mano-vacobhyām anumeya-vartmano*  
*deva kriyāyāṁ pratiyanty athāpi hi*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! Your name and form, representing your qualities, birth and activities, cannot be realized since you are the witness of all things, and can only be inferred by logic and scripture. The devotees realize you through devotional actions.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī:

Your names cannot be realized, but manifest by their śakti when one performs bhakti of hearing and chanting, which produces bhakti with realization.

*tad aśma-sāraṁ hṛdayaṁ batedaṁ*  
*yad gṛhyamāṇair hari-nāma-dheyaiḥ \|*  
*na vikriyetātha yadā vikāro*  
*netre jalaṁ gātra-ruheṣu harṣaḥ \|\|*

**That heart which does not transform on hearing the names of the Lord, even though he shows tears in the eyes and hair standing on end, is made of iron. (SB 2.3.24)**

*nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*mūḍho ’yaṁ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam \|\|*

**Being covered by my bewildering power of** ***māyā*****, I am not visible to all these people. The foolish do not know me, who am without birth and unchanging in qualities. (BG 7.25)**

### Text 37

*śṛṇvan gṛṇan saṁsmarayaṁś ca cintayan*  
*nāmāni rūpāṇi ca maṅgalāni te*  
*kriyāsu yas tvac-caraṇāravindayor*  
*āviṣṭa-cetā na bhavāya kalpate*

**Перевод:**

**The person who engages in hearing, chanting and remembering your auspicious names and forms and who becomes absorbed in those acts at your lotus feet while performing material duties surpasses** ***saṁsāra.***

**Комментарий:**

Thus the worshipers of the Lord become absorbed in you while performing material actions (*kriyāsu*) and do not experience the material world.

### Text 41

*diṣṭyāmba te kukṣi-gataḥ paraḥ pumān*  
*aṁśena sākṣād bhagavān bhavāya naḥ*  
*mābhūd bhayaṁ bhoja-pater mumūrṣor*  
*goptā yadūnāṁ bhavitā tavātmajaḥ*

**Перевод:**
