There is a difference in prakaṭa and aprakaṭa: two manifestations, two identities,and two pastimes. But they recognized them as non-different. They thus seemed to merge into (*praviṣṭāḥ iva*) the aprakaṭa manifestation with its name and form (*nāma-rūpe*) but actually did not, since the entities are non-different to begin with. *Nāma-rūpa* is a compound.

They seemed to enter into an identity with him. This indicates there was actual difference, just as the ātmās of the sages, endowed with waking, dreaming and deep sleep states because of upādhis, seem to enter into the tūrīya, the state of samādhi. But the fourth state is spread in the other three states. The difference arises by upādhis. Giving up the upādhis, it appears that these states enter the fourth state. The gopīs gave up everything which were obstacles to attaining Kṛṣṇa.

They seemed to enter into state of possessiveness. This was done partially. Just as rivers seem to enter an ocean, they seemed to enter a state where they could not distinguish different between the prakaṭa and aprakaṭa states.

### Text 13

*mat-kāmā ramaṇaṁ jāram asvarūpa-vido ’balāḥ*  
*brahma māṁ paramaṁ prāpuḥ saṅgāc chata-sahasraśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All those hundreds of thousands of** ***gopīs,*** **desiring me, the supreme Brahman, not knowing my form of power, attained me, a lover who gave them pleasure because of association.**

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 177:**

The cause of the gopīs attaining Kṛṣṇa in both prakaṭa and aprakaṭa pastimes is their bhāva. Having entered the aprakaṭa pastimes, they attained his svarūpa. The meaning is this. In the statement “He glances at great, attractive Bhīṣma (*bhīṣmam udāraṁ darśanīyam kaṭaṁ karoti*) the phrase *kaṭaṁ karoti*, formed of verb (*karoti)* and object *(kaṭam*) acts as a verb (*kaṭaṁ karoti*) with Bhīṣma as the object. Similarly *brahma prāpuḥ* should be taken as a verb (they attained Brahman) with *paramam* and *ramaṇaṁ jāram* as its objects. Thus the meaning is “They attained the Brahman, a supreme form, who is the supremely attractive lover.” The descriptive terms are non-different from the object Brahman because the supreme object is the shelter of all descriptive elements. *Ekaṁ evādvitīyaṁ brahma*: Brahman is one without a second. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1.11) Though the descriptive terms are non-different from Brahman, each one has difference. *Sa ekadhā bhavati dvidhā bhavati*: he is one and becomes two. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad 10.24.26) The order of words is significant also. The emphasis is on the first phrase *ramaṇaṁ jāram* as in a sentence like the following where the first phrase *pacyantāṁ vividhāḥ pākāḥ* has most importance:

*pacyantāṁ vividhāḥ pākāḥ sūpāntāḥ pāyasādayaḥ*  
*saṁyāvāpūpa-śaṣkulyaḥ sarva-dohaś ca gṛhyatām*

**Let many different kinds of food be cooked, from sweet rice to vegetable soups! Many kinds of fancy cakes, both baked and fried, should be prepared. And all the available milk products should be taken for this sacrifice. (SB 10.24.26)**

Another example would be *agni-hotraṁ juhoti yavāgaṁ pacati*: perform the sacrifice and cook the barley.

According to what was explained, the meaning of *tā abalā brahma prāpuḥ paramam* is “The girls attained Brahman, but its supreme form (*paramam*), Bhagavān.” *Brahmaṇo hi pratiṣhāham*: I am the basis of Brahman. (BG 14.27) In that condition, others, hundreds of thousands of gopīs in Gokula, attained Kṛṣṇa from association with his eternal consorts, who are his aṁśas. They attained him by association with the eternal consorts because that association quickly generates a similar bhāva. It was said previously *kevalena hi bhāvena gopyo gāvaḥ*: by intense bhāva the gopīs and cows attained him. (SB 11.12.8-9)What is he called? They attained me, Kṛṣṇa, who is supreme Brahman in human form.

*yo’vatārāṇāṁ madhye śreṣṭho’vatāraḥ ko bhavati \|*  
*yena lokās tuṣṭā devās tuṣṭā bhavanti \|*  
*yaṁ smṛtvā muktā asmāt saṁsārād bhavanti \|*  
*kathaṁ vāsyāvatārasya brahmatā bhavati \|*

**Brahmā spoke. Who is the best among the avatāras, by whom all people and devatās become satisfied, by whose remembrance people become liberated from saṁsāra? How can this avatāra be Svayam Bhagavān? (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad 2.24)**

What was the relationship with you that they attained? They attained *ramaṇam jāram*, a husband, since the etymological meaning is rejected as in the case of *nandana,* whose common meaning is son, though literally it means “one who gives joy.” Etymologically *ramaṇa* (one who gives pleasure) and *nandana* (one who gives joy) have similar meanings. *Mitrā-putra* means *mitrā-nandana* and not *mitrā-pati*. *Mitrā-pati* means *mitrā-ramaṇa* and not *mitrā-putra.* The word *jāra* should have a different meaning (*ramaṇa* and *jāra* have the same meaning if *ramaṇa* is not taken as husband) since different words in a list should indicate different things. It cannot be *jāra* or a paramour. That is only a perception, since the meaning should be different as in the phrase *gopīnām tat-patīnām:* the gopīs and their husbands (who were apparent husbands only, since Kṛṣṇa is their real husband).He must be the husband since they are all aṁśas of the supreme Brahman and he is the protector of all (*pati*). In this way Piṅgalā said:

*santuṣṭā śraddadhaty etad yathā-lābhena jīvatī*  
*viharāmy amunaivāham ātmanā ramaṇena vai*

**Satisfied, having faith in the Lord and maintaining myself with whatever comes of its own accord, I shall enjoy life with only the Lord, because he is the real source of love and happiness. (SB 11.8.40)**

He whom they attained previously as an illicit lover they later attained in his true form. Thus Kṛṣṇa as paramour (*jāra*) is not ultimate but Kṛṣṇa as their husband (*ramaṇa*) isthe ultimate form.Being a husband *(ramaṇa)* in itself does not indicate Kṛṣna, Bhagavān. Thus the word *mām* (me) is included in the verse. The word *mām* is then explained by using the word Brahman. This is another proof that Brahman means Bhagavān.

One may argue that since the word *ramaṇa* comes before *jāra* the perception as husband comes before the perception of paramour. This has to be refuted by various arguments. Unlike the order of *brahma māṁ paramam,* the word *jāram* should be placed first since the state of being a paramour occurs before being a husband. This is the strongest argument of all. Thus the meaning cannot be that he was seen as a husband and then as a paramour. In this way scripture becomes meaningful. For instance in the phrase *dadhnā juhoti:* sacrifice using yogurt, the principle element is the injunction to perform sacrifice and the accessory is the yogurt. Thus the sequence starts from *ramaṇa*being unaccomplished (as *jāra)* and ends with *mām paramam.*

*Nanda-gopa-sutaṁ devi patiṁ me kuru te namaḥ:* I offer respects to the son of Nanda, and our husband. (SB 10.22.4) Being the husband is the complete condition for the gopīs. This determination of the gopīs with spotless love should be fulfilled by the Lord. He personally accepted them. Their desire was fulfilled.

*yātābalā vrajaṁ siddhā mayemā raṁsyathā kṣapāḥ*  
*yad uddiśya vratam idaṁ cerur āryārcanaṁ satīḥ*

**Go now, girls, and return to Vraja. Your desire is fulfilled, for in my company you will enjoy the coming nights. After all, this was the purpose of your vow to worship goddess Kātyāyanī, O pure-hearted ones. (SB 10.22.27)**

In all cases the desired attainment defined as ultimate should agree with the conclusions of rasa scriptures. All ancient and modern scholars, mundane and spiritual have described it in this way (marriage as the conclusion). Rūpa Gosvāmī also in the act called “Fulfillment of Desires” in Lalita-mādhava has shown this and in Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi has concluded this in the stage of *samṛrdhi-sambhoga*, complete enjoyment, full of all rasa.

This is also indicated in Bhāgavatam.

*yat tv ahaṁ bhavatīnāṁ vai dūre varte priyo dṛśām*  
*manasaḥ sannikarṣārthaṁ mad-anudhyāna-kāmyayā*

**But the actual reason why I, your beloved, have stayed far away from your eyes is that I wanted to intensify my meditation upon you and thus draw my mind closer to you. (SB 10.47.34)**

*yā mayā krīḍatā rātryāṁ vane ’smin vraja āsthitāḥ*  
*alabdha-rāsāḥ kalyāṇyo māpur mad-vīrya-cintayā*

**O fortunate ladies! Although some gopīs had to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the rāsa dance to sport with me at night in the forest, they attained me by thinking of my potent pastimes. (SB 10.47.37)**

Meeting in an illicit way is always filled with obstacles. Therefore it is not approved in rasa scriptures as the ultimate spiritual goal. The millions of gopīs in Vraja filled with mahābhāva found it most difficult previously to hide their feelings.

*nija-padābja-dalair dhvaja-vajra*  
*nīrajāṅkuśa-vicitra-lalāmaiḥ*  
*vraja-bhuvaḥ śamayan khura-todaṁ*  
*varṣma-dhurya-gatir īḍita-veṇuḥ*  
*vrajati tena vayaṁ sa-vilāsa*  
*vīkṣaṇārpita-manobhava-vegāḥ*  
*kuja-gatiṁ gamitā na vidāmaḥ*  
*kaśmalena kavaraṁ vasanaṁ vā*

**As Kṛṣṇa strolls through Vraja with his lotus-petal-like feet, marking the ground with the distinctive emblems of flag, thunderbolt, lotus and elephant goad, he relieves the distress the ground feels from the cows’ hooves. As he plays his renowned flute, his body moves slowly with the grace of an elephant. Thus we gopīs, who become agitated by Cupid when Kṛṣṇa playfully glances at us, stand as still as trees, unaware that our hair and garments are slackening. (SB 10.35.16-17)**

In long separation the feelings became intense.

*nivārayāmaḥ samupetya mādhavaṁ*  
*kiṁ no ’kariṣyan kula-vṛddha-bāndhavāḥ*

**Let us directly approach Mādhava and stop him from going. What can our family elders and other relatives do to us? (SB 10.39.28)**

*visṛjya lajjāṁ ruruduḥ sma su-svaraṁ*  
*govinda dāmodara mādhaveti*

**They forgot all shame and loudly cried out, “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” (SB 10.39.31)**

*tā man-manaskā mat-prāṇā mad-arthe tyakta-daihikāḥ*

**Those gopīs are always absorbed in me, and their very lives are ever devoted to me. (SB 10.46.4)**

*iti gopyo hi govinde gata-vāk-kāya-mānasāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇa-dūte samāyāte uddhave tyakta-laukikāḥ*  
*gāyantyaḥ prīya-karmāṇi rudantyaś ca gata-hriyaḥ*  
*tasya saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya yāni kaiśora-bālyayoḥ*

**Thus speaking, the gopīs, whose words, bodies and minds were fully dedicated to Govinda, put aside all their regular work now that Kṛṣṇa’s messenger, Uddhava, had arrived among them. Constantly remembering the activities their beloved Kṛṣṇa had performed in his childhood and youth, they sang about them and cried without shame. (SB 10.47.9-10)**

*kācin madhukaraṁ dṛṣṭvā dhyāyantī kṛṣṇa-saṅgamam*  
*priya-prasthāpitaṁ dūtaṁ kalpayitvedam abravīt*

**One of the gopīs, while meditating on her previous association with Kṛṣṇa, saw a honeybee before her and imagined it to be a messenger sent by her beloved. Thus she spoke as follows. (SB 10.47.11)**

*yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ ca hitvā*  
*bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām*

**The gopīs of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken their relatives and the path of dharma to obtain the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which even the Vedas pursue. (SB 10.47.61)**

*gopyo hasantyaḥ papracchū rāma-sandarśanādṛtāḥ*  
*kaccid āste sukhaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ pura-strī-jana-vallabhaḥ*

**Honored to have the personal audience of Balarāma, the young gopīs*****,*** **smiled and asked him, “Is Kṛṣṇa, the darling of the city women, living happily? (SB 10.65.9)**

*mātaraṁ pitaraṁ bhrātṝn patīn putrān svasṝn api*  
*yad-arthe jahima dāśārha dustyajān sva-janān prabho*

**For Kṛṣṇa’s sake, O descendant of Daśārha, we abandoned our mothers, fathers, brothers, husbands, children and sisters, even though these family relations are difficult to give up. (SB 10.65.11)**

They were determined to stop Kṛṣṇa from going, giving up all shame. They gave up shame because of the appearance of their bhāva, and since all people of Gokula were crying at that time. They thought they could stop him by crying together in front of him. Giving up their household chores shows clearly the appearance of their bhāva. More than that, they gave up their parents and relatives. This was not just the first stirring of love (*pūrva-rāga*) as expressed in SB 10.31.16. Their laughing indicates a condition of madness (*unmāda*) since it was not suitable to laugh at that time. Looking at the bee also is a sign of madness. The unlimited number of gopīs, acting insanely, giving up shame and giving up parents, could not hide their bhāva, because it was uncontrollable mahābhāva. Though this became known, it remained as if unknown by everyone because of everyone’s great pain of separation from Kṛṣṇa. They thought about this only later. By hiding their bhāva for some time, they could enjoy. And when it was finally revealed, it appeared dharmic in actuality for them and others. This is the opinion of the knowers of rasa. Rasa seen as lacking in dharma is destroyed by its vulgarity.

Rasa with adharma is of two types: parakīya (relationship with a woman dependent on another –a husband) and para-sparśa (relationship with a woman touched by another man). In the assembly of Parīkṣit, which was filled with aiśvarya-jñāna, adharmic love was rejected and rasa was produced according to explanations of aiśvarya-jñāna (they were eternally married to Kṛṣṇa in aprakaṭa pastimes). In the assembly of Gokula filled with prema the problem was resolved in order to act according to earthly vision (getting married), taking support of *lokavat līlā kaivalya*: the Lord performs actions as pastimes, absorbed in them like a person of this world. (Brahma-sūtra 2.1.33)

It is also said:

*nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā*  
*manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthānv svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ*

**The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s yogamāyā, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. They did not harbor any jealous feelings against him at any time. (SB 10.33.37)**

This statement should also be correlated. Bewildered by his māyā, they did not hate Kṛṣṇa: they did not find fault in Kṛṣṇa. How can Kṛṣṇa, the very life of our dharma, artha, friends, wives, sons and life airs act wrongly by accepting another’s wife? The māyā is described. They thought their wives were by their sides but these wives were made by māyā in order avoid the event that the wives of the Lord, with spiritual bodies, would be oppressed by another person. This confirms our proposal.

This is also a solution to the following situation:

*antar-gṛha-gatāḥ kāścid gopyo ’labdha-vinirgamāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ tad-bhāvanā-yuktā dadhyur mīlita-locanāḥ*

**Some of the gopīs, however, could not manage to get out of their houses, and instead they remained home with eyes closed, meditating upon him in pure love. (SB 10.29.9)**

His māyā, capable of anything, starting from the time they were married to their apparent husbands, made arrangements of false forms for his dear gopīs who had attraction only for him in order to protect their morality, since his māyā is most careful in these matters. This particular day is representative of other days as well.

In Kūrma Purāṇa, Thirty-second Chapter, it is shown that a chaste woman cannot be defeated by another person. Sītā is given as an example.

*pati-vratādharma-parā rudrāṇy eva na saṁśayaḥ \|*  
*nāsyāṁ parābhāvaṁ kartuṁ śaknotīha janaḥ kvacit \|\|*  
*yathā rāmasya subhagā sītā trailoka-viśrutā \|*  
*patnī dāśarather devī vijigye rākṣaseśvaram \|\|*  
*rāmasya bhāryāṁ vimalāṁ rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ \|*  
*sītāṁ viśāla-nayanāṁ cakame kāla-coditaḥ \|\|*  
*gṛhītvā māyayā veśaṁ carantīṁ vijane vane \|*  
*samāhartuṁ matiṁ cakre tāpasaḥ kila bhāvinīm \|\|*  
*vijñāyā sā ca tad-bhāvaṁ smṛtvā dāśarathiṁ patim \|*  
*jagāma śaraṇaṁ vahnim āvasathyaṁ śuci-smitā \|\|*  
*upatasthe mahā-yogaṁ sarva-pāpa-vināśanam \|*  
*kṛtāñjalī rāma-patnī sākṣāt patim ivācyutam \|\|*  
*namasyāmi mahāyogaṁ kṛtāntaṁ gahanaṁ param \|*  
*dāhakaṁ sarva-bhūtānām īśānaṁ kāla-rūpiṇam \|\| ity ādi \|*  
*iti vahniṁ pūjya japtvā rāma-patnī yaśasvinī \|*  
*dhyāyantī manasā tasthau rāmam unmīlitekṣaṇā \|\|*  
*athāvavasthyād bhagavān havya-vāho maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*āvirāsīt sudīptātmā tejasaiva dahann iva \|*  
*sṛṣṭvā māyāmayīṁ sītāṁ sa rāvaṇa-vadhecchayā \|\|*  
*sītām ādāya dharmiṣṭhāṁ pāvako’ntaradhīyata \|*  
*tāṁ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśīṁ sītāṁ rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ \|*  
*samādāya yayau laṅkāṁ sāgarāntara-saṁshtitām \|*  
*kṛtvā ca rāvaṇa-vadhaṁ rāmo lakṣaṇa-saṁyutaḥ \|*  
*samādāyābhavat sītāṁ śaṅkākulita-mānasaḥ \|*  
*sā pratyayāya bhūtānāṁ sītā māyāmayī punaḥ \|*  
*viveśa pāvakaṁ dīptaṁ dadāha jvalano’pi tām \|*  
*dagdhvā māyāmayīṁ sītāṁ bhagavān ugra-dīdhitiḥ \|*  
*rāmāyādarśayat sītāṁ pāvako’bhūt sura-priyaḥ \|*  
*pragṛhya bhartuś caraṇau karābhyāṁ sā sumadhyamā \|*  
*cakāra praṇatiṁ bhūmau rāmāya janakātmajā \|\|*  
*dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭa-manā rāmo vismayākula-locanaḥ \|*  
*nanāma vahniṁ śirasā toṣayāmāsa rāghavaḥ \|\|*  
*uvāca vahne bhagavan kim eṣā vara-varṇinī \|*  
*dagdhvā bhagavatā pūrvaṁ dṛṣṭyā mat-pārśvam āgatā \|\|*  
*tam āha devo lokānāṁ dāhako havya-vāhanaḥ \|*  
*yathā vṛttaṁ dāśarathiṁ bhūtānām eva sannidhau \|\|*

**A chaste woman is equal to Durgā. There is no doubt. No person can defeat her at any time. Sītā, Rāma’s chaste wife, is famous in the three worlds. The wife of Rāma conquered the king of the demons. Instigated by time, Rāvaṇa, lord of the demons, desired wide-eyed, pure Sītā, the wife of Rāma. Taking a disguise as an ascetic, he decided to steal her as she walked in an isolated forest. Understanding this, she remembered Rāma and, smiling, took shelter of the household fire. She worshipped the great person who destroys all sin. With folded hands she said, “I offer respects to mahāyoga, death personified, who is difficult to understand, who destroys everything, who is the lord of all beings, having the form of time.”**

**Thus worshipping fire, with unblinking eyes she chanted and remained there meditating on Rāma. The fire god appeared, shining brightly as if burning everything with his power. Desiring to kill Rāvaṇa, he made an imitation Sītā. He took Sītā, fixed in dharma, and disappeared. Seeing a person similar to Sītā, Rāvaṇa, lord of the demons, took her and went to Laṅka situated across the ocean.**

**Having killed Rāvaṇa, Rāma, along with Lakṣmaṇa, brought Sītā back. His mind was filled with anxiety. Sītā, made of māyā, to give people faith, entered a blazing fire. The fire burned her up. Having burned up the false Sītā, the fire god, shining brightly, showed Rāma the real Sītā. Fire thus became dear to the devatās. Grasping his two feet, Sītā, daughter of Janaka, offered her respects to Rāma. Overjoyed Rāma, with wide eyes, seeing this, offered respects to the fire with his head and satisfied him. He said, “O fire! O great one! This woman, having been burned by you, has by good fortune come to my side.” (Kūrma Purāṇa 32.513-530)**

One should see also Agni Purāṇa. Though this is not made clear by Vālmīki, his not mentioning it serves to nourish karuṇa-rasa. The arrangement for explanations sometimes depends on someone else.

Chaste women have power and more particularly, the Lord’s women have power.

*ya etasmin mahā-bhāge prītiṁ kurvanti mānavāḥ*  
*nārayo ’bhibhavanty etān viṣṇu-pakṣān ivāsurāḥ*

**Enemies cannot harm the devotees who show affection for this greatly fortunate child, just as the demons cannot harm the devatās. (SB 10.26.21)**

This is Garga’s general statement. This māyā who serves Kṛṣṇa can produce any type of protection, like the household fire of Rāma (which protected Sītā). The spiritual forms were concealed when getting married and sleeping with their apparent husbands. This happened at other times in relation to others also. This was suitable for māyā since her only goal was to increase longing and protect their morality.

The spiritual forms (*svarūpa-siddha*) were present when they spoke to Yaśodā in SB 10.35.14, when they stopped serving their husbands and children (SB 10.29.7) and when they were prevented from joining Kṛṣṇa. (SB 10.29.8) Other examples can also be found.

The cause and power that prevented others from harming them is shown:

*ya etasmin mahā-bhāge prītiṁ kurvanti mānavāḥ*  
*nārayo ’bhibhavanty etān viṣṇu-pakṣān ivāsurāḥ*

**Enemies cannot harm the devotees who show affection for this greatly fortunate child, just as the demons cannot harm the devatās. (SB 10.8.18)**

Though it is said they had children, it refers to the children of the husbands’ relatives. If they had children it would produce rasābhāsa because of irregularity in the vibhāva. It would contradict statements like the following:

*anugrahāya bhaktānāṁ mānuṣaṁ deham āsthitaḥ*  
*bhajate tādṛśīḥ krīḍā yāḥ śrutvā tat-paro bhavet*

**When the Lord assumes a humanlike body to show mercy to his devotees, he engages in such pastimes. Hearing about those pastimes a person becomes dedicated to him. (SB 10.33.36)**

*evaṁ śaśāṅkāṁśu-virājitā niśāḥ*  
*sa satya-kāmo ’nuratābalā-gaṇaḥ*  
*siṣeva ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ*  
*sarvāḥ śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ*

**With gopīs firmly attached to him with anurāga, Kṛṣṇa, whose desires are always pure, who had fixed in his mind enjoyment with them, served the nights lit by the rays of the moon-- all the nights which give shelter to poetic topics or rasa in autumn. (SB 10.33.25)**

Feeding babies means they fed milk to others’ children, not that they breast fed their own children.

*mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ*  
*vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṁ bandhu-sādhvasam*

**Not finding you at home, your mothers, fathers, sons, brothers and husbands are certainly searching for you. Don’t cause anxiety for your family members. (SB 10.29.20)**

This statement by Kṛṣṇa is a joke (mentioning sons) to increase rasa. If it were true that they had sons, it would spoil rasa, for he would not accept them as his own in that condition (being contaminated by another man). Sometimes the gopīs address these men as their husbands *(pati*), but this is usage for persons of material vision, not internal vision. For instance they say:

*yat paty-apatya-suhṛdām anuvṛttir aṅga*  
*strīṇāṁ sva-dharma iti dharma-vidā tvayoktam*

**Our dear Kṛṣṇa, as an expert in religion you have advised us that the proper religious duty for women is to faithfully serve their husbands, children and other relatives. (SB 10.29.32)**

Actually Kṛṣṇa appeared in their minds at all times:

*mām eva dayitaṁ preṣṭham ātmānaṁ manasā gatāḥ*

**Internally, I alone am their dear beloved and, indeed, their very self. (SB 10.46.4)**

The gopīs also say that they are dedicated to him alone.

*paraṁ saukhyaṁ hi nairāśyaṁ svairiṇy apy āha piṅgalā*  
*taj jānatīnāṁ naḥ kṛṣṇe tathāpy āśā duratyayā*

**The greatest happiness is to renounce all desires, as even the prostitute Piṅgalā has declared. Yet even though we know this, we cannot give up our hopes of attaining Kṛṣṇa. (SB 10.47.47)**

They say (treating him as their husband):

*gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇur*  
*dāmodarādhara-sudhām api gopikānām*  
*bhuṅkte svayaṁ yad avaśiṣṭa-rasaṁ hradinyo*  
*hṛṣyat-tvaco ’śru mumucus taravo yathāryaḥ*

**My dear gopīs! What auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Dāmodara’s lips independently and leave only a taste for us gopīs, for whom that nectar is actually meant! The rivers have their hairs standing on end and its relatives the trees shed tears of pleasure just as forefathers shed tears of joy on seeing the good fortune of their descendants. (SB 10.21.9)**

*api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro ’dhunāste*  
*smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṁś ca gopān*  
*kvacid api sa kathā naḥ kiṅkarīṇāṁ gṛṇīte*  
*bhujam aguru-sugandhaṁ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu*

**O Uddhava, does Kṛṣṇa now reside in Mathurā? Does he remember his father’s houses, his relatives and the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does he ever talk about us, his maidservants? When will he lay on our heads his aguru-scented hand? (SB 10.47.21)**

And in the five chapters on the rāsa dance it is said that the husbands never hated Kṛṣṇa (SB 10.33.37)

Durvāsā said to them, *sa vo hi svāmī*: he is your husband. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad 2.22)It is also said *kṛṣṇa-vadhva*: the wives of Kṛṣṇa. (SB 10.33.7)

*bhagavān api tā rātṛīḥ śāradotphulla-mallikāḥ*  
*vīkṣya rantuṁ manaś cakre yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, upon seeing those autumn nights scented with blossoming jasmine flowers, taking shelter of his yogamāya, decided to fulfill the desires of the gopīs.(SB 10.29.1)**

From this it may be concluded that Kṛṣṇa engaged yogamāyā to use or not use her powers and this was known only to her. Thus there were two forms of gopīs which were undetected by the gopīs themselves and others. These two forms were later revealed to the people of Gokula, becoming obvious or revealed by messages from sages and from the sky,in order to produce in the end great happiness without obstacles on the tree of abundant rasa nourished by her for protecting their chastity. These forms were produced in order to avoid hatred from the apparent husbands. *Svarūpeṇa mām eva ramaṇaṁ prāptāḥ*: they attained me as their true husband. Thus Kṛṣṇa alone was their husband. And the desires of the mothers and fathers (that they marry Kṛṣṇa) were also fulfilled.

If Kṛṣṇa actually had illicit relationships, the elder cowherds’ vātsalya for him would disappear. That would not appear if they were married. Bharata however says:

*bahu vāryate khalu yatra pracchanna-kāmukatavaṁ ca*  
*yā ca mitho durlabhatā sā manmathasya paramā ratiḥ*

**That love which causes great opposition because of being against normal dharma, which necessitates the love being kept secret, and which makes it hard for the lovers to meet is the highest type of love. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 1.20)**

Rasa will not occur if there is no opposition. Obstruction occurs not by instilling fear, since Kṛṣṇa was most skillful, but rather by giving him shame. Shame for young cultured boys occurs when others infer that he has some secret affair with someone’s wife.

*yatra hrīḥ śrīḥ sthitā tatra yatra śrīs tatra sannatiḥ \|*  
*sannatir hrīs tathā śrīś ca nityaṁ kṛṣṇe mahātmani \|\|*

**Lakṣmī resides where shyness resides. Where Lakṣmī resides, gentle conduct resides. These three are eternally in Kṛṣṇa. (Hari-vaṁśa 2.101.73)**

Kṛṣṇa, who manifests high rank and fresh youth in Vraja, and is the abode of the highest shame, manifests this shame to a high degree. This produces obstacles, secrecy and difficulty in meeting. Shame is of two types: shyness for proper activities and humiliation from improper acts. In the first type one covers one’s inner feelings. This is not too contrary. The second type produces double contrariness if one who is attached to his good name is suspected of vile acts.

Though he did play constantly with the gopīs (*gopa-nārībhir aniśaṁ krīḍayāmāsa keśavaḥ* Padma Purāṇa 6.252.26), it was impossible that Kṛṣṇa played constantly with others’ wives in an illicit way. The countless gopīs were in great grief if they could not attain Kṛṣṇa as their husband though he was naturally so. The elders advised obligatory dharma as the consolation, because of the false appearance (of their being others’ husbands.)

It was said:

*ramya-keli-sukhenaiva gopa-veśa-dharaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*bahu-prema-rasenātra māsa-dvayam uvāsa ha \|\|*

**Kṛṣṇa in cowherd dress stayed for two months in Gokula, happily playing and experiencing the rasa of prema.**

After that, it is proper that he gave profuse rasa of prema of a most attractive nature to them. (He married them.) The words *gopa-nārībhiḥ* cannot mean others cowherds’ wives. Similarly in the Third Canto Devahūtī is described as *nṛpa-vadhū*, daughter of the king, rather than wife of the king. Obstacles exist not only in illicit love according to Bharata Muni. Even in married life obstacles exist in the form of cowives as in the case of Ratnāvalī and Yayati. However it is said:

*neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhir paroḍhā*  
*tad gokulāmbujadṛśāṁ kulam antarena \|*  
*āśāṁsayā rasa-vidher avatāritānāṁ*  
*kaṁsāriṇā rasika-maṇḍala-śekhareṇa \|\|*

**Poets’ objection to married women enjoying with another man as the main rasa applies only to women other than the women of Gokula, whom Kṛṣṇa, the topmost among tasters, made appear in this world because of a special desire for madhura-rasa.(Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 5.3)**

Those who desired Kṛṣṇa as a husband attained him as explained in SB 11.12.13 (*mat-kāmā ramaṇam)*.

The Lord also fulfilled the vows of the young girls who prayed to have Kṛṣṇa as their husband (*nanda-gopa-sutaṁ devi patiṁ me kuru te namaḥ)*. He accepted them.

*yātābalā vrajaṁ siddhā mayemā raṁsyathā kṣapāḥ*  
*yad uddiśya vratam idaṁ cerur āryārcanaṁ satīḥ*

**Go now, girls, and return to Vraja. Your desire is fulfilled, for in my company you will enjoy the coming nights. After all, this was the purpose of your vow to worship goddess Kātyāyanī, O pure-hearted ones. (SB 10.22.27)**

He was only like an illicit lover (*jāram*) since he was their husband in disguise. Durvāsā has also said:

*anma-jarābhyāṁ bhinnaḥ sthāṇur ayam acchedyo’yaṁ yo’sau saurye*  
*tiṣṭhati yo’sau goṣu tiṣṭhati yo’sau gāḥ pālayati \| yo’sau gopeṣu tiṣṭhati \|*  
*yo’sau sarveṣu vedeṣu tiṣṭhati \| yo’sau sarva-vedair gīyate \|*  
*yo’sau sarveṣu bhūteṣv āviśya bhūtāni vidadhāti sa vo hi svāmī bhavati*

**He who is beyond birth and old age, who is steady in form, qualities, pastimes and abode, who is indivisible, who resides on the bank of the Yamuna, who lives among the cows, who protects the cows, who lives among the cowherds, who resides in all the Vedas, who is praised in all the Vedas, and who, entering all beings, makes them special, is none other than the husband of you gopīs. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad 2.21)**

### Text 14-15

*tasmāt tvam uddhavotsṛjya codanāṁ praticodanām*  
*pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca śrotavyaṁ śrutam eva ca*  
*mām ekam eva śaraṇam ātmānaṁ sarva-dehinām*  
*yāhi sarvātma-bhāvena mayā syā hy akuto-bhayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! Give up duties and forbidden acts, the path of enjoyment and the path of renunciation, desire to hear more about** ***dharma,*** **and what you have already heard about** ***dharma.*** **Surrender to me alone, the soul of all beings, using all methods, with** ***bhāva*** **in your mind. You will be fearless by my mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

Having narrated that the dearest gopīs attained him, he concludes, including Uddhava in that attainment in two verses. Surrender to me alone, the supreme cherished goal, being the supreme shelter of great devotees, a great goal that can be attained just by association with Nārada, Aṅgirā and others who became my dear associates. Worship me with surrender as the ultimate goal. By my mercy you will be without fear for certain (hi). He shows that this surrender is beneficial to all by its nature. I am the Paramātmā of all beings. Full surrender is explained: do it with complete bhava, while giving up other things. Do not take shelter of jñāna (*śrotavyam śrutam*). The word *eva* indicates that even at other times such things should be given up.

### Text 16

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*saṁśayaḥ śṛṇvato vaṁśa tava yogeśvareśvara*  
*na nivartata ātma-stho yena bhrāmyati me manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O Lord of all masters of mystic power, I have heard your words, but the doubt in my heart does not go away. Thus my mind is bewildered.**

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 178:**

Revealing prakaṭa pastimes and entering aprakaṭa pastimes is suggested in questions and answers. Though hearing and understanding your words, I still have doubts. I cannot understand what you said in the last three chapters. Why? This is because your statements such as SB 11.12.10bewilder my mind. Thinking of what happened to the gopīs’ association with you, I cannot maintain my composure.

Previously he spoke of karma-ṁiśra-bhakti (*mayoditeṣu* SB 11.10.1). All karmas should be given up (*nivṛttam karma seveta,* SB 11.10.4). he described in detail ātma-tattva to obtina jñān for devotees with a mixture of jñāna. When Uddhava asked about the jīva’s bondage (SB 11. 10.35) Kṛṣṇa discussed the bound and liberated jīvas, giving the final conclusion. Kṛṣṇa then explained that jñāna cannot be perfected without bhakti (SB 11.11.18) and then showed pure bhakti (SB 11.11.23). He showed that association with devotee is the cause of bhakti. Uddhava asked about the best bhakti and the best devotee (SB 11.11.23) and the Lord explained about them and confirmed the power of pure association. (SB 11.11.48) He advised Uddhava to give karma and jñāna completely. (SB 11.12.14)

Uddhava now speaks so that there will be no doubts. Having heard your words and understood them I have some doubt. I am unable to understand the mahāvākyas in the last three chapters. The doubt does not go away. Because of that my mind is confused. I am very perplexed. Therefore again teach thoroughly. I have been unable to grasp the final conclusion of all the topic. I have heard imperfectly, though I heard.

### Text 17

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*sa eṣa jīvo vivara-prasūtiḥ*  
*prāṇena ghoṣeṇa guhāṁ praviṣṭaḥ*  
*mano-mayaṁ sūkṣmam upetya rūpaṁ*  
*mātrā svaro varṇa iti sthaviṣṭhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: I am the Supreme Lord who gives life to every living being. Manifesting in the various** ***cakras*****, I enter the** ***mūlādhāra-cakra*** **of Brahmā along with** ***prāṇa*** **phase of subtle** ***parā*** **sound. I then rise to the** ***maṇipūra-cakra*** **in the mental phase as** ***paśyantī*** **and to (the** ***anāhata–cakra,*** **the intellectual phase) in subtle form as** ***madhyamā*****. I then take the gross form of short and longs sounds, different intonations, and the syllables of the alphabet.**

**Комментарий:**

There are two types of anxiety (for himself and the gopīs). Kṛṣṇa said that he left the gopīs (SB 11.12.10). Based on that Uddhava feared Kṛṣṇa would also leave him. Did he meet with them somewhere, somehow? Uddhava was anxious to know the details. To remove the two types of anxiety, the present verse is spoken. It destroys the anxiety that he would be left alone, being unable to accept the meaning of the description given by Kṛṣṇa, by the first meaning of the statement.

He describes how he manifests himself as the sound of all the Vedas in order to show that he is the shelter, the leader, and the meaning of all the Vedas, as expressed in SB 11.12.14.

The description of the four main cakras mentioned are in relation to the manifestation of the Vedas from Brahmā. This is correlated with the description in 11.21.38-40:

*yathorṇanābhir hṛdayād ūrṇām udvamate mukhāt*  
*ākāśād ghoṣavān prāṇo manasā sparśa-rūpiṇā*  
*chando-mayo ’mṛta-mayaḥ sahasra-padavīṁ prabhuḥ*  
*oṁkārād vyañjita-sparśa- svaroṣmāntastha-bhūṣitām*  
*vicitra-bhāṣā-vitatāṁ chandobhiś catur-uttaraiḥ*  
*ananta-pārāṁ bṛhatīṁ sṛjaty ākṣipate svayam*

**Just as a spider brings forth from its heart its web and emits it through its mouth, the Supreme Lord, made of supreme bliss, made of the Vedas, taking support of ether, appears as** ***parā*** **sound made of** ***prāṇa,*** **and then creates and destroys, by his mind which produces the consonants and the manifest Vedas--which are unlimited in sound and meaning, decorated with the consonants, vowels, sibilants, and semivowels emanating from the subtle sound** ***oṁ,*** **and which are filled with a variety of languages and meters, each four syllables longer than the previous.**

*Prāṇa* refers to the upādhi in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, whose material substance is *nāda* (*ghoṣavān*). The Vedas are called unlimited (*ananta-pārām*). They are not the samāṣti (sum of jīvas), since they are not restricted by time or space of the prāṇa and other factors. Śrīdhara Svāmī quotes two verses from śruti:

*catvari-vak-parimitā padāni tāni vidur brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ*  
*guha trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṁ vāco manuṣyā vadanti*

**Brāhmaṇas who are wise know that there are four stages of evolution of sound. Three are hidden, and do not reveal themselves. Men call the fourth stage “words.”**

*yā sā mitrāvaruṇa sadanād uccarantī triśaṣṭiṁ*  
*varṇān antaḥ prakaṭa-karaṇaiḥ prāṇa-saṁgāt prasute*  
*tāṁ paśyaṇtīm prathamam uditāṁ madhyamāṁ buddhī-saṁsthāṁ*  
*vācaṁ vaktre karaṇa-viśadāṁ vaikharīṁ ca prapadye*

**Parā manifests from the ādhāra-cakra of Agni and Soma with prāṇa in a subtle form. It produces the sixty-three varṇas of the alphabet by means of two internal senses and a manifested sense internally. The first manifestation is called paśyāntī (that which is not uttered). The third cakra, endowed with discrimination, and which understands “I am uttering this” is called madhyamā. and the fourth producing purity is called vaikhārī.**

There are three vowels with short, long and very long pronunciation, making 9, plus short and long ṛ and l. making 13. The dipthongs (e ai o au) can be long or very long, making 8 more. Total is 21. High, medium and low pitches are included in this total. Visarga, anusvara, jihvāmūlīya and upadhmānīya bring the total to 25.

There are 25 consonants. That total is then 50. Ya, va and la either nasalized or unnasalized – 6 and r makes 57. (Three sibilants and h make 60).

By the second meaning, his second anxiety is destroyed.

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 179:**

The Lord speaks to remove his doubt in two verses and relieves his heart.

That person *(saḥ*), meaning me, the cause of life (*jīvaḥ*), giving life to Vraja-- or the Supreme Lord--manifested in prakaṭa pastimes (*prasūtiḥ*) from the aprakaṭa pastimes (*vivarta*) along with Vraja (*ghoṣeṇa*), equal to my very life (*prāṇeṇa),* and then entered aprakaṭa pastimes (*guḥam praviṣṭaḥ*). I manifest (*sthaviṣṭaḥ*) myself to my intimate associates with my senses (*mātrā*), words (*svara*), song *(varṇa)* and form. To others I am invisible (*sūkṣam*). For more distant devotees I am understood by the mind (*manomayam*).

### Text 18

*yathānalaḥ khe ’nila-bandhur uṣmā*  
*balena dāruṇy adhimathyamānaḥ*  
*aṇuḥ prajāto haviṣā samedhate*  
*tathaiva me vyaktir iyaṁ hi vāṇī*

**Перевод:**

**When sticks of kindling wood are vigorously rubbed together, heat is first situated as heat in the wood, and then by assistance of air, a spark of fire appears. Once the fire is kindled, ghee is added and the fire blazes. Similarly, I gradually become manifest as the sound of the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 180:**

The example of appearance of the Lord is partial, showing the gradual stages. In the Third Canto Uddhava also says *ajo’pi jāto bhagavān yathāgniḥ*: the Lord though unborn, appears like fire. (SB 3.2.15) *Vyaktiḥ* means manifestation. I manifest in this way because (*hi)* this is my word, and I alone know my secret. It is not impossible to do.

### Text 19

*evaṁ gadiḥ karma gatir visargo*  
*ghrāṇo raso dṛk sparśaḥ śrutiś ca*  
*saṅkalpa-vijñānam athābhimānaḥ*  
*sūtraṁ rajaḥ-sattva-tamo-vikāraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, speech, action, motion, excretion, smelling, tasting, seeing, touching, hearing, deciding, discerning, identity,** ***mahat-tattva*****, and transformations of** ***rajas, sattva*** **and** ***tamas*** **are my material manifestation.**

**Комментарий:**

Having shown that the Vedas arise from himself, he shows the manifestation of functions material speech etc. in the world, in order that people give up absorption in the world. Just as the functions of Vedic sound arise through para etc., material speech and other functions arise, having a different meaning as in the two previous verses. But the Vedic sound arises by the svarūpa-śakti whereas material sound arises by māyā. And just as speech arises so does karma etc.

### Text 20

*ayaṁ hi jīvas tri-vṛd abja-yonir*  
*avyakta eko vayasā sa ādyaḥ*  
*viśliṣṭa-śaktir bahudheva bhāti*  
*bījāni yoniṁ pratipadya yadvat*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord becomes the Lord made of the three** ***guṇas.*** **He is one entity and invisible, but by time, possessing many energies, he becomes many forms, just as one seed among many seeds sprouts.**

**Комментарий:**

An example is given in the second half of the verse. The Lord becomes many just as one seed among many sprouts.

### Text 21

*yasminn idaṁ protam aśeṣam otaṁ*  
*paṭo yathā tantu-vitāna-saṁsthaḥ*  
*ya eṣa saṁsāra-taruḥ purāṇaḥ*  
*karmātmakaḥ puṣpa-phale prasūte*

**Перевод:**

**This universe exists in the Lord like a cloth with vertical and horizontal threads. It is like a tree, with no beginning, consisting of the force of** ***māyā,*** **giving birth to the flowers and fruits of happiness and distress.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to understand more clearly he gives metaphors to describe the world.

### Text 23

*adanti caikaṁ phalam asya gṛdhrā*  
*grāme-carā ekam araṇya-vāsāḥ*  
*haṁsā ya ekaṁ bahu-rūpam ijyair*  
*māyā-mayaṁ veda sa veda vedam*

**Перевод:**

**The vultures or householders eat one fruit of the tree and the swans or** ***sannyāsīs*** **eat another fruit of the tree. He who knows me as the universe produced by** ***māyā*** **and as many spiritual forms knows the meaning of the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

After explaining the Vedas and the material universe, he shows in two verses by combining the two together, the conclusion of what was previously stated in verse 14. There are different qualifications for practice and result in what was stated in the Vedas. The swans or the sannyāsīs (*araṇya-vāsāḥ*), who determine the essence from the non-essence, enjoy happiness composed of knowledge and as a result go to Brahman or attain liberation in Brahman. There is no falling into suffering at all from things connected with knowledge. He who knows me to be the form of the universe created by māyā-śakti, and to be of many forms such as the caturvyūha, by the variety of the svarūpa-śakti, knows the essence of the Vedas.

### Text 24

*evaṁ gurūpāsanayaika-bhaktyā*  
*vidyā-kuṭhāreṇa śitena dhīraḥ*  
*vivṛścya jīvāśayam apramattaḥ*  
*sampadya cātmānam atha tyajāstram*

**Перевод:**

**Thus, by worshipping** ***guru,*** **by the axe of** ***jñāna*** **made sharp by** ***bhakti*** **even in a secondary role, by being steady, destroy the subtle body, and with attention attain Paramātmā. Then give up the weapon of** ***jñāna.***

**Комментарий:**

The result of knowledge is described. In the manner described (*evam*), by worshipping guru, by the axe of knowledge, generated from material antaḥkaraṇa, sharpened by prominence of bhakti, purify external portions of the antaḥkaraṇa and then give up the weapon which destroys saṁsāra, knowledge generated by the material antaḥkaraṇa. After giving up that knowledge, attaining Paramātmā (*ātmānam*) by one’s own knowledge, becoming liberated, experience the happiness as suitable to that condition. It will be said:

*evaṁ vimṛśya guṇato manasas try-avasthā*  
*man-māyayā mayi kṛtā iti niścitārthāḥ*  
*sañchidya hārdam anumāna-sad-ukti-tīkṣṇa*  
*jñānāsinā bhajata mākhila-saṁśayādhim*

**Considering that the three states of the intelligence arising from the** ***guṇas*** **are created by my** ***avidyā*** **within me, being firmly convinced of your nature as** ***ātmā,*** **and cutting the three states by the sharp sword of knowledge, by inference and by scriptural statements, worship me, the destroyer of all doubts. (SB 11.13.33)**

## Chapter Thirteen

### Text 2

*sattvād dharmo bhaved vṛddhāt puṁso mad-bhakti-lakṣaṇaḥ*  
*sāttvikopāsayā sattva tato dharmaḥ pravartate*

**Перевод:**

**From an increase in** ***sattva,*** ***dharma*****, characterized by secondary** ***bhakti*** **to me, becomes prominent. One can strengthen** ***sattva*** **by cultivation of** ***sattvika*** **items. From that** ***sattva, dharma*** **arises.**

**Комментарий:**

Having attained association with devotees as was previously mentioned, dharma characterized by bhakti increases by sattva. It is like a special campaka seed planted in the form of a garland. By sprinkling with milk it grows with strength.

### Text 3

*dharmo rajas tamo hanyāt sattva-vṛddhir anuttamaḥ*  
*āśu naśyati tan-mūlo hy adharma ubhaye hate*

**Перевод:**

***Dharma,*** **strengthened by** ***sattva,*** **destroys the influence of** ***rajas*** **and** ***tamas.*** **When** ***rajas*** **and** ***tamas*** **are destroyed,** ***adharma,*** **caused by them, is quickly vanquished.**

**Комментарий:**

Sattva and dharma mutually increase each other.

### Text 5

*tat tat sāttvikam evaiṣāṁ yad yad vṛddhāḥ pracakṣate*  
*nindanti tāmasaṁ tat tad rājasaṁ tad-upekṣitam*

**Перевод:**

**Among the ten items, the great sages have praised and recommended those that are in** ***sattva.*** **They have rejected those in** ***tamas*** **and show indifference for those in** ***rajas.***

**Комментарий:**

The sages are persons like Vyāsa. The good and bad aspects of sattva and other guṇas are shown in Padma Purāṇa.

### Text 6

*sāttvikāny eva seveta pumān sattva-vivṛddhaye*  
*tato dharmas tato jñāna yāvat smṛtir apohanam*

**Перевод:**

**Until one realizes** ***ātmā*** **and destroys the** ***guṇas*** **and the gross and subtle bodies, one must use** ***sattvika*** **items to increase** ***sattva,*** **which increases** ***dharma*** **and then gives rise to** ***jñāna.***

**Комментарий:**

By cultivating sattva, jñāna manifests. One should serve items of sattva to develop realization of ātmā.

### Text 8

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*vidanti martyāḥ prāyeṇa viṣayān padam āpadām*  
*tathāpi bhuñjate kṛṣṇa tat kathaṁ śva-kharāja-vat*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O Kṛṣṇa! Generally human beings know that material life brings great future unhappiness, and still they try to enjoy material life. How can a person in knowledge enjoy just like a dog, an ass or a goat?**

**Комментарий:**

Though they know, why do they enjoy like dogs who do not know? Those who do not know are the same as dogs and enjoy. They know that material objects are the fixed source (*padam*) of future suffering (*āpadam*). This is described in verse 11.

The dog after enjoying sex becomes devoid of a relationship. The donkey, after enjoying a handful of grass shown by the washer man, carries a heavy load. The goat, after enjoying various things constantly, has his head cut off. These animals do not know these results.

### Text 9-10

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*aham ity anyathā-buddhiḥ pramattasya yathā hṛdi*  
*utsarpati rajo ghoraṁ tato vaikārikaṁ manaḥ*  
*rajo-yuktasya manasaḥ saṅkalpaḥ sa-vikalpakaḥ*  
*tataḥ kāmo guṇa-dhyānād duḥsahaḥ syād dhi durmateḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: When the inattentive person mistakenly thinks in his mind that he is the body, terrible** ***rajas*** **overcomes the sattvika mind. The mind in** ***rajas*** **then decides that certain objects are enjoyable and concentrates on them. Then uncontrollable desire arises in the foolish person from absorbing himself in the qualities of the desired object.**

**Комментарий:**

The person loses discriminatory power by particular karmas. When he thinks that the body is the ātmā (*anyathā buddhiḥ*) and that thinking enters the heart, rajas enters and overcomes the sattvika mind. The mind becomes difficult to control. The result is then described.

### Text 11

*karoti kāma-vaśa-gaḥ karmāṇy avijitendriyaḥ*  
*duḥkhodarkāṇi sampaśyan rajo-vega-vimohitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**One who does not control the material senses comes under the control of material desires, and, bewildered by the strong push of** ***rajas,*** **performs material activities, although clearly understanding that the result will be future unhappiness.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he knows (*saṁpaśyan*) that the result will be suffering he performs the actions.

### Text 14

*etāvān yoga ādiṣṭo mac-chiṣyaiḥ sanakādibhiḥ*  
*sarvato mana ākṛṣya mayy addhāveśyate yathā*

**Перевод:**

**This** ***yoga*** **system was taught by my devotees, headed by Sanaka. Having withdrawn the mind from all other objects, one should directly and appropriately absorb it in me.**

**Комментарий:**

*Addhā* means directly.

### Text 15

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*yadā tvaṁ sanakādibhyo yena rūpeṇa keśava*  
*yogam ādiṣṭavān etad rūpam icchāmi veditum*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O Keśava! I desire to know when and in what form did you instruct the science of** ***yoga*** **to Sanaka and his brothers.**

**Комментарий:**

I desire to know the teachings (*rūpam*) when you, the form of parabrahman in human form, the avatārī, taking the form of an avatāra (*yena rūpeṇa*), gave instructions.

### Text 18

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*evaṁ pṛṣṭo mahā-devaḥ svayambhūr bhūta-bhāvanaḥ*  
*dhyāyamānaḥ praśna-bījaṁ nābhyapadyata karma-dhīḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: On being asked, Brahmā, who was born directly from the body of the Lord, who is the creator of all living entities within the material world, and who was the best of the** ***devatās,*** **could not understand the nature of** ***ātmā*** **after considering the matter because his mind was absorbed in creation of the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord gave Brahmā benedictions:

*yāvān ahaṁ yathā-bhāvo yad-rūpa-guṇa-karmakaḥ \|*  
*tathaiva tattva-vijñānam astu te mad-anugrahāt \|\|*

**By my mercy, may you attain perfect realization of whatever dimensions, intentions, forms, qualities and pastimes I manifest. (SB 2.9.32)**

*etan mataṁ samātiṣṭha parameṇa samādhinā \|*  
*bhavān kalpa-vikalpeṣu na vimuhyati karhicit \|\|*

**Follow my instructions in detail, with extreme concentration. You will not be bewildered at any time during your lifetime and its subdivisions. (SB 2.9.37)**

*ṛṣim ādyaṁ na badhnāti pāpīyāṁs tvāṁ rajo-guṇaḥ*  
*yan mano mayi nirbaddhaṁ prajāḥ saṁsṛjato ’pi te*

**Since your mind will be absorbed in me, though you will create the offspring, you, a great sage, will not be bound by** ***rajoguṇa.*** **(SB 3.9.35)**

The benediction was realized by Brahmā:

*na bhāratī me ’ṅga mṛṣopalakṣyate*  
*na vai kvacin me manaso mṛṣā gatiḥ \|*  
*na me hṛṣīkāṇi patanty asat-pathe*  
*yan me hṛdautkaṇṭhyavatā dhṛto hariḥ \|\|*

**O Nārada! My words are never false. The working of the mind is never false. My senses do not fall onto the wrong path. This is because I hold the Lord in my heart, filled great zeal. (SB 2.6.34)**

The Kumāras had also spoken to the Lord:

*yo ’ntarhito hṛdi gato ’pi durātmanāṁ tvaṁ*  
*so ’dyaiva no nayana-mūlam ananta rāddhaḥ*  
*yarhy eva karṇa-vivareṇa guhāṁ gato naḥ*  
*pitrānuvarṇita-rahā bhavad-udbhavena*

**O lord of unlimited qualities! He who resides in the heart, invisible to the sinful, today has been seen by our eyes. When your secret nature was described previously by Brahmā who was born from you, it entered our intelligence through the ears. (SB 3.15.46)**

Still Brahmā could not understand ātmā, because he was preoccupied with activity. This was the will of the Lord to reveal the Lord’s greatness, just as the powers of Vāyu and others were stopped in the story told in the teachings of Haṁsa.

### Text 19

*sa mām acintayad devaḥ praśna-pāra-titīrṣayā*  
*tasyāhaṁ haṁsa-rūpeṇa sakāśam agamaṁ tadā*

**Перевод:**

**Lord Brahmā, desiring the answer to the question, fixed his mind on me. At that time, in my form of Haṁsa, I became visible to Lord Brahmā.**

**Комментарий:**

I appeared in the form of Haṁsa.

### Text 20

*dṛṣṭvā mām ta upavrajya kṛtva pādābhivandanam*  
*brahmāṇam agrataḥ kṛtvā papracchuḥ ko bhavān iti*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing me, the sages, placing Brahmā in the lead, came forward and worshiped my lotus feet. Then they asked, “Who are you?”**

**Комментарий:**

Since they offered respects, their question was not out of ignorance of the Lord but to know his intention.

### Text 21

*ity ahaṁ munibhiḥ pṛṣṭas tattva-jijñāsubhis tadā*  
*yad avocam ahaṁ tebhyas tad uddhava nibodha me*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! The sages, desiring to know the goal of** ***yoga,*** **thus inquired from me who I was. Now please hear as I, master of those with false identity, explain what I spoke to them.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus they are described as inquisitive to know the truth (*tattva-jijñāsubhiḥ*).

### Text 22

*vastuno yady anānātva ātmanaḥ praśna īdṛśaḥ*  
*kathaṁ ghaṭeta vo viprā vaktur vā me ka āśrayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O** ***brāhmaṇas*****! If, when asking me who I am, you believe that I am also a** ***jīva,*** **this question cannot occur if there is no plurality of** ***ātmās*** **in the absolute. I would have to answer in terms of plurality of qualities and type.**

**Комментарий:**

Did you ask who I was, understanding that I was a jīva? Or that I was a material body? Or that I was the supreme Lord? He criticizes the question if they think he is a jīva. If the absolute *(vastunaḥ*) has no variety of jīvas (*ātmanaḥ*), it is improper to make distinctions of particular ātmās. How could you ask such a question? *Yadi* (if) indicates certainty. Therefore, O brāhmaṇas, who is the shelter of me, the speaker, and you, the questioners? Who or what is the source which produces your particular identities as brāhmaṇas etc.? I should answer that.

**Paramātmā Sandarbha 34:**

In this statement Haṁsa, taking the role of a regular jīva, takes the jīvas as being only one entity, imitating a common jñānī guru from a material viewpoint. Though the jīvas are all separate aṁśas, not considering this, he speaks in terms of one jīva, suitable for jñāna, for the Kumāras who desire jñāna.

### Text 23

*pañcātmakeṣu bhūteṣu samāneṣu ca vastutaḥ*  
*ko bhavān iti vaḥ praśno vācārambho hy anarthakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**If you ask “Who are you?” in terms of the five elements, which are actually one entity spread everywhere, your question should still not be asked. My use of words, following your example, is also meaningless.**

**Комментарий:**

He responds if they think he is a material body. Thinking in terms of the absolute (*vastutaḥ*), asking “Who are you?” is meaningless, since you think in terms of the five material elements making up the bodies. If you consider that there is oneness of all bodies, just as all ātmās are one by being similar in nature, the question is still meaningless. “But even the wise speak in this way. You also spoke of us brāhmaṇas and yourself.” This speaking was done to remove these misconceptions (*vācārambhaḥ*). If you like me know the truth, then why ask the truth?

### Text 24

*manasā vacasā dṛṣṭyā gṛhyate ’nyair apīndriyaiḥ*  
*aham eva na matto ’nyad iti budhyadhvam añjasā*

**Перевод:**

**Within this world, whatever is perceived by the mind, speech, eyes or other senses is me alone and nothing besides me. All of you please understand this as it is.**

**Комментарий:**

If you think I am the Lord, this is the response. Whatever is perceived by the mind and senses is only me, since there is nothing other than me, the supreme cause. Without me, nothing exists. Thus the question cannot be asked.

### Text 25

*guṇeṣv āviśate ceto guṇāś cetasi ca prajāḥ*  
*jīvasya deha ubhayaṁ guṇāś ceto mad-ātmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear sons! The mind has a natural proclivity to enter into the sense objects, and similarly the sense objects enter into the mind; but both this material mind and the sense objects are merely designations that cover the spirit soul, related to Paramātmā.**

**Комментарий:**

“If that is so, the senses and mind mutual adhere and remain in that state, joined together. What happens to the jīva? Our question has produced more questions.” The Lord shows the unnatural relationship between the jīva and the senses and mind.

The senses and mind are real. But their relationship with the jīva is due only the covering of the body. This has a relationship with the jīva which is my aṁśa (*mad-ātmanaḥ*). Thus it is not related to me. Just as there is no natural relationship of the clouds arising from the effects of the sun, with the sun’s rays, aṁśas of the sun, and the sun remains far away, so the jīvas, my aṁśas, are related to me.

### Text 26

*guṇeṣu cāviśac cittam abhīkṣṇaṁ guṇa-sevayā*  
*guṇāś ca citta-prabhavā mad-rūpa ubhayaṁ tyajet*

**Перевод:**

**The consciousness remains forever in the sense objects by continual service to them. The sense objects remain strongly in the consciousness. One who absorbs himself in me can give up both.**

**Комментарий:**

The jīva cannot reject the sense objects by his own power. He does this by a portion of the Lord’s śakti obtained by worship, considering himself non-different from the Lord. Absorbed in thoughts of non-difference from me (mad-*rūpaḥ*), which is described in the methods of jñāna, one can give up the sense objects. It can also mean worship through bhakti, in which he meditates on my form.

### Text 27

*jāgrat svapnaḥ suṣuptaṁ ca guṇato buddhi-vṛttayaḥ*  
*tāsāṁ vilakṣaṇo jīvaḥ sākṣitvena viniścitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Waking, sleeping and deep sleep, the three functions of the intelligence, are caused by the three** ***guṇas*****. The** ***jīva is*** **ascertained to be different from these three states since it is only the witness of them.**

**Комментарий:**

The jīva does not have an inherent relationship with the guṇas etc.

### Text 28

*yarhi saṁsṛti-bandho ’yam ātmano guṇa-vṛtti-daḥ*  
*mayi turye sthito jahyāt tyāgas tad guṇa-cetasām*

**Перевод:**

**When bondage in** ***saṁsāra*** **or identity with the body occurs, it produces the influence of the sense objects. When one gives up** ***saṁsāra*** **by concentration on me, one gives up sense objects and material consciousness completely.**

**Комментарий:**

The inability of the jīva to disengage on his own is confirmed. The Lord is identified with the fourth state (*mayi turye*).

*virāṭ hiraṇyagarbhaś ca kāraṇaṁ cety upādhayaḥ*  
*īśasya yat tribhir hīnaṁ turīyaṁ tat padaṁ viduḥ*

**When the Lord is devoid of the three forms of Kṣīrodakaśāyī, Garbhodakaśāyī and Karaṇodakaśāyī, he is known as the fourth form (Vāsudeva). Śrīdhara Svāmī commentary on (SB 11.15.16)**

The answer to the main question is given. The unconscious sense objects and the jīva mutually reject each other by concentration on the Lord.

### Text 29

*ahaṅkāra-kṛtaṁ bandham ātmano ’rtha-viparyayam*  
*vidvān nirvidya saṁsāra- cintāṁ turye sthitas tyajet*

**Перевод:**

**The false identity with the body produces bondage and obstacles to the** ***ātmā.*** **Therefore, an intelligent person, by being situated in the Lord, gives up fear of** ***saṁsāra.***

**Комментарий:**

Again he teaches rejection of the body etc. One who is situated in the Lord (*turye*) gives up thoughts of saṁsāra.

### Text 33

*evaṁ vimṛśya guṇato manasas try-avasthā*  
*man-māyayā mayi kṛtā iti niścitārthāḥ*  
*sañchidya hārdam anumāna-sad-ukti-tīkṣṇa*  
*jñānāsinā bhajata mākhila-saṁśayādhim*

**Перевод:**

**Considering that the three states of the intelligence arising from the** ***guṇas*** **are created by my** ***avidyā*** **within me, being firmly convinced of your nature as** ***ātmā,*** **and cutting the three states by the sharp sword of knowledge, by inference and by scriptural statements, worship me, the destroyer of all doubts.**

**Комментарий:**

It was previously stated:

*tasmāt tvam uddhavotsṛjya codanāṁ praticodanām*  
*pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca śrotavyaṁ śrutam eva ca*  
*mām ekam eva śaraṇam ātmānaṁ sarva-dehinām*  
*yāhi sarvātma-bhāvena mayā syā hy akuto-bhayaḥ*

**O Uddhava! Give up duties and forbidden acts, the path of enjoyment and the path of renunciation, desire to hear more about** ***dharma,*** **and what you have already heard about** ***dharma.*** **Surrender to me alone, the soul of all beings, using all methods, with** ***bhāva*** **in your mind. You will be fearless by my mercy. (SB 11.12.14-15)**

*evaṁ gurūpāsanayaika-bhaktyā*  
*vidyā-kuṭhāreṇa śitena dhīraḥ*  
*vivṛścya jīvāśayam apramattaḥ*  
*sampadya cātmānam atha tyajāstram*

**Thus, by worshipping** ***guru,*** **by the axe of** ***jñāna*** **made sharp by** ***bhakti*** **even in a secondary role, by being steady, destroy the subtle body, and with attention attain Paramātmā. Then give up the weapon of** ***jñāna.*** **(SB 11.12.24)**

This is confirmed by the statement of Haṁsa. Contemplating in this way, you should meditate on me.

### Text 34

*īkṣeta vibhramam idaṁ manaso vilāsaṁ*  
*dṛṣṭaṁ vinaṣṭam ati-lolam alāta-cakram*  
*vijñānam ekam urudheva vibhāti māyā*  
*svapnas tridhā guṇa-visarga-kṛto vikalpaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**One should understand that this world is a misconception, a diversion for the mind, visible but temporary, and flickering like a fire brand. Brahman is one consciousness but manifest as many. The three states arising by the** ***guṇas*** **create various transformations, but these are temporary like a dream.**

**Комментарий:**

The method of producing jñāna is described. One should see the form of the world in which there is a mistake with particulars (*vibhramam*), since it is seen as a composition of mental conceptions. It should be seen as temporary like a pot. It should be seen as continually moving about like a fire brand, since everything is actually the consciousness of Paramātmā. It appears as many by māyā. Māyā is not independent but derives strength from proximity to Paramātmā. Thus the three states produced by transformations of the guṇas are manufactured like a dream. They are manifestations produced by māyā.

### Text 36

*dehaṁ ca naśvaram avasthitam utthitaṁ vā*  
*siddho na paśyati yato ’dhyagamat svarūpam*  
*daivād apetam atha daiva-vaśād upetaṁ*  
*vāso yathā parikṛtaṁ madirā-madāndhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The perfected sage is not aware whether he is seated or standing while situated in the temporary body, since he has realized Brahman. He is like a drunken man who is not aware of receiving, putting on or taking off his clothing.**

**Комментарий:**

The jīvanmukta is described in two verses.

### Text 38

*mayaitad uktaṁ vo viprā guhyaṁ yat sāṅkhya-yogayoḥ*  
*jānīta māgataṁ yajña yuṣmad-dharma-vivakṣayā*

**Перевод:**

**O** ***brāhmaṇas*****! Know that I am Viṣṇu who has come with a desire to teach you** ***dharma.*** **I have spoken the confidential knowledge of Sāṅkhya and** ***aṣṭāṅga-yoga.***

**Комментарий:**

He gives respect to his own words. He reveals himself with a particular purpose. He identifies himself as Viṣṇu (*yajñaḥ*), not identifying Śiva or others as the Supreme Lord. He has taught dharma.

### Text 39

*ahaṁ yogasya sāṅkhyasya satyasyartasya tejasaḥ*  
*parāyaṇaṁ dvija-śreṣṭhāḥ śriyaḥ kīrter damasya ca*

**Перевод:**

**O best of the** ***brāhmaṇas*****! Please know that I am the supreme shelter of the** ***yoga*** **system, analytic philosophy, seeing equally, speaking pleasantly, influence, beauty, fame and self-control.**

**Комментарий:**

He shows that knowing him, everything becomes known and that he is the most excellent.

### Text 40

*māṁ bhajanti guṇāḥ sarve nirguṇaṁ nirapekṣakam*  
*suhṛdaṁ priyam ātmānaṁ sāmyāsaṅgādayo ’guṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All superior qualities, which are eternal, such as equality to all beings and attachment to my devotee, reside in me. I am beyond the material** ***guṇas,*** **not dependent on material qualities, and am the devotees’ friend, giving love to them.**

**Комментарий:**

He teaches knowledge of himself. Those who are not affected by the guṇas (*aguṇāḥ*), who have unlimited qualities such as equality and attachment to devotees (*sāmyāsaṅgādayaḥ*), described in the earth’s statements in the First Canto, worship me since I am the shelter of all beings (*ātmānam*) and thus most excellent. How could they worship anyone else? Because he has this nature, he is beyond the guṇas, not bound to the guṇas like the jīvas by ignorance. By his will, he is not bound up *(nirapekṣakam*). Since they are also beyond the guṇas, they do not worship anyone except me. Being of this nature, I am give benefit to everyone, without motivation (*suhṛdam*) and the abode of unconditional prema for all beings. It is thus proper that such qualities reside in me. The goal is prema bhakti for me, the most excellent being.

### Text 41

*iti me chinna-sandehā munayaḥ sanakādayaḥ*  
*sabhājayitvā parayā bhaktyāgṛṇata saṁstavaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus all of the doubts of the sages headed by Sanaka were destroyed by my words. Worshiping me with transcendental devotion, they chanted my glories with excellent hymns.**

**Комментарий:**

They gave up their doubts and attained bhakti to me. They worshipped me with prema bhakti (*parayā bhaktyā*).

## Chapter Fourteen

### Text 1

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*vadanti kṛṣṇa śreyāṁsi bahūni brahma-vādinaḥ*  
*teṣāṁ vikalpa-prādhānyam utāho eka-mukhyatā*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O Kṛṣṇa! The learned sages recommend various excellent** ***sādhanas*** **for perfecting one’s life. Among them are some superior? Is one among them the best?**

**Комментарий:**

Previously, bhakti was said to be the practice, without considering other processes. (SB 11.12.14) Uddhava inquires in order to confirm this, rejecting other opinions.

### Text 2

*bhavatodāhṛtaḥ svāmin bhakti-yogo ’napekṣitaḥ*  
*nirasya sarvataḥ saṅgaṁ yena tvayy āviśen manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! You have explained the process of unalloyed** ***bhakti*****, by which a devotee removes all material association from his life and is able to fix his mind on you.**

**Комментарий:**

He rejects dependence on other results (*nirasya*).

### Text 3

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*kālena naṣṭā pralaye vāṇīyaṁ veda-saṁjñitā*  
*mayādau brahmaṇe proktā dharmo yasyāṁ mad-ātmakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: By the influence of time, the Vedic knowledge was lost at the time of annihilation. Therefore, when the subsequent creation took place, I spoke to Brahmā the Vedic knowledge in which** ***bhakti*** **is the essence.**

**Комментарий:**

The Vedas were lost by time, at the pralaya, at the end of the kalpa. The variety of the Vedas was lost. The Vedas (*iyam*) explained what you have just explained to me. Results other than absorption in me, such as jñāna or bhakti mixed with jñāna are not what I explained. At the beginning of Brahmā’s first day (*ādau*) the message, in which there is dharma arising from my svarūpa (*mad-ātmakaḥ*)—since it is the essence of hlādinī--was spoken by me to Brahmā.

### Text 5-7

*tebhyaḥ pitṛbhyas tat-putrā deva-dānava-guhyakāḥ*  
*manuṣyāḥ siddha-gandharvāḥ sa-vidyādhara-cāraṇāḥ*  
*kindevāḥ kinnarā nāgā rakṣaḥ-kimpuruṣādayaḥ*  
*bahvyas teṣāṁ prakṛtayo rajaḥ-sattva-tamo-bhuvaḥ*  
*yābhir bhūtāni bhidyante bhūtānāṁ patayas tathā*  
*yathā-prakṛti sarveṣāṁ citrā vācaḥ sravanti hi*

**Перевод:**

**From the forefathers headed by Bhṛgu and other sons of Brahmā appeared many children and descendants, who assumed different forms as** ***devatās*****, demons, human beings, Guhyakas, Siddhas, Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Cāraṇas, Kindevas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, Kimpuruṣas, and so on. All of the many species, along with their respective leaders, appeared with different desires generated from the three modes of material nature. Therefore, because of the different characteristics of the living entities within the universe, there are many explanations of the meaning of the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

From the sons of Brahmā (*pitṛbhyah*) and others (*tebhyaḥ*) many descendants appeared.

### Text 10

*dharmam eke yaśaś cānye kāmaṁ satyaṁ damaṁ śamam*  
*anye vadanti svārthaṁ vā aiśvaryaṁ tyāga-bhojanam*  
*kecid yajñaṁ tapo dānaṁ vratāni niyamān yamān*

**Перевод:**

**Various people claim various paths:** ***karma-mīmāṁsa*****, fame, sense enjoyment, truthfulness, control of the senses, control of the mind, wealth for one’s own use, renunciation, eating, sacrifice, penance, charity, vows,** ***niyamas*** **or** ***yamas.***

**Комментарий:**

Since they did not accept the Lord, persons like Jaimini propagated other ideas. Some taught sva-dharma composed of nitya and naimittika rules. Advaita-yogīs, giving up karma, teach truth, sama and dama. Some, dedicated to karma, teach gain for the self (*svārtham*), with a method and result, but all for the self. In that, some teach enjoyment, wealth, and renunciation (for their gain). The rest of the list are methods.

### Text 11

*ādy-anta-vanta evaiṣāṁ lokāḥ karma-vinirmitāḥ*  
*duḥkhodarkās tamo-niṣṭhāḥ kṣudrā mandāḥ śucārpitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The results of all the processes mentioned are meager, weak, have a beginning and end, are produced by** ***karma,*** **are full of lamentation and end in misery and bewilderment.**

**Комментарий:**

Among them those that act by Vedic rules of action and produce happiness as a result *(lokāḥ*), have a beginning and end. Those which are against the Vedas produce hell.

### Text 12

*mayy arpitātmanaḥ sabhya nirapekṣasya sarvataḥ*  
*mayātmanā sukhaṁ yat tat kutaḥ syād viṣayātmanām*

**Перевод:**

**O learned Uddhava! Those who fix their consciousness on me, giving up all material desires, attain happiness because of me. This cannot possibly be experienced by those engaged in sense gratification.**

**Комментарий:**

They attain happiness by me, the Paramātmā, the dearest form, having eternity, knowledge and bliss (*ātmanā*), by me (*mayā*), manifesting my form with most astonishing form and qualities. How can this happen for those who desire goals other than me (*viṣayātmanām*)?

### Text 13

*akiñcanasya dāntasya śāntasya sama-cetasaḥ*  
*mayā santuṣṭa-manasaḥ sarvāḥ sukha-mayā diśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**One who does not desire anything within this world, who has controlled his senses, who has fixed his intelligence on me, who regards heaven and hell equally, and whose mind is completely satisfied in me finds only happiness wherever he goes.**

**Комментарий:**

He shows the greatness of happiness from experiencing the Lord in two verses.

### Text 14

*na pārameṣṭhyaṁ na mahendra-dhiṣṇyaṁ*  
*na sārvabhaumaṁ na rasādhipatyam*  
*na yoga-siddhīr apunar-bhavaṁ vā*  
*mayy arpitātmecchati mad vinānyat*

**Перевод:**

**One who has fixed his consciousness on me desires neither the position or abode of Brahmā or Indra, nor an empire on the earth, nor sovereignty in the lower planetary systems, nor the eightfold perfection of** ***yoga*****, nor liberation. Such a person desires me alone.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 132:**

Bhakti is the cause of good qualities like jñāna and vairāgya.

*yasyāsti bhaktir bhagavaty akiñcanā*  
*sarvair guṇais tatra samāsate surāḥ*  
*harāv abhaktasya kuto mahad-guṇā*  
*manorathenāsati dhāvato bahiḥ*

**The devatās constantly dwell with all good qualities in that person who has pure bhakti for the Lord. There are no good qualities in the non-devotee who chases after temporary material objects with desire for material pleasure. (SB 5.18.12)**

*yat karmabhir yat tapasā jñāna-vairāgyataś ca yat*  
*yogena dāna-dharmeṇa śreyobhir itarair api*  
*sarvaṁ mad-bhakti-yogena mad-bhakto labhate ’ñjasā*  
*svargāpavargaṁ mad-dhāma kathañcid yadi vāñchati*

**Everything that can be achieved by karma, penance, jñāna, vairāgya, mystic yoga, charity, dharma and all other auspicious means of perfecting life is easily achieved by my devotee through bhakti. If somehow or other my devotee desires Svarga, liberation, or residence in my abode, he easily achieves such benedictions. (SB 11.20.32-33)**

Since bhakti gives the highest happiness by its nature, it makes all practice and results of karma, jñāna and other sādhanas detestable.

*Rasādhipatyam* means ruling the lower planets. *Apunar bhavam* is personal liberation. The devotee who has offered his ātmā to me does not desire any object produced in these places. He desires me, the result of sādhana-bhakti, greater than all puruṣārthas.

### Text 15

*na tathā me priyatama ātma-yonir na śaṅkaraḥ*  
*na ca saṅkarṣaṇo na śrīr naivātmā ca yathā bhavān*

**Перевод:**

**Neither Brahmā, Śiva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, the goddess of fortune nor even my deity are as dear to me as you are.**

**Комментарий:**

Using Uddhava as an example, he shows the excellence of bhakti. Brahmā was a son. Śiva was an assistant, giving happiness (*sam*). Saṅkarṣaṇa was a brother, who was taken from the womb. Śrī was his wife, a shelter of great beauty. Ātma refers to the deity form. They are not pleasing because they are my son, assistant, brother or wife. They are pleasing because of their bhakti. They are not as dear as you, since you have greater bhakti. This shows his great affection for the devotee.

### Text 16

*nirapekṣaṁ muniṁ śāntaṁ nirvairaṁ sama-darśanam*  
*anuvrajāmy ahaṁ nityaṁ pūyeyety aṅghri-reṇubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I always follow the footsteps of my pure devotees, who are free from all personal desire, are rapt in thought of my pastimes, are fixed in me, without any feelings of enmity, and are equal to all conditions of the world. Let me be purified by the dust from their feet!**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised such devotees, objects of his special prema, he praises special devotees, objects of his special respect. *Nirapekṣam* means a devotee with no desires except for the Lord. This devotee is without agitation (*śāntam).* Thus he has no enemies anywhere. He is devoid of thinking of objects as good or bad (*sama-darśanam*). I follow a devotee such as Nārada, because by such good conduct filled with pure bhakti, I develop excellent bhakti for him. How can it be hidden? I should be purified by the dust from their feet. I will be purified from the fault of not responding fully to his bhakti.

### Text 18

*bādhyamāno ’pi mad-bhakto viṣayair ajitendriyaḥ*  
*prāyaḥ pragalbhayā bhaktyā viṣayair nābhibhūyate*

**Перевод:**

**If my devotee has not fully conquered his senses, he may be harassed by material desires, but because of his generally strong** ***bhakti*****, he will not be defeated by sense gratification.**

**Комментарий:**

He is generally not defeated by enjoyment since the Lord is touched by his humble requests to the Lord to interfere. The Lord intervenes because of the great ability of bhakti, composed of full surrender.

### Text 19

*yathāgniḥ su-samṛddhārciḥ karoty edhāṁsi bhasmasāt*  
*tathā mad-viṣayā bhaktir uddhavaināṁsi kṛtsnaśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! Just as a blazing fire turns firewood into ashes, similarly, devotion to me completely burns to ashes sins committed by my devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

He praises all the types of devotees in eight verses. Bhakti with hearing burns all sins to ashes completely.

**Bhakti Sandarbha 125:**

It is also said:

*yathāgniḥ su-samṛddhārciḥ karoty edhāṁsi bhasmasāt \|*  
*pāpāni bhagavad-bhaktis tathā dahati tat-kṣaṇāt \|\|*

**Just as fire turns wood to ashes, bhakti to the Lord burns up sins immediately. (Padma Purāṇa 5.85.31)**

*patitaḥ skhalito bhagnaḥ sandaṣṭas tapta āhataḥ*  
*harir ity avaśenāha pumān nārhati yātanāḥ*

**A person who chants the name of the Lord while falling from a cliff, stumbling on the road, receiving injury his body, being bitten by snakes, tormented with fever or being attacked with sticks will not suffer hellish punishment. (SB 6.2.15)**

Though the potential mood or imperative mood is not used in the verb, the statement can still be regarded as an injunction similar to the statement *pūṣāpraviṣṭa-bhāgo yad āgneyāṣṭā-kapālo bhavati*: the portion of Pūṣā should be divided into eight portions of Agni. This statement is also not expressed as an injunction but acts as such.

Direct injunctions are also given:

*tasmād bhārata sarvātmā bhagavān īśvaro hariḥ \|*  
*śrotavyaḥ kīrtitavyaś ca smartavyaś cecchatābhayam \|\|*

**The Lord who is Paramātmā, Bhagavān and Lord of power, should be heard about, glorified and remembered by those desiring freedom from fear. (SB 2.1.5)**

The word *tasmāt* indicates a reason and thus indicates the fault of not hearing and glorifying the Lord. Just as fire burns by its nature, bhakti also manifests effect without dependence on rules.

*yān āsthāya naro rājan na pramādyeta karhicit*  
*dhāvan nimīlya vā netre na skhalen na pated iha*

**O King! One who accepts this process of devotional service will never be affected by pride. Even while running with eyes closed, he will never trip or fall. (SB 11.2.35)**

The word *su-samṛddhārciḥ* (blazing fire) in the Padma Purāṇa quotation refutes the notions that bhakti is dependent on other sādhana, that it is hard to perfect, and that its results are slow. Thus Padma Purāṇa says the effect is immediate (*tat-kṣaṇāt*).

### Text 20

*na sādhayati māṁ yogo na sāṅkhyaṁ dharma uddhava*  
*na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo yathā bhaktir mamorjitā*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! I am attained by unmixed** ***bhakti.*** **I cannot be attained by mystic** ***yoga*****, Sāṅkhya philosophy,** ***dharma,*** **Vedic study, jñāna or sannyāsa.**

**Комментарий:**

Yoga etc. do not control me (*na* *sādhayati*) or draw my attention as much as strong sādhana-bhakti, unmixed with jñāna or karma.

### Text 21

*bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ śraddhayātmā priyaḥ satām*  
*bhaktiḥ punāti man-niṣṭhā śva-pākān api sambhavāt*

**Перевод:**

**Only by** ***bhakti*** **with full faith can the devotees obtain me, Paramātmā, the object of love.** ***Bhakti*** **fixed in me purifies even a dog eater of his low birth.**

**Комментарий:**

I am attained, and gradually controlled by pure bhakti, preceded by faith. That bhakti is fixed firmly in me (*man-niṣṭhā*).

### Text 22

*dharmaḥ satya-dayopeto vidyā vā tapasānvitā*  
*mad-bhaktyāpetam ātmānaṁ na samyak prapunāti hi*

**Перевод:**

**Neither** ***dharma*** **endowed with honesty and mercy nor knowledge obtained with great penance can completely purify one’s consciousness if they are bereft of loving service to me.**

**Комментарий:**

Dharma without desire and brahma-jñāna according to scriptures (*vidyā*) endowed with concentration of mind (*tapasā*) cannot purify the mind devoid of bhakti—desire to please me (*mad-bhaktyā*)-- of desires for material enjoyment and liberation.

### Text 23

*kathaṁ vinā roma-harṣaṁ dravatā cetasā vinā*  
*vinānandāśru-kalayā śudhyed bhaktyā vināśayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Without** ***bhakti*** **how can the heart melt? Without melting of the heart, how can one’s hairs stand on end and tears come to the eyes? Without hair standing on end and tears in the eyes how can the consciousness become purified?**

**Комментарий:**

This is a statement in the negative. Hairs standing on end is a sign of melting of the heart. Tears of bliss are special signs of the melted heart. Melting of the heart is the interior or essential nature of bhakti. Without those signs, how can one understand the heart has melted? Without the melted heart, how could bhakti appear? Without bhakti how could the heart be purified?

### Text 24

*vāg gadgadā dravate yasya cittaṁ*  
*rudaty abhīkṣṇaṁ hasati kvacic ca*  
*vilajja udgāyati nṛtyate ca*  
*mad-bhakti-yukto bhuvanaṁ punāti*

**Перевод:**

**A devotee whose speech is choked up, whose heart is melted, who cries continually and sometimes laughs, sometimes feels ashamed, sometimes sings loudly and sometimes dances—a devotee thus fixed in loving service to me purifies the entire universe.**

**Комментарий:**

A person endowed with bhakti, if he is the object of my prema, purifies the world, what to speak of his own heart, his associates, his village, his state, his country, continent and the whole Jambudvīpa.

### Text 25

*yathāgninā hema malaṁ jahāti*  
*dhmātaṁ punaḥ svaṁ bhajate ca rūpam*  
*ātmā ca karmānuśayaṁ vidhūya*  
*mad-bhakti-yogena bhajaty atho mām*

**Перевод:**

**Just as gold, when smelted in fire, gives up its impurities and attains its pure state, similarly the** ***ātmā*** **becomes purified of all contamination caused by impressions of** ***karma*** **by** ***bhakti-yoga*** **and then serves me directly.**

**Комментарий:**
