Internal cleanliness, external cleanliness, chanting the holy names of the Lord, austerity, sacrifice, faith, hospitality, worship of me, visiting holy places, acting and desiring only for the supreme interest, satisfaction, and service to** ***guru*** **are the twelve** ***niyamas.*** **These twenty-four elements bestow all desired benedictions upon those persons who devotedly cultivate them.**

**Комментарий:**

Yamas and niyamas both are twelve in number (*ubhayoḥ*).

### Text 36

*śamo man-niṣṭhatā buddher dama indriya-saṁyamaḥ*  
*titikṣā duḥkha-sammarṣo jihvopastha-jayo dhṛtiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Absorbing the intelligence in me constitutes** ***śama*****, and complete discipline of the senses is** ***dama.*** **Tolerance means patiently enduring suffering, and steadfastness means conquering the tongue and genitals.**

**Комментарий:**

Śama means steadiness of the antaḥkaraṇa. I consider the yamas to be rules related to the senses which are dependent on the antaḥkaraṇa.

### Text 37

*daṇḍa-nyāsaḥ paraṁ dānaṁ kāma-tyāgas tapaḥ smṛtam*  
*svabhāva-vijayaḥ śauryaṁ satyaṁ ca sama-darśanam*

**Перевод:**

**Supreme charity is to give up aggression toward others and real austerity is renunciation of enjoyment. Real heroism is to conquer one’s natural tendency to enjoy material life and truth is seeing all beings as one’s self in happiness or distress.**

**Комментарий:**

*Sama-darśanam* is according to the following:

*nārāyaṇa-parāḥ sarve na kutaścana bibhyati*  
*svargāpavarga-narakeṣv api tulyārtha-darśinaḥ*

**Devotees solely engaged in the service of Nārāyaṇa never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation and the hellish planets are all the same. (SB 6.17.28)**

### Text 39

*dharma iṣṭaṁ dhanaṁ nṝṇāṁ yajño ’haṁ bhagavattamaḥ*  
*dakṣiṇā jñāna-sandeśaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ paraṁ balam*

**Перевод:**

**The respectable wealth for human beings is possessing** ***dharma,*** **and I, Svayam Bhagavān, am sacrifice. Religious remuneration (*****dakṣiṇā*****) is informing friends after a festival of one’s realization of bliss, and the greatest strength is the** ***prāṇāyāma*** **system.**

**Комментарий:**

The best gift one can receive is obtaining instructions of knowledge. The cause of attaining such instructions is one’s great devotion to the ācārya (who consequently gives the instructions). The sponsor of a sacrifice does not give instructions on jñāna, but gives gold etc. Or I Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān (*bhagavattamaḥ*) am sacrifice, since by knowledge of me one attains the results of sacrifice.

*sarve vedāḥ sarva-vidyāḥ sa-śāstrāḥ*  
*sarve yajñāḥ sarva ījyaś ca kṛṣṇaḥ \|*  
*viduḥ kṛṣṇaṁ brāhmaṇās tattvato ye*  
*teṣāṁ rājan sarva-yajñāḥ samāptāḥ \|\|*

**Kṛṣṇa is all the Vedas, all knowledge all scriptures, all sacrifices, all worship. O king! Brāhmaṇas who know Kṛṣṇa in truth have completed all sacrifices. (Mahābhārata)**

The words following the ācārya or concerning performance of the sacrifice according to his order are the gift, since they satisfy the Lord, since they result ultimately in knowledge of him.

### Text 40

*bhago ma aiśvaro bhāvo lābho mad-bhaktir uttamaḥ*  
*vidyātmani bhidā-bādho jugupsā hrīr akarmasu*

**Перевод:**

**Lordship means my controlling power. Gain means gaining** ***bhakti.*** **Knowledge is nullifying what is not** ***ātmā*** **in the** ***jīva.*** **Real modesty is dislike of sinful activities.**

**Комментарий:**

Knowledge means negating ideas that I am a devatā, I am strong, I am young etc. (*bhidā-bādhaḥ*).

### Text 45

*eta uddhava te praśnāḥ sarve sādhu nirūpitāḥ*  
*kiṁ varṇitena bahunā lakṣaṇaṁ guṇa-doṣayoḥ*  
*guṇa-doṣa-dṛśir doṣo guṇas tūbhaya-varjitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus, Uddhava, I have elucidated all of the matters of inquiry, which are suitable for liberation. There is no need for a more elaborate description of good and bad qualities, since to see good and bad is itself a bad quality. The best quality is to transcend seeing good and bad qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

What I have explained in response to your question is not generally so interesting to me. Most interesting are the qualities arising from yama and niyama just described.

The Lord then points out the fault in producing negative results. Why describe more about good and bad qualities? Elaboration comes from discussing unessential matters. By discussion of spiritual matters, the discussion becomes one chief subject. That should be the result of discussing good and bad qualities. Discerning qualities to be cultivated and faults to be avoided is also a fault. It is a good quality to be devoid of seeing good and bad. Transcending seeing good and bad, one cultivates the highest goal naturally, since depending on seeing good and bad is inferior.

## Chapter Twenty

### Text 1

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*vidhiś ca pratiṣedhaś ca nigamo hīśvarasya te*  
*avekṣate ’raviṇḍākṣa guṇaṁ doṣaṁ ca karmaṇām*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa! You are the Supreme Lord, and thus the Vedic literatures, consisting of positive and negative injunctions, constitute your order. Such literatures focus upon the good and bad qualities of work.**

**Комментарий:**

Not knowing the Lord’s intention, he asks to hear more topics in two verses. One sees good qualities as puṇya and bad qualities as sins.

### Text 3

*guṇa-doṣa-bhidā-dṛṣṭim antareṇa vacas tava*  
*niḥśreyasaṁ kathaṁ nṝṇāṁ niṣedha-vidhi-lakṣaṇam*

**Перевод:**

**Without seeing in terms of good and bad in the Vedas, which are your words, composed of orders and prohibitions, how can man achieve liberation?**

**Комментарий:**

Without seeing good and bad, how will orders and prohibitions in karma-kāṇḍa take place and how will liberation take place for men? Or, without your words of orders and prohibitions, how will liberation take place? Or without seeing good and bad, how will your words describing orders and prohibitions produce truth and liberation? All the Vedas use orders and prohibitions to purify the antaḥkaraṇa to attain liberation.

### Text 4

*pitṛ-deva-manuṣyānāṁ vedaś cakṣus taveśvara*  
*śreyas tv anupalabdhe ’rthe sādhya-sādhanayor api*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! Your Vedas are the best cause of knowledge for Pitṛs,** ***devatās*** **and humans. The Vedas are the means and goal of liberation and Svarga.**

**Комментарий:**

The Vedas are the means for and goal of realizing the form and powers of the Lord (*anupalabdhe arthe*).

### Text 5

*guṇa-doṣa-bhidā-dṛṣṭir nigamāt te na hi svataḥ*  
*nigamenāpavādaś ca bhidāyā iti ha bhramaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The distinction observed between piety and sin comes from your own Vedic knowledge and does not arise by itself. By rejecting the Vedas with their injunctions and prohibitions as you seem to be doing now, such distinction between piety and sin will be nullified. I will be bewildered.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing good and bad is prescribed in scriptures. How can one reject the scriptures concerning piety and sin previously described? Seeing good and bad arises from the Vedas, which are your order. It does not arise by itself since if seeing in this way arose on its own, it would be destroyed, subject to argument. Since it arises from the Vedas, by having meaning and purpose, it will not be destroyed. Confusion will clearly (*ha*) arise by that rejection.

Since by attaining meaning confusion is destroyed, by your words of the Vedas, destroy the confusion.

### Text 6

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*yogās trayo mayā proktā nṝṇāṁ śreyo-vidhitsayā*  
*jñānaṁ karma ca bhaktiś ca nopāyo ’nyo ’sti kutracit*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: Because I desire that human beings may achieve perfection, I have presented three methods—the path of** ***jñāna,*** **the path of** ***karma*** **and the path of** ***bhakti*****. Besides these three, there no other means of elevation.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord first teaches three yogas in order to explain non-contradiction by difference in qualification, in the same topic, piety and sin, previously described. There are plentiful descriptions of piety and sin for persons practicing karma. The most elevated person should not see in terms of piety and sin (SB11.19.45).

**Bhakti Sandarbha 170:**

Akiñcana-bhakti is situated in the highest position. To show fixation in a particular qualification, a new section commences.

Rejecting extraneous elements, one should act to create favorability to the Lord. There are three forms of creating favorability: the form of jñāna, resulting in realizing the Lord’s Brahman aspect with no qualities; the form of bhakti, resulting in realizing Bhagavān, with qualities; and the form of offering karmas, a means to achieve the other two forms. These are established as methods of jñāna, bhakti and karma for people of differing qualifications. There are no other methods. *Yogaḥ* means methods. The methods are explained by me, the source of scripture, with the desire that people attain liberation, artha-dharma-kāma, and prema (*śreyaḥ*). Bhakti is distinct from karma.

### Text 7

*nirviṇṇānāṁ jñāna-yogo nyāsinām iha karmasu*  
*teṣv anirviṇṇa-cittānāṁ karma-yogas tu kāminām*

**Перевод:**

***Jñāna-yoga*** **is recommended for those who are unattached to material life and thus reject material activities.** ***Karma-yoga*** **is recommended for those who are not disgusted with material life and have great attachment to pleasures.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 171:**

Two verses explain the causes of qualification. Among the methods (*iha*) jñāna is for people detached from happiness derived from objects in this and the next life (*nirviṇṇām*) and who have renounced actions both worldly and Vedic as sādhana (*nyāsinām*). This indicates persons who have developed desire for liberation by great determination. Jñāna-yoga gives results (*siddhi-daḥ*) for these people with detachment and renunciation. Karma yoga gives results for persons who are attached to happiness in this world and the next and cannot give up actions to attain them (*anirviṇṇa-cetasām*). Results arise according to the determination of the performer.

### Text 8

*yadṛcchayā mat-kathādau jāta-śraddhas tu yaḥ pumān*  
*na nirviṇṇo nāti-sakto bhakti-yogo ’sya siddhi-daḥ*

**Перевод:**

**If by unexpected association with devotees one develops faith in my topics, that person, being neither very disgusted with nor attached to material life, is qualified for** ***bhakti*** **and will achieve perfection.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 171:**

Bhakti does not depend on caste as karma does:

*te vai vidanty atitaranti ca deva-māyāṁ*  
*strī-śūdra-hūṇa-śabarā api pāpa-jīvāḥ \|*  
*yady adbhuta-krama-parāyaṇa-śīla-śikṣās*  
*tiryag-janā api kim u śruta-dhāraṇā ye \|\|*

**Women*****,*** **śūdras, Hūṇas, Śabaras and other sinfully born persons also certainly cross over the material world and know the Lord if they learn about the qualities of the devotees of the Lord. If even animals can understand, how much more quickly can humans, who hear from the mouth of guru, understand the Lord? (SB 2.7.46)**

Its cause is faith alone. That is explained in verse SB 11.20.8 above. Faith arises by auspiciousness arising from the completely independent mercy obtained by associating with devotees (*yadṛcchayā).* It is said:

*śuśrūṣoḥ śraddadhānasya vāsudeva-kathā-ruciḥ \|*  
*syān mahat-sevayā viprāḥ puṇya-tīrtha-niṣevaṇāt \|\|*

**O brāhmaṇas! Attraction for topics concerning Kṛṣṇa will arise by service to the great devotees, followed by faith, by surrender to the feet of the guru*****,*** **and by the desire to hear. (SB 1.2.16)**

### Text 9

*tāvat karmāṇi kurvīta na nirvidyeta yāvatā*  
*mat-kathā-śravaṇādau vā śraddhā yāvan na jāyate*

**Перевод:**

**As long as one does not become detached from daily and periodic duties or has not awakened his faith in hearing topics about me, one must perform one’s prescribed duties of** ***varṇāśrama.***

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 172:**

The commentary says “Karma means nitya and naimittika karmas.”

There is the following objection:

*śruti-smṛtī mamaivājñe yas te ullaṅghya vartate \|*  
*ājñā-cchedī mama dveṣī mad-bhakto ’pi na vaiṣṇavaḥ \|\|*

**Whoever ignores śruti and smṛti, thus disrespecting me, even if he is my devotee, is not a Vaiṣṇava, breaks my order and hates me.**

However, this fault does not apply, since verse (SB 11.20.9) above gives a superior order (one can give up karmas after being fixed in bhakti). Rather one will disobey the Lord’s order if one who has developed detachment from karmas and faith in bhakti still performs those karmas.

*ājñāyaivaṁ guṇān doṣān mayādiṣṭān api svakān*  
*dharmān santyajya yaḥ sarvān māṁ bhajeta sa tu sattamaḥ*

**A person who, understanding good and bad aspects of dharma as taught by me gives up all his duties and simply worships me is the best of all. (SB 11.11.32)**

The commentary says, “He gives up duties because of strong bhakti, by being qualified with detachment. This detachment is indicated by Karabhājana:

*devarṣi-bhūtāpta-nṛṇāṁ pitṝṇāṁ*  
*na kiṅkaro nāyam ṛṇī ca rājan*  
*sarvātmanā yaḥ śaraṇaṁ śaraṇyaṁ*  
*gato mukundaṁ parihṛtya kartam*

**O King! One who has given up all varṇāśrama duties and has taken full shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, who offers shelter to all, is not a debtor to or servant of the devatās, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives or Pitṛs. (SB 11.5.41)”**

The devotee is not a servant of the devatās or sages but a servant of the Lord. Thus he need not perform actions dedicated to them. He gives up duties (*kartam)*. Or he gives up seeing differences: he does not see the devatās as independent. Thus it is said:

*ayaṁ devo munir vandya eṣa brahmā bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*ity ākhyā jāyate tāvad yāvan nārcayate harim \|\|*

**As long as one does not worship Viṣṇu one should offer respects to devatās, sages, Brahmā and Bṛhaspati. (Garuḍa Purāṇa 1.235.20)**

It is not necessary for the devotee to perform atonements for sins since the tendency for sin does not exist in the surrendered person. If a sin sometimes occurs, atonement for the sin occurs as a by-product of remembering the Lord. That is mentioned in a later verse:

*sva-pāda-mūlam bhajataḥ priyasya*  
*tyaktānya-bhāvasya hariḥ pareśaḥ*  
*vikarma yac cotpatitaṁ kathañcid*  
*dhunoti sarvaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭaḥ*

**One who has thus given up all other engagements and has taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Supreme Lord is very dear to the Lord. If such a surrendered soul accidentally commits some sinful activity, the Supreme Lord, great because of his affection for the devotee, seated within everyone’s heart, immediately takes away the reaction to such sin. (SB 11.5.42)**

This person has given up devotion to devatās (*tyaktānya-bhāvasya*). Surrender (*śaraṇa* in SB 11.5.41) means faith since it is described that the person has given up karma. Faith means conviction in the meaning of scriptures. Scripture is a cause of fear for those who have not surrendered and causes no fear in the surrendered. One who has faith surrenders.

### Text 10

*sva-dharma-stho yajan yajñair anāśīḥ-kāma uddhava*  
*na yāti svarga-narakau yady anyan na samācaret*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! A person who is situated in his prescribed duty, properly worshiping by Vedic sacrifices but not desiring the results will not go to the heavenly planets; similarly, by not performing forbidden activities he will not go to hell.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 174:**

Having explained the qualifications for karma, jñāna and bhakti, the Lord then instructs that even karma should lead to worship of the Lord.

Not desiring results is done with the understanding that this is the Lord’s order. In association with jñānīs, one offers the results to the Lord in this way only. In association with devotees, one then strives to satisfy the Lord with the offering.

### Text 11

*asmiḹ loke vartamānaḥ sva-dharma-stho ’naghaḥ śuciḥ*  
*jñānaṁ viśuddham āpnoti mad-bhaktiṁ vā yadṛcchayā*

**Перевод:**

**One who is situated in his prescribed duty, free from sinful activities and cleansed of material contamination, in this very life obtains transcendental knowledge or, by fortune,** ***bhakti*** **to me.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 175:**

By the good fortune of mercy from association of devotees, such a person attains bhakti.

*etāvān eva yajatām iha niḥśreyasodayaḥ \|*  
*bhagavaty acalo bhāvo yad bhāgavata-saṅgataḥ \|\|*

**Auspiciousness arises for the worshippers of devatās if steady devotion for the Lord arises in them from association with devotees. (SB 2.3.11)**

### Text 12

*svargiṇo ’py etam icchanti lokaṁ nirayiṇas tathā*  
*sādhakaṁ jñāna-bhaktibhyām ubhayaṁ tad-asādhakam*

**Перевод:**

**The residents of both heaven and hell desire human birth on the earth planet because human life facilitates** ***jñāna*** **and** ***bhakti,*** **whereas neither heavenly nor hellish bodies provide such opportunities.**

**Комментарий:**

Heaven and hell are not suitable for practicing jñāna or bhakti. One becomes absorbed in great enjoyment in Svarga. One becomes absorbed in great suffering in hell. It is not that jñāna and bhakti are forbidden in those places, though they disqualify one from karmas, for it is said:

*tad upary api bādarāyaṇaḥ sambhavāt*

**It should be accepted that devatās, who are above men also worship Brahman, because they have bodies. That is Lord Bādarāyaṇa's opinion. (Brahma-sūtra 1.3.26)**

### Text 13

*na naraḥ svar-gatiṁ kāṅkṣen nārakīṁ vā vicakṣaṇaḥ*  
*nemaṁ lokaṁ ca kāṅkṣeta dehāveśāt pramādyati*

**Перевод:**

**A human being who is wise should never desire Svarga or hell. A human being should also never desire continuous residence on the earth, for by such absorption in the material body one forgets about** ***jñāna*** **and** ***bhakti.***

**Комментарий:**

Therefore, attaining a human body, one should practice jñāna and bhakti and not desire Svarga

### Text 14

*etad vidvān purā mṛtyor abhavāya ghaṭeta saḥ*  
*apramatta idaṁ jñātvā martyam apy artha-siddhi-dam*

**Перевод:**

**A wise person, knowing that the human body, though temporary, allows attainment of perfection, should act for freedom from** ***saṁsāra*** **before death. Knowing the use of the human body, he should not be lazy.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes the path of vijñāna along with vairagya.

### Text 23

*nirviṇṇasya viraktasya puruṣasyokta-vedinaḥ*  
*manas tyajati daurātmyaṁ cintitasyānucintayā*

**Перевод:**

**When a person, considering what has been said, becomes disgusted with the world and detached from it by contemplating the subject with analysis, his mind gives up its false identity with the body.**

**Комментарий:**

Afraid of saṁsāra *(nirvinnasya*) he becomes detached from it (*viraktasya*).

### Text 24

*yamādibhir yoga-pathair ānvīkṣikyā ca vidyayā*  
*mamārcopāsanābhir vā nānyair yogyaṁ smaren manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**One should remember Paramātmā by following** ***yamas*** **and** ***niyamas*** **in** ***aśṭāṅga-yoga,*** **by analysis of elements, by knowledge, by worship of my form, and not by any other methods.**

**Комментарий:**

He should have no interest in other methods and goals (*na anyaiḥ*).

### Text 25

*yadi kuryāt pramādena yogī karma vigarhitam*  
*yogenaiva dahed aṁho nānyat tatra kadācana*

**Перевод:**

**If, because of inattention, a** ***jñānī*** **accidentally commits an abominable activity, then by the very practice of** ***jñāna,*** **he should burn to ashes the sinful reaction, without employing any other procedure.**

**Комментарий:**

The person qualified for jñāna is not touched by faults or good qualities arising from karma. He practices yoga as an aṅga of jñāna (*yogena*).

### Text 26

*sve sve ’dhikāre yā niṣṭhā sa guṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ*  
*karmaṇāṁ jāty-aśuddhānām anena niyamaḥ kṛtaḥ*  
*guṇa-doṣa-vidhānena saṅgānāṁ tyājanecchayā*

**Перевод:**

**When the** ***jñānī*** **or devotee remains situated according to his qualification it is praised as a good quality. With a desire to give up material enjoyment, there should be restriction on** ***karma*** **for the practitioners of** ***karma*** **who are innately impure, by following the rules and avoiding the prohibitions.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus offering karmas, practicing pure jñāna and pure bhakti are established according to qualification. One should be situated according to one’s qualification. Doing the opposite is a fault.

By the orders and prohibitions mentioned in the karma scriptures the person who is impure should restrict the karmas. Or “How is yoga possible? Or how will material identity be destroyed by karmas?”

He shows that since karmas are by their nature faulty, among them, some may be considered auspicious by quality and indicates that yoga by its nature has good qualities.

There is some very bitter nīma. In the world there are some species which are sweet and some which are bitter. Similarly, some karmas are by their nature impure. By applying rules and prohibitions on these karmas they are restricted, with a desire that the attachments are given up. It is impossible for them to suddenly give up those actions, so it is done gradually.

### Text 27-28

*jāta-śraddho mat-kathāsu nirviṇṇaḥ sarva-karmasu*  
*veda duḥkhātmakān kāmān parityāge ’py anīśvaraḥ*  
*tato bhajeta māṁ prītaḥ śraddhālur dṛḍha-niścayaḥ*  
*juṣamāṇaś ca tān kāmān duḥkhodarkāṁś ca garhayan*

**Перевод:**

**Having developed faith in topics about me and being disgusted with all** ***karmas*****, a devotee knows that all enjoyments are filled with misery. But he is unable to given them up. Still, with affection for me, with faith and determination, he will continue worshipping me, while at the same time partaking of those enjoyments which give rise to suffering and yet condemning them.**

**Комментарий:**

The path of bhakti is described in two verses. One should develop faith (*jāta-śraddhaḥ*) in my topics and other things related to me. One should fear other activities. However, he may not be able to give the results of old pious acts.

**Bhakti Sandarbha 172:**

Thus verse 11.20.28 explains that he is not completely detached and not too attached. This is the devotee’s initial state. This person should worship me (*bhajeta mām*). This means he is qualified for ananya-bhakti, whereas another person is qualified for jñāna by developing vairāgya. This is because bhakti is independent of other factors since it has its own śakti. This is explained later:

*tasmān mad-bhakti-yuktasya yogino vai mad-ātmanaḥ*  
*na jñānaṁ na ca vairāgya prāyaḥ śreyo bhaved iha*

**Therefore, for a devotee engaged in bhakti, with mind fixed on me, the cultivation of knowledge and renunciation is generally not beneficial for bhakti.**

*yat karmabhir yat tapasā jñāna-vairāgyataś ca yat*  
*yogena dāna-dharmeṇa śreyobhir itarair api*  
*sarvaṁ mad-bhakti-yogena mad-bhakto labhate ’ñjasā*  
*svargāpavargaṁ mad-dhāma kathañcid yadi vāñchati*

**Everything that can be achieved by karma, penance, jñāna, vairāgya, mystic yoga, charity, dharma and all other auspicious means of perfecting life is easily achieved by my devotee through bhakti. If somehow or other my devotee desires Svarga, liberation, or residence in my abode, he easily achieves such benedictions. (SB 11.20.32-33)**

This means that bhakti does not even depend on indifference to karma. That indifference will arise by faith that bhakti is the supreme method. Thus the qualification of being disgusted with karma merely explains this phenomenon. Though jñāna and karma also depend on faith, since, without that, internal and external inclination will not arise, in the case of bhakti faith alone is the cause. That is its specialty. Depending on strong faith, one is able to perform bhakti. Without faith, ananya-bhakti will not occur. And sometimes, if one has slight faith, bhakti can destroyed. One should not be too detached or too attached, but later, when faith in the Lord’s topics develops, karma will be given up.

However, even without faith, bhakti takes place.

*sakṛd api parigītaṁ śraddhayā helayā vā*  
*bhṛguvara nara-mātraṁ tārayet kṛṣṇa-nāma*

**The name of Kṛṣṇa chanted with faith or without faith delivers all men. (Skanda Purāṇa)**

*satāṁ prasaṅgān mama vīrya-saṁvido*  
*bhavanti hṛt-karṇa-rasāyanāḥ kathāḥ*  
*taj-joṣaṇād āśv apavarga-vartmani*  
*śraddhā ratir bhaktir anukramiṣyati*

**From association with the best devotees, topics of my glorious pastimes become directly realized, bringing the devotee to niṣṭhā. Then the topics become an elixir for the heart and ears at the stage of ruci. By taste for these topics, faith (arising after hearing), bhāva and then prema for the Lord who is the destroyer of material life, quickly develop in sequence. (SB 3.25.25)**

One sees results even before faith:

*mriyamāṇo harer nāma gṛṇan putropacāritam*  
*ajāmilo ’py agād dhāma kim uta śraddhayā gṛṇan*

**Ajāmila, by chanting the name of the Lord to indicate his son while dying, attained the abode of the Lord. What then will happen if one chants with faith? (SB 6.2.49)**

Faith is an aṅga of understanding the abhidheya presented in scriptures, since it is a form of conviction. Thus it is not included as an aṅga of the performance of bhakti.

“Bhakti should not depend on rules to produce its results, just as fire does not depend on rules to burn wood since hearing and chanting about the Lord possess the śakti of the Lord’s svarūpa. Why should bhakti depend on faith or anything else? And even without faith, sometimes one sees attainment of perfection in fools. It was said that chanting with or without faith (*śraddhayā helayā vā*) delivers humans. If one acts without thinking intentionally of offense (*helayā*), and without wicked intention, it does not interfere with bhakti. But if one intentionally commits offense, this will interfere with bhakti. For instance, Vena chanted the name of the Lord with envy and bhakti did not appear. In the same way, sometimes the śakti of a substance is impeded. For instance the fire’s power to burn is impeded by damp wood.

*śraddhayopāhṛtaṁ preṣṭhaṁ bhaktena mama vāry api*

**Actually, whatever is offered to me with faith by my devotee—even if only a little water—is most dear to me.**

*bhūry apy abhaktopāhṛtaṁ na me toṣāya kalpate*  
*gandho dhūpaḥ sumanaso dīpo ’nnādyaṁ ca kiṁ punaḥ*

**Even excellent presentations do not satisfy me if they are offered by nondevotees. But I am pleased by any insignificant offering made by devotees, what to speak of presentations of fragrant oil, incense, flowers and palatable foods. (SB 11.27.17-18)”**

In the above verses faith and *bhakti* refer to respect (*bhakti* does not refer to the activities of bhakti). This respect destroys the offense which produces disrespect, in order to produce excellent results in the form of the Lord’s satisfaction.

Therefore faith is not an aṅga of bhakti, but is a special qualification for ananya-bhakti, just as knowledge, desire and ability are qualifications for karma. This special qualification is what is designated in *mat-kathādau* *jāta-śraddhas tu* (SB 11.20.8) and *jāta-śraddho mat-kathāsu* (SB 11.20.27).

*Tato bhajeta māṁ* (SB 11.20.28) means “after developing faith, one should worship me. *Tataḥ* also indicates “no limits to who can perform it.” Thus even ātmārāmas start bhakti. This indicates bhakti’s ruling position. Thus it is said later:

*na kiñcit sādhavo dhīrā bhaktā hy ekāntino mama*  
*vāñchanty api mayā dattaṁ kaivalyam apunar-bhavam*

**But intelligent devotees, completely dedicated to me alone, do not desire liberation even if I offer it to them. (SB 11.20.34)**

To announce bhakti’s ruling position, it is said that karma and jñāna cannot produce results without bhakti.

Having stated that the cause of qualification for ananya-bhakti is faith alone, that person worships the Lord (SB 11.20.28) and practices with faith (*śraddhāluḥ)*. He develops āsakti (*dhṛḍha-niṣcayaḥ*) after ruci (*prītaḥ*). He is devoid of interruption in concentrated practice. Because he cannot suddenly give up the desires, he despises them for later they will produce lamentation. In this verse *kāmān* means enjoyments which are not sinful, for in scriptures it is stated that one should not engage in such sinful acts.

### Text 29

*proktena bhakti-yogena bhajato māsakṛn muneḥ*  
*kāmā hṛdayyā naśyanti sarve mayi hṛdi sthite*

**Перевод:**

**When an intelligent person engages constantly in worshiping me through** ***bhakti*****, as previously described by me, all material desires within the heart are destroyed, since I am situated in the heart.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhakti burns up all desires.

### Text 30

*bhidyate hṛdaya-granthiś chidyante sarva-saṁśayāḥ*  
*kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi mayi dṛṣṭe ’khilātmani*

**Перевод:**

***Ahaṅkāra*** **is cut and all doubts are destroyed. On seeing the Lord in the mind and with the eyes, all** ***karmas*** **are destroyed.**

**Комментарий:**

All doubts including the idea that it is impossible to see the Lord, are ended and karmas are destroyed.

*tad adhigama uttara-pūrvārdhayor aśleṣa-vināśau tad-vyapadeśāt*

**With attainment of Brahman, present sinful actions have no effect and previous karmas are destroyed since that is indicated the śruti. (Brahma-sūtra 4.1.13)**

### Text 31

*tasmān mad-bhakti-yuktasya yogino vai mad-ātmanaḥ*  
*na jñānaṁ na ca vairāgya prāyaḥ śreyo bhaved iha*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, for a devotee engaged in** ***bhakti,*** **with mind fixed on me, the cultivation of knowledge and renunciation is not beneficial for** ***bhakti.***

**Комментарий:**

For persons qualified for bhakti, involvement in karma and jñāna is not approved. Thus that person is not touched by the faults and good qualities that produce them.

Since bhakti destroys ahaṅkāra, the practices of jñāna and vairagya are not beneficial for the devotee, what to speak of karma-yoga, since they create obstacles to bhakti and require great but useless endeavor. The repetition of the negative *na* indicate that these should not be done at all. *Prāyaḥ* indicates deliberation. The practices are not accepted as a rule. For the devotees, there is no use in practicing jñāna and vairagya. Though this is so, just as on the path of direct liberation, some have a tendency for gradual liberation, some devotees may have a tendency for gradual progress in bhakti. This is described in *brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā* (BG 18.54). Bhakti has no dependence on jñāna or other processes since in bhakti, prema, the king of results, produces itself.

### Text 32-33

*yat karmabhir yat tapasā jñāna-vairāgyataś ca yat*  
*yogena dāna-dharmeṇa śreyobhir itarair api*  
*sarvaṁ mad-bhakti-yogena mad-bhakto labhate ’ñjasā*  
*svargāpavargaṁ mad-dhāma kathañcid yadi vāñchati*

**Перевод:**

**Everything that can be achieved by** ***karma,*** **penance,** ***jñāna, vairāgya,*** **mystic** ***yoga,*** **charity,** ***dharma*** **and all other auspicious means of perfecting life is easily achieved by my devotee through** ***bhakti.*** **If somehow or other my devotee desires Svarga, liberation, or residence in my abode, he easily achieves such benedictions.**

**Комментарий:**

For that purpose he shows the power of bhakti particularly in two verses.

**Bhakti Sandarbha 84:**

Material happiness and the happiness of liberation are attainable by purifying one’s existence. Happiness surpassing that is available also: Vaikuṇṭha.

All this is available if, somehow or other, some devotee desires it for assisting bhakti. For instance Citraketu desired Svarga and there chanted the glories of the Lord. (SB 6.17.3) Śukadeva desired liberation. He came out the womb of his mother by his request when Kṛṣṇa prevented māyā from attacking him extending over time which became like a mustard seed on the horn of a cow. This is narrated in Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa. Liberation can assist bhakti, for Gītā says *brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā:* coming to the level of Brahman one then attains bhakti. One who desires Vaikuṇṭha enters a desired group of the Lord’s attendants. By prema one attains one’s desired situation by the desire to serve directly the lotus feet of the Lord.

*yac ca vrajanty animiṣām ṛṣabhānuvṛttyā*  
*dūre yamā hy upari naḥ spṛhaṇīya-śīlāḥ*  
*bhartur mithaḥ suyaśasaḥ kathanānurāga-*  
*vaiklavya-bāṣpa-kalayā pulakī-kṛtāṅgāḥ*

**Those who are far above rules by following the Lord with dedication, who are superior to us, and whose qualities are desirable by us, and whose bodies develop goose bumps and uncontrolled tears through attraction to discussions of the Lord possessing most excellent qualities, enter Vaikuṇṭha. (SB 3.15.25)**

### Text 35

*nairapekṣyaṁ paraṁ prāhur niḥśreyasam analpakam*  
*tasmān nirāśiṣo bhaktir nirapekṣasya me bhavet*

**Перевод:**

**It is said that the process which is without dependence on other processes or results is the best process. Therefore a person who does not desire any rewards and does not depend on other processes develops** ***bhakti*** **for me.**

**Комментарий:**

The practice of such bhakti is similar.

### Text 36

*na mayy ekānta-bhaktānāṁ guṇa-doṣodbhavā guṇāḥ*  
*sādhūnāṁ sama-cittānāṁ buddheḥ param upeyuṣām*

**Перевод:**

**The fully dedicated devotees who see equally everywhere and who have achieved the Lord who is superior to** ***prakṛti*** **do not have the** ***guṇas*** **which give rise to qualities of good and bad.**

**Комментарий:**

As the person doing niṣkāma-karma is not contaminated by the faults of sakāma-karma, the person qualified for jñāna is not contaminated by the faults of karma. The person qualified for bhakti is not contaminated by the faults of either type of karma or of jñāna. The person having perfection in bhakti is not contaminated by the faults of the previous four persons. The final result is shown in this verse, as was expressed previously:

*eta uddhava te praśnāḥ sarve sādhu nirūpitāḥ*  
*kiṁ varṇitena bahunā lakṣaṇaṁ guṇa-doṣayoḥ*  
*guṇa-doṣa-dṛśir doṣo guṇas tūbhaya-varjitaḥ*

**Thus, Uddhava, I have elucidated all of the matters of inquiry, which are suitable for liberation. There is no need for a more elaborate description of good and bad qualities, since to see good and bad is itself a bad quality. The best quality is to transcend seeing good and bad qualities. (SB 11.19.45)**

## Chapter Twenty-one

### Text 1

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*ya etān mat-patho hitvā bhakti-jñāna-kriyātmakān*  
*kṣudrān kāmāṁś calaiḥ prāṇair juṣantaḥ saṁsaranti te*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: Those who give up my methods,** ***bhakti, jñāna*** **and** ***niṣkāma-karma*****, and instead cultivate insignificant sense enjoyment by the fickle senses, undergo the continual cycle of material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrīdhara Svāmī speaks of those who practice niṣkāma-karma. They have not developed a sense of vairagya. Those who purified, fixed in jñāna, have developed vairagya. Those are fixed in bhakti have developed faith. Those who have not come to jñāna or bhakti, and not even to niṣkāma-karma cultivate sense enjoyment (*kṣudrāṇ kāmān*) and have all faults. The desires produced by performance karma, jñāna and bhakti may be material or spiritual.

### Text 2

*sve sve ’dhikāre yā niṣṭhā sa guṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ*  
*viparyayas tu doṣaḥ syād ubhayor eṣa niścayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Being fixed according to one’s qualification is a good quality, and to be fixed in something not of one’s qualification is a bad quality. This is how good and bad are determined.**

**Комментарий:**

Good and bad qualities are described considering the previous adhikāras in order to determine good and bad objects in the world. Being fixed sakāma-karma, niṣkāma karma, vairagya and śraddhā, and performing the various yogas, is a good quality. Not being fixed is a bad quality. This determines good and bad for both materially and spiritually qualified persons (*ubhayoḥ*). However the material sādhanas produce good qualities whereas the spiritual sādhana (bhakti) produces perfection. Jñāna and karma must have a mixture of bhakti to attain results. Without a portion of bhakti in jñāna and karma, the goal of those sādhanas cannot be achieved. Without bhakti, they fail. Since bhakti does not depend on them and produces all results, if one mixes bhakti with karma or jñāna, bhakti fails.

Thus being fixed in karma with the help of a little bhakti is a good quality for the person qualified for karma. Similarly being fixed in jñāna with a little bhakti is a good quality for the jñānī. But being fixed in pure bhakti, what to speak of bhakti in the form of prema, is the best quality for the devotee. Doing less or more than one’s qualification is a fault. Doing less destroys the lesser method, and doing more than one’s qualification disqualifies one from attaining its goal.

### Text 3

*śuddhy-aśuddhī vidhīyete samāneṣv api vastuṣu*  
*dravyasya vicikitsārthaṁ guṇa-doṣau śubhāśubhau*  
*dharmārthaṁ vyavahārārthaṁ yātrārtham iti cānagha*

**Перевод:**

**O sinless Uddhava! In order to resolve doubts about certain objects among general objects, they are established as good or bad, pure or impure, auspicious or inauspicious. In terms of** ***dharma*** **they are classed as pure or impure. In terms of common dealings they are classed as good and bad, and in terms of circumstance they are classed as auspicious or inauspicious.**

**Комментарий:**

According to different qualifications, good and bad are described in different circumstances. Objects are classes as pure or impure, auspicious or inauspicious, good and bad, according to scripture, to resolve doubts about them. Using objects without consideration of good or bad, but considering pure or impure should still be considered in terms of good or bad. Using objects with consideration of good and bad in terms of function, without considering use for dharma and auspicious or inauspicious, should be considered good or bad. Thus the statements about good and bad are only general. The list of purposes should not be exactly correlated with pure and impure, good and bad and auspicious and inauspicious, as this is not seen anywhere. The usage is according to the spiritual scriptures, not other works.

Dharma and yatra (physical subsistence) involve different motives.

### Text 4

*darśito ’yaṁ mayācāro dharmam udvahatāṁ dhuram*

**Перевод:**

**I have revealed this way of life for persons bearing the burden of** ***dharma.***

**Комментарий:**

The conduct, filled with happiness, is shown by me for persons bearing the weight of bhakti (*dharmam*) since it has arisen by bhakti, the svarūpa of happiness.

### Text 6

*vedena nāma-rūpāṇi viṣamāṇi sameṣv api*  
*dhātuṣūddhava kalpyanta eteṣāṁ svārtha-siddhaye*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! Although all material bodies are composed of the same five elements and are thus equal, the Vedic literatures conceive of different names and forms in relation to such bodies so that the living entities may achieve their goal of life.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the same material elements are used, since all beings are constituted of ātmā without guṇas and matter filled with fault, different names such as Brahmā and different forms (higher or lower) are employed to indicate good or bad, like classifying nīma according to taste. The purpose is for jīvas to achieve dharma etc. according to their tendency or qualification. The form limits the tendency. Gradually the jīvas proceed to liberation.

### Text 7

*deśa-kālādi-bhāvānāṁ vastūnāṁ mama sattama*  
*guṇa-doṣau vidhīyete niyamārthaṁ hi karmaṇām*

**Перевод:**

**O saintly Uddhava! In order to restrict materialistic activities, I have established that which is proper and improper among all material things, space and time.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to restrict (*niyamārtham*) activities I have established proper and improper. This is concerning objects not related to the Lord.

*vanaṁ tu sāttviko vāso grāmo rājasa ucyate*  
*tāmasaṁ dyūta-sadanaṁ man-niketaṁ tu nirguṇam*

**Residence in the forest is in the mode of goodness, residence in a town is in the mode of passion, residence in a gambling house displays the quality of ignorance, and residence in a place where I reside is beyond the** ***guṇas.*** **(SB 11.25.25)**

*sāttvikaḥ kārako ’saṅgī rāgāndho rājasaḥ smṛtaḥ*  
*tāmasaḥ smṛti-vibhraṣṭo nirguṇo mad-apāśrayaḥ*

**A performer of action who is free of attachment is in** ***sattva*****, a performer of action overcome by sense objects is in** ***rajas*****, and a performer of action who is devoid of inquiry is in** ***tamas.*** **But a performer of action who has taken shelter of me alone is beyond the** ***guṇas.*** **(SB 11.25.26)**

The shelter of the guṇas is beyond the guṇas. In the form of the Vedas I (*mama*) have established the classification.

### Text 8

*akṛṣṇa-sāro deśānām abrahmaṇyo ’sucir bhavet*  
*kṛṣṇa-sāro ’py asauvīra- kīkaṭāsaṁskṛteriṇam*

**Перевод:**

**Among places, those bereft of the spotted antelope, those devoid of devotion to the** ***brāhmaṇas,*** **those possessing spotted antelopes but having unrespectable Kīkaṭas, unclean people or deserts are all considered to be impure.**

**Комментарий:**

Though a place has the spotted antelope but is devoid of qualified persons who respect brāhmaṇas, it is impure even if devoid of Kīkaṭas. If a place has qualified persons who respect brāhmaṇas, it is pure, even if there are Kīkaṭas.

### Text 10

*dravyasya śuddhy-aśuddhī ca dravyeṇa vacanena ca*  
*saṁskāreṇātha kālena mahatvālpatayātha vā*

**Перевод:**

**An object’s purity or impurity is established by application of another object, by words, by cleaning, by the effects of time or according to size.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses describe purity.

### Text 14

*snāna-dāna-tapo-’vasthā- vīrya-saṁskāra-karmabhiḥ*  
*mat-smṛtyā cātmanaḥ śaucaṁ śuddhaḥ karmācared dvijaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The self can be cleansed by bathing, charity, austerity, age, conduct, purification rituals, prescribed duties and, above all, by remembrance of me. The** ***brāhmaṇa*** **and others should be duly purified before performing their specific activities.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembrance of the Lord is an independent item.

*apavitraḥ pavitro vā sarvāvasthāṁ gato ’pi vā*  
*yaḥ smaret puṇḍarīkākṣaṁ sa bāhyābhyantara-śuciḥ*

**Whether one is pure or contaminated, and regardless of one’s external situation, simply, by remembering the lo­tus-eyed Personality of Godhead, one can cleanse one’s in­ter­nal and external existence. (Garuḍa Purāṇa)**

This is mentioned, not for general usage, but for purification of impure items without remedy, since remembrance of the Lord has unfailing effects in all circumstances.

*harir harati pāpāni duṣṭa-cittair api smṛtaḥ*

**The Lord destroys sins. Even sinful persons should remember him.**

### Text 19

*viṣayeṣu guṇādhyāsāt puṁsaḥ saṅgas tato bhavet*  
*saṅgāt tatra bhavet kāmaḥ kāmād eva kalir nṛṇām*

**Перевод:**

**One becomes attached because of thinking that an object is good. From that attachment desire arises. From desire quarrel arises.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses trace the decline of a person with attachments.

### Text 23

*phala-śrutir iyaṁ nṝṇāṁ na śreyo rocanaṁ param*  
*śreyo-vivakṣayā proktaṁ yathā bhaiṣajya-rocanam*

**Перевод:**

**The rewards promised in scripture are not the ultimate benefit for man but are merely enticements for liberating him. They are like promises of candy spoken to induce a child to take beneficial medicine.**

**Комментарий:**

Having criticized persons desiring material objects, he criticizes persons desiring spiritual goals. The person gives the child medicine by promising something else.

### Text 27

*kāminaḥ kṛpaṇā lubdhāḥ puṣpeṣu phala-buddhayaḥ*  
*agni-mugdhā dhūma-tāntāḥ svaṁ lokaṁ na vidanti te*

**Перевод:**

**Those who are full of lust, avarice and greed mistake mere flowers to be the actual fruits. Bewildered by the glare of fire and fatigued by its smoke, they cannot recognize the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

*Svam lokam* means “one’s shelter.”

### Text 28

*na te mām aṅga jānanti hṛdi-sthaṁ ya idaṁ yataḥ*  
*uktha-śastrā hy asu-tṛpo yathā nīhāra-cakṣuṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! Persons dedicated to sense gratification obtained through honoring the Vedic rituals cannot understand that I am situated in everyone’s heart and that the entire universe is non-different from me and emanates from me, because their eyes are covered by ignorance.**

**Комментарий:**

They cannot understand me because I am beyond the guṇas.

### Text 35

*vedā brahmātma-viṣayās tri-kāṇḍa-viṣayā ime*  
*parokṣa-vādā ṛṣayaḥ parokṣaṁ mama ca priyam*

**Перевод:**

**The Vedas, divided into three divisions, ultimately reveal worship of the Lord. The Vedic sages and** ***mantras*****, however, state this indirectly, since they know that I prefer this indirect method.**

**Комментарий:**

The Vedas deal with the ātmā, the highest root, Bhagavān, who is the greatest (*brahma*). The cause of being invisible to all is given. Indirect expression is dear to me.

*eṣa mohaṁ sṛjamy āśu yo janān mohayiṣyati*  
*tvaṁ ca rudra mahā-bāho moha-śastrāṇi kāraya*  
*atathyāni vitathyāni darśayasva mahā-bhuja*  
*prakāśaṁ kuru cātmānaṁ aprakāśaṁ ca māṁ kuru*

**I will quickly create illusion. O Śiva, you who will bewilder people! Make deceptive scriptures. Reveal what is false. Reveal yourself and hide me. (Varāha Purāṇa)**

He reveals his intention in the following:

*iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā*  
*vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru \|\|*

**Thus I have explained a scripture more secret than the secret knowledge of** ***mantras*****. Considering this thoroughly, do as you wish to do. (BG 18.63)**

He is hidden because all are not qualified:

*rājan patir gurur alaṁ bhavatāṁ yadūnāṁ*  
*daivaṁ priyaḥ kula-patiḥ kva ca kiṅkaro vaḥ*  
*astv evam aṅga bhagavān bhajatāṁ mukundo*  
*muktiṁ dadāti karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam*

**O King Parīkṣit! Kṛṣṇa was the protector, instructor, object of worship, giver of affection, and the protector of both the Yadus and Pāṇḍavas. But he was sometimes your servant. The Lord gives liberation but not even** ***bhāva-bhakti*** **to those who worship him. (SB 5.6.28)**

### Text 36

*śabda-brahma su-durbodhaṁ prāṇendriya-mano-mayam*  
*ananta-pāraṁ gambhīraṁ durvigāhyaṁ samudra-vat*

**Перевод:**

**The sound of the Vedas is very difficult to comprehend and manifests on different levels within the** ***prāṇa*****, mind, intelligence and senses. This Vedic sound is unlimited and deep like the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. The Vedas are difficult comprehend though they are made of prāṇa, mind and senses, and appear in the form of para, paśyantī and vaikharī, in those places, appearing like material sound, since they are unlimited as sound, deep in terms of meaning, and impossible to enter (*durvigāhyam*). Even if one enters, the meaning cannot be understood.

### Text 37

*mayopabṛṁhitaṁ bhūmnā brahmaṇānanta-śaktinā*  
*bhūteṣu ghoṣa-rūpeṇa biseṣūrṇeva lakṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**The Vedas, which are spread everywhere by me because I possess many forms, pervade everywhere as Brahman, and possess unlimited powers, are perceived by the wise as** ***nāda*** **within all beings, subtle as the threads within the lotus stalk.**

**Комментарий:**

If the Vedas have this nature, why do they appear in prāṇa?” They manifest in these places by me (*mayopabṛṁhitam*). “The Vedas manifest in unlimited Vaikuṇṭha and in unlimited universes. How does it manifest from you alone?” I possess unlimited śakti as the greatest being by nature (*brahma*). “That which is spread everywhere should be unlimited. The Vedas do not appear to be unlimited.” They are seen by yogīs as nāda, the invisible form of praṇava. It is said:

*amātro’nanta-mātraś ca dvaitasyopaśamaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*oṅkāro vidito yena sa munir netaro janaḥ \|\|*

**It is without measure and of infinite measure. It is all auspicious, destroying duality. He who knows oṁ is the only wise man. (Māṇḍukya-kārikā 26-29)**

### Text 38-40

*yathorṇanābhir hṛdayād ūrṇām udvamate mukhāt*  
*ākāśād ghoṣavān prāṇo manasā sparśa-rūpiṇā*  
*chando-mayo ’mṛta-mayaḥ sahasra-padavīṁ prabhuḥ*  
*oṁkārād vyañjita-sparśa- svaroṣmāntastha-bhūṣitām*  
*vicitra-bhāṣā-vitatāṁ chandobhiś catur-uttaraiḥ*  
*ananta-pārāṁ bṛhatīṁ sṛjaty ākṣipate svayam*

**Перевод:**

**Just as a spider brings forth from its heart its web and emits it through its mouth, the Supreme Lord, made of supreme bliss, made of the Vedas, taking support of ether, appears as** ***parā*** **sound made of** ***prāṇa,*** **and then creates and destroys, by his mind which produces the consonants and the manifest Vedas--which are unlimited in sound and meaning, decorated with the consonants, vowels, sibilants, and semivowels emanating from the subtle sound** ***oṁ,*** **and which are filled with a variety of languages and meters, each four syllables longer than the previous.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses describe how the Vedas arise from the Lord in the form of para, paśyantī etc. through prāṇa, the mind and senses. The spider from its heart, through the mouth, emits its web. Similarly the Lord (*prabhuḥ*), my aṁśa Paramātmā, the very form of the highest bliss *(amṛta-mayaḥ*), by his śakti becoming the Vedas (*chando-mayaḥ*) endowed with all knowledge, taking support of ether, manifests in the ādhāra-cakra of Hiraṇyagarbha and creates para sound (*bṛhatīm*). Then becoming slightly audible as nāda (*ghoṣavān*) it manifests as madhyama sound in the navel cakra. Then becoming filled with prāṇa in the heart, from oṁ it attains the form of nāda and manifests as paśyantī by the mind with a touch of awareness of different syllables (*sparśa-rūpiṇā*). Then it manifests as vaikharī, the Vedas with branches (*sahasra-padavīm*), with manifested consonants, vowels, silibants and semivowels a well as meters (*chandobhiḥ*).

At another time, the Vedas enter the Lord. The mātrās are short, long and extended, the svaras are low, middle and high pitch. There are forty-nine consonants with *kṣa* being included in the consonants and sibilants.

### Text 42

*kiṁ vidhatte kim ācaṣṭe kim anūdya vikalpayet*  
*ity asyā hṛdayaṁ loke nānyo mad veda kaścana*

**Перевод:**

**What do the Vedas instruct as action? What is the final meaning of the Vedas? What alternatives do the Vedas raise? No one except me or my dear devotee knows the intended meaning of the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

I know the meaning of the Vedas which arise from me.

### Text 43

*māṁ vidhatte ’bhidhatte māṁ vikalpyāpohyate tv aham*  
*etāvān sarva-vedārthaḥ śabda āsthāya māṁ bhidām*  
*māyā-mātram anūdyānte pratiṣidhya prasīdati*

**Перевод:**

**The Vedas indicate** ***bhakti*** **as the action and indicate me as the meaning. I am the meaning of all the Vedas. I, as** ***karma*** **and** ***jñāna,*** **am proposed and rejected as alternatives. The Vedas, taking shelter of me, proposing** ***karma*** **and** ***jñāna*** **and then rejecting them as** ***māyā*****, become happy by giving the devotees bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

I the form of Kṛṣṇa am the ultimate meaning of the Vedas. That is shown in the last two lines.

The Vedas and whatever follows the Vedas (*śabdaḥ*) rejecting the world (*māyā-mātram*), describing my various avatāras (*bhidām*), taking support (*āsthāya*) of me (*mām*) in the form of Kṛṣṇa, become successful (*prasīdati*). Gītā says:

*vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva cāham \|\|*

**And I am also known by all the** ***Vedas*****. I have made the** ***Vedānta*** **to explain myself, since I alone know the** ***Vedas.*** **(BG 15.15)**

## Chapter Twenty-two

### Text 1-3

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*kati tattvāni viśveśa saṅkhyātāny ṛṣibhiḥ prabho*  
*navaikādaśa pañca trīṇy āttha tvam iha śuśruma*  
*kecit ṣaḍ-viṁśatiṁ prāhur apare pañca-viṁśatiṁ*  
*saptaike nava ṣaṭ kecic catvāry ekādaśāpare*  
*kecit saptadaśa prāhuḥ ṣoḍaśaike trayodaśa*  
*etāvattvaṁ hi saṅkhyānām ṛṣayo yad-vivakṣayā*  
*gāyanti pṛthag āyuṣmann idaṁ no vaktum arhasi*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava inquired: O Lord! O master of the universe! How many different elements of creation have been enumerated by the great sages? I have heard you personally describe a total of twenty-eight—God, the** ***jīva*****, the** ***mahat-tattva*****, false ego, the five gross elements, the ten senses, the mind, the five subtle objects of perception and the three modes of nature. But some authorities say that there are twenty-six elements, while others cite twenty-five or else seven, nine, six, four or eleven, and even others say that there are seventeen, sixteen or thirteen elements. What did the sages have in mind when they calculated the creative elements in such different ways? O Lord with an eternal form! Kindly explain this to me.**

**Комментарий:**

Having made the goal of karma-kāṇḍa secondary, and determined that jñāna-kāṇḍa up to Svayam Bhagavān is the primary topic, Uddhava inquires in order to discard different arguments in the meaning of jñāna-kāṇḍa. Śrīdhara Svāmī says that people disagree in defining what are the real existing objects as effects. *Āyuṣman* (O ever living person!) indicates that the Lord eternally possesses life.

### Text 4

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*yuktaṁ ca santi sarvatra bhāṣante brāhmaṇā yathā*  
*māyāṁ madīyām udgṛhya vadatāṁ kiṁ nu durghaṭam*

**Перевод:**

**Lord Kṛṣṇa replied: Because all material elements are present in the other elements, all these sages speak the truth. It is not difficult for disputants who have taken shelter of my** ***māyā*** **to argue.**

**Комментарий:**

Presenting his own view through all the other views, he praises them all. The brāhmaṇas, those who know the Vedas, speak the truth (*yuktam*). “If everyone is correct, why do they reject other opinions and establish their individual opinions.”

They take shelter of my māyā. Since the place for illusion of water in the desert is not limited, there can be any number of illusions. Thus, one can establish twenty-eight elements. Māyā is not the acintya-śakti, but rather ignorance which manifests falsity. Since they take shelter of māyā, and māyā takes shelter of me alone, it is proper that they should know it belongs to me alone. They have some truth but my truth manifests everything.

### Text 5

*naitad evaṁ yathāttha tvaṁ yad ahaṁ vacmi tat tathā*  
*evaṁ vivadatāṁ hetuṁ śaktayo me duratyayāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When philosophers argue, “I don’t choose to analyze this particular case in the same way that you have,” the cause of their arguments is my insurmountable** ***śakti*****.**

**Комментарий:**

This is explained. My śaktis in the form of various arguments are the causes.

### Text 6

*yāsāṁ vyatikarād āsīd vikalpo vadatāṁ padam*  
*prāpte śama-dame ’pyeti vādas tam anu śāmyati*

**Перевод:**

**But for those who have fixed their intelligence on me and controlled their senses, differences of perception disappear and consequently the argument ceases.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of the contact with the acintya-śakti, all different opinions (*vikalpaḥ*) of various philosophers have appeared. The opinions disappear when the senses are controlled and the mind is fixed on me (*śama-dame*). After that, naturally, the arguments cease, since they understand the outstanding supreme Lord.

### Text 7

*parasparānupraveśāt tattvānāṁ puruṣarṣabha*  
*paurvāparya-prasaṅkhyānaṁ yathā vaktur vivakṣitam*

**Перевод:**

**O best among men! Because subtle and gross elements mutually enter into one another, philosophers may desire to calculate the number of elements in terms of causes or effects according to their personal desire and thus arrive at different totals.**

**Комментарий:**

According to the desire of the speaker, various numbers of elements arise.

### Text 8

*ekasminn api dṛśyante praviṣṭānītarāṇi ca*  
*pūrvasmin vā parasmin vā tattve tattvāni sarvaśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All subtle material elements are actually present within their gross effects; similarly, all gross elements are present within their subtle causes. Thus we can find all material elements within any single element.**

**Комментарий:**

All the elements are seen to enter into one element. And the one element enters into all the other elements.

### Text 11

*puruṣeśvarayor atra na vailakṣaṇyam aṇv api*  
*tad-anya-kalpanāpārthā jñānaṁ ca prakṛter guṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**There is little difference between the Lord and the** ***jīva.*** **To think of them as extremely different is useless.** ***Jñāna*** **arises from the** ***guṇas*** **of** ***prakṛti*** **and is thus useless for gaining proper vision.**

**Комментарий:**

The ātmā cannot be understood, what to speak of the Paramātmā. In order to understand Paramātmā or the Lord, some knowers of truth impart knowledge that the Lord is different from the jīva. That Lord is self-revealing knowledge. Others however, not understanding the distinction, think without distinction of a conscious entity and propound that. That is expressed here. According to them, the jīva should not have knowledge. Knowledge is a quality of prakṛti. Since the jīva wanders about in the currents of the guṇas, it should have no relationship with knowledge.

### Text 12

*prakṛtir guṇa-sāmyaṁ vai prakṛter nātmano guṇāḥ*  
*sattvaṁ rajas tama iti sthity-utpatty-anta-hetavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

***Prakṛti*** **is the equilibrium of the** ***guṇas.*** **The** ***guṇas*** **belong to** ***prakṛti*****, not the** ***jīva.*** **These modes—goodness, passion and ignorance—are the causes of the creation, maintenance and destruction of this universe, and thus cannot inhere in the eternal** ***jīva.***

**Комментарий:**

“You maintain twenty-eight elements. How can twenty-six elements be correct?” to erase that doubt, the Lord establishes his previous point. The equilibrium of the guṇas is prakṛti. The guṇas of prakṛti cannot be the ātmā. The guṇas of prakṛti are not the qualities of the jīva (knowledge and bliss), what to speak of being the qualities of the Lord. The guṇas of prakṛti are the cause of material creation and destruction. The word *anta* means atyantika-pralaya. This means liberation. Ignorance is the cause of destruction, since it is caused by karma. Knowledge (*sattva*) is the cause of liberation.

### Text 13

*sattvaṁ jñānaṁ rajaḥ karma tamo ’jñānam ihocyate*  
*guṇa-vyatikaraḥ kālaḥ svabhāvaḥ sūtram eva ca*

**Перевод:**

**In this world** ***sattva*** **is recognized as knowledge,** ***rajas*** **is action and** ***tamas*** **is ignorance. The Lord is identified with time, the agitator of the** ***guṇa*****s.** ***Svabhāva*** **or change arising from action is the same as** ***mahat-tattva.***

**Комментарий:**

The descriptions are indications only and not definitive of their natures. Since all of prakṛti is insentient, and the indication of knowledge (in sattva) is by relationship with a shadow of consciousness, sattva is not a cause of knowledge about the Lord.

When sattva manifests, knowledge of the Lord does not arise. The sun does not manifest from its ābhāsa within a room. The Lord is self-manifesting.

*sa yad ajayā tv ajām anuśayīta guṇāṁś ca juṣan*  
*bhajati sarūpatāṁ tad anu mṛtyum apeta-bhagaḥ*  
*tvam uta jahāsi tām ahir iva tvacam ātta-bhago*  
*mahasi mahīyase ’ṣṭa-guṇite ’parimeya-bhagaḥ*

**The** ***jīva*** **contacts matter by the influence of** ***māyā,*** **takes on a material form due to** ***upādhis,*** **and enjoys material objects. He thus experiences** ***saṁsāra.*** **You, however, avoid the material energy in the same way that a snake abandons its old skin. Glorious in your possession of eight mystic powers, you display unlimited greatness. (SB 10.87.38)**

According to this, the jīva, by being subject to beginningless ignorance, has his knowledge covered. For liberation he must search out some other entity that gives knowledge. The supreme Lord is thus ascertained. One who hears about him repeats the message. From the Lord comes the jīva’s knowledge.

*parābhidhyānāt tu tirohitaṁ tato hy asya bandha-viparyayau*

**Dreams disappear by the will of the Lord. This is not surprising since the Lord (through māyā) is also the cause of bondage and liberation of the jīva. (Brahma-sūtra 3.2.5)**

This knowledge is accepted by others and should be given to them since it is an aṁśa of the svarūpa-śakti, included in the Lord. The three guṇas are parts of prakṛti, which is composed of them. They are nothing more than that. This is determined by those who enumerate twenty-six elements. Having established the twenty-six elements, the three guṇas of prakṛti are additional.

Limiting the number to that, there are nine, eleven, five and three. We hear that you are these elements. By repeating the question, this is counted as your opinion. The three guṇas are shown first, as causes of having additional elements.

The agitation (*vyatikaraḥ*) of the guṇas arises by time, which is made active by the Lord. Impressions of karma are the cause of the jīva attaining particular bodies. This is called *svabhāva.* By me, made of time, the universe becomes endowed with karma.

Sūtra is the mukhya-prāṇa, composed of kriyā-śakti. Mahat-tattva is connected to sūtra.

### Text 14

*puruṣaḥ prakṛtir vyaktam ahaṅkāro nabho ’nilaḥ*  
*jyotir āpaḥ kṣitir iti tattvāny uktāni me nava*

**Перевод:**

**I have described the nine basic elements as the** ***jīva, prakṛti, mahat-tattva,*** ***ahaṅkāra,*** **ether, air, fire, water and earth.**

**Комментарий:**

He enumerates nine and eleven elements in two and half verses. *Puruṣaḥ* is the jīva, and v*yaktam* is mahat-tattva, filled with jñāna-śakti. The five gross elements are also listed.

### Text 16

*śabdaḥ sparśo raso gandho rūpaṁ cety artha-jātayaḥ*  
*gaty-ukty-utsarga-śilpāni karmāyatana-siddhayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sound, touch, taste, smell and form are the sense objects of the knowledge-acquiring senses. Movement, speech, excretion of wastes and semen, and manufacture are functions of the working senses, but these are not counted as elements.**

**Комментарий:**

The sense objects are listed. It indicates other items such as the Lord, to make twenty-eight elements. Movement etc. are rejected as elements. Other things are also rejected by this statement.

### Text 17

*sargādau prakṛtir hy asya kārya-kāraṇa-rūpiṇī*  
*sattvādibhir guṇair dhatte puruṣo ’vyakta īkṣate*

**Перевод:**

**Taking the form of the causal and resulting (*****kāraṇa*** **and** ***kārya)*** **elements,** ***prakṛti*** **accepts creation and destruction of the universe through the** ***guṇas*****. The Lord does not undergo transformation but merely remains the witness.**

**Комментарий:**

In two verses, he describes everything that the philosophers enumerate.

### Text 21

*catvāry eveti tatrāpi teja āpo ’nnam ātmanaḥ*  
*jātāni tair idaṁ jātaṁ janmāvayavinaḥ khalu*

**Перевод:**

**Some philosophers propose the existence of four basic elements, of which three—fire, water and earth—emanate from the fourth, the Lord. By these elements the creation of the products in this universe arose.**

**Комментарий:**

According this idea, from ātmā, four elements arise. By these four, the world arises, as the appearance of effects (*avayavinaḥ*). Ether is not considered, as it is invisible. Air is also subtle.

### Text 27

*evaṁ me puṇḍarīkākṣa mahāntaṁ saṁśayaṁ hṛdi*  
*chettum arhasi sarva-jña vacobhir naya-naipuṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa! O omniscient Lord! Cut this great doubt out of my heart with your words, which exhibit your great skill in reasoning.**

### Text 28

*tvatto jñānaṁ hi jīvānāṁ pramoṣas te ’tra śaktitaḥ*  
*tvam eva hy ātma-māyāyā gatiṁ vettha na cāparaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**From you alone through your energy, the** ***jīvas’*** **knowledge arises and disappears. No one but you can understand the real nature of your illusory potency.**

**Комментарий:**

The difference between the Lord and the jīva was the Lord’s opinion. The Lord as the cause is now shown. Through your śakti, the functions of māyā, the jīva’s knowledge appears and disappears. The Lord’s cruelty through lack of power is refuted. “How can knowledge manifest from me, for jīvas covered by māyā. How does knowledge disappear by māyā for the ātmā which is self-revealing?” In answer to the first question, your śakti removes māyā. By rejecting you, jīva can be defeated. The twenty-eight (with sattva-guṇa giving knowledge) assist the twenty six.

### Text 33

*yo ’sau guṇa-kṣobha-kṛto vikāraḥ*  
*pradhāna-mūlān mahataḥ prasūtaḥ*  
*ahaṁ tri-vṛn moha-vikalpa-hetur*  
*vaikārikas tāmasa aindriyaś ca*

**Перевод:**

***Ahaṅkāra,*** **which arises from** ***mahat-tattva,*** **arising from agitation of** ***prakṛti*****, has three forms:** ***sattva, tamas*** **and** ***rajas.*** **These cause a variety of opinions caused by ignorance.**

### Text 34

*ātmāparijñāna-mayo vivādo*  
*hy astīti nāstīti bhidārtha-niṣṭhaḥ*  
*vyartho ’pi naivoparameta puṁsāṁ*  
*mattaḥ parāvṛtta-dhiyāṁ sva-lokāt*

**Перевод:**

**Those who do not know Paramātmā, who are fixed in goals other than me, engage in arguments concerning the reality or unreality of the world, and do not cease to argue, though they achieve no results. They have turned their thoughts from me, the Lord, who gives regard only to the devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

How to destroy ahaṅkāra? It is said:

*bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād*  
*īśād apetasya viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ*  
*tan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ*  
*bhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devate ātmā*

**For the** ***jīva*** **averse to the Lord, there will be** ***saṁsāra*** **consisting of identity with body and lack of identity with the soul, because of his absorption in the material coverings on the soul, arising from the Lord’s** ***māyā.*** **Therefore, the intelligent person, taking** ***guru*** **as his Lord and very self, should fully worship the Lord with pure** ***bhakti.*** **(SB 11.2.37)**

One should put aside refusing the existence of the Lord and become favorable to the Lord. For persons whose intelligence is turned away from me, their shelter (*sva-lokāt*), there will be arguments between oneself and others about existence or nonexistence of ātmā and the Lord of one’s svarūpa (*ātmā-parijñānam*). Though without meaning, the arguments will never end. As long as the person does not recognize me, he will engage in arguments and not attain knowledge. On accepting me, knowledge will arise as a secondary result. The main result is attaining me. This is the parama-puruṣārtha.

### Text 35-36

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*tvattaḥ parāvṛtta-dhiyaḥ sva-kṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ prabho*  
*uccāvacān yathā dehān gṛhṇanti visṛjanti ca*  
*tan mamākhyāhi govinda durvibhāvyam anātmabhiḥ*  
*na hy etat prāyaśo loke vidvāṁsaḥ santi vañcitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O supreme master! Please explain to me how persons with diverted intelligence accept superior and inferior bodies by their materialistic activities and then give up such bodies. O Govinda, this topic is very difficult for foolish persons to understand. Bewildered by your** ***māyā,*** **no one generally knows this.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. How does the inactive ātmā go from one body to another?

### Text 37

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*manaḥ karma-mayaṁ ṇṝṇām indriyaiḥ pañcabhir yutam*  
*lokāl lokaṁ prayāty anya ātmā tad anuvartate*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: The material mind of man, dependent on** ***karma,*** **travels along with the five senses from one material body to another. The** ***ātmā,*** **although different from this mind, follows it.**

**Комментарий:**

The ātmā, riding on the mind, also goes. When the mind moves, the ātmā moves.

### Text 40

*janma tv ātmatayā puṁsaḥ sarva-bhāvena bhūri-da*  
*viṣaya-svīkṛtiṁ prāhur yathā svapna-manorathaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O most charitable Uddhava! What is called birth is simply a person’s total identification with a new body. One accepts the new body just as one completely accepts the experience of a dream or a fantasy as reality.**

**Комментарий:**

In a dream, the past appears like the present.

### Text 46

*mā svasya karma-bījena jāyate so ’py ayaṁ pumān*  
*mriyate vāmaro bhrāntyā yathāgnir dāru-saṁyutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**A person does not actually take birth out of the seed of** ***karma*****, nor, being immortal, does he die. By illusion the living being appears to be born and to die, just as fire in connection with firewood appears to begin and then cease to exist though the element lasts for the lifetime of Brahmā.**

**Комментарий:**

Even for the ignorant people, birth and death do not exist. Their existence is like mistaking a rope for a snake. This is Śrīdhara Svāmī’s explanation.

### Text 53

*nṛtyato gāyataḥ paśyan yathaivānukaroti tān*  
*evaṁ buddhi-guṇān paśyann anīho ‘py anukāryate*

**Перевод:**

**Just as one may imitate persons whom one sees dancing and singing, similarly the soul, although never the doer of material activities, is thus forced to imitate the qualities of the intelligence.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of the qualities of intelligence, a jīva has false knowledge, since the observer and the object observed have different qualities.

### Text 57

*tasmād uddhava mā bhuṅkṣva viṣayān asad-indriyaiḥ*  
*ātmāgrahaṇa-nirbhātaṁ paśya vaikalpikaṁ bhramam*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O Uddhava, do not try to enjoy sense objects with the material senses. Recognize that ignorance based on false identity with the body, which produces non-attainment of the self.**

**Комментарий:**

Though speaking to Uddhava, he is teaching others. The Lord himself says:

*noddhavo ’ṇv api man-nyūno yad guṇair nārditaḥ prabhuḥ*  
*ato mad-vayunaṁ loka grāhayann iha tiṣṭhatu*

**Uddhava is not less than me, because he is master of** ***māyā*** **and not at all lacking in any spiritual quality. He should remain on this earth, giving knowledge of me to the world. (SB 3.4.31)**

### Text 61

*su-duḥṣaham imaṁ manya ātmany asad-atikramam*  
*viduṣām api viśvātman prakṛtir hi balīyasī*  
*ṛte tvad-dharma-niratān śāntāṁs te caraṇālayān*

**Перевод:**

**O soul of the universe! It is very difficult for a person to tolerate the offenses committed against him by ignorant people. Even a person who knows the method of toleration has strong intolerance in his nature. Only your devotees, who are fixed in your qualities and who have achieved peace by residing at your lotus feet, are devoid of this intolerance.**

**Комментарий:**

Only persons who engage in hearing about you and glorifying you do not have intolerance. This is not surprising for me. You have given examples of others in this chapter, not the devotees.

## Chapter Twenty-three

### Text 4

*kathayanti mahat puṇyam itihāsam ihoddhava*  
*tam ahaṁ varṇayiṣyāmi nibodha su-samāhitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! In this regard a most purifying story is told, and I shall now describe it to you. Please listen with attention.**

**Комментарий:**

He illustrates with a story.

### Text 10

*tad-avadhyāna-visrasta- puṇya-skandhasya bhūri-da*  
*artho ’py agacchan nidhanaṁ bahv-āyāsa-pariśramaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O magnanimous Uddhava, by his neglect of these** ***devatās*** **he depleted his stock of piety and all his wealth. He had gained this wealth with great fatigue and effort.**

**Комментарий:**

Some portion of wealth only disappeared. Because of good impressions, with a desire for liberation, he offered the remaining portion wealth to the Lord.

### Text 13

*tasyaivaṁ dhyāyato dīrghaṁ naṣṭa-rāyas tapasvinaḥ*  
*khidyato bāṣpa-kaṇṭhasya nirvedaḥ su-mahān abhūt*

**Перевод:**

**Meditating for a long time, having lost his fortune and feeling great pain and lamentation, his throat choked up with tears, he experienced a powerful feeling of renunciation.**

**Комментарий:**

Though miserable, overcoming all offenses, a special impression from long past arose.

### Text 28

*nūnaṁ me bhagavāṁs tuṣṭaḥ sarva-deva-mayo hariḥ*  
*yena nīto daśām etāṁ nirvedaś cātmanaḥ plavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, who comprises all the** ***devatās,*** **must be satisfied with me. He has brought me to this suffering condition and detachment, which is the boat to carry me over this ocean of material life.**

**Комментарий:**

From his impressions, he realized a relationship with the Lord. Since sacrifices involved the Lord, the Lord’s worship manifested at that time.

### Text 29

*so ’haṁ kālāvaśeṣeṇa śoṣayiṣye ’ṅgam ātmanaḥ*  
*apramatto ’khila-svārthe yadi syāt siddha ātmani*

**Перевод:**

**I will perform austerities and with full attention I shall meditate on the lotus feet of the Lord. If the remainder of my life is like this, I shall reach perfection.**

**Комментарий:**

If the remainder of my life is like this, concentrating with attention on the Lord (*ātmani*) who is highest human goal, having direct vision of him, I will destroy the gross and subtle bodies (*aṅgam*).

### Text 31

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*ity abhipretya manasā hy āvantyo dvija-sattamaḥ*  
*unmucya hṛdaya-granthīn śānto bhikṣur abhūn muniḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: His mind thus determined, that most excellent Avantī** ***brāhmaṇa*** **was able to untie the knots of self-interest caused by** ***ahaṅkāra.*** **He then assumed the role of a peaceful and silent** ***sannyāsī*** **mendicant.**

**Комментарий:**

*Bhikṣuḥ* means sannyāsī.

### Text 45

*dānaṁ sva-dharmo niyamo yamaś ca*  
*śrutaṁ ca karmāṇi ca sad-vratāni*  
*sarve mano-nigraha-lakṣaṇāntāḥ*  
*paro hi yogo manasaḥ samādhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Charity, prescribed duties,** ***niyama*** **and** ***yama,*** **hearing from scripture, pious works and purifying vows all have as their final aim the subduing of the mind, since control of the mind is the best** ***yoga.***

**Комментарий:**

Everything aims at controlling all mental functions (*manas*). More than having knowledge in the mind, the jīva must have natural knowledge of the Lord. Without that, the mental functions cannot be controlled.

### Text 50

*janas tu hetuḥ sukha-duḥkhayoś cet*  
*kim ātmanaś cātra hi bhaumayos tat*  
*jihvāṁ kvacit sandaśati sva-dadbhis*  
*tad-vedanāyāṁ katamāya kupyet*

**Перевод:**

**If you say that people are the cause of my happiness and distress, then where is the place for the soul in such a conception? Happiness and distress pertain not to the soul but simply to the interactions of two material bodies. If someone bites his tongue with his own teeth, at whom can he become angry when he suffers?**

**Комментарий:**

Though the jīva is the main factor in all bodies, what is its role if people are the cause of happiness and distress? The same goes for the tongue.

### Text 51

*duḥkhasya hetur yadi devatās tu*  
*kim ātmanas tatra vikārayos tat*  
*yad aṅgam aṅgena nihanyate kvacit*  
*krudhyeta kasmai puruṣaḥ sva-dehe*

**Перевод:**

**If you say that the** ***devatās*** **who rule the bodily senses cause suffering, still, what role does the** ***ātmā*** **have, since two** ***devatās*** **become the causes and objects of infliction? Since the** ***devatās*** **operate all the limbs in all bodies, when one limb of the body attacks another limb in the same body, with whom can the person in that body be angry?**

**Комментарий:**

When someone’s’ hand hits the face, at whom does one become angry? Can one become angry at the devatā? Indra, lord of the hand, is in my body and the other person’s body. How can one become angry at him?

### Text 52

*ātmā yadi syāt sukha-duḥkha-hetuḥ*  
*kim anyatas tatra nija-svabhāvaḥ*  
*na hy ātmano ’nyad yadi tan mṛṣā syāt*  
*krudhyeta kasmān na*

**Перевод:**

**If the** ***jīva*** **were the cause of happiness and distress, because it is conscious, then we could not blame others, since happiness and distress would be simply the nature of the** ***jīva.*** **Only** ***jīva*** **exists anyway, but if you say something else exists, it is a superimposition on the jīva. Since happiness and distress do not actually exist in this concept, why become angry at oneself or others?**

**Комментарий:**

It is superimposed on the jīva by ignorance (*mṛṣā*).

### Text 55

*kālas tu hetuḥ sukha-duḥkhayoś cet*  
*kim ātmanas tatra tad-ātmako ’sau*  
*nāgner hi tāpo na himasya tat syāt*  
*krudhyeta kasmai na parasya dvandvam*

**Перевод:**

**If we accept time as the cause of happiness and distress, that experience still cannot apply to the spirit soul, since time is a manifestation of the Lord’s spiritual potency and the living entities are also expansions of the Lord’s spiritual potency. Fire does not burn its own flames or sparks, nor does the cold harm its own snowflakes. The** ***jīva*** **is transcendental and beyond the experience of material happiness and distress. At whom, therefore, should one become angry?**

**Комментарий:**

The jīva is an aṁśa of the Lord, and time and the Lord are one. Thus the jīva is also similar to time (*tad-ātmakaḥ*).

### Text 56

*na kenacit kvāpi kathañcanāsya*  
*dvandvoparāgaḥ parataḥ parasya*  
*yathāhamaḥ saṁsṛti-rūpiṇaḥ syād*  
*evaṁ prabuddho na bibheti bhūtaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The influence of happiness and suffering for the** ***jīva,*** **who is superior to all else, cannot arise from any means proposed by anyone. It arises only from the mind, which gives shape to** ***saṁsāra.*** **One who becomes enlightened does not fear, though covered with matter.**

**Комментарий:**

The jīva who is by his svarūpa beyond māyā (*parasya*) is superior to other things *(parataḥ*).

### Text 57

*etāṁ sa āsthāya parātma-niṣṭhām*  
*adhyāsitāṁ pūrvatamair maharṣibhiḥ*  
*ahaṁ tariṣyāmi duranta-pāraṁ*  
*tamo mukundāṅghri-niṣevayaiva*

**Перевод:**

**Becoming fixed in** ***ātmā*** **and slightly fixed in Paramātmā, as established by the previous sages, I shall cross over the insurmountable ocean of nescience by service to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The mind should be fixed in Paramātmā. Without service to the feet of Mukunda, there will be disturbance. Considering in this way, there are problems in fixing the mind on him. I will take support of service to the Lord. The Lord spoke correctly:

*su-duḥṣaham imaṁ manya ātmany asad-atikramam*  
*viduṣām api viśvātman prakṛtir hi balīyasī*  
*ṛte tvad-dharma-niratān śāntāṁs te caraṇālayān*

**O soul of the universe! It is very difficult for a person to tolerate the offenses committed against him by ignorant people. Even a person who knows the method of toleration has strong intolerance in his nature. Only your devotees, who are fixed in your qualities and who have achieved peace by residing at your lotus feet, are devoid of this intolerance. (SB 11.22.61)**

### Text 59

*sukha-duḥkha-prado nānyaḥ puruṣasyātma-vibhramaḥ*  
*mitrodāsīna-ripavaḥ saṁsāras tamasaḥ kṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**No other force besides bewilderment of the mind makes the soul experience happiness and distress.** ***Saṁsāra*** **in the form of friends, neutral parties and enemies are caused by ignorance.**

**Комментарий:**

Saṁsāra in the form of friends, neutrals and enemies gives happiness and distress. Saṁsāra is nothing else but this. It is produced by ignorance. It causes bewilderment of the mind (*ātma-vibrhamaḥ*)

## Chapter Twenty-four

### Text 1

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*atha te sampravakṣyāmi sāṅkhyaṁ pūrvair viniścitam*  
*yad vijñāya pumān sadyo jahyād vaikalpikaṁ bhramam*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: Now I shall describe to you Sāṅkhya, which has been perfectly established by ancient authorities. By understanding this, a person can immediately give up the illusion of identity with the body.**

**Комментарий:**

In his commentary Śrīdhara Svāmī uses the word *prakṛti*. This is also called *pradhāna.*

### Text 2

*āsīj jñānam atho artha ekam evāvikalpitam*  
*yadā viveka-nipuṇā ādau kṛta-yuge ’yuge*

**Перевод:**
