**Considering that the three states of the intelligence arising from the** ***guṇas*** **are created by my** ***avidyā*** **within me, being firmly convinced of your nature as** ***ātmā,*** **and cutting the three states by the sharp sword of knowledge, by inference and by scriptural statements, worship me, the destroyer of all doubts. (SB 11.3.33)**

### Text 24

*nātmā vapuḥ pārthivam indriyāṇi*  
*devā hy asur vāyur jalam hutāśaḥ*  
*mano ’nna-mātraṁ dhiṣaṇā ca sattvam*  
*ahaṅkṛtiḥ khaṁ kṣitir artha-sāmyam*

**Перевод:**

**The material body made of earth, the senses, their presiding** ***devatās, prāṇa,*** **intelligence, mind,** ***citta*****, and** ***ahaṅkāra*****, are not the** ***ātmā.*** **The external air, water, fire, ether and earth, the** ***tan-mātras*** **and** ***prakṛti*** **are not the** ***ātmā*****.**

**Комментарий:**

He lists various objects which are like rays of the sun, thereby refuting contrary ideas.

### Text 25

*samāhitaiḥ kaḥ karaṇair guṇātmabhir*  
*guṇo bhaven mat-suvivikta-dhāmnaḥ*  
*vikṣipyamāṇair uta kiṁ nu dūṣaṇaṁ*  
*ghanair upetair vigatai raveḥ kim*

**Перевод:**

**For one who has properly realized my form, what credit is there if his senses—mere products of the material modes—are perfectly concentrated in meditation? And on the other hand, what blame is incurred if his senses happen to become agitated? Indeed, what does it mean to the sun if the clouds come and go?**

**Комментарий:**

For the person fixed on the form of the Lord, there is no dependence on purification of the jīva. For the person fixed on the form of the lord, is it good quality to have controlled senses, and a bad quality to have unsteady senses?

### Text 26

*yathā nabho vāyv-analāmbu-bhū-guṇair*  
*gatāgatair vartu-guṇair na sajjate*  
*tathākṣaraṁ sattva-rajas-tamo-malair*  
*ahaṁ-mateḥ saṁsṛti-hetubhiḥ param*

**Перевод:**

**Just as the sky is not affected by the coming and going of the qualities of air, fire, water and earth, or by the seasons, so the jīva fixed in knowledge is not affected by** ***ahaṅkāra*** **or by contamination of** ***sattva, rajas*** **or** ***tamas*****, the causes of material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

For the supreme entity like the sun globe there is no relationship at all with matter. That is shown by an example. Causes of saṁsāra exist only (*param*) for the jīva filled with ahaṅkāra and upādhis (*ahaṁ-mateḥ*) and not for the jīva having fixed jñāna-śakti.

### Text 27

*tathāpi saṅgaḥ parivarjanīyo*  
*guṇeṣu māyā-raciteṣu tāvat*  
*mad-bhakti-yogena dṛḍhena yāvad*  
*rajo nirasyeta manaḥ-kaṣāyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nevertheless, until one has completely eliminated from his mind all attraction to sense objects by firmly practicing devotional service to me, one must very carefully avoid associating with the material modes, which are produced by my illusory energy.**

**Комментарий:**

There is limitation for the jñānī not having realization. He must become successful by bhakti.

### Text 28

*yathāmayo ’sādhu cikitsito nṛṇāṁ*  
*punaḥ punaḥ santudati prarohan*  
*evaṁ mano ’pakva-kaṣāya-karma*  
*kuyoginaṁ vidhyati sarva-saṅgam*

**Перевод:**

**Just as an improperly treated disease recurs and gives repeated distress to the patient, the mind that is not completely purified of its perverted tendencies and** ***karma*** **will remain attached to material things and repeatedly torment the imperfect** ***yogī.***

**Комментарий:**

In spite of obstacles, the yogī is not destroyed. Later, it will be said in relation to the imperfect yogī:

*yoga-caryām imāṁ yogī vicaran mad-apāśrayaḥ*  
*nāntarāyair vihanyeta niḥspṛhaḥ sva-sukhānubhūḥ*

**The** ***yogī*** **who has taken shelter of me, free from hankering because he experiences the happiness of the soul within, is never defeated by obstacles while executing this process of** ***yoga.*** **(SB 11.28.44)**

### Text 30

*karoti karma kriyate ca jantuḥ*  
*kenāpy asau codita ā-nipatāt*  
*na tatra vidvān prakṛtau sthito ’pi*  
*nivṛtta-tṛṣṇaḥ sva-sukhānubhūtyā*

**Перевод:**

**The** ***jīva*** **performs action, inspired by Paramātmā, and is made to take a different body by that action. This cycle continues until universal devastation. The** ***jñānī,*** **however, though situated in his body, having experienced his own constitutional bliss, gives up all material desires and does not engage in action or its effects.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses describe how the perfect yogī has no destruction.

### Text 33

*pūrvaṁ gṛhītaṁ guṇa-karma-citram*  
*ajñānam ātmany aviviktam aṅga*  
*nivartate tat punar īkṣayaiva*  
*na gṛhyate nāpi visṛyya ātmā*

**Перевод:**

**In the state of bondage, ignorance which made into variety by actions created by the** ***guṇas*** **was accepted as the self, without investigation. O Uddhava! Ignorance is destroyed by** ***jñāna.*** **But** ***ātmā*** **is never accepted or rejected.**

**Комментарий:**

The jīva becomes different because of accepting and rejecting guṇas and karma. The relationship with the guṇas and karmas arises from ignorance.

### Text 34

*yathā hi bhānor udayo nṛ-cakṣuṣāṁ*  
*tamo nihanyān na tu sad vidhatte*  
*evaṁ samīkṣā nipuṇā satī me*  
*hanyāt tamisraṁ puruṣasya buddheḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the sun rises, it destroys the darkness covering men’s eyes, but it does not create the eye, which in fact was existent all along. Similarly, my** ***vidyā-śakti*** **will destroy the covering on knowledge for a person who has my glance of mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

Revelation for the Lord’s aṁśa arises spontaneously from destruction of ignorance, by the Lord’s mercy. The particle of consciousness is not created. *Me samīkṣa* means (having my glance of mercy).

### Text 35

*eṣa svayaṁ-jyotir ajo ’prameyo*  
*mahānubhūtiḥ sakalānubhūtiḥ*  
*eko ’dvitīyo vacasāṁ virāme*  
*yeneṣitā vāg-asavaś caranti*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord is self-luminous, unborn and immeasurable. He is pure consciousness. Knowing him, everything is known. He is one alone, and without compare. He is beyond words but by him the power of speech and the life airs are set into motion.**

**Комментарий:**

Revelation of *tat* (the Lord) reveals everything on its own, by manifesting to the ātmā.

By knowing him, everything is known *(sakalānubhūtiḥ*), since he is all knowledge (*mahānubhūtiḥ*).

### Text 36

*etāvān ātma-sammoho yad vikalpas tu kevale*  
*ātman ṛte svam ātmānam avalambo na yasya hi*

**Перевод:**

**Since only one** ***ātmā*** **exists, seeing duality is one’s own bewilderment. It has no basis except the** ***jīva*** **himself.**

**Комментарий:**

“Duality is produced when illusion takes shelter of the pure Brahman or tat-padārtha. It is said *āśrayatva-viṣayatva-bhāginī nirvibhāga-citir eva kevalā*: the indivisible consciousness divides into āśraya and viṣaya. (Sārīrika-bhāsya). How is it that by your mercy, illusion of another entity takes place. Are you Brahman or the Lord, who creates upādhis resulting in illusion?”

*Vikalpa* means illusion of duality. The support for illusion exists only for the jīva, because there is no support for illusion in that which is devoid of relationship with anything else (*kevale*).

*hlādinī sandhinī saṁvit tvayy ekā sarva-saṁsthitau \|*  
*hlāda-tāpa-kārī miśrā tvayi no guṇa-varjite \|\|*

**In you who are the shelter of all spiritual qualities exist the energies of hlādinī, sandhinī and saṁvit. In you who are devoid of material qualities, the mixture of happiness and distress found in the material world does not exist. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12.68)**

*hlādinyā saṁvidā śliṣṭaḥ saccidānanda īśvaraḥ \|*  
*svāvidyā-saṁvṛto jīvaḥ saṅkleśa-nikarākaraḥ \|\|*

**The Lord full of eternity, knowledge and bliss is embraced by the hlādinī and saṁvit śaktis. The jīva, the very form of suffering, is surrounded by his own ignorance. (Sarvajña-sūkta)**

### Text 37

*yan nāmākṛtibhir grāhyaṁ pañca-varṇam abādhitam*  
*vyarthenāpy artha-vādo ’yaṁ dvayaṁ paṇḍita-māninām*

**Перевод:**

**The duality of the five material elements is perceived only in terms of names and forms. Those who say this duality is real are pseudo scholars vainly proposing the non-existent.**

**Комментарий:**

“If duality is superimposed upon one’s svarūpa, when knowledge arises by the mercy of the Lord, the illusion should be understood. But it is not so. It is a combination like cooked grains. Why should illusion disappear by knowledge alone?” Some raise this doubt. Though it is imposed by the ignorance of the jīva, duality does not exist in the way that silver exists in the shop of a merchant. Rather without beginning, the previous illusion generates the later imposition. Then what is the Lord? What is his mercy? Others raise this doubt. These doubts are expressed in this verse.

Forms made of the five elements are perceived with names etc. and cannot be annulled by thought, since it is accomplished by the combination of the perceiver and other factors. Some think in this way. They think that objects are words only, without a substantial substance. Only falsely learned persons think of duality, and not the truly learned. Since perceiver and perceived, the source of form and the form, the spiritual and the material, light and darkness are impossible to combine, the perception of duality arises by ignorance alone. The six elements are simply superimposed. It is like the horns of a rabbit, who actually has upraised ears.

## Chapter Twenty-nine

### Text 1

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*su-dustarām imāṁ manye yoga-caryām anātmanaḥ*  
*yathāñjasā pumān siddhyet tan me brūhy añjasācyuta*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O Acyuta, I think that the method of** ***yoga*** **described by you is very difficult for one who cannot control his mind. Therefore please explain to me immediately how someone can more quickly attain perfection.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 326:**

Though the Lord speaks of results generated by bhakti accompanied by jñāna at the end of the previous chapter, Uddhava, the greatest devotee, cannot accept even a little jñāna in bhakti. Because it is difficult in most cases, one will not achieve the final result and because bhakti, which he desired to hear about, is easy to execute, and one will definitely achieve the results, bhakti alone should be practiced. That is the intention of his statement in the two verses.

### Text 2

*prāyaśaḥ puṇdarīkākṣa yuñyanto yogino manaḥ*  
*viṣīdanty asamādhānān mano-nigraha-karśitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Lord! Generally those** ***yogīs*** **who try to absorb their minds in Brahman experience frustration. Because of their inability to perfect** ***samādhi*****, they become fatigued in their attempt to bring the mind under control.**

### Text 3

*athāta ānanda-dughaṁ padāmbujaṁ*  
*haṁsāḥ śrayerann aravinda-locana*  
*sukhaṁ nu viśveśvara yoga-karmabhis*  
*tvan-māyayāmī vihatā na māninaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Lord of the universe! Therefore, discerning men joyfully take shelter of your lotus feet, the source of bliss. But those who take pride in their accomplishments in** ***yoga*** **and** ***karma*** **fail to take shelter of you and are defeated by your illusory energy.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 326:**

With no regard for jñāna, practicing bhakti alone, devotees practice bhakti to the form of Kṛṣṇa alone, without giving attention to the results of jñāna and yoga. That is explained in the next four verses.

Because some (*yogīs*) are depressed in their attempts, therefore (*athātaḥ*) those skillful at discerning the essence (*haṁsāḥ*) happily (*sukham*) serve with certainty (*nu*) your lotus feet, filled with all bliss. Since Uddhava was directly seeing Kṛṣṇa’s feet when he was speaking, he does not say “your lotus feet” but simply “the lotus feet.” These pure devotees (*amī*) are not obstructed by activities of yoga, which is your māyā, because of which they do not become proud. In this sādhana they think that they achieve results from the Lord’s unconditional mercy to the fallen, not by their own efforts in yoga.

### Text 4

*kiṁ citram acyuta tavaitad aśeṣa-bandho*  
*dāseṣv ananya-śaraṇesu yad ātma-sāttvam*  
*yo ’rocayat saha mṛgaiḥ svayam īśvarāṇāṁ*  
*śrīmat-kirīṭa-taṭa-pīḍita-pāda-pīṭhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O infallible Lord! O friend of all beings! It is not very astonishing that you are dependent on your servants who have taken exclusive shelter of you. As Rāmacandra, you displayed special affection for monkeys such as Hanumān while** ***devatās*** **shook your foot pedestal with the tips of their crowns,**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 327:**

The devotee receives the results of jñāna and yoga, but not only that, much more. O friend of the completely surrendered (*aśeṣa-bandho*), or friend of all, even the demons! You give benefit to all without discrimination in the form of liberation etc. This is not astonishing for you to do. You are dependent (*ātma-sāttvam*) on your completely surrendered devotees, who are averse to jñāna and yoga, such as Bali. For example you say:

*na sādhayati māṁ yogo na sāṅkhyaṁ dharma uddhava*  
*na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo yathā bhaktir mamorjitā*

**O Uddhava! I am attained by unmixed bhakti. I cannot be attained by mystic yoga, Sāṅkhya philosophy, dharma, Vedic study, austerity or renunciation. (SB 11.14.20)**

You do not show any prejudice for species or qualities among the living beings who surrender. This is seen your intimate pastimes. You enjoyed sakhya-bhāva (*saha*) with the animals of Vṛndāvana. But what is your other nature? Śiva, Brahmā and others (*īśvarānām)* bowed to your foot pedestal. You give liberation, which is the highest fruit for the jñānīs and yogīs, to demons. But you are dependent on your servants like the Pāṇḍavas. You act as their friend, messenger and guard. The intention of Uddhava is to say that bhakti to Kṛṣṇa alone is the process.

### Text 5

*taṁ tvākhilātma-dayiteśvaram āśritānāṁ*  
*sarvārtha-daṁ sva-kṛta-vid visṛjeta ko nu*  
*ko vā bhajet kim api vismṛtaye ’nu bhūtyai*  
*kiṁ vā bhaven na tava pāda-rajo-juṣāṁ naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**What person who knows the mercy that you show to your devotees could reject you, the dearest among all** ***jīvas*****, the Supreme Lord of all, who gives all perfections to the devotees who take shelter of you? Who would reject you and accept something for the sake of material enjoyment or liberation, which simply leads to forgetfulness of you? And what lack is there for us who are engaged in the service of the dust of your lotus feet?**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 328:**

The result is described. What person who knows what favors you have done for him (*sva-kṛta-vit*), having revealed to him your beauty as described in SB 3.28.13, could reject you, as described in the previous line (*tam tvā)*? There are some persons like the following:

*evaṁ harau bhagavati pratilabdha-bhāvo*  
*bhaktyā dravad-dhṛdaya utpulakaḥ pramodāt*  
*autkaṇṭhya-bāṣpa-kalayā muhur ardyamānas*  
*tac cāpi citta-baḍiśaṁ śanakair viyuṅkte*

**The unfortunate yogī who has developed love for the Lord, full of all sweet qualities, whose heart is somewhat soft because of devotion, whose body hairs stand on end in ecstasy, who is constantly overcome with intense tears of joy, gradually withdraws his hook-like mind from the Lord’s form. (SB 3.28.34)**

But no one can give you up: he who gives you up is most ungrateful.

And who are you? You are dearer than a million lives to all beings by your nature (*akhilātma-dayita*) and are the controller *(īśvaram*). You give everything to those who take shelter of you. The word *nu* indicates conjecture. Who would accept devatās or another sādhana, and reject you, for wealth and power (*bhūtyai)* or for liberation (*vismṛtaye)?* No one would do so. All these results are included in bhakti to you that we perform. What is not achieved by those who worship your foot dust? The word *vā* in the last line indicates disinterest in these results.

*yat karmabhir yat tapasā jñāna-vairāgyataś ca yat*  
*yogena dāna-dharmeṇa śreyobhir itarair api*  
*sarvaṁ mad-bhakti-yogena mad-bhakto labhate ’ñjasā*  
*svargāpavargaṁ mad-dhāma kathañcid yadi vāñchati*

**Everything that can be achieved by karma, penance, jñāna, vairāgya, mystic yoga, charity, dharma and all other auspicious means of perfecting life is easily achieved by my devotee through bhakti. If somehow or other my devotee desires Svarga, liberation, or residence in my abode, he easily achieves such benedictions. (SB 11.20.32-33)**

### Text 6

*naivopayanty apacitiṁ kavayas taveśa*  
*brahmāyuṣāpi kṛtam ṛddha-mudaḥ smarantaḥ*  
*yo ’ntar bahis tanu-bhṛtām aśubhaṁ vidhunvann*  
*ācārya-caittya-vapuṣā sva-gatiṁ vyanakti*

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord! Intelligent persons cannot fully express their indebtedness to you, even if they were endowed with the lifetime of Brahmā, because on remembering what you have done form them, their joy increases even more: appearing externally as** ***guru*** **and internally as Paramātmā, you reveal the goal of** ***prema*** **to the devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 328:**

O Lord! The wise (*kavayaḥ*), even with a life span like Brahmā’s, remembering your assistance (*kṛtam*), becoming ever increasingly blissful (*ṛddha-mudaḥ*) because of bhakti to you, cannot see (*upayanti*) how they can repay you (*apacitim*). Therefore they never give you up. What you have done is described. For some among all embodied souls, those who have received your mercy, you destroy obstacles *(aśubham*) to your bhakti and reveal understanding of yourself (*sva-gatim*) externally through a guru (*ācārya-vapuṣā*) and internally as a form revealed through meditation (*caittya-vapuṣā*).

### Text 7

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity uddhavenāty-anurakta-cetasā*  
*pṛṣṭo jagat-krīḍanakaḥ sva-śaktibhiḥ*  
*gṛhīta-mūrti-traya īśvareśvaro*  
*jagāda sa-prema-manohara-smitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus questioned by the most affectionate Uddhava, Kṛṣṇa, the supreme controller of all controllers, who utilizes the universe for his pastimes and assumes three forms by his energies, began to reply, displaying his attractive smile filled with love.**

**Комментарий:**

Without regard for being the lord of lords, Kṛṣṇa spoke with affection. As the lord of lords he has three forms. Through his śakti he has vibhūtis endowed with some of his portions. That is the lowest type. He manifests as Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva. That is the medium type. He manifests as the lord of Mahā-viṣṇu. That is the highest type.

### Text 12

*mām eva sarva-bhūteṣu bahir antar apāvṛtam*  
*īkṣetātmani cātmānaṁ yathā kham amalāśayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With a pure heart the** ***jñānī*** **should see the complete form of Paramātmā, within all beings and also within oneself, present both externally and internally, just like the ether spreads everywhere without being contaminated.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 330:**

The Lord then speaks about the greatness of bhakti. To devotees like Uddhava, he speaks of pure bhakti in four verses. Then for others not so inclined, he considers by his mercy other things in order to encourage his worship. Since people are generally inclined to compete with others, he considered that they could only worship his form as antaryāmī as a means of somehow making them favorable. In order to make them quickly give up the competitive mood and turn towards the Lord, he teaches worship of himself in the form of his portion, the antaryāmī.

*atha vā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna \|*  
*viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam ekāṁśena sthito jagat \|\|*

**But what is the use of knowing all these individual vibhūtis, Arjuna? Please understand: by just one portion of myself, I am firmly established in this universe. (BG 10.42)**

Thus the Lord says:

*mām eva sarva-bhūteṣu bahir antar apāvṛtam*  
*īkṣetātmani cātmānaṁ yathā kham amalāśayaḥ*

**With a pure heart one should see me, the complete form of Paramātmā, within all beings and also within oneself, present both externally and internally, just like the ether spreads everywhere without being contaminated. (SB 11.29.12)**

The commentary says, “In three verses the Lord speaks about essential bhakti. One should see me situated as the Lord (*ātmānam*) in all beings (*ātmani*). That Lord is complete, being outside and inside (*bahiḥ antaḥ*). How can this be? He cannot be covered or restrained (*apāvrṭam*). How is this possible? He is without limbs and spreads everywhere like ether.” One should see only me, the form of Kṛṣṇa, not the form of antaryāmī. In this manner, it becomes essential (antaraṅga) bhakti.

### Text 13-14

*iti sarvāṇi bhūtāni mad-bhāvena mahā-dyute*  
*sabhājayan manyamāno jñānaṁ kevalam āśritaḥ*  
*brāhmaṇe pukkase stene brahmaṇye ’rke sphuliṅgake*  
*akrūre krūrake caiva sama-dṛk paṇḍito mataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O brilliant Uddhava! The person who respects all beings as Brahman and contemplates this, who sees equally the** ***brāhmaṇa*** **and the outcaste, the thief and the giver of charity to** ***brāhmaṇas*** **, the sun and the sparks of fire, the gentle and the cruel, is a true** ***jñānī.***

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 331:**

Though taking shelter of the vision of antaryāmī (*kevalaṁ jñānam*), honoring and thinking of all entities as being situated as my form (*mad-bhāvena*) in the manner previously explained, one is considered to be learned. He sees me in the brāhmaṇa and others.

### Text 19

*ayaṁ hi sarva-kalpānāṁ sadhrīcīno mato mama*  
*mad-bhāvaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu mano-vāk-kāya-vṛttibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I consider this process—using one’s mind, words and bodily functions for realizing me within all living beings—to be the easiest process of the** ***jñānī*** **to realize Brahman*****.***

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 332:**

This type of worship quickly destroys competition. (verse 14). There is no other easy process for attaining Brahman for the *jñānī.* (verse 15) To practice this vision one should offer respects to all beings. (16) The result of this worship is manifestation of Kṛṣṇa everywhere spontaneously. (verse 17) Referring to verse 18 there is a similar usage of the word *Brahman* in the verse where the Lord speaks to the Pracetas:

*navyavad dhṛd aye yaj jño brahmaitad brahma-vādibhiḥ*  
*na muhyanti na śocanti na hṛṣyanti yato gatāḥ*

**Those who have attained my form which is known as Brahman by the followers of Brahman are not bewildered. They do not lament and do not rejoice, since I, full of knowledge, have entered their fresh lotus hearts. (SB 4.30.20)**

The commentary says that Brahman refers to a fresh manifestation of Bhagavān. Thus the result of this worship is seeing Bhagavān everywhere. Or the word Brahman is used in Gopāla-tāpanī to indicate Kṛṣṇa in the following:

*yo ’vatārāṇāṁ madhye śreṣṭho ’vatāraḥ ko bhavati \|*  
*yena lokās tuṣṭā devās tuṣṭā bhavanti \|*  
*yaṁ smṛtvā muktā asmāt saṁsārād bhavanti \|*  
*kathaṁ vāsyāvatārasya brahmatā bhavati \|*

**Brahmā spoke. Who is the best among the avatāras, by whom all people and devatās become satisfied, by whose remembrance people become liberated from saṁsāra? How can this avatāra be Svayam Bhagavān (*****brahmatā*****)? (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad 2.24)**

Thus the result of the process is to see Parabrahman in human form. After stating this, Kṛṣṇa praises such worship as topmost:

*ayaṁ hi sarva-kalpānāṁ sadhrīcīno mato mama*  
*mad-bhāvaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu mano-vāk-kāya-vṛttibhiḥ*

**I consider this process—using one’s mind, words and bodily functions for realizing me within all living beings—to be the easiest process to realize me*****.*** **(SB 11.29.19)**

I consider this to be the correct method (*sadhrīcīnaḥ*) among all methods (*sarva-kalānām*): thinking of (*bhāvaḥ*) my form (*mat*) in all beings.

### Text 20

*na hy aṅgopakrame dhvaṁso mad-dharmasyoddhavāṇv api*  
*mayā vyavasitaḥ samyaṅ nirguṇatvād anāśiṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! Because I have personally established it, the process of** ***niṣkāma-bhakti*** **is beyond the** ***guṇas.*** **Thus even by starting and not completing the process, there is no destruction of results.**

**Комментарий:**

There are no obstacles related to my dharma, what to speak of anything having to assist it.

### Text 21

*yo yo mayi pare dharmaḥ kalpyate niṣphalāya cet*  
*tad-āyāso nirarthaḥ syād bhayāder iva sattama*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava, greatest of saints! If** ***bhakti*** **is offered to me without personal motivation, endeavoring for results is useless, just as expressions of fear or lamentation are useless in dangerous situations.**

**Комментарий:**

What to speak of direct bhakti, even indirect bhakti (bhakti by superimposition) is glorified.

**Bhakti Sandarbha 33:**

Dharma prescribed by the Vedas done as an offering to me, if offered without desire for results (*niṣphalāya kalpate*), dharma done with effort, will not be useless (*nirarthaḥ*). When the actions are done without desire for enjoyment, they do not create obstacles for bhakti and are thus not useless. Since acts are offered to Kṛṣṇa favorably, how much more useful they are than acts offered unfavorably, which also give results. This is made clear by an example. The efforts of Kaṁsa and others, related to the Lord by fear or hatred, were not useless since those efforts gave them liberation.

### Text 22

*eṣā buddhimatāṁ buddhir manīṣā ca manīṣiṇām*  
*yat satyam anṛteneha martyenāpnoti māmṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**The devotee is the most intelligent among the intelligent and the most his temporary body and attains me, the only truth, though he is an inconsequential** ***jīva*****.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhakti is justly glorified since it brings about attainment of me, Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, the cause of all bliss (*amṛtam*) and the cause of all existence (*satyam*).

### Text 23

*eṣa te ’bhihitaḥ kṛtsno brahma-vādasya saṅgrahaḥ*  
*samāsa-vyāsa-vidhinā devānām api durgamaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus have I related to you—both in brief and in detail—a complete survey of Brahman. Even for the** ***devatās,*** **this science is very difficult to comprehend.**

**Комментарий:**

I explained bhakti-yoga (*eṣaḥ*), the means of attaining the Lord, in summarized form (*samāsa-vidhinā*) (SB 10.29.22) and with details (*vyāsa-vidhinā*). (SB 11.7.6) This is difficult to understand even for the devatās fixed in sattva. It is said in the Sixth Canto:

*devānāṁ śuddha-sattvānām ṛṣīṇām amalātmanām \|*  
*bhaktir mukunda-caraṇe na prāyeṇopajāyate \|\|*

***Bhakti*** **to the Lord’s lotus feet rarely develops even in the** ***devatās*** **with minds possessing** ***sattva-guṇa*** **and in pure sages. (SB 6.14.2)**

### Text 24

*abhīkṣṇaśas te gaditaṁ jñānaṁ vispaṣṭa-yuktimat*  
*etad vijñāya mucyeta puruṣo naṣṭa-saṁśayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I have repeatedly spoken this knowledge to you with clear reasoning. Anyone who properly understands it will become free from all doubts and attain liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

Jñāna does not directly result in attainment of the Lord, but liberation.

### Text 25

*su-viviktaṁ tava praśnaṁ mayaitad api dhārayet*  
*sanātanaṁ brahma-guhyaṁ paraṁ brahmādhigacchati*

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who fixes his attention on these clear answers to your questions will attain the eternal secret of the Vedas—the form of the supreme Brahman.**

**Комментарий:**

Searching through everything from previous to later, the result, attaining me, will happen in any case, through sādhana and siddha bhakti, since you are dedicated to me. One will attain param brahma (*brahma guhyam*), me.

*yūyaṁ nṛ-loke bata bhūri-bhāgā*  
*lokaṁ punānā munayo 'bhiyanti*  
*yeṣāṁ gṛhān āvasatīti sākṣād*  
*gūḍhaṁ paraṁ brahma manuṣya-liṅgam*

**You Pāṇḍavas are most fortunate in this world. Sages who purify the planets come and visit your houses because the Supreme Brahman personally resides in your houses in a human form. (SB 7.10.48)**

### Text 26

*ya etan mama bhakteṣu sampradadyāt su-puṣkalam*  
*tasyāhaṁ brahma-dāyasya dadāmy ātmānam ātmanā*

**Перевод:**

**One who liberally disseminates this knowledge among my devotees is the bestower of Brahman. I give myself to him.**

**Комментарий:**

Meeting my devotee brings this result. What more can be said? I become controlled by that devotee (*dadāmy ātmānām*).

### Text 27

*ya etat samadhīyīta pavitraṁ paramaṁ śuci*  
*sa pūyetāhar ahar māṁ jñāna-dīpena darśayan*

**Перевод:**

**He who loudly recites this supreme knowledge, which is the pure and purifying, becomes purified day by day, by revealing me to others with the lamp of knowledge.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of simply reciting this knowledge, without understanding it, is stated.

This knowledge is without any fault (*śuci*) and removes all faults (*paramam pavitram*) of the hearer and reciter. It is not surprising that the reciter becomes purified. Not only that, it shows me by the lamp of knowledge to those who have heard.

### Text 28

*ya etac chraddhayā nityam avyagraḥ śṛṇuyān naraḥ*  
*mayi bhaktiṁ parāṁ kurvan karmabhir na sa badhyate*

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who regularly listens to this knowledge with faith and attention, while engaging in my pure devotional service, will never become bound by** ***karma.***

**Комментарий:**

The special result for those who constantly hear with faith is described.

### Text 29

*apy uddhava tvayā brahma sakhe samavadhāritam*  
*api te vigato mohaḥ śokaś cāsau mano-bhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava! O friend! Have you now completely understood Brahman? Are the confusion and lamentation that arose in your mind now dispelled?**

**Комментарий:**

Overcome with mercy, Kṛṣṇa pacifies Uddhava. Uddhava had confusion concerning the unexpected condition of the devotees and lamentation that they would not attain him again. The conversation you have had with me explained the various results from hearing. Do you have any doubt about these results or concerning my associates?

### Text 30

*naitat tvayā dāmbhikāya nāstikāya śaṭhāya ca*  
*aśuśrūṣor abhaktāya durvinītāya dīyatām*

**Перевод:**

**You should not share this instruction with anyone who is hypocritical, atheistic or dishonest, or with anyone who hears without faith, who is not a devotee, or who is not humble.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Uddhava’s clear understanding, he then teaches using negative and positive statements in two verses.

### Text 31

*etair doṣair vihīnāya brahmaṇyāya priyāya ca*  
*sādhave śucaye brūyād bhaktiḥ syāc chūdra-yoṣitām*

**Перевод:**

**This knowledge should be taught to one who is free from these bad qualities, who is dedicated to the welfare of the** ***brāhmaṇas,*** **and who is kindly disposed, saintly and pure. And if common workers and women are found to have devotion for the Supreme Lord, one should speak it to them.**

**Комментарий:**

If they have bhakti, one should teach this even to śūdras and women. They are also qualified.

### Text 32

*naitad vijñāya jijñāsor jñātavyam avaśiṣyate*  
*pītvā pīyūṣam amṛtaṁ pātavyaṁ nāvaśiṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**When an inquisitive person comes to understand this knowledge, he has nothing further to know. After all, one who has drunk sweet nectar cannot drink anything else.**

**Комментарий:**

Since bhakti is the sādhana and the result, nothing remains to be known. One who has drunk the sweetest nectar cannot drink anything else.

### Text 33

*jñāne karmaṇi yoge ca vārtāyāṁ daṇḍa-dhāraṇe*  
*yāvān artho nṛṇāṁ tāta tāvāṁs te ’haṁ catur-vidhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Through analytical knowledge, ritualistic work, mystic yoga, mundane business and politics, people seek to advance in religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation. Whatever men can accomplish in these multifarious ways I give to my devotee.**

**Комментарий:**

I have taught you in order that you teach others. I am everything, both your sādhana and your sādhya. Jñāna gives liberation, karma gives dharma and kāma. Yoga gives various astonishing siddhis. Occupations and politics give various worldly articles (*artha*). These are the four types mentioned in the verse.

### Text 34

*martyo yadā tyakta-samasta-karmā*  
*niveditātmā vicikīrṣito me*  
*tadāmṛtatvaṁ pratipadyamāno*  
*mayātma-bhūyāya ca kalpate vai*

**Перевод:**

**When a person who gives up all** ***karmas*** **offers himself entirely to** ***guru*** **and eagerly desires to render service to me alone, he achieves freedom from death and, more important, is qualified to be an associate of mine in** ***prema*****.**

**Комментарий:**

Enough of speaking about you. I give the ordinary human the most extraordinary result.

### Text 35

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*sa evam ādarśita-yoga-mārgas*  
*tadottamaḥśloka-vaco niśamya*  
*baddhāñjaliḥ prīty-uparuddha-kaṇṭho*  
*na kiñcid ūce ’śru-pariplutākṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Hearing these words spoken by Kṛṣṇa, and having thus been shown the entire path of** ***yoga*****, Uddhava folded his hands, but his throat choked up with love and his eyes overflowed with tears. Thus he could say nothing.**

**Комментарий:**

He had been shown the complete path of yoga by Kṛṣṇa (*ādarśita-yoga-mārgaḥ*).

### Text 36

*viṣṭabhya cittaṁ praṇayāvaghūrṇaṁ*  
*dhairyeṇa rājan bahu-manyamānaḥ*  
*kṛtāñjaliḥ prāha yadu-pravīraṁ*  
*śīrṣṇā spṛśaṁs tac-caraṇāravindam*

**Перевод:**

**O King! Steadying his mind, which had become overwhelmed with love, with determined effort, Uddhava, thinking himself successful and touching the Lord’s lotus feet with his head, spoke with folded hands to greatest hero of the Yadu dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to cover his rising sorrow of separation, he desired to make himself joyful by thinking of his good fortune of having mercifully attained instructions from Kṛṣṇa (*bahu-manyamānaḥ*).

### Text 37

*śrī-uddhava uvāca*  
*vidrāvito moha-mahāndhakāro*  
*ya āśrito me tava sannidhānāt*  
*vibhāvasoḥ kiṁ nu samīpa-gasya*  
*śītaṁ tamo bhīḥ prabhavanty ajādya*

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava said: O unborn, primeval Lord! My great ignorance has now been dispelled by your merciful association. Indeed, how can cold, darkness and fear exert their power over one who has approached the brilliant sun?**

**Комментарий:**

The great darkness concerning the impossibility of attaining you (*moha-mahāndhakāraḥ*) and the confusion which took shelter of me have gone completely because of your nature of being close by, with a sower of your merciful glance, what to speak of your teachings.

### Text 39

*vṛkṇaś ca me su-dṛḍhaḥ sneha-pāśo*  
*dāśārha-vṛṣṇy-andhaka-sātvateṣu*  
*prasāritaḥ sṛṣṭi-vivṛddhaye tvayā*  
*sva-māyayā hy ātma-subodha-hetinā*

**Перевод:**

**The firm rope of affection for the families of the Dāśārhas, Vṛṣṇis, Andhakas and Sātvatas—a rope you originally cast over me by your illusory energy for the purpose of developing your family—is now cut off by the weapon of knowledge of the self.**

**Комментарий:**

The rope of affection that you spread by your māyā to increase your family, has been cut by the weapon of understanding ātmā, spoken by you to me. That rope of affection for them was accepted by me because they were related to you. Or, the rope of affection was cut by me previous to meeting you, but after the killing of Kaṁsa, by your mercy to your deveotees (*sva-māyayā*), in order to increase the affection of the world for you, it spread out. Your mercy took the form of the weapon of realizing Brahman. How then can I reject it?

### Text 40

*namo ’stu te mahā-yogin prapannam anuśādhi mām*  
*yathā tvac-caraṇāmbhoje ratiḥ syād anapāyinī*

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances unto you, O greatest of** ***yogīs*****! Please instruct me, surrendered to you, so that I may have constant attachment to your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

By your mercy my highest desire will be achieved. With pitiful voice he again prays. Please make me surrendered. He has some special desire in the surrender. There should be constant attraction to your lotus feet.

### Text 41

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*gacchoddhava mayādiṣṭo badary-ākhyaṁ mamāśramam*  
*tatra mat-pāda-tīrthode snānopasparśanaiḥ śuciḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O Uddhava! On my order, go to Badarikāśrama. Purify yourself by sipping and bathing in the holy waters there, which have emanated from my lotus feet.**

### Text 42

*Īkṣayālakanandāyā vidhūtāśeṣa-kalmaṣaḥ*  
*vasāno valkalāny aṅga vanya-bhuk sukha-niḥspṛhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**By your glance you should destroy the unlimited sins present in the Alakanandā River. Dress yourself in bark and eat whatever is naturally available in the forest. Be content and free from desire.**

**Комментарий:**

Even though the attachment to my lotus feet that you prayed for has already been achieved, it will increase spontaneously by separation from me. It does not depend on any other practice. You will undergo difficulties by separation from me. To teach the world act according to sādhana, do not undergo fasting etc. On completing what I desire in terms of teaching the world, your desire will be achieved. This is explained in four and half verses.

Go to that place. By going there and by the nature of following the order, your desire will be fulfilled on its own. There, naturally you will not have desires for worldly happiness. The Lord is established in Badarikāśrama. Situated in pain of separation in the place of my constant pastimes, you will experience great difficulties.

By your glance you will purify the Alakananda River of its sorrow arising from the touch of sinful people with unlimited contamination.

### Text 43-44

*titikṣur dvandva-mātrāṇāṁ suśīlaḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ*  
*śāntaḥ samāhita-dhiyā jñāna-vijñāna-saṁyutaḥ*  
*matto ’nuśikṣitaṁ yat te viviktam anubhāvayan*  
*mayy āveśita-vāk-citto mad-dharma-nirato bhava*  
*ativrajya gatīs tisro mām eṣyasi tataḥ param*

**Перевод:**

**Be tolerant of all dualities, good-natured, self-controlled, peaceful and endowed with knowledge and realization. With fixed attention, reveal to the sages these instructions filled with special discrimination that I have imparted to you. Fix your words and thoughts upon me, and always be absorbed in my qualities. Help the sages cross beyond the conditions of the three** ***guṇas*** **and finally you will come to me.**

**Комментарий:**

Reveal these instructions which were well deliberated by me (*viviktam*) as in verse 40.

Crossing over the famous stages of kaniṣṭha, madhyama and uttama (*tisraḥ gatīḥ*), you will attain something superior (*param*) to those (*tataḥ*). What is that? It is me. He says this with mercy. He said to Arjuna:

*man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru*  
*mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo ’si me \|\|*

**Being my devotee, offer your mind to me. Offer articles to me in worship. Offer respects to me. I promise that you will come to me alone without doubt, for you are most dear to me. (BG 18.65)**

### Text 49

*bhava-bhayam apahantuṁ jñāna-vijñāna-sāraṁ*  
*nigama-kṛd upajahre bhṛṅga-vad veda-sāram*  
*amṛtam udadhitaś cāpāyayad bhṛtya-vargān*  
*puruṣam ṛṣabham ādyaṁ kṛṣṇa-saṁjñaṁ nato ’smi*

**Перевод:**

**Since he is the author of the Vedas, the Lord, like a bee, has extracted the real essence from the Vedas in order to destroy fear of material existence. This essence of all knowledge and self-realization is like the nectar extracted from the milk ocean, which the Lord as Mohinī made his devotees drink while cheating the demons. I offer my obeisances to that Supreme Lord, the original and greatest of all beings, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The one avatāra destroys fear of saṁsāra and gives nectar. Though one should offer respects for these reasons, he is also the first. I offer respects to that person. This shows his great respect. He is also puruṣa, the first of all.

*pūrvam evāham ihāsam iti tat-puruṣasya puruṣatvam*

**It is said “In the beginning I alone existed in this world.” Because the Lord was the only person existing previously, he is called the** ***puruṣa.*** **(*****Taittirīya Āraṇyaka*** **1.23.1)**

*Ṛṣabhaḥ* means the best.

**Kṛṣna Sandarbha 38:**

He says *kṛṣṇa-saṁjñam* (he who is called Kṛṣṇa) so that he cannot be mistaken for any other form. By offering respects to that form he indicates that the form is eternal. Śrīdhara Svāmī says the verse means, “I offer respects to the son of Nanda, the highest bliss.”

## Chapter Thirty

### Text 2

*brahma-śāpopasaṁsṛṣṭe sva-kule yādavarṣabhaḥ*  
*preyasīṁ sarva-netrāṇāṁ tanuṁ sa katham atyajat*

**Перевод:**

**After his dynasty met destruction from the curse of the** ***brāhmaṇas,*** **how could the best of the Yadus give up his body, the dearest object of all eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

How could he give up his body? This means he did not give up his body. He makes clear the desire in his heart. The reason he did not give up his body is that he was the highest bliss for all those who experienced prema. This included the ātmārāmas.

### Text 3

*pratyākraṣṭuṁ nayanam abalā yatra lagnaṁ na śekuḥ*  
*karṇāviṣṭaṁ na sarati tato yat satām ātma-lagnam*  
*yac-chrīr vācāṁ janayati ratiṁ kiṁ nu mānaṁ kavīnāṁ*  
*dṛṣṭvā jiṣṇor yudhi ratha-gataṁ yac ca tat-sāmyam īyuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Once their eyes were fixed upon his transcendental form, women were unable to withdraw them, and once that form had entered the ears of the sages and became fixed in their hearts, it would never depart. What to speak of acquiring fame, the great poets who described the beauty of the Lord’s form would have their words invested with joy. And by seeing that form on Arjuna’s chariot, all the warriors on the battlefield of Kurukṣetra attained the liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

Causes for the impossibility of giving up his body are listed. The respected gopīs, controlled by prema which is desired by all the devotees could not withdraw their eyes from him. How could he make his body do something contrary to this? That would be contrary to the following statement:

*visṛjati hṛdayaṁ na yasya sākṣād*  
*dharir avaśābhihito 'py aghaugha-nāśaḥ*  
*praṇaya-rasanayā dhṛtāṅghri-padmaḥ*  
*sa bhavati bhāgavata-pradhāna uktaḥ*

**He who binds the lotus feet of the Lord by ropes of love, and whose heart the Lord, destroyer of heaps of sin, does not leave, even if beckoned accidentally, is called the best of devotees. (SB 11.2.55)**

And thus the form entered the ears of the best ātmārāmas, the highest of devotees, and never departed. The great poets like Vyāsa had their words invested with joy. And there was a special reason why he could not give up that body (it could not have been material): seeing the form, the warriors achieved liberation. Even his devotees achieve bodies beyond time. Then how was it possible for Kṛṣṇa to have a perishable body?

*mat-sevayā pratītaṁ te sālokyādi-catuṣṭayam*  
*necchanti sevayā pūrṇāḥ kuto 'nyat kāla-viplutam*

**My devotees, who are always satisfied to be engaged in my service, are not interested even in the four principles of liberation \[sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya and sārṣṭi\], although these are automatically achieved by their service. What then is to be said of any perishable happiness? (SB 9.4.67)**

### Text 4

*śrī ṛṣir uvāca*  
*divi bhuvy antarikṣe ca mahotpātān samutthitān*  
*dṛṣṭvāsīnān su-dharmāyāṁ kṛṣṇaḥ prāha yadūn idam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having observed many disturbing signs in the sky, on the earth and in outer space, Kṛṣṇa addressed the Yadus assembled in the Sudharmā council hall as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Accepting these points, Śukadeva explains what was questioned.

### Text 9

*vidhir eṣa hy ariṣṭa-ghno maṅgalāyanam uttamam*  
*deva-dvija-gavāṁ pūjā bhūteṣu paramo bhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This is indeed the appropriate process for counteracting our imminent adversity, and it is sure to bring about the highest good fortune. Such worship of the** ***devatās, brāhmaṇas*** **and cows can earn the highest auspiciousness for all living entities.**

**Комментарий:**

Counteracting adversity indicates attaining a manifestation of his spiritual planet.

### Text 12

*tatas tasmin mahā-pānaṁ papur maireyakaṁ madhu*  
*diṣṭa-vibhraṁśita-dhiyo yad-dravair bhraśyate matiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then, their intelligence covered by fate, they liberally indulged in drinking sweet liquor, which can completely intoxicate the mind.**

**Комментарий:**

Their intelligence was covered by the will of the Lord (*diṣṭa*). All this has been done by māyā, as explained in the next verse. This will be established. Contrary stories told in other Purāṇas are also explanations created by māyā.

### Text 24

*brahma-śāpopasṛṣṭānāṁ kṛṣṇa-māyāvṛtātmanām*  
*spardhā-krodhaḥ kṣayaṁ ninye vaiṇavo ’gnir yathāvanam*

**Перевод:**

**The violent anger of these warriors, who were overcome by the** ***brāhmaṇas’*** **curse and bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency, now led them to their annihilation, just as a fire that starts in a bamboo grove destroys even places beyond the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

The anger led to their destruction (*kṣayam*). The actual meaning is that the destruction led them to the eternal abode. The fire in the bamboo grove spread accidently to human habitation (a*vanam*).

### Text 25

*evaṁ naṣṭeṣu sarveṣu kuleṣu sveṣu keśavaḥ*  
*avatārito bhuvo bhāra iti mene ’vaśeṣitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When all the members of his dynasty were thus destroyed, Kṛṣṇa thought to himself that the earth would suffer.**

**Комментарий:**

He thought that on disappearing and giving up the earth, the earth would suffer great difficulties.

### Text 26

*rāmaḥ samudra-velāyāṁ yogam āsthāya pauruṣam*  
*tatyāja lokaṁ mānuṣyaṁ saṁyojyātmānam ātmani*

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma then sat down on the shore of the ocean and ascertained constant union with Kṛṣṇa. Merging his manifest form with his unmanifest form, he left this earth planet.**

**Комментарий:**

Ascertaining constant union with Kṛṣṇa (*pauruṣam*), uniting himself in his manifestation of the prakaṭa pastimes with the manifestation of the aprakaṭa pastimes (*ātmani*), considering them non-different, Balarāma left the earth.

### Text 27

*rāma-niryāṇam ālokya bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*niṣasāda dharopasthe tuṣṇīm āsādya pippalam*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, seeing the departure of Balarāma, silently sat down on the ground under a nearby** ***pippala*** **tree.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa’s actions are described in six verses.

### Text 40

*ity ādiṣṭo bhagavatā kṛṣṇenecchā-śarīriṇā*  
*triḥ parikramya taṁ natvā vimānena divaṁ yayau*

**Перевод:**

**So instructed by the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who assumes the best body by his own will, the hunter circumambulated the Lord three times and bowed down to him. Then the hunter departed in an airplane to the spiritual sky.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord manifests his form in the world by his will (*icchā-śarīriṇā*). There is no other cause.

### Text 44

*iti bruvati sūte vai ratho garuḍa-lāñchanaḥ*  
*kham utpapāta rājendra sāśva-dhvaja udīkṣataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O foremost of kings! While the chariot driver was still speaking, before his very eyes the Lord’s chariot rose up into the sky along with its horses and its flag, which was marked with the emblem of Garuḍa.**

**Комментарий:**

It is said:

*evaṁ dhyāyati govinda ākāśāt sūrya-varcasau*  
*rathāv upasthitau sadyaḥ sa-sūtau sa-paricchadau*

**As Kṛṣṇa, protector of the earth, was thinking in this way, two chariots as effulgent as the sun suddenly descended from the sky. They were complete with drivers and equipment. (SB 10.50.11)**

Now a chariot appeared similar to Dāruka’s. He was astonished. Dāruka was left there to carry out actions at a later time.

### Text 46

*gaccha dvāravatīṁ sūta jñātīnāṁ nidhanaṁ mithaḥ*  
*saṅkarṣaṇasya niryāṇaṁ bandhubhyo brūhi mad-daśām*

**Перевод:**

**O driver, go to Dvārakā and tell our family members about the mutual destruction of their relatives, the disappearance of Saṅkarṣaṇa and my condition of unmanifest pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Tell them of the destruction (*nidhanam*) of their relatives. The real meaning is “Tell them of the attainment of complete wealth of unmanifested pastimes.” They had followed the Lord.

### Text 47

*dvārakāyāṁ ca na stheyaṁ bhavadbhiś ca sva-bandhubhiḥ*  
*mayā tyaktāṁ yadu-purīṁ samudraḥ plāvayiṣyati*

**Перевод:**

**You and your relatives should not remain in Dvārakā, the capital of the Yadus, because once I have abandoned that city it will be inundated by the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

The ocean would actually surrounded the place so that they would leave the place to avoid the flooding.

### Text 49

*tvaṁ tu mad-dharmam āsthāya jñāna-niṣṭha upekṣakaḥ*  
*man-māyā-racitām etāṁ vijñayopaśamaṁ vraja*

**Перевод:**

**You, Dāruka, should be firmly situated in devotion to me, fixed in spiritual knowledge and unattached to material considerations. Understanding these pastimes to be a display of my illusory potency, you should remain peaceful.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to pacify Dāruka, he explains that the pastimes of the club up to Arjuna’s defeat are a display of the Lord’s māyā.

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 123:**

You, Dāruka, fixed in knowledge, knowing the truth of my pastimes, trusting *(āsthāya*) my nature of associating with my associates as an equal and of protecting my devotees, knowing that this disappearance pastime revealed at this time to be my illusory work, being indifferent to lamentation rising by external vision, free from agitation of the heart (*upaśamam),* attain me *(vraja).* The word *tu* indicates that others would be bewildered but it is not suitable for Dāruka to be bewildered since Dāruka is eternal, having appeared from Vaikuṇṭha. The word *etām* (this pastime) indicates one should not explain it in a different way since he had just received the meaning of that pastime. The pastime was not what it appeared to be.

One sees this arrangement in the Mahābhārata, where Yamarāja speaks to Yudhiṣṭhira about Bhīma and others going to hell:

*na ca te bhrātaraṁ pārtha! narakasthā viśāṁ pate \|*  
*māyaiṣā devarājena mahendreṇa prayojitā \|\|*

**O king! Your brother is not in hell. This is an illusion created by the Lord.**

### Text 50

*ity uktas taṁ parikramya namaskṛtya punaḥ punaḥ*  
*tat-pādau śīrṣṇy upādhāya durmanāḥ prayayau purīm*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ordered, Dāruka circumambulated the Lord and offered obeisances to him again and again. He placed Lord Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet upon his head and then with a sad heart went back to the city.**

**Комментарий:**

He was sad, according to external appearance.

## Chapter Thirty-one

### Text 5

*bhagavān pitāmahaṁ vīkṣya vibhūtīr ātmano vibhuḥ*  
*saṁyojyātmani cātmānaṁ padma-netre nyamīlayat*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Brahmā, the grandfather of the universe, along with the other** ***devatās,*** **who were his** ***vibhūtis,*** **the Lord fixed his mind within himself, and closed his eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord, seeing Brahmā and the devatās (*vibhūtīḥ)*, his expansions, drew them near and closed his eyes, fixing his mind on his svarūpa in order to teach how to give up the body, giving up siddhis, and to hide the nature of his form from them.

### Text 6

*lokābhirāmāṁ sva-tanuṁ dhāraṇā-dhyāna-maṅgalam*  
*yoga-dhāraṇayāgneyyā- dagdhvā dhāmāviśat svakam*

**Перевод:**

**Without performing meditation to burn up his body, which was all-attractive to world and the object of all contemplation and meditation, Kṛṣṇa entered into his abode.**

**Комментарий:**

Though there seems to some contrary meaning, the meaning is discerned through the verses containing the instructions, similarly to the meaning of statements in the Upaniṣads. *Ākāśas tal-liṅgād*: the word *ākāśa* denotes Brahman, because of indications in the text. (*Vedānta–sūtra* 1.1.22)

Destroying the idea that his body was burned up, the word can also be taken as *adaghvā* (not being burned up). His body was attractive to the whole world. This indicates that he was the shelter of the universe. Taking a wider meaning of the word *loka,* it includes the eternal associates of Mahā-vaikuṇṭha, the ātmārāmas or jñānīs and living entities down to the plants. He gave pleasure to them all. What more can be said? He gave pleasure to the greatest devotees but he was also the shelter of the sādhakas, because he was the auspicious object of meditation and contemplation (*dhāraṇa-dhyāna-maṅgalam*). For the meditators he was the form of auspiciousness. How could it be otherwise?

His abode and his body were dependent on him (*sva, svakam*). These two adjectives indicate his svarūpa. *Svakam* indicates a secondary item and *sva-tanum* indicates the chief item (to emphasize the nature of his body). The compound indicates a continuous relationship: he always possesses that body. *Dhāma svakam* indicates dependence on the Lord, and thus why would *sva-tanu* also not indicate dependence of his body on the Lord’s will? Thus his body was not burned up through meditation. What purpose would burning up his body serve? It is like scratching a limb which is not itchy.

Śrīdhara Svāmī explains that the yogīs die by their will, by burning up their bodies. But Kṛṣṇa’s departure was different. He meditated on fire. That is true. But his body was not burned up and he entered his abode. After teaching yogīs how to give up the body, he disappeared. It cannot be otherwise. This is one astonishing pastime.

*ity aṅgopadiśanty eke vismṛtya prāg udāhṛtam*  
*muni-vāsa-nivāse kiṁ ghaṭetāriṣṭa-darśanam*

**Some men proposed that the troubles were due to Akrūra’s absence, but they had forgotten the glories of the Supreme Lord, which they themselves had so often described. Indeed, how can calamities occur in a place where the Lord, the residence of all the sages, resides? (SB 10.57.31)**

*evaṁ vadanti rājarṣe ṛṣayaḥ kecanānvitāḥ*  
*yat sva-vāco virudhyeta nūnaṁ te na smaranty uta*

**Such is the account given by some sages, O wise King, but those who speak in this illogical way are contradicting themselves, having forgotten their own previous statements. (SB 10.77.30)**

Though this is the Lord’s nature, other sages have different ideas-- which are not corrected by the king of sages Śukadeva. What to speak of this incident. In order to refute the contrary ideas the phrase *lokābhirāmām* is modified by various words.

In order to hide his nature, the Lord shows things by māyā. These appearances are what various sages describe. This will be shown in verse 8. Even previous to this incident, his form was not manifest to some persons. *Nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ*: I am not revealed to everyone, but am hidden by yoga-māyā. (BG 9.25) They imagine another form as in *virāḍ aviduṣam*: the ignorant saw Kṛṣṇa as material. (SB 10.43.17) By the Lord’s māyā he appears differently by eyes made to see illusion They describe the Lord’s body as material. He did not burn up his body but burned a body made by his māyā.

The same is indicated by *icchā-śarīrābhiprāyeṇa*: he accepted a body by his will. The contrary ideas are intolerable. By his free will, he created a body and by his free will he disappeared. Meditating on fire was also an appearance. These terms are explained in Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha.

Or according to the statement that the Lord manifests his form in this world by his desire (*icchā-śarīram*) he performed his actions mentioned in this verse by manifesting a particular body (getting burned up) to fulfill his desires. By his desire, māyā acted in a certain way. That is also a proper explanation. The meaning that the sages show by indirect expression is proper since it follows the Lord’s desire.

*vedā brahmātma-viṣayās tri-kāṇḍa-viṣayā ime*  
*parokṣa-vādā ṛṣayaḥ parokṣaṁ mama ca priyam*

**The Vedas, divided into three divisions, ultimately reveal worship of the Lord. The Vedic sages and** ***mantras*****, however, state this indirectly, since they know that I prefer this indirect method. (SB 11.21.35)**

### Text 10

*brahma-rudrādayas te tu dṛṣṭvā yoga-gatiṁ hareḥ*  
*vismitās tāṁ praśaṁsantaḥ svaṁ svaṁ lokaṁ yayus tadā*

**Перевод:**

**A few of the** ***devatās,*** **however—notably Brahmā and Śiva—could ascertain that the Lord’s mystic power was working, and thus they became astonished. All the** ***devatās*** **praised the Lord’s mystic power and then returned to their own planets.**

**Комментарий:**

Some of the devatās perceived the truth of the matter.

### Text 11

*rājan parasya tanu-bhṛj-jananāpyayehā*  
*māyā-viḍambanam avehi yathā naṭasya*  
*sṛṣṭvātmanedam anuviśya vihṛtya cānte*  
*saṁhṛtya cātma-mahinoparataḥ sa āste*

**Перевод:**

**O King! You should understand that the Supreme Lord’s appearance and disappearance, which resemble those of embodied conditioned souls, are actually a show enacted by his illusory energy, just like the performance of an actor. After creating this illusion he entered into it, played within it for some time, and at last destroyed it, withdrawing from it by his own power. Thus he remains.**

**Комментарий:**

The Yādavas could not have material bodies, what to speak of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa.

The siddhānta is given.

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 124:**

Nārada has said concerning his own body:

*prayujyamāne mayi tāṁ śuddhāṁ bhāgavatīṁ tanum \|*  
*ārabdha-karma-nirvāṇo nyapatat pāñca-bhautikaḥ \|\|*

**Having been awarded a transcendental body befitting an associate of the Lord, the body made of five material elements, with karmas relating to the present body, fell away. (SB 1.6.28)**

Know that the activities *(īhāḥ)* of the associates of Kṛṣṇa (*parasya),* in which he maintain bodies (*tanu-bhṛt*), (ie. the Yadus), which appear and disappear (*jananāpyaya*), are only an imitation produced by the Lord’s māyā. It is similar to a magician (*naṭaḥ)*. The magician is alive, but shows that he is killed, burned and then shows that he creates a new body. It is not surprising since the Lord has inconceivable śakti to create the universe etc. That is explained in the second part of the verse. Thus, for the foolish people, shadow forms of Balarāma and others, are introduced in the description of the illusory pastime to cause a different perception. In Skanda Purāṇa, Lakṣmaṇa’s death should not be accepted. In the Nārāyaṇa kavaca it is shown that Balarāma is acknowledged as the eternal protector of the worshipper, having powers more extraordinary than Śeṣa’s.

Jarāsandha also says:

*tava rāma yadi śraddhā yudhyasva dhairyam udvaha*  
*hitvā vā mac-charaiś chinnaṁ dehaṁ svar yāhi māṁ jahi*

**You, Balarāma, should gather your courage and fight with me, if you think you can do it. You may either give up your body when it is cut to pieces by my arrows, and thus attain to heaven, or else kill me. (SB 10.50.18)**

Śrīdhara Svāmī gives the correct meaning to this. Thinking that Balarāma’s body was indestructible, out of dissatisfaction, he speaks the alternative: kill me.

*Lokābhirāmāṁ sva-tanuṁ*: his body was most attractive to all people. (SB 11.31.6) Śrīdhara Svāmī comments on this, saying his body could not be burned, since the Lord has powers superior to the powers of a yogī.The skillful explanations are established by *kaimutya*. He says “Even today worshippers see that beautiful form.” Thus, he agrees with what has been said. The worshippers see the Lord with his associates. It is not possible that they die, because they have spiritual bodies.

### Text 12

*martyena yo guru-sutaṁ yama-loka-nītaṁ*  
*tvāṁ cānayac charaṇa-daḥ paramāstra-dagdham*  
*jigye ’ntakāntakam apīśam asāv anīśaḥ*  
*kiṁ svāvane svar anayan mṛgayuṁ sa-deham*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa brought the son of his** ***guru*** **back from the planet of death in the boy’s selfsame body, and as the ultimate giver of protection he saved you also when you were burned by the weapon of Aśvatthāmā. He conquered in battle even Śiva, who deals death to the agents of death, and he sent the hunter Jarā directly to Vaikuṇṭha in his human body. How could such a personality be unable to protect himself?**

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 125:**

Since the associates are protected by Kṛṣṇa they cannot be destroyed.

Kṛṣṇa brought the son of his guru who had gone to Yamaloka in the body born of his guru, which had been devoured by Pañcajana. The power of a brahma weapon should not be considered strong: he protected you from the brahmāstra when you were burned by it. What more can be said? He conquered Śiva in a battle of arrows. He sent the hunter Jarā in his body to a special Vaikuṇṭha *(svaḥ*). Can he not protect the Yadus *(sva*)? Thus their destruction is a faulty perception and not according to the actual pastime. He took them to his abode in their spiritual bodies.

### Text 13

*tathāpy aśeṣa-sthiti-sambhavāpyayeṣv*  
*ananya-hetur yad aśeṣa-śakti-dhṛk*  
*naicchat praṇetuṁ vapur atra śeṣitaṁ*  
*martyena kiṁ sva-stha-gatiṁ pradarśayan*

**Перевод:**

**Although Kṛṣṇa, being the possessor of infinite powers, is the only cause of the creation, maintenance and destruction of innumerable planets, he did not desire to remain with his manifested pastimes on earth. What is the use of this mortal world or its people? But he made known his destination to the** ***devatās.***

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 126:**

“Let us accept that the associates went to the Lord’s abode in their bodies. There, Svayam Bhagavān exists. They have no pain of separation. If the Lord is capable of doing this, why does he not have other persons similar to them appear in the material world along with him and stay there for some time to give mercy to mortals along with them?” The Lord and his associates have unshakeable bonds of friendship (and cannot be separated). Though he is the only cause of creation, maintenance and destruction, because *(yat*) he has unlimited powers of this nature, having made the Yadus disappear, he did not desire to keep his body there any longer. He took his body to his abode. The reason is given. Without my associates, what is the use of the material world? He showed particularly, according to his desire, the destination of those who had gone to his abode.

### Text 21

*arjunaḥ preyasaḥ sakhyuḥ kṛṣṇasya virahāturaḥ*  
*ātmānaṁ sāntvayām āsa kṛṣṇa-gītaiḥ sad-uktibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Arjuna felt great distress over separation from Kṛṣṇa, his dear friend. But he consoled himself by remembering the pure words the Lord had sung to him.**

**Комментарий:**

The pure words of Kṛṣṇa were *mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo’si me*: you will come to me. I promise you since you are dear to me. (BG 7.25). Mahābhārata says:

*dadarśa tatra govindaṁ brāhmeṇa vapuṣānvitam*  
*tenaiva dṛṣṭa-pūrveṇa sādṛśyenopasūcitam*  
*dīpyamānaṁ sva-vapuṣā divyair astrair upaskṛtam*  
*upāsyamānaṁ vīreṇa phālgunena suvarcasā*  
*yathā svarūpaṁ kaunteyas dadarśa madhusūdanam*  
*tāv ubhau puruṣa-vyāghrau samudvīkṣya yudhiṣṭhiram \|*  
*yathārhaṁ pratipedāte pūjayā deva-pūjitau \|\|*

**Yudhiṣṭhira saw Kṛṣṇa endowed with a spiritual body, which was similar to the form he had previously seen. Kṛṣṇa was shining with his body, decorated with attractive weapons, and was worshipped by brave Arjuna who was also shining. He saw Kṛṣṇa in his svarūpa. Seeing Yudhiṣṭhira, the two heroes, worshipable by the devatās met him and worshipped him.**

### Text 23

*dvārakāṁ hariṇā tyaktāṁ samudro ’plāvayat kṣaṇāt*  
*varjayitvā mahā-rāja śrīmad-bhagavad-ālayam*

**Перевод:**

**As soon as Dvārakā was abandoned by the Supreme Lord, the ocean flooded it on all sides, O King, sparing only his palace.**

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 181:**

By material vision, he left Dvārakā. But the next verse says he lives there eternally. Thus he did not give up Dvārakā (*hariṇā atyaktām* instead of *hariṇā tyaktām*). In any case the water spread everywhere like a moat, covering everything. The ocean submerged everything by the order of the Lord. There was an external covering (in the form of flooding) of the houses of material persons, who were sent to Hastināpura.The place was destroyed in this way because, built by Viśvakarmā, it was mixed with the material world for prakaṭa pastimes. And Sudharma hall came from Svarga. In the aprakaṭa pastimes, there is another more splendid hall than that. However the ocean did not destroy the palaces of the Lord, the glorious houses of the Yadus. Even today one can sometimes see something far off in the ocean. The greatness of the place is famous. Addressing Parīkṣit as *mahārāja* (great king) indicates the fame of the place. Or *mahārāja* is a modifier: the ocean flooded everything except the city of Dvārakā, the eternal abode of Kṛṣṇa (*bhagavad-ālayam)* where the great Yadu kings (*mahārāja*) resided. Not only did the city remain, but in the palace Kṛṣṇa eternally resides (*nityam sannihitaḥ*). Why would the inhabitants not live there? The word Bhagavān means the Lord endowed with all his powers such as the Yādavas.

The place is described. By remembering the place, since one cannot see the manifested place, one destroys all contamination. There is no possibility of the place of the Lord being otherwise.

Viṣṇu Purāṇa says:

*plāvayāmāsa tāṁ śūnyāṁ dvārakāṁ ca mahodadhiḥ \|*  
*nityaṁ sannihitas tatra bhagavān keśavo yataḥ \|\|*  
*tad atīva mahā-puṇyaṁ sarva-pāpa-praṇāśanam \|*  
*viṣṇu-krīḍānvitaṁ sthānaṁ dṛṣṭvā pāpāt pramucyate \|\|*

**The ocean flooded the empty city of Dvārakā. Since Kṛṣṇa resides there eternally, seeing that place most pure, filled with the Lord’s pastimes, destroyer of all sins, one becomes free of sin. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.38.9-10)**

In Hari-vaṁśa Nārada, sent by Indra, says to the Yadus:

*kṛṣṇo bhogavatīṁ ramyām ṛṣi-kāntāṁ mahā-yaśāḥ \|*  
*dvārakām ātmasāt kṛtvā samudraṁ gamayiṣyati \|\|*

**Kṛṣṇa will make Dvārakā, attractive and full of enjoyment, dear to the sages and most famous, one with himself, and make the ocean flood it. (Hari-vaṁśa 2.102.32)**

*Ātmasāt kṛtvā* means he did not leave the place.

### Text 28

*itthaṁ harer bhagavato rucirāvatāra-*  
*vīryāṇi bāla-caritāni ca śantamāni*  
*anyatra ceha ca śrutāni gṛṇan manuṣyo*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ paramahaṁsa-gatau labheta*

**Перевод:**

**The auspicious exploits of the attractive incarnations of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, and also the pastimes he performed as a child in Vṛṇdāvana are described in this** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **and in other scriptures. Anyone who clearly chants these descriptions of his pastimes will attain supreme** ***bhakti*** **to Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is the goal of perfect sages.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of hearing about Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes is attainment of Kṛṣṇa and the highest bhakti. Those who hear the pastimes attain supreme bhakti to Kṛṣṇa, the goal of paramahaṁsas who are attracted to his pastimes, what to speak of his devotees.

The last two types do not yet have spiritual bodies in the spiritual world.

This is bhāva, the sprout of prema.

The devotees have made their goal of life affection for me, the Lord, and do not show affection for persons who enjoy talks about people attached to eating and drinking and who have houses, wives, sons and wealth. The devotees with prema realize the Lord according to their worship. (SB 5.5.3)

He sees all objects as devotees of the Lord.

This is described in Gopāla-campū.

The *gopīs* were always completely thattached to me with the deepest love. Therefore, when my uncle Akrūra brought my brother Balarāma and me to the city of Mathurā, suffering extreme mental distress because of separation from me, they could not find any other source of happiness. (SB 11.12.10)

Later in this chapter and In SB 11.21.36 commentary these are also explained. There seems to be a little contradiction, so these have been consolidated to make something consistent.

Mind is real, though momentary, and everything else is error.

The error is not caused by lack of discrimination between memory and perception but two different perceptions combining.

Each mantra as a presiding deity. The presiding deity of Kṛṣṇa mantra is Durgā.

Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 8.391

The Lord rejected the erroneous process of dying at will which is practiced by yogīs.He did not burn up his body by meditating on fire, because his body was attractive to all people and was the object of contemplation and meditation.

## Canto Twelve

## Chapter One

### Text 1-2

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*yo 'ntyaḥ purañjayo nāma bhaviṣyo bārahadrathaḥ*  
*tasyāmātyas tu śunako hatvā svāminam ātma-jam*  
*pradyota-saṁjñaṁ rājānaṁ kartā yat-pālakaḥ sutaḥ*  
*viśākhayūpas tat-putro bhavitā rājakas tataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The last king mentioned of the future rulers of the Māgadha dynasty was Purañjaya, a descendant of Bṛhadratha. Purañjaya's minister Śunaka will assassinate the king and install his own son, Pradyota, on the throne. The son of Pradyota will be Pālaka, his son will be Viśākhayūpa, and his son will be Rājaka.**

**Комментарий:**

*śrīrādhākṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ*  
*dvādaśakramasandarbhe sandarbhāṇāṁ samāhṛtiḥ*  
*kriyate yannideśena sa me ’nanyagatergatiḥ*

**He by whose order this collection of sandarbhas is made into the Twelfth Krama Sandarbha is the goal of this person with no other goal.**

Having indicated clearly that Kṛṣṇa is the āśraya, and one’s personal deity up to the eleventh canto, the Twelfth canto commences to summarize the Purāṇa.

Having shown that when Kṛṣṇa disappeared the people would lament, Śukadeva will show that those who worship him will attain deliverance.

### Text 21-26

*kṛṣṇa-nāmātha tad-bhrātā bhavitā pṛthivī-patiḥ*  
*śrī-śāntakarṇas tat-putraḥ paurṇamāsas tu tat-sutaḥ*  
*lambodaras tu tat-putras tasmāc cibilako nṛpaḥ*  
*meghasvātiś cibilakād aṭamānas tu tasya ca*  
*aniṣṭakarmā hāleyas talakas tasya cātma-jaḥ*  
*purīṣabhīrus tat-putras tato rājā sunandanaḥ*  
*cakoro bahavo yatra śivasvātir arin-damaḥ*  
*tasyāpi gomatī putraḥ purīmān bhavitā tataḥ*  
*medaśirāḥ śivaskando yajñaśrīs tat-sutas tataḥ*  
*vijayas tat-suto bhāvyaś candravijñaḥ sa-lomadhiḥ*  
*ete triṁśan nṛpatayaś catvāry abda-śatāni ca*  
*ṣaṭ-pañcāśac ca pṛthivīṁ bhokṣyanti kuru-nandana*

**Перевод:**

**The brother of Balī, named Kṛṣṇa, will become the next ruler of the earth. His son will be Śāntakarṇa, and his son will be Paurṇamāsa. The son of Paurṇamāsa will be Lambodara, who will father Mahārāja Cibilaka. From Cibilaka will come Meghasvāti, whose son will be Aṭamāna. The son of Aṭamāna will be Aniṣṭakarmā. His son will be Hāleya, and his son will be Talaka. The son of Talaka will be Purīṣabhīru, and following him Sunandana will become king. Sunandana will be followed by Cakora and then the eight Bahus, among whom Śivasvāti will be a great subduer of enemies. The son of Śivasvāti will be Gomatī. His son will be Purīmān, whose son will be Medaśirā. His son will be Śivaskanda, and his son will be Yajñaśrī. The son of Yajñaśrī will be Vijaya, who will have two sons, Candravijña and Lomadhi. These thirty kings will enjoy sovereignty over the earth for a total of 456 years, O son of the Kurus.**

**Комментарий:**

*Aniṣṭakarmā* modifies Hāleya. (Hāleya would be his son). Eight Bahus are not mentioned by name. The ninth was called Śivasvāti. Gomatī and his son Purīmān are two kings.

### Text 27

*saptābhīrā āvabhṛtyā daśa gardabhino nṛpāḥ*  
*kaṅkāḥ ṣoḍaśa bhū-pālā bhaviṣyanty ati-lolupāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then will follow seven kings of the Ābhīra race from the city of Avabhṛti, and then ten Gardabhīs. After them, sixteen greedy kings of the Kaṅkas will rule.**

**Комментарий:**

The total until Lomadhi is thirty kings.

## Chapter Two

### Text 6

*dūre vāry-ayanaṁ tīrthaṁ lāvaṇyaṁ keśa-dhāraṇam*  
*udaraṁ-bharatā svārthaḥ satyatve dhārṣṭyam eva hi*  
*dākṣyaṁ kuṭumba-bharaṇaṁ yaśo 'rthe dharma-sevanam*

**Перевод:**

**A sacred place will be taken to consist of no more than a reservoir of water located at a distance, and beauty will be thought to depend on one's hairstyle. Filling the belly will become the goal of life, and one who is audacious will be accepted as truthful. He who can maintain a family will be regarded as an expert man and the principles of religion will be observed only for the sake of reputation.**

**Комментарий:**

For beauty people will dress their hair.

### Text 29

*viṣṇor bhagavato bhānuḥ kṛṣṇākhyo 'sau divaṁ gataḥ*  
*tadāviśat kalir loka pāpe yad ramate janaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the seven sages entered Maghā constellation, when Viṣṇu, the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, the ray of Kṛṣṇa, went to Vaikuṇṭha, Kali entered this world, and people then began to take pleasure in sinful activities.**

**Комментарий:**

**Kṛṣṇa sandarbha 107:**

When Kṛṣṇa, the sun, who has the guṇāvatāra Viṣṇu as his ray, since Viṣṇu is his aṁśa, departed for Vaikuṇṭha (*divaṁ gataḥ*)--a particular manifestation of Mathurā, Dvārakā and Gokula beyond material vision--at that time Kali entered the world. Though these manifestations are situated on earth, by the antardhāna-śakti (śakti which makes invisible) they are present there without touching the earth. Thus the great kadamba tree and other items mentioned in Varāha Purāṇa are not touched by earth and other material elements. The manifestation of Mathurā or Gokula which is visible to material people, touching the earth by mercy, appears in the world. Thus the visible kadamba is touched by earth, stone etc. at that time. When the Lord appears in this visible manifestation of the abode, he contacts earth with his touch and exists there. Now however, he remains in the untouched manifestation (invisible), and thus does not touch the earth. That is the meaning of “touching the earth with his feet. “The meaning here is that the two states are different and non-different. Though the verse says that as long as Kṛṣṇa was present Kali could not enter, Kali actually entered a little before his disappearance.

### Text 30

*yāvat sa pāda-padmābhyāṁ spṛśan āste ramā-patiḥ*  
*tāvat kalir vai pṛthivīṁ parākrantuṁ na cāśakat*

**Перевод:**

**As long as Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the husband of Lakṣṁī, touched the earth with his lotus feet, Kali could not subdue this planet.**

**Комментарий:**

Kali could not subdue the planet. However previous to this, Kali had entered and spread a little.

## Chapter Three

### Text 9-13

*pṛthuḥ purūravā gādhir nahuṣo bharato 'rjunaḥ*  
*māndhātā sagaro rāmaḥ khaṭvāṅgo dhundhuhā raghuḥ*  
*tṛṇabindur yayātiś ca śaryātiḥ śantanur gayaḥ*  
*bhagīrathaḥ kuvalayāśvaḥ kakutstho naiṣadho nṛgaḥ*  
*hiraṇyakaśipur vṛtro rāvaṇo loka-rāvaṇaḥ*  
*namuciḥ śambaro bhaumo hiraṇyākṣo 'tha tārakaḥ*  
*anye ca bahavo daityā rājāno ye maheśvarāḥ*  
*sarve sarva-vidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve sarva-jito 'jitāḥ*  
*mamatāṁ mayy avartanta kṛtvoccair martya-dharmiṇaḥ*  
*kathāvaśeṣāḥ kalena hy akṛtārthāḥ kṛtā vibho*

**Перевод:**

**Such kings as Pṛthu, Purūravā, Gādhi, Nahuṣa, Bharata, Kārtavīrya Arjuna, Māndhātā, Sagara, Rāma, Khaṭvāṅga, Dhundhuhā, Raghu, Tṛṇabindu, Yayāti, Śaryāti, Śantanu, Gaya, Bhagīratha, Kuvalayāśva, Kakutstha, Naiṣadha, Nṛga, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Vṛtra, Rāvaṇa, who made the whole world lament, Namuci, Śambara, Bhauma, Hiraṇyākṣa and Tāraka, as well as many other demons and kings who were powerful controllers, were full of knowledge, heroic, all-conquering and unconquerable. Nevertheless, O almighty Lord, they lived their lives intensely trying to possess me. Those who were materialistic were unsuccessful byn passing of time and have become only historical accounts.**

**Комментарий:**

Five verses describe the kings. All these persons even the demons were possessive of me and existed in me. Or all the śūras, full of knowledge, those who were devotees or avatāras, perfect with śaktis of jñāna and kriyā, who conquered all and were unconquerable, were possessive of me. The word *sarva* is repeated to express great joy and confirmation. Those who are attached by nature to matter (*martya-dharminaḥ*) in time were unsuccessful and became only stories.

### Text 14

*kathā imās te kathitā mahīyasāṁ*  
*vitāya lokeṣu yaśaḥ pareyuṣām*  
*vijñāna-vairāgya-vivakṣayā vibho*  
*vaco-vibhūtīr na tu pāramārthyam*

**Перевод:**

**O mighty Parīkṣit! I have related to you the narrations of all these great devotees who attained the Lord, who spread their fame throughout the world, with a desire to speak about their renunciation and their realization of the Lord. I have not spoken to show the power of words, but to give you the highest spiritual knowledge.**

**Комментарий:**

**Bhakti Sandarbha 250:**

Though Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are included among the kings for showing renunciation, they are included only in the manner of the crowd of umbrella bearers (some of whom are not carrying umbrellas), since their stories illustrate more than that. Though everything in the Bhāgavatam should relate to rasa, since it is the highest sweetest fruit on the desire tree of the Vedas (SB 1.1.3), sometimes there is direct bhakti with various rasas starting with śānta and sometimes there is assistants for those rasas. (Thus stories of kings are there to encourage distaste for material rasa.) There are also degrees in the bhakti-rasas described in the Bhāgavatam (not just the highest rasa).

### Text 15

*yas tūttamaḥ-śloka-guṇānuvādaḥ*  
*saṅgīyate 'bhīkṣṇam amaṅgala-ghnaḥ*  
*tam eva nityaṁ śṛṇuyād abhīkṣṇaṁ*  
*kṛṣṇe 'malāṁ bhaktim abhīpsamānaḥ*

**The person who desires pure** ***bhakti*** **to Kṛṣṇa should hear the narrations of the Lord’s glorious qualities, the constant chanting of which destroys everything inauspicious.**

He should hear with great concentration those glorifications of the Lord’s avatāras. The result of everything is stated. He desires pure bhakti to Kṛṣṇa, famous as a cowherd.

### Text 20

*tretāyāṁ dharma-pādānāṁ turyāṁśo hīyate śanaiḥ*

**In Tretā-yuga each leg of religion is gradually reduced by one quarter by the influence of the four pillars of irreligion—lying, violence, dissatisfaction and quarrel.**

This should be understood according to the Sandarbha explanation of the First Canto.

### Text 32

*dasyūtkṛṣṭā janapadā vedāḥ pāṣaṇḍa-dūṣitāḥ*  
*rājānaś ca prajā-bhakṣāḥ śiśnodara-parā dvijāḥ*

### Text 43

*kalau na rājan jagatāṁ paraṁ guruṁ*

*yan-nāmadheyaṁ mriyamāṇa āturaḥ*

*mriyamāṇair abhidhyeyo bhagavān parameśvaraḥ*

### Text 51

*kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**
