*sa ciraṁ māyayā viṣṇor bhrāmitaḥ karśito bhṛśam*  
*śiva-vāg-amṛta-dhvasta- kleśa-puñjas tam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Mārkaṇḍeya, having been forced by Viṣṇu's illusory energy to wander about for a long time in the water of dissolution, had become extremely exhausted. But Śiva's words of nectar vanquished his accumulated suffering. Thus he addressed Śiva.**

**Комментарий:**

He was made to wander about by Viṣṇu’s māyā, having accepted it by his own will.

Śiva was shown to be absorbed in Viṣṇu.

### Text 29

*dharmaṁ grāhayituṁ prāyaḥ pravaktāraś ca dehinām*  
*ācaranty anumodante kriyamāṇaṁ stuvanti ca*

**Перевод:**

**Generally it is to induce embodied souls to accept religious principles that the authorized teachers exhibit ideal behavior, encouraging and praising** ***dharma*** **which is being performed.**

**Комментарий:**

Generally they teachers act properly to induce people, who think that actions of their bodies are their actions (*dehīnām)* to accept dharma. Sometimes they do so by their own taste. The speakers (*pravaktāraḥ*) are distinguished from them.

### Text 30

*naitāvatā bhagavataḥ sva-māyā-maya-vṛttibhiḥ*  
*na duṣyetānubhāvas tair māyinaḥ kuhakaṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Such behavior of the Supreme Lord, which the Lord produces by his own bewildering potency, does not spoil his power any more than a magician's powers are diminished by his exhibition of tricks.**

**Комментарий:**

Accepting the Lord as the chief of these persons, he denies any fault in the Lord in three verses. The reason that the Lord is not at fault is explained. The power of the Lord is not spoiled by his actions (*vṛttibhiḥ*) which are full of his mercy (*māyā-maya*), being controlled by his affection, for his devotees (*sva)*. He thinks, “I should do this for my devotees.” An opposite example is given. The power of a magician are spoiled by his tricks. Another version has *na duṣyeta* (instead of *praduṣyeta*). The Lord’s powers are not spoiled as the magician’s powers are spoiled.

### Text 31-32

*sṛṣṭvedaṁ manasā viśvam ātmanānupraviśya yaḥ*  
*guṇaiḥ kurvadbhir ābhāti karteva svapna-dṛg yathā*  
*tasmai namo bhagavate tri-guṇāya guṇātmane*  
*kevalāyādvitīyāya gurave brahma-mūrtaye*

**Перевод:**

**I offer my obeisances to that Supreme Lord, who has created this entire universe simply by his desire and has then entered into it as** ***antaryāmī.*** **By making the modes of nature act, he seems to be the direct creator of this world, just as a dreamer seems to be acting within his dream. I offer respects to the Lord, who manifests the three** ***guṇas,*** **who controls the** ***guṇas,*** **who is pure, without equal, who is the** ***guru,*** **the Brahman.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses show how the Lord is not touched by fault. Having created the universe by his mind (*manasā)* or his will, using matter made of guṇas, entering it personally (*ātmanā*), establishing it by entering, and destroying it as well, he seemed to be the agent of action, but he is not. The creation takes place by the guṇas (*kurvadbhiḥ*). The guṇas do everything, like consciousness acting by its proximity to the body. He is not directly involved since he acts by his will alone, which is an ābhāsa of being an agent. Even the jīva, the Lord’s taṭastha aṁśa, in creating a dream through ignorance, is actually not related to it. What to speak of the Lord.

I offer respects to the Lord who has three qualities of amṛta, abhaya and kṣema (*tri-guṇāya*), whose qualities like aiśvarya (*guṇa*) arise from his svarūpa *(ātmane*), who is devoid of association with prakṛti (*kevalāya*), who has no equal (*advitīyāya*), and who is thus the teacher of all (*gurave*) and whose svarūpa is the Vedas (*brahma)*, which teach about him.

### Text 34

*varam ekaṁ vṛṇe 'thāpi pūrṇāt kāmābhivarṣaṇāt*  
*bhagavaty acyutāṁ bhaktiṁ tat-pareṣu tathā tvayi*

**Перевод:**

**But I do request one benediction from you, who are full of all perfection and able to shower down the fulfillment of all desires. I ask to have unfailing devotion for the Supreme Lord and for his devotees, especially you.**

**Комментарий:**

I ask for unfailing devotion to the Lord and then to you who are dependent on him (*tvayi*). This was said to Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi:

*kiṁ varṇaye tava vibho yad-udīrito 'suḥ*  
*saṁspandate tam anu vāṅ-mana-indriyāṇi*  
*spandanti vai tanu-bhṛtām aja-śarvayoś ca*  
*svasyāpy athāpi bhajatām asi bhāva-bandhuḥ*

**O Almighty Lord, how can I possibly describe you? You awaken the vital air, which then impels the mind, senses and power of speech to act. This is true for all ordinary conditioned souls and even Brahmā and Śiva. So it is certainly true for me. Nevertheless, you become the intimate friend of those who worship you. (SB 12.8.40)**

### Text 41

*etat kecid avidvāṁso māyā-saṁsṛtir ātmanaḥ*  
*anādy-āvartitaṁ nṝṇāṁ kādācitkaṁ pracakṣate*

**Перевод:**

**Some unintelligent persons explain Mārkaṇḍeya’s unique experience as symbolic of human beings in beginningless ignorance undergoing repeated cycles.**

**Комментарий:**

Some ignorant people explain that what Mārkaṇḍeya saw, a display of the Lord’s (*ātmanaḥ*) māyā because of his request, was the occasional devastation produced by the Lord, which takes place regularly without beginning. This would take place and would be seen in other kalpas and manvantaras as well.

### Text 42

*ya evam etad bhṛgu-varya varṇitaṁ*  
*rathāṅga-pāṇer anubhāva-bhāvitam*  
*saṁśrāvayet saṁśṛṇuyād u tāv ubhau*  
*tayor na karmāśaya-saṁsṛtir bhavet*

**Перевод:**

**O best of the Bhṛgus, this account concerning Mārkaṇḍeya is infused with the potency of the Supreme Lord. Anyone who properly narrates or hears it will never again undergo material existence, composed of impressions of** ***karma.***

**Комментарий:**

Anyone who narrates or anyone who hears (*u)* will not undergo saṁsāra.

## Chapter Eleven

### Text 2-3

*tāntrikāḥ paricaryāyāṁ kevalasya śriyaḥ pateḥ*  
*aṅgopāṅgāyudhākalpaṁ kalpayanti yathā ca yaiḥ*  
*tan no varṇaya bhadraṁ te kriyā-yogaṁ bubhutsatām*  
*yena kriyā-naipuṇena martyo yāyād amartyatām*

**Перевод:**

**All good fortune to you! Please explain to us, who are very eager to learn, the process of** ***kriyā-yoga,*** **worship of Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī, by which method the followers of** ***tantra*** **conceive of the limbs, associates, weapons and ornaments of the Lord in terms of certain** ***vibhūtis,*** **and by which expertise one attains immortality.**

**Комментарий:**

Please describe to us kriyā-yoga where followers of tantra worship the limbs, associates, weapons and ornaments of Viṣṇu, who is non-different from those limbs etc. (*kevalasya*), known as the lord of Lakṣmī, his svarūpa-śakti, as vibhūtis of māyā, by which even the person absorbed in matter can attain immortality.

### Text 4

*sūta uvāca*  
*namaskṛtya gurūn vakṣye vibhūtīr vaiṣṇavīr api*  
*yāḥ proktā veda-tantrābhyām ācāryaiḥ padmajādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sūta Gosvāmī said: Offering obeisances to my** ***gurus,*** **I shall repeat to you the description of the** ***vibhūtis*** **of Viṣṇu given in the Vedas and** ***tantras*** **by great authorities, beginning from lotus-born Brahmā.**

**Комментарий:**

I will speak of the ordinary vibhūtis of Viṣṇu and also the vibhūtis which arise from his svarūpa (*vaiṣṇavīḥ*).

### Text 5

*māyādyair navabhis tattvaiḥ sa vikāra-mayo virāṭ*  
*nirmito dṛśyate yatra sa-citke bhuvana-trayam*

**Перевод:**

**That form of the Lord is the universal form, composed of the nine basic elements of creation, starting with the unmanifest nature, and their subsequent transformations. When it is instilled with consciousness, the three planetary systems become visible within it.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses make one statement. In that universal form, endowed with consciousness (*sa-citke*) in the form of the totality of jīvas, the three worlds become visible.

### Text 6-8

*etad vai pauruṣaṁ rūpaṁ bhūḥ pādau dyauḥ śiro nabhaḥ*  
*nābhiḥ sūryo 'kṣiṇī nāse vāyuḥ karṇau diśaḥ prabhoḥ*  
*prajāpatiḥ prajananam apāno mṛtyur īśituḥ*  
*tad-bāhavo loka-pālā manaś candro bhruvau yamaḥ*  
*lajjottaro 'dharo lobho dantā jyotsnā smayo bhramaḥ*  
*romāṇi bhūruhā bhūmno meghāḥ puruṣa-mūrdhajāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This is the representation of the Supreme Lord as the universal person, in which the earth is his feet, the** ***antarikṣa*** **his navel, the heavenly planets his head, the sun his eyes, the air his nostrils, the directions his ears, the Prajāpati his genitals, death his anus and the moon his mind. The** ***devatās*** **protecting the various planets are his many arms. The god of death is his eyebrows, shame his lower lip, greed his upper lip, delusion his smile, and moon light his teeth. The trees are the Lord's bodily hairs, and the clouds are the hair on his head.**

**Комментарий:**

“The earth is his feet” means the śakti of his feet is worshipped as non-different from the śakti of the earth.

### Text 10

*kaustubha-vyapadeśena svātma-jyotir bibharty ajaḥ*  
*tat-prabhā vyāpinī sākṣāt śrīvatsam urasā vibhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Upon his chest the almighty, unborn Lord bears the pure** ***jīva*** **in the form of the** ***vibhūti*** **known as the Kaustubha gem along with the Śrīvatsa mark, which is the direct manifestation of this gem's expansive effulgence.**

**Комментарий:**

Similarly the Lord’s Kaustubha manifests in the world as the jīvas (*svātma-jyotiḥ*).

The jīva as revealed by the senses is accepted to be Śrīvatsa.

### Text 16

*indriyāṇi śarān āhur ākūtīr asya syandanam*  
*tan-mātrāṇy asyābhivyaktiṁ mudrayārtha-kriyātmatām*

**Перевод:**

**His arrows are said to be the senses, and his chariot is the active, forceful mind. His external appearance is the subtle objects of perception, and the gestures of his hands are the essence of all purposeful activity.**

**Комментарий:**

The mind (*ākūtīḥ*) endowed with kriyā-śakti is called the Lord’s chariot. The sense objects are called the Lord’s manifestation. Purposeful actions are his hand gestures (*mudrayā*), such as abhaya-mūdra etc.

### Text 17

*maṇḍalaṁ deva-yajanaṁ dīkṣā saṁskāra ātmanaḥ*  
*paricaryā bhagavata ātmano durita-kṣayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s circular abode is the place where the** ***devatās*** **worship the Supreme Lord, spiritual initiation is the means of purification for the spirit soul, and rendering devotional service to the Lord is the process for eradicating all one's sinful reactions.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord’s abode shaped like a circle (*maṇḍalam*) is the place where the devatās worship the Lord. Dīksā is qualification for directly attaining the Lord (*saṁskāraḥ*).

### Text 18

*bhagavān bhaga-śabdārthaṁ līlā-kamalam udvahan*  
*dharmaṁ yaśaś ca bhagavāṁś cāmara-vyajane 'bhajat*

**Перевод:**

**Playfully carrying a lotus, which represents the various qualities designated by the word** ***bhaga,*** **the Supreme Lord accepts service from a pair o*****f cāmara*** **fans, which are religion and fame.**

**Комментарий:**

His spiritual lotus represents spiritual qualities (*bhaga*). They are considered non-different.

### Text 19

*ātapatraṁ tu vaikuṇṭhaṁ dvijā dhāmākuto-bhayam*  
*tri-vṛd vedaḥ suparṇākhyo yajñaṁ vahati pūruṣam*

**Перевод:**

**O** ***brāhmaṇas*****! The Lord's umbrella represents fearlessness found in Vaikuṇṭha, and Garuḍa, who carries the Lord of sacrifice, is the sacrifice mentioned in the three Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord’s umbrella represents Vaikuṇṭha created by the son of Vikuṇṭhā above Brahmaloka. One should think of that place as the umbrella of Nārāyaṇa, the presiding deity of the universal form.

### Text 20

*anapāyinī bhagavatī śṛīḥ sākṣād ātmano hareḥ*  
*viṣvakṣenas tantra-mūrtir viditaḥ pārṣadādhipaḥ*  
*nandādayo 'ṣṭau dvāḥ-sthāś ca te 'ṇimādyā harer guṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī, who never leaves the Lord's side, appears with him in this world as the representation of his internal potency. Viṣvaksena, the chief among his personal associates, is known to be the personification of the Pañcarātra and other** ***tantras.*** **And the Lord's eight doorkeepers, headed by Nanda, are his mystic perfections, beginning with** ***aṇimā.***

**Комментарий:**

**Bhagavat Sandarbha 118:**

The commentary says, “She is the constant śakti of the Lord because she is the cit form of his svarūpa (*sākṣād ātmanaḥ*). She is non-different from him.”

Using the word *sākṣāt* differentiates her from māyā (who is a indirect form):

*vilajjamānayā yasya sthātum īkṣā-pathe ’muyā \|*  
*vimohitā vikatthante mamāham iti durdhiyaḥ \|\|*

**The ignorant jīvas, bewildered by māyā who is ashamed to stand in sight of the Lord, boast about “I” and “mine.” (SB 2.5.13)**

Her constant nature is described:

*paramātmā hari devas tac-chaktiḥ śrīr ihoditā \|*  
*śrīr devī prakṛtiḥ proktā keśavaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*na viṣṇunā vinā devī na hariḥ padmajāṁ vinā \|\|*

**The Lord, ātmā in all beings, arose here with his śakti named Śrī. She is called Devī or Prakṛti, and he is called Keśava. She is never without Viṣṇu and he is never without her. (Hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātra)**

*nityaiva sā jagan-mātā viṣṇoḥ śrīr anapāyinī \|*  
*yathā sarva-gato viṣṇus tathaiveyaṁ dvijottama \|\|*

**O brāhmaṇa! The mother of the universe, Śrī, is eternally the consort of Viṣṇu. Just Viṣṇu is everywhere, she is also everywhere. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.8.17)**

*evaṁ yathā jagat-svāmī deva-devo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*avatāraṁ karoty eṣā tathā śrīs tat-sahāyinī \|\|*

**Just as the Lord of the universe Janārdana incarnates in this world, his consort also incarnates with him. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9.142)**

*aparaṁ tv akṣaraṁ yā sā prakṛtir jaḍa-rūpikā \|*  
*śrīḥ parā prakṛtiḥ proktā cetanā viṣṇu-saṁśrayā \|\|*  
*tām akṣaraṁ paraṁ prāhuḥ parataḥ param akṣaram \|*  
*harir evākhila-guṇa akṣara-trayam īritam \|\|*

**Prakṛti who is inferior and eternal is unconscious. Śrī is superior prakṛti, conscious and under the direct shelter of Viṣṇu. She is eternal and superior. The Lord endowed with all qualities is superior to her and eternal. Thus there are three eternal entities. (Skanda Purāṇa)**

### Text 21

*vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaḥ puruṣaḥ svayam*  
*aniruddha iti brahman mūrti-vyūho 'bhidhīyate*

**Перевод:**

**Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha are the names of the direct personal expansions of Svayam Bhagavān, O** ***brāhmaṇa*** **Śaunaka.**

### Text 22

*sa viśvas taijasaḥ prājñas turīya iti vṛttibhiḥ*  
*arthendriyāśaya-jñānair bhagavān paribhāvyate*

**Перевод:**

**One can conceive of the Supreme Lord in terms of awakened consciousness, dreaming, deep sleep, and spiritual consciousness, by knowledge gained through external objects, the senses and the mind.**

**Комментарий:**

The caturvyūha are imagined as parts of the universal form as explained in two verses.

### Text 23

*aṅgopāṅgāyudhākalpair bhagavāṁs tac catuṣṭayam*  
*bibharti sma catur-mūrtir bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, master of the four states, who removes suffering for those who worship him as his four expansions, each exhibiting limbs, associates, weapons and ornaments, maintains the four phases of existence.**

**Комментарий:**

The four maintain four types of consciousness with limbs, associates weapons and ornaments. The four states are worshipped as non-different from the limbs etc.

### Text 24

*dvija-ṛṣabha sa eṣa brahma-yoniḥ svayaṁ-dṛk*  
*sva-mahima-paripūrṇo māyayā ca svayaitat*  
*sṛjati harati pātīty ākhyayānāvṛtākṣo*  
*vivṛta iva niruktas tat-parair ātma-labhyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord is the revealer of the Vedas, and he reveals himself. He is full in his own powers but by his** ***māyā*** **he creates, maintains and destroys through Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva. Though his knowledge is never covered, he can be described by the devotees. He is attained only by his devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

He is glorified as the object of various types of worship. His svarūpa-śakti is shown by being the revealer of the Vedas, being self-manifesting and being full of power. To remove the doubt of being contaminated by māyā it is stated that he is not covered by māyā. This is because he carries out creation independently (*svayā*). He creates, maintains and destroys by that famous māyā. He can be described by the devotees (*tat-paraiḥ*) as if he were in their hands (*vivṛtaḥ iva*) since he can be realized in the heart (*ātma-labhyaḥ*) by them.

### Text 25

*śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-sakha vṛṣṇy-ṛṣabhāvani-dhrug-*  
*rājanya-vaṁśa-dahanānapavarga-vīrya*  
*govinda gopa-vanitā-vraja-bhṛtya-gīta*  
*tīrtha-śravaḥ śravaṇa-maṅgala pāhi bhṛtyān*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa! O friend of Arjuna! O chief among the descendants of Vṛṣṇi! O destroyer of those kings who are disturbing elements on this earth! O Lord whose prowess never deteriorates! O Govinda! O Lord who gives pleasure to the ears by the fame which purifies the universe, which is sung by Uddhava, the servant of the** ***gopīs*** **of Vraja! O Lord, please protect your devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

He prays to the Lord, showing the identity of that Lord by chanting his names. Or he prays to the Lord while indicating that this Lord is his goal. Kṛṣṇa-sakha and other names indicate Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā. Govinda and other name indicate Kṛṣṇa in Vraja.

The order is reversed with Dvārakā names first, which shows his position.

O Kṛṣṇa who is glorified by the cowherds, the gopīs and other servants in Vraja and by us! Give perfection (*pāh*i) to us, full of faith on the path (*bhṛtyān*). This shows the necessity of hearing Bhāgavatam as the sādhana and sādhya.

### Text 26

*ya idaṁ kalya utthāya mahā-puruṣa-lakṣaṇam*  
*tac-cittaḥ prayato japtvā brahma veda guhāśayam*

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who rises early in the morning and, with a purified mind, chants this description of the universal form, will realize Bhagavān, difficult to understand.**

**Комментарий:**

He will realize the nature of Bhagavān (*brahma*) difficult to understand (*guhāśayam*).

### Text 27-28

*śrī-śaunaka uvāca*  
*śuko yad āha bhagavān viṣṇu-rātāya śṛṇvate*  
*sauro gaṇo māsi māsi nānā vasati saptakaḥ*  
*teṣāṁ nāmāni karmāṇi niyuktānām adhīśvaraiḥ*  
*brūhi naḥ śraddadhānānāṁ vyūhaṁ sūryātmano hareḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śaunaka said: O Sūta! Śukadeva explained to Parīkṣit about the seven associations of the sun god in the different months. Please describe to us, who have great faith in your words, the different sets of seven personal features and associates that the sun-god exhibits during each month, along with their names and activities. The associates of the sun-god, who serve their lord, are expansions of the sun, who is a form of the Supreme Lord, and are engaged by the Lord in their service.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. “Having heard about Bhagavān, why are you eager to hear about the sun god’s associates?” They are the vyūha of the sun whose antaryāmī is the Lord (*sūryātmano hareḥ*). Thus we hear about the Lord. This is the meaning of gāyatrī worship.

### Text 29

*sūta uvāca*  
*anādy-avidyayā viṣṇor ātmanaḥ sarva-dehinām*  
*nirmito loka-tantro 'yaṁ lokeṣu parivartate*

**Перевод:**

**Sūta Gosvāmī said: The sun, created by Viṣṇu, the Supreme Soul of all embodied beings, through his beginningless material energy, travels among all the planets, establishing the movements of the planets.**

**Комментарий:**

The sun (*ayam*) arising from Viṣṇu by beginningless māyā (*anādy-avidyayā*) travels among the planets.

### Text 30

*eka eva hi lokānāṁ sūrya ātmādi-kṛd dhariḥ*  
*sarva-veda-kriyā-mūlam ṛṣibhir bahudhoditaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, the one soul of all the worlds and the original creator, and the sun is also the soul of the worlds. He is the source of all the ritualistic activities prescribed in the Vedas and has been divided in twelve forms by the Vedic sages.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus the Lord is identified with the sun. The Lord is described. He is the ātmā of all worlds (*eka ātmā lokānām*) and the sun as well is their ātmā.

## Chapter Twelve

### Text 1

*sūta uvāca*  
*namo dharmāya mahate namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vedhase*  
*brahmaṇebhyo namaskṛtya dharmān vakṣye sanātanān*

**Перевод:**

**Sūta Gosvāmī said: Offering my obeisances to** ***bhakti*****; to Lord Kṛṣṇa, the supreme creator; and to all the** ***brāhmaṇas*** **like Vyāsa*****,*** **I shall now describe the eternal activities of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Kṛṣṇa, famous as Svayam Bhagavān, the source of all avatāras (*vedhase*). Showing courtesy because of his humility, he offers respects to brāhmaṇas. I will describe bhakti (describing the Lord’s pastimes) famous as the eternal dharma:

*kālena naṣṭā pralaye vāṇīyaṁ veda-saṁjñitā*  
*mayādau brahmaṇe proktā dharmo yasyāṁ mad-ātmakaḥ*

**The Supreme Lord said: By the influence of time, the Vedic knowledge was lost at the time of annihilation. Therefore, when the subsequent creation took place, I spoke to Brahmā the Vedic knowledge in which** ***bhakti*** **is the essence. (SB 11.14.3)**

These are described in verses like SB 12.12.47

### Text 2

*etad vaḥ kathitaṁ viprā viṣṇoś caritam adbhutam*  
*bhavadbhir yad ahaṁ pṛṣṭo narāṇāṁ puruṣocitam*

**Перевод:**

**O great sages, I have narrated to you the wonderful pastimes of Viṣṇu, about which you inquired from me. Hearing such narrations is the suitable engagement for a person who is a human being.**

**Комментарий:**

In bhakti, hearing the pastimes of the Lord is the chief activity. Summarizing the great story, he begins to list the events chronologically. These stories are suitable for a human among humans, not the animal among humans. He criticizes the materialistic persons.

*śva-viḍ-varāhoṣṭra-kharaiḥ saṁstutaḥ puruṣaḥ paśuḥ \|*  
*na yat-karṇa-pathopeto jātu nāma gadāgrajaḥ \|\|*

**This human animal, whose ear has never heard about Kṛṣṇa, is praised by dogs, hogs, camels and donkeys. (SB 2.3.19)**

Or the stories which concern the Lord (*puruṣa*) are suitable for jīvas (*nārānām*).

### Text 3

*atra saṅkīrtitaḥ sākṣāt sarva-pāpa-haro hariḥ*  
*nārāyaṇo hṛṣīkeśo bhagavān sātvatām patiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This literature fully glorifies the Supreme Lord, who is the destroyer of sin, the shelter of the** ***jīvas,*** **the master of the senses, and master of the Sātvatas.**

**Комментарий:**

In the Bhāgavatam (*atra*), the supreme Lord (*hariḥ*) who manifests unlimited names like Bhagavān, is chiefly glorified directly (*sākṣāt*)—by his qualities, form and pastimes. These two different natures by predominance of one are then shown. He is the shelter of all jīvas (*nārāyaṇaḥ*). He is the inspiration for all the senses as Paramātmā (*hṛṣīkeṣaḥ*). This is one nature. The second is described: he is Bhagavān and the master of the Sātvatas. Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa is glorified as the king of the Yadus.

### Text 4

*atra brahma paraṁ guhyaṁ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam*  
*jñānaṁ ca tad-upākhyānaṁ proktaṁ vijñāna-saṁyutam*

**Перевод:**

**In this work, the great secret of impersonal Brahman along with the process** ***jñāna*** **along with its realization is presented through descriptions of the creation and destruction of the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

In glorifying Bhagavān, Brahman, which is the manifestation of the Lord without qualities, and which is generally characterized by creation of the universe, is described.

### Text 5

*bhakti-yogaḥ samākhyāto vairāgyaṁ ca tad-āśrayam*  
*pārīkṣitam upākhyānaṁ nāradākhyānam eva ca*

**Перевод:**

**The following topics are also narrated: the process of devotional service together with its subsidiary feature of renunciation, and the histories of Mahārāja Parīkṣit and the sage Nārada.**

**Комментарий:**

To accomplish this, the purpose of brahma-kāṇḍa, the meaning of the Vedas, is shown with explanations of jñāna, vijñāna and bhakti, each increasing in excellence, and detachment suitable for that (*vairāgyam*). Having stated the general contents, the topics are listed in order, starting with Parīkṣit’s history.

### Text 27

*yatrāvatīṛṇo bhagavān kṛṣṇākhyo jagad-īśvaraḥ*  
*vasudeva-gṛhe janma tato vṛddhiś ca gokule*

**Перевод:**

***Bhāgavatam*** **describes how Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Bhagavān, Lord of the universe, descended into this Yadu dynasty, how he took birth in the home of Vasudeva, and how he then grew up in Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

The word *ca* indicates his birth in Gokula (as well as in the prison). Otherwise the word *tu* would be used to say “he took birth in Vasudeva’s house but grew up in Gokula.” This is proved in Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha 147-153, with verses like *nandas tv aṭmaja utpannaḥ.* (SB 10.5.1)

### Text 31-33

*damanaṁ kāliyasyāher mahāher nanda-mokṣaṇam*  
*vrata-caryā tu kanyānāṁ yatra tuṣṭo 'cyuto vrataiḥ*  
*prasādo yajña-patnībhyo viprāṇāṁ cānutāpanam*  
*govardhanoddhāraṇaṁ ca śakrasya surabher atha*  
*yajñabhiṣekaḥ kṛṣṇasya strībhiḥ krīḍā ca rātriṣu*  
*śaṅkhacūḍasya durbuddher vadho 'riṣṭasya keśinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The chastisement of the serpent Kāliya; the rescue of Nanda Mahārāja from a great snake; the severe vows performed by the young** ***gopīs*****, who thus satisfied Lord Kṛṣṇa; the mercy he showed the wives of the Vedic** ***brāhmaṇas*****, who felt remorse; the lifting of Govardhana Hill followed by the worship and bathing ceremony performed by Indra and the Surabhi cow; Lord Kṛṣṇa's nocturnal pastimes with the cowherd girls; and the killing of the foolish demons Śaṅkhacūḍa, Ariṣṭa and Keśī—all these pastimes are recounted.**

**Комментарий:**

The repentance of the brāhmaṇas was however rather subtle. It is mentioned so that one will investigate the issue. The bathing ceremony performed by Indra and Surabhi is described.

### Text 36

*mathurāyāṁ nivasatā yadu-cakrasya yat priyam*  
*kṛtam uddhava-rāmābhyāṁ yutena hariṇā dvijāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then, O** ***brāhmaṇas,*** **this scripture recounts how Kṛṣṇa, while residing in Mathurā in the company of Uddhava and Balarāma, performed pastimes for the satisfaction of the Yadu dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

Uddhava is shown to be similar to Balarāma by mentioning the two together.

### Text 40-41

*caidya-pauṇḍraka-śālvānāṁ dantavakrasya durmateḥ*  
*śambaro dvividaḥ pīṭho muraḥ pañcajanādayaḥ*  
*māhātmyaṁ ca vadhas teṣāṁ vārāṇasyāś ca dāhanam*  
*bhārāvataraṇaṁ bhūmer nimittī-kṛtya pāṇḍavān*

**Перевод:**

**There are descriptions of the great exertion and the deaths of the King of Cedi, Pauṇḍraka, Śālva, the foolish Dantavakra, Śambara, Dvivida, Pīṭha, Mura, Pañcajana and other demons, along with a description of how Vārāṇasī was burned to the ground. The** ***Bhāgavatam*** **also recounts how L Kṛṣṇa relieved the earth's burden by engaging the Pāṇḍavas in the Battle of Kurukṣetra.**

**Комментарий:**

Great efforts and death is connected with all the demons in the list.

### Text 47

*patitaḥ skhalitaś cārtaḥ kṣuttvā vā vivaśo gṛṇan*  
*haraye nama ity uccair mucyate sarva-pātakāt*

**Перевод:**

**If when falling, slipping, feeling pain or sneezing one involuntarily cries out in a loud voice, "Obeisances to Lord Hari!" one will be automatically freed from all sins.**

**Комментарий:**

If one is freed from sins by such chanting how much more will be achieved by chanting with devotion.

### Text 51

*na yad vacaś citra-padaṁ harer yaśo*  
*jagat-pavitraṁ pragṛṇīta karhicit*  
*tad dhvāṅkṣa-tīṛthaṁ na tu haṁsa-sevitaṁ*  
*yatrācyutas tatra hi sādhavo 'malāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Those colorful words that do not describe the glories of the Lord, who alone can sanctify the whole universe, are considered to be a place of pilgrimage for crows, and are never used by those situated in transcendental knowledge. Where the Lord is glorified the devotees are without contamination.**

**Комментарий:**

Where the Lord is glorified (*yatrācyutaḥ*), the devotees are without contamination

### Text 52

*tad vāg-visargo janatāgha-samplavo*  
*yasmin prati-ślokam abaddhavaty api*  
*nāmāny anantasya yaśo 'ṅkitāni yat*  
*śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti sādhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The use of words in which, though not perfectly composed, there are the names of the Lord and descriptions of his glories which devotees hear, sing, and again receive, destroys the sins of all people.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse is explained in the First Canto. When there is a great speaker, others listen. When the person is a great speaker, he sings. When there is no great speaker, they repeat the words only (*gṛṇanti*).

### Text 64

*purāṇa-saṁhitām etām adhītya prayato dvijaḥ*  
*proktaṁ bhagavatā yat tu tat padaṁ paramaṁ vrajet*

**Перевод:**

**A** ***brāhmaṇa*** **who diligently reads this essential compilation of all the Purāṇas will go to the supreme destination, which the Supreme Lord Himself has herein described.**

**Комментарий:**

Immediate results are promised to encourage persons with material desires.

### Text 66

*kali-mala-saṁhati-kālano 'khileśo*  
*harir itaratra na gīyate hy abhīkṣṇam*  
*iha tu punar bhagavān aśeṣa-mūrtiḥ*  
*paripaṭhito 'nu-padaṁ kathā-prasaṅgaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nārāyaṇa, the soul of the universal form, who annihilates the accumulated sins of the Kali age, is not glorified much in other works. But Bhagavān, who has unlimited forms, is abundantly and constantly described throughout the various narrations of this** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*****.**

**Комментарий:**

**Paramātmā Sandarbha 107:**

Nārāyaṇa, who is the antaryāmī of the universe (*akhileśaḥ*) or Viṣṇu, its protector, who is the destroyer (*kālanaḥ)* of the collection of sins of Kali, is not glorified or is not glorified much (*abhīkṣṇam)* in other works (*itaratra*) which propound karma or Brahman. The word *tu* indicates emphasis. But Bhagavān is glorified constantly in Bhāgavatam (*iha*). He who has unlimited avatāra forms (*aśeṣa-mūrtiḥ*) is glorified as such. In other works he is described without much investigation. Described in each verse of Bhāgavatam with various narrations, Bhagavān alone is revealed (*paṭhitah)* completely (*pari*).

### Text 69

*sva-sukha-nibhṛta-cetās tad-vyudastānya-bhāvo*  
*'py ajita-rucira-līlākṛṣṭa-sāras tadīyam*  
*vyatanuta kṛpayā yas tattva-dīpaṁ purāṇaṁ*  
*tam akhila-vṛjina-ghnaṁ vyāsa-sūnuṁ nato 'smi*

**Перевод:**

**Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the son of Vyāsadeva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who destroys of all sin, and who, though fixed in his own bliss with no distractions, became attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and mercifully spread the** ***Bhāgavatam*** **which describes Kṛṣṇa and reveals the** ***rasa*** **of his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

He offers respects and indicates the conclusion of the whole scripture by reviewing the devotion in the heart of the speaker. Śukadeva destroys all obstacles or apathy to the proper bhāva (*akhila-vṛjina-ghnam*). The word *ajita* (unconquered) indicates Kṛṣṇa alone, as the principle form of the Lord because of his completeness. This was made clear in the First Canto, in discussing Vyāsa’s samādhi.

## Chapter Thirteen

### Text 4-9

*brāhmaṁ daśa sahasrāṇi pādmaṁ pañcona-ṣaṣṭi ca*  
*śrī-vaiṣṇavaṁ trayo-viṁśac catur-viṁśati śaivakam*  
*daśāṣṭau śrī-bhāgavataṁ nāradaṁ pañca-viṁśati*  
*mārkaṇḍaṁ nava vāhnaṁ ca daśa-pañca catuḥ-śatam*  
*catur-daśa bhaviṣyaṁ syāt tathā pañca-śatāni ca*  
*daśāṣṭau brahma-vaivartaṁ laiṅgam ekādaśaiva tu*  
*catur-viṁśati vārāham ekāśīti-sahasrakam*  
*skāndaṁ śataṁ tathā caikaṁ vāmanaṁ daśa kīrtitam*  
*kaurmaṁ sapta-daśākhyātaṁ mātsyaṁ tat tu catur-daśa*  
*ekona-viṁśat sauparṇaṁ brahmāṇḍaṁ dvādaśaiva tu*  
*evaṁ purāṇa-sandohaś catur-lakṣa udāhṛtaḥ*  
*tatrāṣṭadaśa-sāhasraṁ śrī-bhāgavataṁ iṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**The** ***Brahmā Purāṇa*** **consists of ten thousand verses, the** ***Padma Purāṇa*** **of fifty-five thousand,** ***Viṣṇu Purāṇa*** **of twenty-three thousand, the** ***Śiva Purāṇa*** **of twenty-four thousand and** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **of eighteen thousand. The** ***Nārada Purāṇa*** **has twenty-five thousand verses, the** ***Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa*** **nine thousand, the** ***Agni Purāṇa*** **fifteen thousand four hundred, the** ***Bhaviṣya Purāṇa*** **fourteen thousand five hundred, the** ***Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa*** **eighteen thousand and the** ***Liṅga Purāṇa*** **eleven thousand. The** ***Varāha Purāṇa*** **contains twenty-four thousand verses, the** ***Skanda Purāṇa*** **eighty-one thousand one hundred, the** ***Vāmana Purāṇa*** **ten thousand, the** ***Kūrma Purāṇa*** **seventeen thousand, the** ***Matsya Purāṇa*** **fourteen thousand, the** ***Garuḍa Purāṇa*** **nineteen thousand and the** ***Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa*** **twelve thousand. Thus the total number of verses in all the Purāṇas is four hundred thousand. Eighteen thousand of these belong to the** ***Bhāgavatam*****.**

**Комментарий:**

The details are given in Matsya Purāṇa:

*aṣṭādaśa-purāṇāni kṛtvā satyavatī-sutaḥ*  
*bhāratākhyānam akhilaṁ cakre tad upabṛṁhitam*  
*lakṣaṇaikena tat proktaṁ vedārtha-paribṛṁhitam*  
*vālmīkināpi yat proktaṁ rāmopākhyānam uttamam*  
*brahmaṇā ’bhihitaṁ tac ca śata-koṭi-pravistarāt*  
*āhṛtya nāradenaiva vālmīkāya punaḥ punaḥ*  
*vālmīkinā ca lokeṣu dharma-kāmārtha-sādhanam*  
*evaṁ sapādāḥ pañcaite lakṣāste parikīrtitāḥ.*

**Having written the eighteen Purāṇas, Vyāsa wrote the Mahābhārata, with a hundred thousand verses, filled with the same material, and reinforcing the meaning of the Vedas. There is the excellent story of Rāma by Vālmīki, told originally by Brahmā in a billion verses. Nārada summarized it, and gave it to Vālmīki. It was recited by Vālmīki to the people to attain dharma, artha and kāma. The total number of verses in the Purāṇas and Itihāsas is 525,000.**

### Text 10

*idaṁ bhagavatā pūrvaṁ brahmaṇe nābhi-paṅkaje*  
*sthitāya bhava-bhītāya kāruṇyāt samprakāśitam*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord first revealed the** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **to Brahmā. At the time, Brahmā, frightened by material existence, was sitting on the lotus flower that had grown from the Lord's navel.**

### Text 11-12

*ādi-madhyāvasāneṣu vairāgyākhyāna-saṁyutam*  
*hari-līlā-kathā-vrātā- mṛtānandita-sat-suram*  
*sarva-vedānta-sāraṁ yad brahmātmaikatva-lakṣaṇam*  
*vastv advitīyaṁ tan-niṣṭhaṁ kaivalyaika-prayojanam*

**Перевод:**

**From beginning to end, the** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **is full of the Lord’s pastimes which give bliss to devotees endowed with a sense of renunciation. This** ***Bhāgavatam*** **is the essence of all Vedānta philosophy because its subject matter is one Brahman, a substance with no duality. The main goal of the work is prema alone.**

**Комментарий:**

The Bhāgavatam is described in three verses. It was revealed by Kṛṣṇa (*bhagavatā*) to Brahmā, situated on the lotus in the navel of Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu.

*Sat* (in *sat-suram*) refers to ātmārāmas as in the following:

*itthaṁ satāṁ brahma-sukhānubhūtyā dāsyaṁ gatānāṁ para-daivatena*  
*māyāśritānāṁ nara-dārakeṇa sākaṁ vijahruḥ kṛta-puṇya-puñjāḥ*

**In this way with an abundance of splendor caused by Kṛṣṇa, they played with him, who was pure consciousness known as Brahman for the jñānīs, who was the Supreme Lord for the devotees with** ***dāsya-bhāva*** **and who was an ordinary human child for those covered by material illusion. (SB 10.12.11)**

“This jñāna is seen to become blue and then yellow (through awareness of objects). It is temporary. How can Bhāgavatam state that this jñāna is eternal and without a second?”

*sarva-vedānta-sāraṁ yad brahmātmaikatva-lakṣaṇam*  
*vastv advitīyaṁ tan-niṣṭhaṁ kaivalyaika-prayojanam*

**This Bhāgavatam** **is the essence of all Vedānta philosophy because its subject matter is one Brahman, a substance with no duality. The main goal of the work is pure bhakti. (SB 12.13.12)**

Brahman’s svarūpa is described in the following *satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma*: Brahman is existence, knowledge and bliss. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.1)

He is the cause of the universe. That is stated in the following. *Yenāśrutaṁ śrutaṁ bhavati:* by this entity what was not heard becomes heard. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1.3) *Yad-vijñānena sarva-vijñānaṁ pratijñātam:* by knowing him, everything becomes known. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) This is the promise. *Sad eva saumyedam agra āsīt:* O gentle one, the Lord exists before everything else. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.2.1) The Lord is satya-saṅkalpa (all his desires are fulfilled). *Tad aikṣata bahu syām*: he glanced, thinking “Let me be many.” (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)

In the following, though the jīva is actually separate from the Lord, by calling him *idam (anena*), it is indicated that the jīva is a portion of the Paramātmā by calling him *ātmā.* He accompanies the Lord who is the greatest, who is endowed with his svarūpa and his śakti.

*anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi*

**Let me enter with the jīva, ātmā, and divide name and form. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.3.2)**

In this statement spoken by the Lord, the jīva is considered to be one with the Lord since he is devoid of extreme difference, according to what Vyāsa saw in samādhi. The ātmā is an aṁśa of the Lord. *mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke*: the jīva is my aṁśa. (BG 15.7) *aṁśo nānā-vyapadeśā*: the jīva is a part of the Lord because of many scriptural statements. (Brahma-sūtra 2.3.41) Thus, in statements like *tattvam asi*: you are that (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7) there is identity of the Lord and jīva since the jīva is a conscious aṁśa of the Lord. Speaking of identity is a most effective means of presenting jñāna in the beginning.

The essence of all Vedānta (*sarva-vedānta-sāram*), having *advitīya- vastu* as the sole object (*niṣṭham*), is Bhāgavatam. This is understood from the previous verse:

*ādi-madhyāvasāneṣu vairāgyākhyāna-saṁyutam*  
*hari-līlā-kathā-vrātā- mṛtānandita-sat-suram*

**From beginning to end, the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is full of the Lord’s pastimes which give bliss to devotees endowed with a sense of renunciation. (SB 12.13.11)**

*Kaivalyaika-prayojanam* is explained. *Kevala* means pure, such as pure bhakti which is devoid of cheating (SB 1.1.2). That condition is called *kaivalya*. It is devoid of desires for material benefit or liberation. In the commentary on *kaivalya-sammata-pathas tv atha bhakti-yogaḥ* (SB 2.3.12) Śrīdhara Svāmī says that *kaivalya sammata-patha* means bhakti-yoga. This is the method to attain the Lord. That bhakti is called prema, since that the chief type of bhakti. Thus *kaivalyam* means the goal, prema for Bhagavān. This is understood from the following:

*sālokya-sārṣṭi-sāmīpya- sārūpyaikatvam apy uta*  
*dīyamānaṁ na gṛhṇanti vinā mat-sevanaṁ janāḥ*

**The devotees do not accept living on my planet, having similar powers, staying close to me, or having a similar form, what to speak of merging into me, when these things are offered, unless it involves service to me. (SB 3.29.13)**

### Text 13

*prauṣṭhapadyāṁ paurṇamāsyāṁ hema-siṁha-samanvitam*  
*dadāti yo bhāgavataṁ sa yāti paramāṁ gatim*

*jñānena vaiyāsaki-śabditena*  
*bheje khagendra-dhvaja-pāda-mūlam \|\|*

*sarva-vedānta-sāraṁ hi śrī-bhāgavatam iṣyate*

Bhāgavatam is explained. Rasa is described in *pibata bhāgavataṁ rasamālayam:* drink the rasa of Bhāgavatam. (SB 1.1.2)

*nātyantikaṁ vigaṇayanty api te prasādaṁ*  
*kimv anyad arpita-bhayaṁ bhruva unnayais te*  
*ye ’ṅga tvad-aṅghri-śaraṇā bhavataḥ kathāyāḥ*  
*kīrtanya-tīrtha-yaśasaḥ kuśalā rasa-jñāḥ*

**Persons who have realized you do not regard attainment of impersonal liberation as your mercy, what to speak of attaining a material position like Indra which is subject to fear caused by the Lord raising his eyebrow. O Lord! Those devotees, surrendered to your lotus feet, are expert knowers of** ***rasa*** **derived from narrations about your fame, which should be chanted and which purify everyone like a** ***tīrtha.*** **(SB 3.15.48)**

### Text 16

*nimna-gānāṁ yathā gaṅgā devānām acyuto yathā*  
*vaiṣṇavānāṁ yathā śambhuḥ purāṇānām idam tathā*

**Перевод:**

**Just as the Gaṅgā is the greatest of all rivers, Acyuta is the supreme among deities and Śiva is the greatest of Vaiṣṇavas, so** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **is the greatest of all Purāṇas.**

*Thus Bhāgavatam is the greatest scripture.*

### Text 18

*śrīmad-bhāgavataṁ purāṇam amalaṁ yad vaiṣṇavānāṁ priyaṁ*  
*yasmin pāramahaṁsyam ekam amalaṁ jñānaṁ paraṁ gīyate*  
*tatra jñāna-virāga-bhakti-sahitaṁ naiṣkarmyam āviskṛtaṁ*  
*tac chṛṇvan su-paṭhan vicāraṇa-paro bhaktyā vimucyen naraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This glorious** ***Bhāgavatam*** **is the spotless Purāṇa, and therefore dear to the Vaiṣṇavas. It as well describes pure** ***jñāna*** **beneficial even for** ***paramahaṁsas.*** **This** ***Bhāgavatam*** **rejects the process of** ***karma*** **and is endowed with the processes of j*****ñāna, vairāgya*** **and** ***bhakti.*** **Anyone who contemplates** ***Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*** **and who properly hears and chants it with devotion becomes completely freed from all obstacles to bhakti.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhāgavatam is dear to the devotees. Then secondary qualities are listed. Anyone who hears Bhāgavatam becomes liberated from all obstacles to bhakti.

### Text 19

*kasmai yena vibhāsito 'yam atulo jñāna-pradīpaḥ purā*  
*tad-rūpeṇa ca nāradāya munaye kṛṣṇāya tad-rūpiṇā*  
*yogīndrāya tad-ātmanātha bhagavad-rātāya kāruṇyatas*  
*tac chuddhaṁ vimalaṁ viśokam amṛtaṁ satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi*

**Перевод:**

**I meditate upon that pure, spotless Nārāyaṇa, who is free from suffering and death and who previously revealed this incomparable lamp of knowledge to Brahmā. Brahmā then spoke it to the sage Nārada, who narrated it to Kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyana Vyāsa. Śrīla Vyāsa revealed this** ***Bhāgavatam*** **to the greatest of sages, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, and Śukadeva mercifully spoke it to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.**

**Комментарий:**

Having shown the general conclusion in verse 12, he gives the conclusion, showing that Bhagavān is the work’s ultimate goal, supporting the first verse *janmady asya* (SB 1.1.1)

**Paramātmā Sandarbha 106:**

This work was revealed (*vibhasitaḥ)* to Brahmā, situated in the lotus in the navel of Garbhodakaśāyī, by Bhagavān, whose form is described in the Second Canto, and who showed Mahā-vaikuṇṭha to Brahmā. The work was not produced at that time however. The Bhāgavatam (*ayam*) at the beginning of first parārdha (*purā*) was given by Brahmā (*tad-rūpena*) to Nārada and later by Nārada (*tad-rūpinā*) to Vyāsa (*kṛṣṇāya*). And by Vyāsa (*tad-ātmanā*) it was given to Śukadeva (*yogīndrāya*). It was given by Śukadeva (*tad-ātmanā,* understood) to Parīkṣit (*bhagavad-rātāya*). By using the phrases *tad-rūpeṇa, tad-rūpinā,* and *tad-ātmanā* it is indicated that not only was *catuḥślokī* revealed each time but that, absorbed in their forms (*tad-rūpeṇa* etc.), they revealed the complete Purāṇa. It should be understood that finally Sūta speaks to the sages and says “I also speak the Purāṇa to you.” However he does not utter this out of humility. Thus the greatness of the teachers of Bhāgavatam among all teachers is shown. The sampradāya through Saṅkarṣaṇa is not separately mentioned as it is included in the revelation of Vyāsa.

We should meditate on the supreme being known as Bhagavān (*satyam paraṁ dhīmahi*). *Param* means Bhagavān as in the *sahasra nāma stotra. Yat tat param anutttamam:* he is the supreme Bhagavān without compare. *Ādyo ‘vatāraḥ puruṣah parasya:* the first avatāra (Mahā-viṣṇu) is an expansion of Bhagavān (*parasya*). (SB 2.6.42)

This verse also explains that the work is the meaning of gāyatrī, shown by the word *dhīmahi,* since it inspires the intelligence of Brahmā and others. It is said *gāyatrī-bhāṣya-rūpo’ sau bhāratārtha-vinirṇayaḥ:* Bhāgavatam is the commentary on the gāyatrī and explains the Mahābhārata. (Garuḍa Purāṇa)

### Text 20

*namas tasmai bhagavate vāsudevāya sākṣiṇe*  
*ya idam kṛpayā kasmai vyācacakṣe mumukṣave*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the Supreme Lord, Vāsudeva, the witness of my task, who mercifully explained this to Brahmā when he desired to give up everything devoid of bhakti.**

**Комментарий:**

Having summarized the meaning of Bhāgavatam, he offers respects to his guru, the supreme Lord. Brahmā desires to give up everything devoid of bhakti.

### Text 21

*yogīndrāya namas tasmai śukāya brahma-rūpiṇe*  
*saṁsāra-sarpa-daṣṭaṁ yo viṣṇu-rātam amūmucat*

**Перевод:**

**I offer my humble obeisances to Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the best of** ***yogīs*****, and the very form of** ***para-brahman*****, who saved Mahārāja Parīkṣit, bitten by the snake of material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

He offers respects to his teacher. Śukadeva was the chief of sages (*yogīndrāya*) spreading bhakti-yoga, concentrating completely on surrender to Kṛṣṇa. He brought about the appearance of the Lord (*brahma-rūpiṇe*). In verse 19 he is also referred to as *yogīndra*. Having remembering Śukadeva’s greatness he remembers his mercy.

*Saṁsāra* means that in which one wanders about (*saṁsarati*). It means the material world. Parīkṣit (*viṣṇu-rātam*) was bitten by the snake of the material world, whose poison spread everywhere, because he could not tolerate existence after Kṛṣṇa’s disappearance. He was pained by separation. Śukadeva freed him. He inspired him to cross over that suffering of separation. The suffering caused by Takṣaka was not considered by Parīkṣit or Śukadeva. The cause of Parīkṣit’s prema was getting mercy from the Lord (*viṣṇu-rātam*). He was a most intimate associate of the Lord.

### Text 22

*bhave bhave yathā bhaktiḥ pādayos tava jāyate*  
*tathā kuruṣva deveśa nāthas tvaṁ no yataḥ prabho*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord of lords! O master! Please grant us pure devotional service at your lotus feet, life after life.**

### Text 23

*nāma-saṅkīrtanaṁ yasya sarva-pāpa praṇāśanam*  
*praṇāmo duḥkha-śamanas taṁ namāmi hariṁ param*

**Перевод:**

**I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Lord, whose names when chanted, destroy all sins. Offering of obeisances to him destroys all suffering.**

**Комментарий:**

*nāma cintāmaṇiḥ kṛṣṇaś caitanya-rasa-vigrahaḥ \|*  
*pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-mukto ’bhinnatvān nāma-nāminoḥ \|\|*

**The name of the Lord is cintāmaṇi. It is Kṛṣṇa himself, a form of consciousness and rasa. It is complete, pure, and eternally liberated since there is no difference between the name and Kṛṣṇa himself. (Padma Purāṇa)**

*suvarṇa-varṇo hemāṅgo varāṅgaś candanāṅgadī \|*  
*sannyāsa-kṛt samaḥ śānto niṣṭhā-śānti-parāyaṇaḥ \|\|*

**He had a form like gold (*****suvarṇa-varṇaḥ*****). He had places desirable as gold (*****hemāṅgaḥ*****). He had beautiful limbs (*****varāṅgaḥ*****). He had armlets which please the devotees’ hearts (*****candanāṅgad*****ī). He took sannyāsa (*****sannyasa-kṛt*****). He reflected on the confidential pastimes of the Lord (*****śamaḥ*****). He was detached from everything except Kṛṣṇa (*****śāntaḥ*****). He was fixed in the sacrifice of chanting the Lord’s names (*****niṣṭhā*****). He pacified the advaitins who were against bhakti by performing kīrtana (*****śāntaḥ*****). He was the highest refuge for person of various bhāvas, up to mahābhāva (*****parāyaṇam*****).**

*evaṁ sahasra-nāmoktaṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-saṁjñitaḥ \|*  
*māṁ pāyād aparādhebhyaḥ sva-premāṁśena puṣyatu \|\|*

**Thus Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is described in the thousand names of Viṣṇu. May he protect me from offenses and nourish me with a portion of his prema.**

Here ends Krama Sandarbha, the seventh among the Sandarbhas which use Bhāgavatam as their source, and which contain the expert instructions of Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs, most revered members of the grand assembly of all Vaiṣṇavas, following the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa Caitanya-deva, who descended to distribute his worship, in order to purify Kali-yuga. All Glories to the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. All glories to Kṛṣṇa.

Vaiśeṣikas and Nyāyikas say that an object, though compromised of atomic parts, is a completely new creation. The effect, the object, is not present in subtle form in the cause, atoms.

The esoteric meaning is: I am the worshipper of the Lord. I am a conscious particle of the Lord. I belong to the Lord.” Considering this and considering the lotus feet of the Lord, surrender to the Lord. You will not see Takṣaka, your body or the universe separate from the Lord, because of fainting with bliss on seeing Kṛṣṇa.

This Rāma is Paraśurāma. The story is in *Mahābhārata.*

A slightly different list of the ten characteristics of a Mahā-purāṇa is given in the Twelfth Canto.

The negative element is expressed in the next line*. na tatra caksur gacchati na vag gacchati no manah*: the eye does not go there, the voice does not go there, nor the mind.

SB 3.8.7 relates that Saṅkarṣaṇa spoke the Bhāgavatam to Sanat-kumāra.
